# React Aria behavior inventory: collections and forms

Every behavior asserted by the React Aria and React Spectrum test suites for the collection and form
components, extracted test by test so a headless UI library can build a conformance suite against it.
Each bullet names one asserted behavior and cites the test it came from. Companion document:
the interactions and overlays half of the same suite.

## Sources

- Repo: https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum
- Commit: 4693fcc844a341107e7dd26fe456edb1e269e44c (committed 2026-09-09)
- Mined: 2026-09-13
- Scope: collections and forms. Menu, listbox, select, combobox, autocomplete, selection and
  typeahead, collections, slider, number field, text field, search field, form, label, tag group,
  grid list, table, calendar, date field, date picker, link, breadcrumbs, landmark.
- Not covered here: interactions (press, hover, focus, keyboard, long press, move), overlays
  (dialog, popover, tooltip, modal, tray, toast), drag and drop, tree, tabs, and the color
  components. Column resizing and virtualizer layout math were skipped deliberately.
- Reading the tests beats reading the docs for two reasons. The tests pin exact attribute values and
  exact announcement strings, and a good third of them exist only to hold down a browser or screen
  reader quirk. Those bullets say so, and they are the ones worth copying first.
- Deliberate omissions inside the scoped components: the column-resize suites
  (TableSizing.test.tsx, ariaTableResizing.test.tsx, tableResizingTests.tsx) and the drag and drop
  suites (TableDnd.test.js, ListViewDnd.test.js, the react-aria dnd tests) were not mined; drag and
  drop only appears where a component's own test file covers it in passing.
- Both halves of a parameterized test count as one bullet when the assertion is the same and the
  parameter only changes a locale or an interaction type; the bullet names the parameters instead.

## menu

### Roles and attributes

- Given a Menu with two Sections built from an items array and aria-labelledby="label", when rendered, then the container has role menu and aria-labelledby "label". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/Menu.test.js: "$Name renders properly")
- Given the same sectioned Menu, when rendered, then it contains 2 elements with role group, and each group has an aria-labelledby pointing at an existing heading element that carries role="presentation". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/Menu.test.js: "$Name renders properly")
- Given the same sectioned Menu with 2 sections, when rendered, then exactly 1 element with role separator is present. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/Menu.test.js: "$Name renders properly")
- Given the same sectioned Menu, when rendered, then 5 elements with role menuitem exist with text Foo, Bar, Baz, Blah and Bleh, each has a tabindex attribute, and none has aria-disabled. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/Menu.test.js: "$Name renders properly")
- Given an Item with textValue "Label" containing an icon, a Text label, a Text slot="description" and a Keyboard shortcut, when rendered, then the menuitem has aria-labelledby set to the label element id and aria-describedby set to "<description id> <keyboard id>" in that order. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/Menu.test.js: "supports complex menu items with aria-labelledby and aria-describedby")
- Given a Section with aria-label="Section" wrapping an Item with aria-label="Item" whose only child is an icon, when rendered, then the group has aria-label "Section", the menuitem has aria-label "Item", and the menuitem has neither aria-labelledby nor aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/Menu.test.js: "supports aria-label on sections and items")
- Given a Menu with aria-label="Test", when rendered, then the menu element has aria-label "Test". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/Menu.test.js: "supports aria-label")
- Given a Menu with data-testid="test", when rendered, then the menu element has attribute data-testid="test", so unknown data attributes pass through to the DOM. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/Menu.test.js: "supports custom data attributes")
- Given a Menu with selectedKeys={['alpha']} but no selectionMode prop, when rendered, then no hidden img checkmark element exists, so selection indicators require an explicit selectionMode. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/MenuTrigger.test.js: "should not show checkmarks if selectionMode not defined")
- Given a MenuTrigger whose Menu has two Items with href, when the menu is opened, then both items render as A elements with role menuitem for selectionMode none, menuitemradio for single and menuitemcheckbox for multiple, and each keeps its href ("https://google.com" and "https://adobe.com"); parameterized by describe.each over trigger type mouse, Enter, Space and it.each over selectionMode none, single, multiple. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/Menu.test.js: "with selectionMode = %s")
- Given useMenuTrigger with empty props and a closed state, when the hook is rendered, then menuTriggerProps has no aria-controls, no aria-expanded, a truthy aria-haspopup, and menuProps has a truthy id plus aria-labelledby equal to menuTriggerProps.id. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/menu/useMenuTrigger.test.js: "should return default props for menu and menu trigger")
- Given useMenuTrigger with state.isOpen true, when the hook is rendered, then menuTriggerProps['aria-controls'] equals menuProps.id, aria-expanded is truthy, and menuProps.aria-labelledby still equals menuTriggerProps.id. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/menu/useMenuTrigger.test.js: "should return proper aria props for menu and menu trigger if menu is open")
- Given useMenuTrigger with props {type: 'menu'}, when the hook is rendered, then menuTriggerProps['aria-haspopup'] is truthy. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/menu/useMenuTrigger.test.js: "returns the proper aria-haspopup based on the menu's type")
- Given useMenuItem with isVirtualized true for three items, when rendered, then the menuitems have aria-posinset "1", "2" and "3", that is 1-based and not 0-based. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/menu/useMenu.test.tsx: "sets correct aria-posinset (1-based) for virtualized menu items")
- Given useMenuItem with isVirtualized true for three items, when rendered, then every menuitem has aria-setsize "3", matching the total item count. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/menu/useMenu.test.tsx: "sets correct aria-setsize for virtualized menu items")
- Given a virtualized menu with two Sections of two items each rendered through useMenuSection, when rendered, then 2 elements with role group exist and each group's aria-labelledby resolves to a heading element in the DOM whose text matches /^Group [12]$/. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/menu/useMenu.test.tsx: "sets global aria-posinset across sections")
- Given the same sectioned virtualized menu, when rendered, then aria-posinset runs globally 1, 2, 3, 4 across sections rather than restarting per section, and aria-setsize is "4" on the first and last items. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/menu/useMenu.test.tsx: "sets global aria-posinset across sections")
- Given a virtualized Section with aria-label="Actions" and no title heading, when rendered, then the single group has aria-label "Actions" and no aria-labelledby attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/menu/useMenu.test.tsx: "labels a section group via aria-label when the section has no heading")
- Given an ActionMenu with no aria-label, when rendered, then the trigger button has aria-label "More actions", and after opening the menu has aria-labelledby equal to the button id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/ActionMenu.test.js: "basic test")
- Given an ActionMenu with aria-label="Custom Aria Label", when rendered, then the trigger button has aria-label "Custom Aria Label" instead of the default. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/ActionMenu.test.js: "custom aria label")
- Given a MenuTrigger, when the trigger is activated, then the menu has aria-labelledby equal to the trigger button id, the button has aria-expanded "true" and aria-controls equal to the menu id, and after the second activation the button has aria-expanded "false"; asserted by the shared verifyMenuToggle helper used by the longPress tests. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/MenuTrigger.test.js: "should open the menu on longPress")
- Given a MenuTrigger with trigger="longPress", when rendered, then the button has aria-describedby pointing at an element whose text is "Long press or press Alt + ArrowDown to open menu". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/MenuTrigger.test.js: "should open the menu on longPress")
- Given a ContextualHelpTrigger with isUnavailable wrapping a menu Item, when the menu is open, then that menuitem has aria-haspopup "dialog". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/MenuTrigger.test.js: "can open a sub dialog with hover")
- Given a ContextualHelpTrigger with isUnavailable={false}, when the menu is open, then the item has no hidden img icon and does not have aria-haspopup "dialog". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/MenuTrigger.test.js: "can not open a sub dialog with hover if isUnavailable is false")
- Given a ContextualHelpTrigger with isUnavailable wrapping an Item, when the menu is open, then the unavailable item renders a hidden-role img icon that itself does not carry aria-hidden. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/MenuTrigger.test.js: "adds the expected spectrum icon")
- Given a static or dynamic SubmenuTrigger menu, when the root menu opens, then only the submenu trigger item (index 1) contains a hidden img chevron while its neighbours do not, and that item has aria-haspopup "menu", aria-expanded "false" and data-key "Lvl 1 Item 2"; parameterized by it.each over static and dynamic renderers. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/SubMenuTrigger.test.tsx: "renders $Name submenu")
- Given the submenu trigger is hovered open, then two menus exist, the submenu has aria-labelledby equal to the trigger item id, and the trigger item has aria-expanded "true" and aria-controls equal to the submenu id; the nested level 2 trigger item likewise has a chevron img, aria-haspopup "menu", aria-expanded going false to true, data-key "Lvl 2 Item 3" and aria-controls equal to the third menu id, and each submenu has 3 menuitems. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/SubMenuTrigger.test.tsx: "renders $Name submenu")
- Given a Menu with aria-label "Animals", three MenuItems and a MenuSection containing a Header and three items, when rendered, then the menu element, every group element and every menuitem element have a data-rac attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should have the base set of aria and data attributes")
- Given a Menu and MenuItems with no className, when rendered, then the menu has class exactly "react-aria-Menu" and every menuitem has class exactly "react-aria-MenuItem". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should render with default classes")
- Given className "menu" on the Menu and "item" on each MenuItem, when rendered, then the menu class attribute is exactly "menu" and each menuitem class attribute is exactly "item", replacing the defaults. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should render with custom classes")
- Given data-foo="bar" on the Menu and data-bar="foo" on each MenuItem, when rendered, then the menu has data-foo="bar" and each menuitem has data-bar="foo". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support DOM props")
- Given a render prop on Menu and MenuItem that spreads the received props onto a div, when rendered, then the menu element and every menuitem element have data-custom="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support custom render function")
- Given a MenuItem render prop and no href on the item, when the render function is called, then "href" is not present in the props object it receives. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support custom render function")
- Given a MenuItem with href="#foo" and a render prop returning an anchor, when rendered, then the render function receives props.href === "#foo", each menuitem element has an href attribute, and the menu and menuitems have data-custom="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support custom render function as a link")
- Given a MenuContext.Provider with slots {test: {'aria-label': 'test'}} and a Menu with slot="test" and aria-label undefined, when rendered, then the menu has slot="test" and aria-label="test". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support the slot prop")
- Given a MenuItem containing Text slot="label" "Copy", Text slot="description" "Copy the selected text" and a Keyboard element "⌘C", when rendered, then the menuitem has aria-labelledby pointing at an element whose text is "Copy", and the text of the elements referenced by aria-describedby joined by spaces is "Copy the selected text ⌘C". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support slots")
- Given a Separator between two MenuItems, when rendered, then an element with role separator exists and has class "react-aria-Separator". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support separators")
- Given a Separator with className="my-separator", when rendered, then the separator element has class "my-separator". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support separators with custom class names")
- Given a Menu with selectionMode="multiple" and two MenuSections each containing a Header and three items, when rendered, then there are exactly 2 group elements, each with class "react-aria-MenuSection", and the first group has aria-labelledby pointing at an element with text "Veggies". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support sections")
- Given a Menu with an items array of two objects and a function child, when rendered, then the menuitem text contents are ["Cat", "Dog"]. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support dynamic collections")
- Given disabledKeys ['cat'] and a MenuItem className callback reading isDisabled, when rendered, then the first menuitem has aria-disabled="true" and class "disabled". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support disabled state")
- Given a MenuItem with the isDisabled prop, when rendered, then that menuitem has aria-disabled="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support isDisabled prop on items")
- Given a Menu with renderEmptyState returning "No results" and an empty child array, when rendered, then the menu has data-empty="true" and contains one menuitem whose text content is "No results". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support empty state")
- Given two MenuItems with href and the menu's selectionMode, when rendered, then the item role is menuitem for "none", menuitemradio for "single" and menuitemcheckbox for "multiple", both items are A elements, and their href attributes are "https://google.com" and "https://adobe.com". (describe.each over type = mouse and keyboard, it.each over selectionMode = none, single, multiple) (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "with selectionMode = %s")
- Given a MenuTrigger, when the menu is open, then the element matching ".react-aria-Popover" that contains the menu has data-trigger="MenuTrigger". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support menu trigger")
- Given a MenuTrigger with trigger="contextMenu" and the menu closed, when rendered, then the trigger button has no aria-haspopup, no aria-expanded and no aria-controls, and no element with role menu is in the document. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support a context menu trigger")
- Given a context menu opened by right click, when the menu is open, then the trigger button still has no aria-expanded and no aria-controls, and the popover containing the menu has data-trigger="MenuTrigger". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support a context menu trigger")
- Given a SubmenuTrigger wrapping a MenuItem inside an open menu, when the submenu is closed, then the trigger menuitem has aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded="false", data-has-submenu="true" and no data-open attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support a submenu trigger")
- Given an open submenu, when it is open, then the ".react-aria-Popover" ancestor of the submenu has data-trigger="SubmenuTrigger" and the trigger menuitem has data-hovered="true", aria-expanded="true" and data-open="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support a submenu trigger")
- Given a SubmenuTrigger nested inside a submenu, when the outer submenu is open, then the nested trigger menuitem has aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded="false", data-has-submenu="true" and no data-open, and after hovering it gains data-hovered="true", aria-expanded="true" and data-open="true" and its popover has data-trigger="SubmenuTrigger". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support nested submenu triggers")
- Given a menu whose sections contain a SubmenuTrigger, when opened with the menu tester, then getSections() returns 2 groups each with class "react-aria-MenuSection" whose aria-labelledby targets read "Actions" and "Settings", 7 menuitems are present, the popover has data-trigger="MenuTrigger", and getSubmenuTriggers() has length 1. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support sections")
- Given the submenu of that sectioned menu is opened via the tester, when open, then it has 6 options and 2 groups with class "react-aria-MenuSection" whose aria-labelledby targets read "Work" and "Personal". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support sections")
- Given a SubmenuTrigger whose second child is a Popover containing a form rather than a Menu, when the subdialog is open, then the ".react-aria-Popover" ancestor of the second dialog has data-trigger="SubmenuTrigger" and the submenu trigger item has data-hovered="true", aria-expanded="true" and data-open="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should contain focus for subdialogs")
- Given a Menu of 50 items wrapped in a Virtualizer with ListLayout and rowHeight 25, with HTMLElement clientWidth and clientHeight mocked to 100, when the menu is opened with the mouse, then fewer than 50 menuitems are rendered, the first has aria-posinset="1" and aria-setsize="50", and the last has aria-posinset equal to the rendered item count. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/VirtualizedMenu.test.tsx: "should support virtualized menu")
- Given a MenuTrigger with a Button and a closed menu, when rendered, then the trigger button exists with aria-haspopup="true", aria-expanded="false" and type="button", it contains the text "Menu Button", and no menu element exists. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaMenu.test-util.tsx: "has default behavior (button renders, menu is closed)")
- Given a MenuTrigger, when the menu is opened by clicking the trigger, then the menu has aria-labelledby equal to the trigger button's id and the trigger has aria-expanded="true" and aria-controls equal to the menu's id. ### Accessibility tooling

- Given a Menu with neither aria-label nor aria-labelledby, when rendered, then console.warn is called with "An aria-label or aria-labelledby prop is required for accessibility."; the test uses `using spyWarn` explicit resource management to restore the spy. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/Menu.test.js: "warns user if no aria-label is provided")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a submenu tray on a 700px screen, when a submenu trigger is hovered, then no submenu opens (1 menu remains), and only a touch press opens it; hovering another item afterwards does not close the open submenu either, so hover open and close are disabled in the tray. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/SubMenuTrigger.test.tsx: "should not open/close submenus on hover")
- Given the tray submenu tests, the comment notes user-event pointer presses are detected as virtual presses in jsdom, so the tests call the triggerTouch helper instead. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/SubMenuTrigger.test.tsx: "should open sub menus in the same tray on touch press")
- Given the closeOnSelect=false test, a TODO comment records that this behavior is not yet implemented in React Aria Components. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/MenuTrigger.test.js: "$Name doesn't close on menu item selection if closeOnSelect=false")
- Given the submenu render test, a TODO comment says these structural assertions belong in Chromatic tests instead. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/SubMenuTrigger.test.tsx: "renders $Name submenu")
- Given the it.each over "menu item" and "submenu trigger" for hovering out of a deep submenu, both branches in fact hover menuItems[0], so the two parameterizations exercise the same target. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/SubMenuTrigger.test.tsx: "should close the sub menu if the user hovers a $Name from a earlier sub menu")
- Given the test named for shift tabbing out of a subdialog, it actually renders in the ar-AE locale, focuses the unavailable item with two ArrowDown presses, presses ArrowLeft and only asserts the dialog is visible, so the name does not match what it pins down. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/MenuTrigger.test.js: "will close everything if the user shift tabs out of the subdialog")
- Given the longPress "should not open menu on click", "should not open menu on short press (default threshold set to ${DEFAULT_LONG_PRESS_TIME}ms)", "should not open the menu on Enter" and "should not open the menu on Space" tests, all four perform the identical TouchA press and assert on the getMenuOrThrow helper reference rather than calling it, so the Enter and Space paths are not actually exercised. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/MenuTrigger.test.js: "should not open menu on click")
- Given refs passed to Menu, MenuSection and MenuItem, when rendered, then each ref's current is an HTMLElement instance and the section element has aria-label="Felines". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support refs")
- Given a Menu with an onScroll prop, when a scroll event is fired on the menu element, then onScroll is called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should support onScroll")
- Given a MenuTrigger wrapped in UNSAFE_PortalProvider whose getContainer returns a custom div, when the trigger is clicked, then the menu's closest ancestor matching [data-testid="custom-container"] is that div. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should render the menu in the portal container")
- Given a Menu with three items plus a MenuLoadMoreItem with isLoading, when rendered, then the tester reports 4 options, the fourth has text "Loading...", and the parent element of the element with data-testid "loadMoreSentinel" has the inert attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should render the loading element when isLoading is true")
- Given the same menu without isLoading, when rendered, then there are 3 options, no "Loading..." text exists, and the loadMoreSentinel element is still in the document. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should render the sentinel but not the loading indicator when not loading")
- Given an empty items array with renderEmptyState, when rendered, then there is 1 option with text "empty state" and no "Loading..." text while the sentinel is present; after rerendering with isLoading there are 2 options, the second has text "empty state" and "Loading..." is present, so the loader renders even when the menu is empty. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should properly render the renderEmptyState if menu is empty")
- Given a mocked IntersectionObserver and a menu rendered with isLoading and onLoadMore, when observe is inspected then it was last called with the loadMoreSentinel element and onLoadMore has not fired; triggering the observer callback with isIntersecting true calls onLoadMore once, and after rerendering without isLoading the sentinel is observed again and another intersection brings onLoadMore to 2 calls, so loading state does not gate onLoadMore. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should only fire onLoadMore when intersection is detected regardless of loading state")

## listbox

### Roles and attributes

- Given a Spectrum ListBox with three sections and aria-labelledby="label", when rendered, then the element with role="listbox" exists and has aria-labelledby="label", and getSections returns one group per section (3), each with an aria-labelledby that points at an existing heading element carrying role="presentation". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "renders properly")
- Given the same three-section Spectrum ListBox, when rendered, then every section after the first has a divider immediately before its heading with role="presentation" and class spectrum-Menu-divider. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "renders properly")
- Given the same three-section Spectrum ListBox, when rendered, then there are 7 options (the sum of all section children), each option has a tabindex, no aria-selected, no aria-disabled, an aria-posinset numbered 1..7 continuing across section boundaries, and an aria-setsize, and findOption resolves Foo, Bar, Baz, Blah and Bleh by text. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "renders properly")
- Given a Spectrum ListBox option containing an icon, a Text label and a Text slot="description", when rendered, then the option has aria-labelledby equal to the label element id and aria-describedby equal to the description element id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports complex options with aria-labelledby and aria-describedby")
- Given a Spectrum ListBox with aria-label="Test", when rendered, then the listbox has aria-label="Test". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports aria-label")
- Given a Spectrum Section with aria-label="Section" containing an Item with aria-label="Item" whose only child is an icon, when rendered, then the group has aria-label="Section", the option has aria-label="Item", and the option has neither aria-labelledby nor aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports aria-label on sections and items")
- Given a Spectrum ListBox with data-testid="test", when rendered, then the listbox element has data-testid="test". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports custom data attributes")
- Given Spectrum Items rendered with data-name={item.name}, when rendered, then the first option has data-name="Foo". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "items support custom data attributes")
- Given a Spectrum ListBox with selectionMode="multiple", when rendered, then the listbox has aria-multiselectable="true". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports selecting multiple items")
- Given a Spectrum ListBox with items={[]} and isLoading, when rendered, then there is exactly 1 option and it contains a progressbar with aria-label="Loading…" and no aria-valuenow. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "should display a spinner while loading")
- Given a Spectrum ListBox with 2 items and isLoading, when rendered, then there are 3 options and the last one contains a progressbar with aria-label="Loading more…" and no aria-valuenow. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "should display a spinner inside the listbox when loading more")
- Given a react-aria-components ListBox with plain items and a ListBoxSection, when rendered, then the listbox, every section and every option carry the data-rac attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should have the base set of aria and data attributes")
- Given a default react-aria-components ListBox, when rendered, then the listbox has class="react-aria-ListBox" and every option has class="react-aria-ListBoxItem". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should render with default classes")
- Given className="listbox" on ListBox and className="item" on each ListBoxItem, when rendered, then the listbox has class="listbox" and every option has class="item". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should render with custom classes")
- Given data-foo="bar" on ListBox and data-bar="foo" on each ListBoxItem, when rendered, then the listbox has data-foo="bar" and every option has data-bar="foo". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support DOM props")
- Given a render prop on both ListBox and ListBoxItem that spreads props onto a div with data-custom="true", when rendered, then the listbox and every option have data-custom="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support custom render function")
- Given a ListBoxItem with href="#foo" and a render prop returning an anchor with data-custom="true", when rendered, then every option has an href and data-custom="true" and the listbox has data-custom="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support custom render function as a link")
- Given aria-label="test" on each ListBoxItem, when rendered, then every option has aria-label="test". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support aria-label on the listbox items")
- Given a ListBoxContext.Provider supplying slots={{test: {'aria-label': 'test'}}} and a ListBox with slot="test" and no aria-label, when rendered, then the listbox has slot="test" and aria-label="test". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support the slot prop")
- Given a ListBoxItem with textValue="Read" containing Text slot="label" and Text slot="description", when rendered, then the option has aria-labelledby pointing at an element with text "Read" and aria-describedby pointing at an element with text "Read only". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support slots")
- Given two ListBoxSections, the first with a Header "Veggies" and the second with aria-label="Protein", both with data-test-prop values, when rendered, then there are 2 groups each with class react-aria-ListBoxSection, the first has aria-labelledby pointing at the "Veggies" header, the second has aria-label="Protein", and each keeps its data-test-prop value. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support sections")
- Given a ListBox with renderEmptyState={() => 'No results'} and no children, when rendered, then the listbox has data-empty="true" and a single option contains the text "No results". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support empty state")
- Given a ListBox with disabledKeys={['cat']} in multiple selection mode and className={({isDisabled}) => ...}, when rendered, then the first option has aria-disabled="true" and class "disabled". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support disabled state")
- Given a ListBoxItem with isDisabled, when rendered, then that option has aria-disabled="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support isDisabled prop on items")
- Given a ListBox using useDragAndDrop with getItems, when rendered, then the first option has the draggable attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support draggable items")
- Given an AsyncListbox with isLoading and 3 items plus a ListBoxLoadMoreItem, when rendered, then there are 4 options, the last contains "Loading...", and the loadMoreSentinel test id element has a parent with the inert attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should render the loading element when loading")
- Given an AsyncListbox with 3 items and no isLoading, when rendered, then there are 3 options, no "Loading..." text is present, and the loadMoreSentinel element is still in the document. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should render the sentinel but not the loading indicator when not loading")
- Given an AsyncListbox with items={[]} and renderEmptyState, when rendered, then there is 1 option containing "empty state", no "Loading..." text, and the loadMoreSentinel is present. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should properly render the renderEmptyState if listbox is empty")
- Given that same empty AsyncListbox, when rerendered with isLoading, then there are 2 options with the empty state as the second one, "Loading..." is present, and the loadMoreSentinel is still present. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should properly render the renderEmptyState if listbox is empty")
- Given a Picker with two Sections of complex Items (icon plus Text, one with a Text slot="description"), when opened, then there are 6 options and 2 group elements, each group has aria-labelledby equal to the id of its heading text ("Section 1", "Section 2"), each heading element has role="presentation", and each group contains its own options. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports sections and complex items")
- Given that same open Picker, when the options are inspected, then each option has aria-labelledby equal to the id of its own label Text node, and the option with a Text slot="description" also has aria-describedby equal to that description element's id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports sections and complex items")

### Keyboard

- Given a Spectrum ListBox with autoFocus="first", when ArrowDown then ArrowUp are pressed, then focus moves to the second option and back to the first. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "allows user to change menu item focus via up/down arrow keys")
- Given autoFocus="first" and shouldFocusWrap, when ArrowUp is pressed on the first option, then the last option receives focus, and when ArrowDown is pressed there, focus returns to the first option. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "wraps focus from first to last/last to first item if up/down arrow is pressed if shouldFocusWrap is true")
- Given selectionMode="single" and disabledKeys=['Baz'] with autoFocus="first", when ArrowDown is pressed twice and ArrowUp twice from the first option, then focus goes option 0, 1, 3 and back 1, 0, skipping the disabled option 2. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports disabled items")
- Given selectionMode="single", when the test util toggles selection of option index 4 with keyboardActivation "Space" and interactionType "keyboard", then that option gets aria-selected="true", exactly one checkmark image exists in the listbox, and onSelectionChange is called once with a set containing "Bleh". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports using space key to change item selection")
- Given a ListBoxItem with isDisabled between two enabled items, when Tab focuses the first option and ArrowDown is pressed, then focus skips the disabled option and lands on the third option. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support isDisabled prop on items")
- Given a ListBox with orientation="horizontal", when Tab then ArrowRight, ArrowRight, ArrowLeft are pressed, then focus moves first option, second, third, then back to the second. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support horizontal orientation")
- Given a ListBox with layout="grid" and getBoundingClientRect mocked to a two column grid of 100x40 cells, when Tab then ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight are pressed, then focus moves option 0, 2, 1, 0, 1. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support grid layout")
- Given a 3x3 vertical grid layout ListBox with mocked getBoundingClientRect, when ArrowDown is pressed past the last row and ArrowUp past the first row, then focus stops at option 6 and option 0 respectively and no TypeError is thrown. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should not throw TypeError at boundaries of vertical grid layout when keyboard navigating (up/down)")
- Given layout="grid" with orientation="horizontal" and a two row mocked layout, when Tab then ArrowRight, ArrowUp, ArrowUp, ArrowDown are pressed, then focus moves option 0, 2, 1, 0, 1. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support horizontal grid layout")
- Given a 3x3 horizontal grid layout ListBox with mocked getBoundingClientRect, when ArrowRight is pressed past the last column and ArrowLeft past the first column, then focus stops at option 6 and option 0 respectively and no TypeError is thrown. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should not throw TypeError at boundaries of horizontal grid layout when keyboard navigating (left/right)")
- Given a 3x3 grid layout ListBox with selectionMode="single" and a keyboard ListBox tester configured with layout "grid", when toggleOptionSelection targets option index 5, then the text "1,1", then index 8, then each targeted option ends with aria-selected="true" and document.activeElement. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support keyboard navigation across grid layout via the test util")
- Given a Virtualizer with ListLayout rowHeight 25 around a 50 item ListBox scrolled to show items 7..14, when Tab then End are pressed, then 9 options are rendered, the last being "Item 49", so the focused last item is scrolled into view while the previous window stays mounted. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support virtualizer")
- Given a draggable ListBox with renderDropIndicator, when Enter is pressed on the first option to start a keyboard drag, then 4 options are drop indicators with class react-aria-DropIndicator and aria-labels "Insert before Cat", "Insert between Cat and Dog", "Insert between Dog and Kangaroo" and "Insert after Kangaroo", the first having data-drop-target="true" and the text "Test". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should render drop indicators")
- Given a keyboard drag in progress, when ArrowDown then Enter are pressed, then focus moves to the "Insert between Cat and Dog" indicator, data-drop-target moves from the first to the second indicator, and onReorder is called once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should render drop indicators")
- Given a draggable ListBox with disabledKeys={['dog']}, when a keyboard drag is started and ArrowDown pressed repeatedly, then the drop positions visited are "Insert before Cat", "Insert between Cat and Dog", "Insert between Dog and Kangaroo" and "Insert after Kangaroo", so positions around the disabled item are not skipped, and Escape cancels the drag. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should not skip drop positions before/after a disabled item")
- Given two ListBoxes where the second accepts onItemDrop, when a keyboard drag starts in the first and lands in the second, then the second listbox's first option has data-drop-target="true", the other two do not, focus is on that option, and pressing Enter calls onItemDrop once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support dropping on options")
- Given two ListBoxes where the second accepts onRootDrop, when a keyboard drag starts in the first, then focus moves to the second listbox element which has data-drop-target="true", and Enter calls onRootDrop once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support dropping on the root")
- Given a draggable ListBox with orientation="horizontal", when Enter starts a keyboard drag on the first option and ArrowRight is pressed, then the focused drop indicator goes from "Insert between Cat and Dog" to "Insert between Dog and Kangaroo", and Escape cancels. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support horizontal orientation")
- Given a draggable ListBox with layout="grid" and a mocked two column layout, when Enter starts a keyboard drag on the first option and ArrowDown is pressed, then the focused drop indicator goes from "Insert between Cat and Dog" to "Insert after Kangaroo". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support grid layout")
- Given a draggable ListBox with layout="grid" and orientation="horizontal" and a mocked two row layout, when Enter starts a keyboard drag on the first option and ArrowRight is pressed, then the focused drop indicator goes from "Insert between Cat and Dog" to "Insert after Kangaroo". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support horizontal grid layout")
- Given a virtualized draggable ListBox with onAction and useDragAndDrop, when Enter is pressed on the focused first option, then onAction is called once with key 0, onReorder is not called, and no react-aria-DropIndicator options are rendered, so plain Enter does not start a drag. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support onAction with drag and drop in virtualized list")
- Given that same virtualized draggable ListBox, when Alt+Enter is pressed on the first option, then drop indicators appear, the active element has an aria-label containing "Insert", onAction is not called again, and ArrowDown followed by Enter calls onReorder once and removes all drop indicators. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support onAction with drag and drop in virtualized list")
- Given a ListBox with selectionMode="multiple" and onKeyDown that calls e.continuePropagation() plus onKeyUp on items, when Tab then Enter then Escape are pressed, then onKeyUp fires once on Tab, and after Enter onKeyDown/onKeyUp are each at 1 and onSelectionChange at 1, and after Escape onKeyDown/onKeyUp are each at 2 and onSelectionChange at 2. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should call key handler when key is pressed on item")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given selectionMode="single", when option index 4 is clicked with user-event, then it gets aria-selected="true", it holds the only checkmark image in the listbox, and onSelectionChange is called once with a set containing "Bleh". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports using click to change item selection")
- Given selectionMode="single" with disabledKeys=['Baz'], when the disabled option is clicked, then it keeps aria-selected="false", has aria-disabled="true", no checkmark images exist, and onSelectionChange is not called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports disabled items")
- Given a react-aria-components ListBox with selectionMode="multiple" and hover callbacks plus className={({isHovered}) => ...}, when an option is hovered, then it gains data-hovered="true" and class "hover" and onHoverStart and onHoverChange each fire once; when unhovered, both are removed and onHoverEnd fires once with onHoverChange at 2. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support hover")
- Given a draggable ListBox with selectionMode="none", when an option is hovered and unhovered, then data-hovered="true" is added and then removed, so draggable options show hover state even when not selectable or actionable. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should show hover state on draggable options even when not selectable/actionable")
- Given a ListBox with no selection or action on its items, when an option is hovered, then it never gets data-hovered or the "hover" class and onHoverStart, onHoverChange and onHoverEnd are never called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should not show hover state when item is not interactive")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" and className={({isPressed}) => ...}, when MouseLeft is pressed down on an option, then it has data-pressed="true" and class "pressed", and on release both are removed. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support press state")
- Given a non-interactive ListBox item, when MouseLeft is pressed and released on it, then it never gets data-pressed or the "pressed" class. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should not show press state when not interactive")
- Given a ListBox with onAction on both the list and an item, when the first option is clicked, then the list onAction is called with "cat" and the item onAction is called once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support onAction on list and list items")
- Given a ListBox, when triggerOptionAction is used on the first option, then onAction is called once, parameterized over interactionType mouse, keyboard and touch. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support onAction, interactionType: $interactionType ")
- Given a ListBox with selectionMode="multiple", selectionBehavior="replace" and onAction, when triggerOptionAction fires a single press on the first option, then one option is selected and onAction is not called; when it fires a double click on the second option, then still one option is selected and onAction is called once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should trigger onAction on double click if selectionBehavior="replace"")
- Given a ListBox with selectionMode="multiple", selectionBehavior="toggle", onAction and installPointerEvent with interactionType "touch", when the first option is tapped, then nothing is selected and onAction fires once; when it is long pressed, then that option becomes selected and onAction is still at 1; a subsequent tap on the second option selects it too, giving 2 selected options. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should trigger selection on long press if both onAction and selection exist (touch only)")
- Given selectionMode="single" and no shouldSelectOnPressUp, when MouseLeft is pressed down on an option, then onSelectionChange has already been called once, and releasing does not call it again. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should select an item on pressing down when shouldSelectOnPressUp is not provided")
- Given selectionMode="single" with shouldSelectOnPressUp={false}, when MouseLeft is pressed down on an option, then onSelectionChange is called once and release does not call it again. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should select an item on pressing down when shouldSelectOnPressUp is false")
- Given selectionMode="single" with shouldSelectOnPressUp={true}, when MouseLeft is pressed down on an option, then onSelectionChange is not called, and it is called once only on release. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should select an item on pressing up when shouldSelectOnPressUp is true")
- Given a ListBox item with onAction, onPressStart, onPressEnd, onPress and onClick, when triggerOptionAction runs on option index 1, then each of the five callbacks is called exactly once, parameterized over interactionType mouse and keyboard. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support press events on items when using $interactionType")
- Given a draggable ListBox and a second empty ListBox that contains only a ListBoxLoadMoreItem with onRootDrop, when native dragstart on the first option is followed by dragenter and dragover on the empty listbox, then the empty listbox gets data-drop-target="true", and a drop event calls onRootDrop once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support dropping into an empty ListBox with a ListBoxLoadMoreItem")
- Given a real browser ListBox with layout="grid", display:grid over 3 columns of 100px and selectionMode="single", when toggleOptionSelection targets options 5, 0 and 8 in turn, then each gets aria-selected="true" and becomes document.activeElement, parameterized over interactionType $interactionType mouse and keyboard (vitest browser mode, vitest-browser-react). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.browser.test.tsx: "selects an option via $interactionType in real browser grid layout")

### Focus management

- Given a react-aria-components ListBox with autoFocus, when rendered, then document.activeElement is the listbox element itself rather than an option. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support autoFocus")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with shouldFocusOnHover and className={({isFocusVisible}) => ...}, when Tab focuses the first option, then it has data-focus-visible="true", class "focus" and no data-hovered; after an ArrowDown keydown and keyup, data-focus-visible and the class are removed. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support focus ring")
- Given a ListBox with shouldFocusOnHover, when the first option is hovered, then it receives real DOM focus, and a following ArrowDown moves focus to the second option. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should focus options on hovering with shouldFocusOnHover")
- Given shouldFocusOnHover set to false or undefined, when an option is hovered, then it does not receive focus, parameterized over both values. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should not focus options on hovering when shouldFocusOnHover is not true")
- Given the Spectrum FocusExample story with 6 options, when Tab and two ArrowDowns focus the third option, then that option has aria-posinset="3", aria-setsize="6" and real focus, and Enter gives it aria-selected="true". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "should move focus to the next item that is not disabled")
- Given the focused and selected third option is removed through a confirmation alertdialog, when the dialog closes, then the ListBox has 5 options, the alertdialog is gone, focus is forwarded from the ListBox back onto the option now at index 2, and that option reports aria-posinset="3" and aria-setsize="5". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "should move focus to the next item that is not disabled")
- Given two selected options are then removed through the same dialog flow, when the dialog closes, then 3 options remain and focus lands on option 0 with aria-posinset="1" and aria-setsize="3". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "should move focus to the next item that is not disabled")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given selectionMode="single" with defaultSelectedKeys=['Blah'] and autoFocus="first", when rendered, then exactly one option is selected, it is document.activeElement, it has aria-selected="true" and tabindex="0", contains the text "Blah" and a checkmark image. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports defaultSelectedKeys (uncontrolled)")
- Given that uncontrolled single-selection ListBox, when Enter selects option index 4 through the keyboard, then only "Bleh" is selected with aria-selected="true", there is exactly one checkmark image in the whole listbox, and onSelectionChange is called once with a set containing "Bleh". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports defaultSelectedKeys (uncontrolled)")
- Given selectionMode="single" with controlled selectedKeys=['Blah'] and autoFocus="first", when rendered, then option 3 is focused, has aria-selected="true" and tabindex="0", and holds the single checkmark. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports selectedKeys (controlled)")
- Given that controlled single-selection ListBox, when Enter is pressed on option 4, then option 4 stays aria-selected="false", option 3 stays selected with its checkmark, only one checkmark exists, and onSelectionChange is still called once with a set containing "Bleh". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports selectedKeys (controlled)")
- Given selectionMode="multiple", when option 3 then option 1 are clicked, then both get aria-selected="true" and a checkmark, there are 2 checkmarks total, and onSelectionChange is called twice with sets containing "Blah" then "Bar". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports selecting multiple items")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with defaultSelectedKeys=['Foo','Bar'], when rendered, then 2 checkmarks exist and options 0 and 1 have aria-selected="true" with texts "Foo" and "Bar". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports multiple defaultSelectedKeys (uncontrolled)")
- Given that uncontrolled multiple-selection ListBox, when option 4 is clicked, then it becomes aria-selected="true" with a checkmark, 3 checkmarks exist, and onSelectionChange is called once with a set containing "Bleh", "Foo" and "Bar". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports multiple defaultSelectedKeys (uncontrolled)")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with controlled selectedKeys=['Foo','Bar'], when rendered, then 2 checkmarks exist on options 0 and 1, and when option 4 is clicked it stays aria-selected="false" with no checkmark, the count stays at 2, and onSelectionChange is called once with a set containing "Bleh". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports multiple selectedKeys (controlled)")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with defaultSelectedKeys=['Foo','Bar'], when the first selected option is clicked again, then it becomes aria-selected="false" with no checkmark, one checkmark remains, and onSelectionChange is called once with a set containing "Bar". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports deselection")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with defaultSelectedKeys=['Foo','Bar'] and disabledKeys=['Baz'], when the disabled option is clicked, then it keeps aria-selected="false", has aria-disabled="true", the checkmark count stays at 2, and onSelectionChange is not called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports disabledKeys")
- Given selectionMode="none", when an option is clicked and Space and Enter keydowns are fired on two other options, then none of them get aria-selected="true", no checkmark images exist, and onSelectionChange is never called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "prevents selection of any items")
- Given a react-aria-components ListBox with selectionMode="multiple" and className={({isSelected}) => ...}, when toggleOptionSelection runs on the first option and then again, then aria-selected="true" and class "selected" are added and then removed. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support selection state")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given a ListBox with selectionMode="multiple" inside a Modal and Dialog opened from a DialogTrigger, when an option is selected with Enter and Escape is pressed once, then the option stays in the document but becomes aria-selected="false" and the modal stays open; a second Escape removes the option from the document and calls onOpenChange a second time with false. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should clear selection on first Escape, then allow the modal to close on the second Escape")

### SSR and hydration

- Given a Spectrum ListBox with three Items inside a Provider, when server rendered and hydrated, then no errors are thrown. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.ssr.test.js: "should render without errors")
- Given a react-aria-components ListBox with three ListBoxItems inside React.StrictMode where a button conditionally inserts a fourth item, when server rendered, then the HTML already contains options with text Left, Middle, Right; after hydration the same three options are present, and clicking the button yields Left, Middle, Extra, Right in that order. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.ssr.test.js: "should render without errors")
- Given a react-aria-components ListBox with two ListBoxSections each with a Header, when server rendered and hydrated, then both groups are labelled by their Header text "Veggies" and "Protein" and contain options Lettuce, Tomato, Onion and Ham, Tuna, Tofu respectively, both on the server output and after hydration. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.ssr.test.js: "should render with sections")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given a Spectrum ListBox rendered with aria-labelledby undefined and no aria-label, when rendered, then console.warn is called with "If you do not provide a visible label, you must specify an aria-label or aria-labelledby attribute for accessibility". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "warns user if no aria-label is provided")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a Spectrum ListBox with items=[] and isLoading showing a spinner, when rerendered without isLoading, then the progressbar is removed from the document. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "should display a spinner while loading")
- Given a Spectrum ListBox with 2 items and isLoading showing 3 options, when rerendered without isLoading, then there are 2 options and the progressbar is removed from the document. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "should display a spinner inside the listbox when loading more")
- Given a Spectrum ListBox of 100 items with maxHeight 200, clientHeight mocked to 200 and listbox scrollHeight mocked to 4800, when rendered, then 6 options are rendered (5 rows of 48px fit plus one third overscan), and after scrolling to 250, 1500 and 5000 with scroll events, onLoadMore is called exactly once. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "should fire onLoadMore when scrolling near the bottom")
- Given a Spectrum ListBox driven by useAsyncList with maxHeight 300 whose first page of 5 items exactly fills the mocked scrollHeight of 300, when the list settles, then a second page loads automatically giving 10 options and onLoadMore having been called once. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "should fire onLoadMore if there aren't enough items to fill the ListBox ")
- Given a react-aria-components ListBox with onScroll, when a scroll event is fired on the listbox, then onScroll is called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support onScroll")
- Given a Virtualizer with ListLayout rowHeight 25 around a 50 item ListBox and clientWidth/clientHeight mocked to 100, when rendered, then only 7 options are rendered ("Item 0" through "Item 6"), each with aria-setsize="50" and an aria-posinset. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support virtualizer")
- Given that virtualized ListBox, when scrollTop is set to 200 and a scroll event is fired, then 8 options are rendered, "Item 7" through "Item 14". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support virtualizer")
- Given a virtualized AsyncListbox with 50 items, isLoading and loaderHeight 30, when rendered, then 8 options are rendered with the last containing "Loading...", that loader row has no aria-posinset and no aria-setSize, its parent is positioned at top 1250px (50 items times 25px) with height 30px, and the loadMoreSentinel inside it has a parent with the inert attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should always render the sentinel even when virtualized")
- Given a virtualized AsyncListbox without isLoading, when rendered, then 7 options are rendered with no "Loading..." text and the sentinel's grandparent is at top 1250px with height 0px and inert; with items=[] the empty state is the only option at top 0px height 0px; and with items=[] plus isLoading the loader row is rendered first with the empty state second and the sentinel wrapper at top 0px height 30px. (skipped in repo, with a code comment that the tree renders empty when run after the preceding virtualized test because contextSize stays 0) (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should not reserve room for the loader if isLoading is false")
- Given an AsyncListbox with onLoadMore and a mocked IntersectionObserver, when rendered with isLoading, then observe is last called with the loadMoreSentinel element and onLoadMore has not fired; triggering an isIntersecting callback calls onLoadMore once even while loading. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should only fire loadMore when intersection is detected regardless of loading state")
- Given that same AsyncListbox rerendered without isLoading, when the intersection callback is triggered again, then observe is still watching the same sentinel and onLoadMore reaches 2 calls, so loadMore depends only on intersection and not on loading state. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should only fire loadMore when intersection is detected regardless of loading state")
- Given refs on ListBox, ListBoxSection and ListBoxItem, when rendered, then each ref current is an instance of HTMLElement. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support refs")
- Given a Spectrum ListBox with selectionMode="none" and two Items with href, when each is triggered, then both options are anchor elements with an href and the default click handler fires once with target an HTMLAnchorElement whose href is https://google.com/, parameterized over %s mouse and keyboard. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "should support links with selectionMode="none"")
- Given a Spectrum ListBox with link Items and selectionMode single or multiple, when each item is triggered, then the default click fires per item with the matching anchor href and neither option gets aria-selected="true", parameterized over selectionMode "%s" single and multiple and over %s mouse and keyboard. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "should support links with selectionMode="%s"")
- Given a react-aria-components ListBox with selectionMode="none" and two ListBoxItems with href, when each is triggered, then both options are anchors with href and the default click fires once with href https://google.com/, parameterized over %s mouse and keyboard. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support links with selectionMode="none"")
- Given a react-aria-components ListBox with link items and selectionMode single or multiple, when each item is triggered, then the default click fires once per item with the matching anchor href and neither option becomes aria-selected="true", parameterized over selectionMode "%s" single and multiple and over %s mouse and keyboard. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support links with selectionMode="%s"")
- Given a react-aria-components ListBox with link items, selectionBehavior="replace" and selectionMode single or multiple, when the first item is single clicked (mouse) or Space is pressed (keyboard), then no default click fires and the item becomes aria-selected="true"; a double click or Enter then fires the default click once with href https://google.com/, parameterized over selectionMode "%s" single and multiple and over %s mouse and keyboard. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support links with selectionMode="%s" selectionBehavior="replace"")
- Given a Spectrum Provider with router={{navigate, useHref}} and an Item href="/one" with routerOptions={{foo: 'bar'}}, when the item is triggered, then its rendered href is "/base/one" and navigate is called with ('/one', {foo: 'bar'}), while an external https://adobe.com item does not call navigate but does fire the default click, parameterized over %s mouse and keyboard. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "works with RouterProvider")

## select

### Roles and attributes

- Given a Picker with label "Test" and data-testid, when rendered, then the trigger button has aria-haspopup="listbox" and data-testid="test", the label "Test" is visible and the placeholder value "Select…" is visible. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "renders correctly")
- Given a Picker, when opened by mouse, then the trigger has aria-expanded="true" and aria-controls equal to the listbox id, the listbox is visible, onOpenChange was called once with true, and the listbox contains 3 options with text "One", "Two", "Three". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can be opened on mouse down")
- Given an open Picker, when it is closed by clicking the trigger again, then aria-expanded becomes "false" and the aria-controls attribute is removed from the trigger. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can be closed by clicking on the button")
- Given a Picker with a visible label, when rendered, then the trigger has aria-labelledby="<value id> <label id>" (value element first, label second) and both the label and the value span have ids. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports labeling with a visible label")
- Given a Picker with a visible label, when opened, then the listbox has aria-labelledby equal to the label id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports labeling with a visible label")
- Given a Picker with aria-label="Test" and no visible label, when rendered, then the trigger keeps aria-label="Test" and gets aria-labelledby="<value id> <trigger id>", and when opened the listbox has aria-labelledby equal to the trigger id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports labeling via aria-label")
- Given a Picker with aria-labelledby="foo", when rendered, then the trigger has aria-labelledby="<value id> foo", and when opened the listbox has aria-labelledby="foo". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports labeling via aria-labelledby")
- Given a Picker with both aria-label="Test" and aria-labelledby="foo", when rendered, then the trigger has aria-label="Test" and aria-labelledby="<value id> <trigger id> foo", and when opened the listbox has aria-labelledby="<trigger id> foo". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports labeling via aria-label and aria-labelledby")
- Given a Picker with isRequired and necessityIndicator="label", when rendered, then the "(required)" span is not aria-hidden, the label element (the span's parent) has an id, the trigger has aria-labelledby="<value id> <label id>", and when opened the listbox has aria-labelledby equal to that label id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports labeling with a visible label that includes the necessity indicator")
- Given a Picker with description="Please select an item.", when rendered, then the description element has an id and the trigger has aria-describedby equal to that id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports description")
- Given a Picker with isInvalid and errorMessage="Please select a valid item.", when rendered, then the error message element has an id and the trigger has aria-describedby equal to that id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports error message")
- Given a Picker with isLoading and no items, when rendered, then a progressbar inside the trigger has aria-label="Loading…" and no aria-valuenow, and the trigger has aria-describedby equal to the progressbar id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "should display a spinner while loading")
- Given a loading Picker, when isLoading is removed by rerender, then the progressbar is unmounted and the trigger has no aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "should display a spinner while loading")
- Given a Picker with both description and isLoading, when rendered, then the trigger has aria-describedby="<description id> <progressbar id>", and when isLoading is removed the trigger has aria-describedby equal to just the description id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "should display a spinner while loading")
- Given a Picker with 2 items and isLoading, when opened, then the listbox has 3 options and the third contains a progressbar with aria-label="Loading more…" and no aria-valuenow. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "should display a spinner inside the listbox when loading more")
- Given an open Picker showing a load-more spinner, when isLoading is removed by rerender, then the listbox has 2 options and the progressbar is no longer in the document. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "should display a spinner inside the listbox when loading more")
- Given a Picker with isDisabled, when clicked, then no listbox is rendered, onOpenChange was not called, the trigger keeps aria-expanded="false" and the trigger does not receive focus. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "does not open on mouse down when isDisabled is true")
- Given a RAC Select with Label, SelectValue, description Text and errorMessage Text slots, when rendered, then the outer element carries the data-foo="bar" prop, the trigger shows the default placeholder "Select an item" and has no data-pressed, the trigger aria-labelledby resolves to the SelectValue element (class react-aria-SelectValue) then the Label (class react-aria-Label, text "Favorite Animal"), and aria-describedby resolves to "Description Error". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "provides slots")
- Given a RAC Select, when opened, then the trigger has data-pressed="true", the listbox has class react-aria-ListBox, and its closest .react-aria-Popover ancestor exists and has data-trigger="Select". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "provides slots")
- Given a SelectContext provider supplying slots {test: {'aria-label': 'test'}} and a Select with slot="test", when rendered, then the .react-aria-Select element has slot="test" and the trigger has aria-label="test". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support slot")
- Given a Select with a custom render function, when rendered, then the outer element receives the custom props, including data-custom="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support custom render function")
- Given a Select with data-testid passed twice (on TestSelect and as an override), when rendered, then exactly one element carries the data-testid and it has class react-aria-Select, so data- attributes land only on the outer element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should render data- attributes only on the outer element")
- Given a Select with allowsEmptyCollection, an empty ListBox and renderEmptyState, when opened, then the listbox has data-empty="true" and a single element with role="option" containing "No results". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support empty state")
- Given a Select with selectionMode="multiple", when opened, then the listbox has aria-multiselectable="true" and contains 3 options. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support multiple selection")
- Given a Select with a Label, Button, Text and ListBox all inside the Popover, when opened, then the Label inside the popover has no "for" attribute, the Button inside has no aria-expanded and the Text inside has no id, so Select contexts are cleared inside the popover. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should clear contexts inside popover")
- Given a Picker with real timers, when rendered, then the trigger has aria-haspopup="listbox" and data-testid="test", the label is visible and the value shows "Select…"; when opened the trigger has aria-expanded="true" and aria-controls equal to the listbox id and onOpenChange was called once with true. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/TempUtilTest.test.js: "basic flow without test util helpers")
- Given a Picker with jest fake timers, when rendered and opened after act(() => jest.runAllTimers()), then the trigger has aria-haspopup="listbox" and data-testid="test", the listbox is visible with 3 options, the trigger has aria-expanded="true" and aria-controls equal to the listbox id, and onOpenChange was called once with true. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/TempUtilTest.test.js: "basic flow without test util helpers")

### Keyboard

- Given a closed Picker with the trigger focused, when Space keydown and keyup fire on the trigger, then the listbox opens with 3 options, onOpenChange was called once with true, the trigger has aria-expanded="true" and aria-controls equal to the listbox id, and focus moves to the first option. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can be opened on Space key down")
- Given a closed Picker driven with interactionType keyboard, when Enter is pressed on the focused trigger, then the listbox opens, onOpenChange was called once with true, aria-expanded is "true", aria-controls matches the listbox id and focus is on the first option. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can be opened on Enter key down")
- Given a closed Picker, when ArrowDown keydown and keyup fire on the trigger, then the listbox opens and focus moves to the first option. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can be opened on ArrowDown key down and auto focuses the first item")
- Given a closed Picker, when ArrowUp keydown and keyup fire on the trigger, then the listbox opens and focus moves to the last option. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can be opened on ArrowUp key down and auto focuses the last item")
- Given a Picker whose middle item has key="" and which was opened with ArrowDown so the first option is focused, when ArrowDown is pressed twice then ArrowUp once on the listbox, then real DOM focus moves to the second option (the key="" one), then the third, then back to the second. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can change item focus with arrow keys, even for item key=""")
- Given an open Picker with focus on the listbox, when ArrowDown is pressed twice and then Space, then focus moves to the first then second option, onSelectionChange was called once with "two", the listbox is removed and after the restore-focus rAF the trigger is focused and shows "Two". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can select items with the Space key")
- Given a Picker driven with interactionType keyboard, when opened with Enter and the option "Two" is reached with arrow keys and confirmed with Enter, then onSelectionChange was called once with "two", focus is back on the trigger and the trigger shows "Two". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can select items with the Enter key")
- Given an open Picker with disabledKeys={['two']} and focus on the first option, when ArrowDown is pressed, then focus skips the aria-disabled="true" second option and lands on the third option, and Enter there calls onSelectionChange once with "three". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "skips disabled items")
- Given a closed Picker with the trigger focused via Tab, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then onSelectionChange is called once with "one" and the trigger shows "One". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "move selection on Arrow-Left/Right")
- Given a closed Picker whose selection is the first item, when ArrowLeft is pressed again, then the trigger still shows "One" (selection is clamped at the start of the collection). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "move selection on Arrow-Left/Right")
