- Given a closed Picker showing "One", when ArrowRight is pressed twice, then the trigger shows "Two" then "Three" with onSelectionChange call counts 2 then 3; a third ArrowRight leaves it at "Three" with the count still 3 (clamped at the end); then ArrowLeft twice walks back to "Two" (count 4) and "One" (count 5). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "move selection on Arrow-Left/Right")
- Given an open Picker with isOpen (controlled), when Escape keydown and keyup fire on the listbox, then the listbox stays visible and onOpenChange was called once with false. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "does not close in controlled open state")
- Given an open Picker with defaultOpen, when Escape keydown and keyup fire on the listbox, then the listbox is removed, aria-expanded becomes "false", aria-controls is removed and onOpenChange was called once with false. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "closes in default open state")
- Given a Picker with isDisabled, when Space keydown and keyup fire on the trigger, then no listbox is rendered, onOpenChange was not called, aria-expanded stays "false" and the trigger is not focused. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "does not open on Space key press when isDisabled is true")
- Given a Picker with links on items, when Enter keydown and keyup fire on the first option, then the listbox closes, the trigger still shows "Select…" (no selection is made) and the window click target is an HTMLAnchorElement with href "https://google.com/". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports links on items with %s" parameterized with 'keyboard' via it.each(['mouse', 'keyboard']))
- Given a closed RAC Select with a focused trigger and options keyed 0, 1, 2, when ArrowRight is pressed, then onSelectionChange was called once with the falsy key 0 and the trigger shows "0". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support arrow key navigation to a falsy key")
- Given a closed RAC Select reached with Tab, when ArrowRight is held for 2 repeat keydown events ({ArrowRight>2/}), then the selection advances twice, the last onChange call is with 1 and the trigger shows "1". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support repeat keydown events when holding an arrow key")
- Given a RAC Select with a name and interactionType keyboard, when "Kangaroo" is selected via keyboard, then the trigger text changes from the placeholder "Select an item" to "Kangaroo". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "select can select an option via keyboard")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given a closed Picker, when the trigger is clicked, then the listbox becomes visible with 3 options, onOpenChange was called once with true, and the trigger gets aria-expanded="true" plus aria-controls equal to the listbox id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can be opened on mouse down")
- Given a closed Picker, when touchStart fires on the trigger, then no listbox is rendered yet; only after touchEnd does the listbox open with onOpenChange called once with true, aria-expanded="true", aria-controls set and focus on the listbox, so the Picker opens on touch up rather than touch down. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can be opened on touch up")
- Given an open Picker, when the trigger is clicked a second time, then the listbox is removed, onOpenChange was called twice with the last call false, and after the restore-focus rAF the trigger is focused. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can be closed by clicking on the button")
- Given an open Picker, when document.body is clicked, then the listbox is removed, aria-expanded becomes "false", aria-controls is removed and onOpenChange was called twice with the last call false. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can be closed by clicking outside")
- Given an open Picker with focus on the listbox, when the option "Three" is clicked, then onSelectionChange was called once with "three", the popover closes, focus returns to the trigger and the trigger shows "Three". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can select items on press")
- Given a Picker with items keyed "", 0 and false, when each of "Empty", "Zero" and "False" is selected in turn, then onSelectionChange is called with "", then "0", then "false", focus returns to the trigger each time and the trigger shows "Empty", "Zero", "False" respectively. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can select items with falsy keys")
- Given an open Picker with focus on the listbox, when mouseEnter fires on the second option, then that option receives real DOM focus; ArrowDown then moves focus to the third option and Enter selects "three", closing the listbox and restoring focus to the trigger which shows "Three". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "focuses items on hover")
- Given a Picker with defaultSelectedKey="two" that is open with the selected option focused, when the already-selected option "Two" is pressed, then onSelectionChange is not called, the listbox closes, focus returns to the trigger and it still shows "Two" (no deselection in single selection mode). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "does not deselect when pressing an already selected item")
- Given a Picker whose items have href props, when the first option is clicked, then the options are rendered as A elements with the given hrefs, the listbox closes, the trigger still shows "Select…" and the window click target is an HTMLAnchorElement with href "https://google.com/". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports links on items with %s" parameterized with 'mouse' via it.each(['mouse', 'keyboard']))
- Given a Provider with a router {navigate, useHref} and a Picker whose first item has href="/one" and routerOptions={{foo: 'bar'}}, when that option is clicked (with mockClickDefault installed), then the option renders href="/base/one" and navigate was called with ('/one', {foo: 'bar'}). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "works with RouterProvider")
- Given a RAC Select, when the second option is clicked after opening, then the trigger shows "Dog". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "provides slots")
- Given a RAC Select with shouldCloseOnSelect={false} in single selection mode, when the option "Dog" is selected, then the trigger shows "Dog" and keeps data-pressed="true" because the popover stays open. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should stay open on selecting an option if shouldCloseOnSelect is false and single selection mode")
- Given a RAC Select with shouldCloseOnSelect and selectionMode="multiple", when the option "Dog" is selected, then the trigger shows "Dog" and no longer has data-pressed="true" because the popover closed. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should close on selecting an option if shouldCloseOnSelect is true and multiple selection mode")
- Given a RAC Select whose item keys are the numbers 0 to 4, when the trigger is clicked and the first option is clicked, then the trigger shows "0", so 0 is accepted as a valid value. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support falsy (0) as a valid default value")
- Given a RAC Select with an empty ListBox, when the trigger is clicked, then no popover is rendered; after rerendering with a ListBox containing only a ListBoxLoadMoreItem isLoading, clicking the trigger still renders no popover. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "shouldn't allow the user to open the select if there are no items")
- Given a Picker with a decoy element with role="listbox" elsewhere in the tree, when the Select tester selects the option "Three", then the tester resolves the real listbox through the trigger's aria-controls, the trigger shows "Three" and onSelectionChange was called once with "three". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/TempUtilTest.test.js: "basic flow with test util user")
- Given a Picker with fake timers, when the Select tester selects the option "Three", then the trigger shows "Three" and onSelectionChange was called once with "three". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/TempUtilTest.test.js: "basic flow with test util user")
- Given a RAC Select with Label, Button, SelectValue, description and errorMessage Text slots and a Popover ListBox, when the Select tester selects "Cat" under real timers, then the trigger shows "Cat" and onSelectionChange was called once with "cat". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/TempUtilTest.test.js: "works with RAC Select")
- Given the same RAC Select under jest fake timers, when the Select tester selects "Cat", then the trigger shows "Cat" and onSelectionChange was called once with "cat". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/TempUtilTest.test.js: "works with RAC Select")
- Given simulateMobile() and a Picker, when the Select tester opens it, then the listbox is rendered inside the element with data-testid="tray", so mobile renders the options in a tray. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/TempUtilTest.test.js: "check for tray")

### Focus management

- Given a closed Picker, when it is opened by mouse, then document.activeElement is the listbox itself rather than any option. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can be opened on mouse down")
- Given a closed Picker, when it is opened on touch up, then document.activeElement is the listbox. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can be opened on touch up")
- Given a Picker with selectedKey="four" and a mocked scrollIntoView module, when it is opened by click, then focus is on the fourth option and scrollIntoView was last called with (listbox, document.activeElement). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "scrolls the selected item into view on menu open")
- Given an open Picker, when it is closed with Escape via the Select tester, then document.activeElement is the trigger. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can be closed by pressing the Escape key")
- Given an open Picker and a button outside it, when that outside button is focused, then the listbox closes and FocusScope.restoreFocus still pulls focus back to the trigger, so document.activeElement is the Picker trigger rather than the outside button. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "closes on blur")
- Given an open Picker with inputs before and after it, when Tab keydown fires on the focused element, then the listbox stays in the document with aria-expanded="true" and aria-controls intact and focus remains on the listbox, so Tab does not move focus out. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "does not shift focus when tabbing")
- Given an open Picker dismissed through its hidden dismiss button, when the timers for the restore-focus rAF run, then document.activeElement is the trigger. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "should have a hidden dismiss button for screen readers")
- Given a Picker with a visible label, when the label element is clicked, then document.activeElement is the trigger button. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "focuses on the picker when you click the label")
- Given a Picker with isOpen (controlled open), when rendered, then the listbox is visible and document.activeElement is the listbox. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports controlled open state")
- Given a Picker with defaultOpen, when rendered, then the listbox is visible and document.activeElement is the listbox. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports default open state")
- Given a Picker with selectedKey="two", when opened, then focus starts on the selected (second) option rather than the listbox, and that option has aria-selected="true" and contains a visible checkmark img. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports controlled selection")
- Given a Picker with defaultSelectedKey="two", when opened, then focus starts on the second option which has aria-selected="true" and contains a visible checkmark img. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports default selection")
- Given a Picker with autoFocus and onFocus/onBlur/onFocusChange spies, when rendered, then the trigger is document.activeElement, onFocus was called and onFocusChange was called with true. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports autofocus")
- Given a Picker with autoFocus between two buttons, when Tab then Shift+Tab then Shift+Tab are pressed, then focus goes to the after button (onBlur once, onFocusChange(false) as call 2), back to the Picker (onFocus twice, onFocusChange(true) as call 3), then to the before button (onBlur twice, onFocusChange(false) as call 4). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "calls onBlur and onFocus for the closed Picker")
- Given a Picker with autoFocus, when it is opened with ArrowDown and the first option is selected with Enter, then onFocus and onFocusChange remain at one call each with true, onBlur was never called and the surrounding buttons' onFocus handlers were never called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "does not call blur when an item is selected")
- Given a RAC Select with autoFocus, when rendered, then document.activeElement is the trigger. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support autoFocus")
- Given a RAC Select with an input before it, a clear Button after the trigger and an input after, when Tab is pressed repeatedly, then focus goes before input, trigger, clear button, after input, and Shift+Tab walks the same order in reverse. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support extra children for use with the state")
- Given a Picker, when it is opened and the option "Three" is clicked under real timers, then the listbox is removed and waitFor confirms document.activeElement becomes the trigger, which then shows "Three". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/TempUtilTest.test.js: "basic flow without test util helpers")
- Given a Picker under fake timers, when it is opened, then document.activeElement is the listbox, and after selecting the third option and running the restore-focus timers document.activeElement is the trigger showing "Three". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/TempUtilTest.test.js: "basic flow without test util helpers")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a Picker with isOpen and onOpenChange, when rendered, then the listbox is open on mount and onOpenChange was never called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports controlled open state")
- Given a Picker with defaultOpen and onOpenChange, when rendered, then the listbox is open on mount and onOpenChange was never called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports default open state")
- Given a Picker, when an option is selected and then the listbox is reopened and closed with Escape, then onSelectionChange is still only called once and onOpenChange has been called 4 times in total, no listbox remains, focus is on the trigger and the trigger still shows "Three", so Escape does not clear the selection. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "does not clear selection on escape closing the listbox")
- Given a Picker with a controlled selectedKey="two", when the first option is selected with Enter, then onSelectionChange was called once with "one" but the trigger still shows "Two" because the prop did not change. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports controlled selection")
- Given a Picker with defaultSelectedKey="two", when the first option is selected with Enter, then onSelectionChange was called once with "one" and the trigger updates to show "One". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports default selection")
- Given a RAC Select with defaultSelectedKey="cat" and items whose children are render props reading isSelected, when rendered, then the trigger shows "Cat". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "supports items with render props")
- Given a RAC Select with defaultSelectedKey={1} and a SelectValue whose children function receives {selectedItem, selectedText}, when rendered, then the trigger shows "1 - Cat". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "supports custom select value")
- Given a RAC Select with placeholder="Select an animal", when rendered, then the trigger shows that placeholder. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "supports placeholder")
- Given a Select whose children are a render prop receiving {isOpen}, when closed the trigger shows "open" and when opened it shows "close". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support render props")
- Given a RAC Select and a separate Button that calls state.setSelectedKey(null) from SelectStateContext, when "Dog" is selected and then that clear button is pressed, then onSelectionChange was called with 'dog' and then with null, for 2 calls total. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support extra children for use with the state")
- Given a RAC Select with selectionMode="multiple", when two options are toggled and the popover is closed, then the trigger shows "Cat and Dog" and onChange was called twice with the last call ['cat', 'dog']. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support multiple selection")
- Given a RAC Select with selectionMode="multiple", when "Cat" and "Dog" are toggled on then "Cat" is toggled off then "Dog" is toggled off, then aria-selected flips accordingly on each option and onChange is called with ['cat', 'dog'], then ['dog'], then []. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support deselection if multiple selection is enabled")
- Given a RAC Select with selectionMode="multiple" and a controlled value={['dog', 'kangaroo']}, when opened, then the trigger shows "Dog and Kangaroo" and the options have aria-selected "false", "true", "true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support controlled multi-selection")
- Given a RAC Select with selectionMode="multiple", defaultValue={[1]} and a SelectValue children function reading selectedItems, when rendered the trigger shows "Cat", and after selecting "Dog" it shows "2 selected items". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "supports custom select value with multi-selection")

### Forms (name, value, validation, form reset, hidden inputs, autofill)

- Given a Picker with autoComplete="address-level1" and the 59 US states as items, when rendered, then a hidden LABEL element containing the picker label text wraps a hidden native select (found by role combobox with hidden: true), the label's parent has aria-hidden="true", the hidden select has tabIndex="-1" and autoComplete="address-level1", and it contains 60 options where option index i > 0 has the text of states[i - 1] (index 0 being the placeholder). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "should have a hidden select element for form autocomplete")
- Given that hidden native select, when input and change events fire on it with target value "CA" (simulating browser autofill), then onSelectionChange was called once with "CA" and the visible trigger shows "California". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "should have a hidden select element for form autocomplete")
- Given a form containing a Picker with name="picker" and no selection, when the form is submitted, then onSubmit fires once and FormData for "picker" is the empty string. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "Should submit empty option by default")
- Given a form containing a Picker with name="picker" and defaultSelectedKey="one", when the form is submitted, then onSubmit fires once and FormData for "picker" is "one". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "Should submit default option")
- Given a form with a controlled Picker name="picker" starting at "one" and a reset input, when the second option is selected the hidden [name=picker] input has value "two", and when the reset input is clicked the hidden input returns to "one". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports form reset")
- Given a Picker with name="picker" and form="test", when rendered, then the hidden [name=picker] input has the attribute form="test". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "should support form prop")
- Given React 19 or newer and a Picker whose defaultSelectedKey comes from useActionState, when the form action is submitted, then the Picker shows "Two" and the hidden input value becomes "two", so the select resets to the new defaultSelectedKey after the action. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "resets to defaultSelectedKey when submitting form action")
- Given a Form containing a Picker with isRequired and validationBehavior="native", when rendered, then the hidden input has the required attribute, input.validity.valid is false and the trigger has no aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports isRequired")
- Given that same required native-validation Picker, when form.checkValidity() runs, then the trigger gets aria-describedby pointing at text "Constraints not satisfied" and document.activeElement is the trigger; selecting the option "One" removes aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports isRequired")
- Given a Picker with validationBehavior="native", defaultSelectedKey="two" and validate returning 'Invalid value' for "two", when rendered the hidden input's validity.valid is false and the trigger has no aria-describedby; when form.checkValidity() runs the trigger gets aria-describedby pointing at "Invalid value" and receives focus; selecting "One" removes aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports validate function")
- Given a Form with validationErrors={{picker: 'Invalid value.'}} set from an onSubmit handler and a Picker with validationBehavior="native", when the submit button is clicked, then the trigger gets aria-describedby pointing at "Invalid value." and the hidden input's validity.valid is false; selecting "One" clears aria-describedby and makes validity.valid true. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports server validation")
- Given a Picker with isRequired, validationBehavior="native" and an errorMessage function reading e.validationDetails.valueMissing, when form.checkValidity() runs, then the trigger's aria-describedby target has the custom text "Please enter a value". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports customizing native error messages")
- Given a Form with a required native-validation Picker and a reset Button, when checkValidity() shows "Constraints not satisfied", then selecting "One" clears aria-describedby and clicking the reset button leaves the trigger with no aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "clears validation on reset")
- Given a Picker with the default validationBehavior (aria), defaultSelectedKey="two" and validate returning 'Invalid value', when rendered, then the trigger already has aria-describedby pointing at "Invalid value" while the hidden input's validity.valid stays true (aria behavior does not set native validity); selecting "One" removes aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports validate function")
- Given a Form with validationErrors={{picker: 'Invalid value'}} and a Picker using the default aria validation behavior, when rendered, then the trigger has aria-describedby pointing at "Invalid value", and selecting "One" removes it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports server validation")
- Given a RAC Select with name="select" and isDisabled, when rendered, then the hidden [name=select] input is disabled. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should send disabled prop to the hidden field")
- Given a form containing a RAC Select with name="select", isRequired and a FieldError, when rendered, then the hidden input has required, its validity.valid is false, the trigger has no aria-describedby and the Select wrapper has no data-invalid. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "supports validation errors")
- Given that same Select, when form.checkValidity() runs, then the trigger gets aria-describedby pointing at "Constraints not satisfied", the Select wrapper gets data-invalid and document.activeElement is the trigger; selecting "Cat" removes both aria-describedby and data-invalid. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "supports validation errors")
- Given a RAC Select with name="select" and form="test", when rendered, then the hidden [name=select] input has form="test". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support form prop")
- Given a Form with a required RAC Select whose selectedKey is controlled, when "Cat" is selected and submit is pressed onSubmit fires once; when the selection is reset to null and submit is pressed again onSubmit is still at one call and the hidden [name=select] input's value is the empty string, so a required select with a null key blocks submission. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should not submit if required and selectedKey is null")
- Given a Form containing a RAC Select with name="select" and selectionMode="multiple", when "Cat" and "Dog" are selected, then FormData.getAll('select') equals ['cat', 'dog']. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support multiple selection")
- Given a Form with a required multiple-selection RAC Select of 320 items and a FieldError, when submit is pressed with nothing selected, then the .react-aria-FieldError element has text "Constraints not satisfied". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support multiple selection form integration with many items")
- Given that same 320 item multiple select, when the first two options are clicked and the popover is closed, then the trigger shows "item0 and item1", FormData.getAll('select') equals ['0', '1'] and pressing submit again leaves no .react-aria-FieldError element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should support multiple selection form integration with many items")
- Given a form containing a RAC Select with name="select" and defaultValue="1", when FormData is constructed in a useEffect on mount, then formData.get('select') is already "1", so the hidden input carries a value immediately after the first render. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "has a value immediately after rendering")
- Given a HiddenSelect for a collection of 5 items with no selected key, when rendered, then it renders without throwing (the collection.size <= 300 branch). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/select/HiddenSelect.test.tsx: "should successfully render for collection.size <= 300 and no selected key")
- Given a HiddenSelect with name="select" for a collection of 400 items and no selected key, when rendered, then it renders without throwing (the collection.size > 300 branch). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/select/HiddenSelect.test.tsx: "should successfully render for collection.size > 300 with a name and no selected key")
- Given a form containing a HiddenSelect with name="select", an empty item list and value="value", when FormData is built from the form right after the initial render, then formData.get('select') equals 'value'. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/select/HiddenSelect.test.tsx: "should have form value after initial render")
- Given a HiddenSelect with label="select" and 5 items, when user.selectOptions picks '5' on the native select found by label text (simulating browser autofill firing change), then onSelectionChange was called with '5'. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/select/HiddenSelect.test.tsx: "should trigger on onSelectionChange when select onchange is triggered (autofill)")
- Given a HiddenSelect with label="select" and 5 items, when rendered, then the native select's first option has value="" and label set to a non-breaking space (the \u00A0 character), so the placeholder option is non-empty. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/select/HiddenSelect.test.tsx: "should include a non-empty placeholder option for native select markup")
- Given a form containing a HiddenSelect with name="select", 5 items and nothing selected, when FormData is built, then formData.get('select') is the empty string. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/select/HiddenSelect.test.tsx: "should submit an empty string when no value is selected")
- Given a HiddenSelect, when rendered, then the element with data-testid="hidden-select-container" has data-a11y-ignore="aria-hidden-focus". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/select/HiddenSelect.test.tsx: "should always add a data attribute data-a11y-ignore="aria-hidden-focus"")
- Given a HiddenSelect, when rendered, then the element with data-testid="hidden-select-container" has the data-react-aria-prevent-focus attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/select/HiddenSelect.test.tsx: "should always add a data attribute data-react-aria-prevent-focus")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given an open Picker, when Escape is pressed on the listbox, then aria-expanded becomes "false", aria-controls is removed, onOpenChange was called twice with the last call false and focus returns to the trigger. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "can be closed by pressing the Escape key")
- Given an open Picker, when focus moves to a button outside it, then the listbox is removed, aria-expanded becomes "false", aria-controls is removed and onOpenChange was called twice with the last call false. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "closes on blur")
- Given an open Picker, when the active element's native blur() fires blur and focusout with relatedTarget null (what Chromium produces on a real tab or app switch), then the listbox stays in the document, aria-expanded stays "true" and onOpenChange is still at one call, so losing focus with no replacement does not close the Picker (see useOverlay.ts comment and issues 4130 / 4922). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "does not close when focus is lost with no replacement, such as switching tabs")
- Given an open Picker, when the buttons are queried, then there are 2 elements with role button and 2 elements labeled "Dismiss", each with aria-label="Dismiss", so hidden dismiss buttons are provided for screen readers. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "should have a hidden dismiss button for screen readers")
- Given an open Picker, when the first hidden "Dismiss" button is clicked, then the listbox is removed from the document, aria-expanded becomes "false", aria-controls is removed and onOpenChange has been called twice with the last call false. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "should have a hidden dismiss button for screen readers")

### SSR and hydration

- Given a Picker with label "Picker" and three Items inside a Provider with the default theme, when server rendered and hydrated via testSSR, then it renders without errors. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.ssr.test.js: "should render without errors")
- Given a RAC Select with defaultSelectedKey="dog" inside React.StrictMode, when server rendered, then the server HTML already has the button textContent "Dog", and after hydration the button textContent is still "Dog". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.ssr.test.js: "should render text of default selected key")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a Picker with sections and complex items, when the option "Cut" is selected with Enter, then onSelectionChange was called once with "cut", the listbox closes, focus returns to the trigger which shows "Cut", and exactly 2 hidden img elements remain in the document. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports sections and complex items")
- Given that Picker reopened after selecting "Cut", when it opens, then focus is on the selected option which has aria-selected="true" and contains 2 hidden img elements (its icon plus the checkmark); navigating down twice and pressing Enter calls onSelectionChange a second time with "puppy", the trigger shows "Puppy", 2 hidden imgs remain in the document and the item's description text "Puppy description super long as well geez" is not visible. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports sections and complex items")
- Given a RAC Select with isInvalid rendered inside a Dialog that also contains a Text errorMessage slot, when rendered, then it does not throw. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "should not throw when rendered inside a Dialog with a Text errorMessage slot")
- Given a RAC Select with isInvalid rendered inside a Dialog with role="alertdialog" that also contains a Text errorMessage slot, when rendered, then it does not throw. ## combobox

### Roles and attributes

- Given a ComboBox with Label, Input, Button, description Text, errorMessage Text and a Popover with a ListBox, when rendered with defaultInputValue "C" and data-foo="bar", then the input has role combobox with value "C", the closest .react-aria-ComboBox has data-foo="bar", the input's aria-labelledby first id resolves to an element with class "react-aria-Label" and text "Favorite Animal", and its aria-describedby ids resolve to the joined text "Description Error". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "provides slots")
- Given a ComboBoxContext.Provider supplying slots {test: {'aria-label': 'test'}}, when the ComboBox is rendered with slot="test", then the .react-aria-ComboBox wrapper has slot="test" and the combobox input has aria-label="test". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support slot")
- Given a ComboBox given a custom render function returning a div with data-custom="true", when rendered, then the .react-aria-ComboBox element has data-custom="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support custom render function")
- Given a ComboBox with data-testid="combo-box", when rendered, then exactly one element carries that test id and it has class react-aria-ComboBox. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should render data- attributes on outer element")
- Given a ComboBox with selectionMode="multiple" and a ComboBoxValue with placeholder "No items selected", when rendered, then .react-aria-ComboBoxValue has text content "No items selected" and the combobox input's aria-describedby contains that element's id. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support multiple selection")
- Given a ComboBox with selectionMode="multiple", when the listbox is opened, then the listbox has aria-multiselectable="true" and renders 3 options. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support multiple selection")
- Given a ComboBox, when rerendered with isReadOnly, then the .react-aria-ComboBox wrapper gains data-readonly, having had no data-readonly attribute beforehand. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support read-only state")
- Given a Spectrum ComboBox, when rendered, then the input has `autoCorrect="off"`, `spellCheck="false"` and `autoComplete="off"`, the trigger button has `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, and the label is visible. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "renders correctly")
- Given an open ComboBox, when inspected, then the listbox has `aria-label="Suggestions"` plus an aria-labelledby of "<listboxId> <fieldLabelId>", the trigger button has `aria-expanded="true"`, `aria-controls` to the listbox, `aria-label="Show suggestions"` and an aria-labelledby of "<buttonId> <fieldLabelId>", the input has aria-controls and `aria-expanded="true"`, and neither the listbox nor its options have a tabIndex because focus stays in the input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "renders correctly")
- Given a closed ComboBox, when rendered, then the input has `aria-autocomplete="list"` and no aria-controls or aria-activedescendant, and the defaults are completionMode suggest with menuTrigger input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "features default behavior of completionMode suggest and menuTrigger input")
- Given a `name` prop, when rendered, then the input has that name attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "propagates the name attribute")
- Given `validationState="invalid"`, when rendered, then the field has `aria-invalid`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should have aria-invalid when validationState=\"invalid\"")
- Given sections in the collection, when the menu opens, then the sections render with their group semantics. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "supports rendering sections")
- Given sections, when navigating, then section headers are not selectable values. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "sections are not valid selectable values")
- Given `useComboBox` with a label and refs, when the hook runs, then labelProps.id exists with an htmlFor matching inputProps.id, the input has `role="combobox"` with `aria-autocomplete="list"`, aria-labelledby to the label, and no aria-controls or aria-activedescendant while closed; listBoxProps has an aria-labelledby of "<listboxId> <labelId>"; and the trigger button has an id, `excludeFromTabOrder`, aria-haspopup, no aria-expanded or aria-controls while closed, plus onPress, onPressStart and onKeyDown handlers. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/combobox/useComboBox.test.js: "should return default props for all the button group elements")

### Keyboard

- Given a ComboBox with onSelectionChange and a keyboard interactionType ComboBox tester, when toggleOptionSelection({option: 'Dog'}) is performed, then onSelectionChange is called with '2', the combobox input has value "Dog" and the listbox is closed (getListbox() returns null). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support selecting an option via keyboard")
- Given a ComboBox with allowsEmptyCollection, a controlled inputValue and a conditionally rendered ListBoxItem with onAction labelled `Create "${inputValue}"`, when the user types "L" and then presses ArrowDown and Enter (interactionType keyboard), then there is 1 option with text 'Create "L"', onAction is called once and the input value becomes "". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support onAction with %s")
- Given the same create-option ComboBox after selecting "Cat", when the user types "s" and presses ArrowDown then Enter, then the single option reads 'Create "Cats"', onAction has been called 2 times total and the input value returns to "Cat". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support onAction with %s")
- Given a ComboBox with selectionMode="multiple", allowsCustomValue, defaultValue ['1','2'] and defaultInputValue "", when the user types "Den" and presses the key under test (parameterized over '{Escape}', '{Enter}' and '{Tab}'), then the listbox is closed, the input keeps the value "Den" and .react-aria-ComboBoxValue still reads "Cat and Dog". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should preserve multi-select value with custom input on %s")
- Given an uncontrolled ComboBox with selectionMode="multiple" and defaultValue ['1','2'], when the listbox is opened and Enter is pressed, then onChange is called once with ['2'], and after ArrowDown and Enter onChange has been called 2 times with the last call receiving []. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should allow the user to deselect items with keyboard when multiselect (uncontrolled)")
- Given a controlled ComboBox with selectionMode="multiple" and value ['1','2'], when the listbox is opened and Enter is pressed, then onChange is called once with ['2'], and after ArrowDown and Enter onChange has been called 2 times with the last call receiving ['1'] (the controlled value never changes). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should allow the user to deselect items with keyboard when multiselect (controlled)")
- Given a closed ComboBox, when ArrowDown is pressed, then onOpenChange fires once with `(true, 'manual')`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "opens the menu on down arrow press")
- Given a closed ComboBox, when ArrowUp is pressed, then onOpenChange fires once with `(true, 'manual')`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "opens the menu on up arrow press")
- Given a closed ComboBox, when the user types, then onOpenChange fires once with `(true, 'input')`, the listbox opens filtered to the match, both the button and the input get aria-controls plus `aria-expanded="true"`, focus stays on the input with no aria-activedescendant, and onSelectionChange does not fire. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "opens the menu on user typing")
- Given `menuTrigger="manual"`, when the user types, then the menu does not open. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "doesn't open the menu on user typing if menuTrigger=manual")
- Given typed text that matches a disabled key, when the menu opens, then the item is listed but nothing is selected and no aria-activedescendant is set. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "doesn't select an item on matching input if it is a disabled key")
- Given an open filtered menu, when a character is typed that matches nothing, then the menu closes and both the button and input report `aria-expanded="false"` with no aria-controls. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "closes the menu if there are no matching items")
- Given an open menu, when ArrowDown, ArrowDown, ArrowUp are pressed, then aria-activedescendant walks the options while focus stays on the input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "allows the user to navigate the menu via arrow keys")
- Given a virtually focused option, when Enter is pressed, then the menu closes, the input value becomes the option text, and onSelectionChange fires once with that key. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "allows the user to select an item via Enter")
- Given a selected option whose text was partially deleted, when the same option is reselected with Enter, then the input text resets to the full option text, onSelectionChange does not fire again, and onInputChange fires with the restored text. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "resets input text if reselecting a selected option with Enter")
- Given `allowsCustomValue` with no focused item, when Enter is pressed, then the menu closes and onSelectionChange fires once with null. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "closes menu on Enter if allowsCustomValue=true and no item is focused")
- Given a virtually focused option that gets filtered out by further typing, when the list updates, then aria-activedescendant is cleared instead of moving to the first remaining option. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "doesn't focus the first key if the previously focused key is filtered out of the list")
- Given an already selected item, when Enter is pressed on it again, then the menu closes and onSelectionChange does not fire. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "closes menu when pressing Enter on an already selected item")
- Given an open menu with typed text, when Escape is pressed, then the input value resets to the last committed value (or empty when nothing was selected) and the menu closes, with aria-activedescendant cleared. Run under a `describe.each` over the controlled and uncontrolled configurations. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should reset the input value and close the menu when pressing escape")
- Given a focused option, when Tab or Shift+Tab moves focus away, then focus leaves the ComboBox and the focused item is selected. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "tab and shift tab move focus away from the combobox and select the focused item")
- Given an open menu with a selected key, when Tab is pressed, then the selected key is retained. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "retains selected key on tab")
- Given an open menu with a selected key, when Enter is pressed, then the selected key is retained. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "retains selected key on enter")
- Given an open menu, when the listbox is scrolled, then the menu closes. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should close menu on scroll")
- Given an open ComboBox, when inputProps.onKeyDown receives Enter, then preventDefault is called once so the form does not submit; after closing the menu and rerendering, Enter no longer calls preventDefault. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/combobox/useComboBox.test.js: "should prevent default on Enter if isOpen")
- Given a closed ComboBox, when Tab is pressed, then `state.commit` is not called; with the menu open, Tab calls commit once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/combobox/useComboBox.test.js: "should only call commit on Tab when the menu is open")
- Given a closed ComboBox, when ArrowDown then ArrowUp reach inputProps.onKeyDown, then `state.open` is called with ('first', 'manual') then ('last', 'manual') and toggle is never called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/combobox/useComboBox.test.js: "calls open and toggle with the expected parameters when arrow down/up/trigger button is pressed")
- Given the trigger button, when onPress fires with `pointerType: 'touch'`, then `state.toggle(null, 'manual')` is called rather than open; with a mouse the toggle happens on onPressStart instead, so touch waits for the release and mouse reacts on press down. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/combobox/useComboBox.test.js: "calls open and toggle with the expected parameters when arrow down/up/trigger button is pressed")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given a ComboBox trigger Button, when the button is clicked to expand the listbox, then the button gains data-pressed, having had no data-pressed attribute while collapsed. - Given an open ComboBox listbox with class "react-aria-ListBox" inside a .react-aria-Popover carrying data-trigger="ComboBox" and 3 options, when the second option is clicked, then the combobox input value becomes "Dog". - Given an open ComboBox whose ListBox has two ListBoxSections with Headers, when the "Fruit" section header is clicked, then the listbox remains in the document and visible, options remain interactive, and clicking the first option then closes the listbox and sets the input value to "Apple". - Given an open ComboBox (onOpenChange called once on open) with the input focused, when the combobox input is clicked, then the listbox stays visible, the combobox keeps focus and onOpenChange is not called again. - Given an open ComboBox, when the trigger button is clicked, then the listbox is removed (getListbox() is null), the combobox input keeps focus and onOpenChange fires once; clicking the button again reopens the listbox, keeps focus on the input and fires onOpenChange once more. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should close the combobox when clicking on the button, and it should reopen if clicked again")
- Given a ComboBox with isReadOnly and menuTrigger="focus", when the input is clicked, then no listbox is rendered. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should not open the menu when isReadOnly")
- Given the create-option ComboBox with allowsEmptyCollection and a controlled inputValue, when the user types "L" and clicks the single 'Create "L"' option (interactionType mouse), then onAction is called once and the input value becomes ""; typing "s" after selecting "Cat" and clicking 'Create "Cats"' brings onAction to 2 calls and restores the input value "Cat". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support onAction with %s")
- Given a closed ComboBox, when the trigger button is clicked, then the menu opens, focus stays in the text input rather than moving to the button, and clicking again closes it. - Given items already loaded, when the trigger button is clicked, then onOpenChange fires with `(true, 'manual')` and no item is auto focused. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "doesn't focus first item if there are items loaded")
- Given a touch device, when the trigger button is tapped, then the menu opens with focus moved into the input, and a second tap closes it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "opens for touch")
- Given a previously focused item and a closed menu, when the menu is reopened, then the focused item is not reset. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "it doesn't reset the focused item when re-opening the menu")
- Given typed filter text, when the trigger button is used to open the menu, then all items are shown rather than the filtered subset. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "shows all items")
- Given an open menu, when an option is clicked, then onSelectionChange fires once with its key. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "can select by mouse")
- Given a selected option with partially deleted text, when the same option is clicked again, then the input resets to the full text, onSelectionChange fires with that key, and onInputChange reports the restored text. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "resets input text if reselecting a selected option with click")
- Given an open menu, when the user mouses down on a menu item, then the input does not lose focus. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "input field doesn't lose focus when user mouse downs on a menu item")
- Given an already selected item, when it is clicked, then the menu closes. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should close the menu if user clicks on a already selected item")

### Focus management

- Given `menuTrigger="focus"`, when the input is focused, then onOpenChange fires once with `(true, 'focus')`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "opens menu when combobox is focused")
- Given `menuTrigger="focus"`, when the trigger button is clicked so the input gains focus, then onOpenChange fires once with `(true, 'focus')` rather than 'manual'. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "opens menu when combobox is focused by clicking button")
- Given a ref on a labelled ComboBox, when rendered, then `ref.current.UNSAFE_getDOMNode()` is the label's parent element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "attaches a ref to the label wrapper")
- Given a ref with no visible label, when rendered, then the ref points at the ComboBox wrapper. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "attaches a ref to the combobox wrapper if no label")
- Given a ref, when `focus()` is called on it, then the combobox input receives focus. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "calling focus() on the ref focuses the input field")
- Given an open menu with a focused option, when Tab is pressed, then the menu closes and the selection is committed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "closes and commits selection on tab")
- Given an open menu with typed text, when the user clicks outside to blur, then the menu closes and the value is committed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "closes and commits selection on blur (clicking to blur)")
- Given `allowsCustomValue` and typed text that is not an item, when the field is blurred, then the custom value is committed and the menu closes. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "closes and commits custom value")
- Given a selected key whose text matches the typed input, when the field is blurred, then the selected key is retained. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "retains selected key on blur if input value matches")
- Given `menuTrigger="manual"`, a non-matching typed value, and no focused item, when the field is blurred, then the input is cleared. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "clears the input field if value doesn't match a combobox option and no item is focused (menuTrigger=manual case)")
- Given typed text matching a disabled option, when the field is blurred, then the input is cleared. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "clears the input field if value matches a disabled combobox option")
- Given a virtually focused option, when the field is blurred, then that option is not selected. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "doesn't select the focused item on blur")
- Given an onBlur on the ComboBox and one on a wrapping element, when focus leaves, then both fire: the blur propagates out of the component. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "propagates blur event outside of the component")
- Given a ComboBox with no trigger button (`buttonRef.current` null) and an onBlur prop, when the input blurs with a null relatedTarget, then onBlur fires once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/combobox/useComboBox.test.js: "should call onBlur when no button provided and you leave the field")

- Given a ComboBox whose ListBox has a Fruit section (Apple, Banana) and a Vegetable section (Cabbage, Broccoli), when the combobox is focused and "p" is typed, then getSections() returns 1 group whose aria-labelledby resolves to text "Fruit" and that group contains exactly 1 option. - Given a ComboBox with defaultItems [{id:1,name:'Cat'},{id:2,name:'Dog'},{id:3,name:'Kangaroo'}] and a dynamic ListBox render function, when the combobox is focused and "c" is typed, then 1 option remains. - Given a ComboBox with allowsEmptyCollection, a renderEmptyState returning "No results" and a ListBoxLoadMoreItem in the ListBox, when the combobox is focused and "p" is typed so nothing matches, then the listbox is still rendered with exactly 1 option whose text content is "No results". - Given a multiple selection ComboBox, when Cat and Dog are toggled on and then Cat is toggled again, then Cat has aria-selected="false", Dog keeps aria-selected="true" and onChange was last called with ['2']; toggling Dog off leaves both aria-selected="false" and onChange last called with []. - Given a ComboBox with selectionMode="multiple", controlled inputValue "C" and controlled value ['2','3'], when the listbox is opened and "a" is typed, then the input value remains "C", onInputChange is called once with "Ca" and onChange is not called. - Given the default menuTrigger, when the input is fully cleared while open, then the menu stays open. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "doesn't closes the menu if you completely clear your textfield and menuTrigger != focus")
