- Given typed text, when filtering runs, then a "contains" match strategy is used, not prefix only. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "filters combobox items using contains strategy")
- Given a typed space only, when filtering runs, then nothing matches and no listbox opens. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should not match any items if input is just a space")
- Given an open menu, when a value is typed that matches nothing, then the menu closes and onOpenChange's last call is `(false, undefined)`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should close the menu when no items match")
- Given a virtually focused option, when more text is typed, then the focused item is cleared. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should clear the focused item when typing")
- Given an uncontrolled ComboBox, when the user types, then the menu opens and the value follows the typing. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "can be uncontrolled")
- Given a controlled `inputValue`, when the user types, then the rendered value does not change and onInputChange reports the attempted value. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "can be controlled")
- Given an uncontrolled ComboBox with a selected item, when the user deletes all the input text, then onSelectionChange fires a second time with null and the option loses `aria-selected="true"`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "if user deletes all text in input (uncontrolled)")
- Given a controlled `inputValue` with a selection, when the text is cleared, then onInputChange fires with the empty string while the displayed value only changes once the parent updates it, and onSelectionChange then fires with null. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "when inputValue is controlled")
- Given a controlled `selectedKey`, when the user deletes all the input text, then onSelectionChange fires with null but the selection in the list does not change because the parent still controls it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "doesn't happen if user deletes all text in input (controlled)")
- Given both `inputValue` and `selectedKey` controlled, when the text is cleared, then onInputChange fires once with the empty string and onSelectionChange never fires. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "does not fire onSelectionChange if both inputValue and selectedKey are controlled")
- Given both selectedKey and inputValue controlled, when the user interacts, then neither piece of internal state updates on its own. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "does not update state")
- Given both controlled, when the props change, then the input and selection both follow. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "updates when selectedKey and inputValue change")
- Given both controlled, when only selectedKey changes, then inputValue is left alone. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "does not update inputValue when only selectedKey changes")
- Given both controlled, when an item is selected, then the menu still closes. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "closes when selecting an item")
- Given a controlled selectedKey but uncontrolled open state, when an already selected item is clicked, then onOpenChange is still called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "calls onOpenChange when clicking on a selected item if selectedKey is controlled but open state isn't ")
- Given only `selectedKey` controlled, when the user types, then the input value updates but the selected key does not. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "updates inputValue state but not selectedKey")
- Given only `selectedKey` controlled, when the prop changes, then the input field updates to the new item's text. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "updates the input field when selectedKey prop changes")
- Given only `inputValue` controlled, when an item is chosen, then the selected key updates but the input value stays under the parent's control. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "updates selectedKey but not inputValue")
- Given only `inputValue` controlled, when the prop changes, then the input field updates. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "updates the input field when inputValue prop changes")
- Given controlled `items`, when text is typed, then the library's default filtering is not applied on top of the provided list. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "does not apply default filtering if controlled items are provided")
- Given a custom filter implemented in onInputChange, when text is typed, then the list shows the custom filtered items. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "updates items with custom filter onInputChange")
- Given a previously selected option and typed text, when the value is committed, then the input text resets to that option and the menu closes. Run under a `describe.each` over the controlled and uncontrolled variants. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should reset the input text and close the menu on committing a previously selected option")
- Given a newly chosen option, when committing, then the input shows the selected item and the menu closes. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should update the input field with the selected item and close the menu on commit")
- Given typed text and a blur, when the blur happens, then the input value resets and the menu closes. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should reset the input value and close the menu on blur")
- Given an invalid typed value, when the field is blurred, then the menu does not reopen. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should not open the menu on blur when an invalid input is entered")
- Given controlled items and a selected key whose textValue no longer matches after an items update, when the items change, then the input value updates to the new text. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should update the input value when items update and selectedKey textValue does't match")
- Given controlled items and a focused ComboBox, when the items update, then the input value is left alone so the user's typing is not clobbered. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "doesn't update the input value when items update but the combobox is focused")
- Given an open menu, when the items prop is replaced, then the listbox rerenders with the new items. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "updates the list of items when items update")
- Given items supplied through a map render function, when the items prop changes, then the list and the input value follow. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "updates the list of items when items update (items provided by map)")
- Given an uncontrolled ComboBox, when the user types, clears, and selects, then the input value and the selected item move independently. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should update both input value and selected item freely")
- Given `defaultSelectedKey` and a `defaultInputValue` that matches it, when rendered, then both are honored. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "supports defaultSelectedKey and defaultInputValue (matching)")
- Given a `defaultInputValue` that does not match `defaultSelectedKey`, when rendered, then the default input value is kept as typed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should keep defaultInputValue if it doesn't match defaultSelectedKey")
- Given `defaultInputValue` alone, when rendered, then no item is selected. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "defaultInputValue should not set selected item")
- Given `defaultSelectedKey` alone, when rendered, then the input value is set from that item. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "defaultSelectedKey should set input value")
- Given typed filter text and `allowsEmptyCollection` style configurations in a `describe.each` matrix, when the menu is opened via the trigger button, via arrow keys, or via menuTrigger focus, then all items are shown for the uncontrolled case and only the filtered ones for the controlled-items case. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "displays all items when opened via trigger button")
- Given the same matrix, when the menu is opened with arrow keys, then the item count matches that configuration's expectation. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "displays all items when opened via arrow keys")
- Given the same matrix with `menuTrigger="focus"`, when the field is focused, then the expected item count shows. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "displays all items when opened via menuTrigger=focus")
- Given the same matrix, when the input value changes, then the list shows the filtered subset and returns to the full list when cleared. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "displays filtered list when input value is changed")
- Given controlled items, when the menu is opened, then it does not expand to all items. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "controlled items combobox doesn't display all items when menu is opened")
- Given `useComboBoxState`, when created, then isOpen is false; calling open sets it true with onOpenChange `(true, undefined)` and close sets it false with `(false, undefined)`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/combobox/useComboBoxState.test.js: "should be closed by default")
- Given `state.open(focusStrategy, reason)`, when called with 'focus', 'input', or 'manual', then onOpenChange receives that reason verbatim, and closing always reports undefined. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/combobox/useComboBoxState.test.js: "onOpenChange should return the reason that open was called")
- Given `state.toggle(focusStrategy, reason)`, when it opens the menu, then onOpenChange receives the same reason values. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/combobox/useComboBoxState.test.js: "onOpenChange should return the reason that toggle was called when opening")
- Given `defaultInputValue: 'hello'`, when the state initializes, then inputValue is "hello". (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/combobox/useComboBoxState.test.js: "can have a default value")
- Given an uncontrolled input value, when setInputValue is called, then the state updates and onInputChange fires with the new value. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/combobox/useComboBoxState.test.js: "fires an event when the value is changed and updates if uncontrolled")
- Given an open ComboBox with no selection, when it closes, then the selected key does not change on its own. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/combobox/useComboBoxState.test.js: "does not change selection on close")
- Given neither value nor defaultValue, when the state initializes, then inputValue is the empty string and typing updates it with onInputChange. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/combobox/useComboBoxState.test.js: "starts blank if no (default) value")
- Given a controlled `inputValue`, when setInputValue is called, then the state value stays and onInputChange reports the attempted value. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/combobox/useComboBoxState.test.js: "can be controlled")
- Given `selectedKey`, when the state initializes, then the selection manager is in single selection mode with that key selected, and changing the selection reports through onSelectionChange while the controlled key stays put. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/combobox/useComboBoxState.test.js: "support selectedKey")
- Given `defaultSelectedKey`, when the state initializes, then single selection mode holds that key and it can change freely. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/combobox/useComboBoxState.test.js: "support defaultSelectedKey")
- Given neither selectedKey nor defaultSelectedKey, when the state initializes, then nothing is selected. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/combobox/useComboBoxState.test.js: "supports default no selection")
- Given both inputValue and selectedKey controlled and already consistent, when the field blurs, then onSelectionChange does not fire. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/combobox/useComboBoxState.test.js: "does not fire onSelectionChange on blur when fully controlled values are already synced")
- Given both controlled with the inputValue out of sync with the selected item, when the field blurs, then onSelectionChange does fire. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/combobox/useComboBoxState.test.js: "fires onSelectionChange on blur when fully controlled inputValue is out of sync")
- Given a closed ComboBox with uncontrolled items, when the underlying items change, then the returned collection is not updated until it reopens, so the list cannot shift under a closed popover. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/combobox/useComboBoxState.test.js: "won't update the returned collection if the combobox is closed (uncontrolled items)")
- Given a closed ComboBox with controlled items, when the items change, then the returned collection likewise stays frozen. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/combobox/useComboBoxState.test.js: "won't update the returned collection if the combobox is closed (controlled items)")

### Forms (name, value, validation, form reset, hidden inputs, autofill)

- Given a ComboBox with name="test" and value="2", when rendered, then the combobox input has no name attribute and value "Dog" while a hidden input carries name="test" and value "2"; when rerendered with formValue="text", the combobox input itself gets name="test" and the hidden input is removed. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support formValue")
- Given a ComboBox with defaultValue="2" and name="combobox" inside a form with a reset input, when the listbox is opened, the first option clicked to change the value to "Cat", and then the reset input clicked, then the input value returns to "Dog" and input[name=combobox] has value "2". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support form reset")
- Given an isRequired ComboBox with a FieldError inside a form, when rendered, then the combobox input has the required attribute, no aria-required, no aria-describedby, validity.valid is false and the wrapper has no data-invalid. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support validation errors")
- Given that isRequired ComboBox, when form.checkValidity() is called, then document.activeElement becomes the combobox input, its aria-describedby resolves to text "Constraints not satisfied" and the .react-aria-ComboBox wrapper has data-invalid. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support validation errors")
- Given the invalid isRequired ComboBox, when the user focuses it, types "C" and clicks the first option, then aria-describedby is still present and validity.valid is true; after tabbing away aria-describedby is removed and the wrapper no longer has data-invalid. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support validation errors")
- Given a ComboBox with form="test", when rendered, then the combobox input has form="test". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support form prop")
- Given a multiple selection ComboBox named "combobox" inside a Form, when Cat and Dog are selected, then new FormData(form).getAll('combobox') equals ['1','2']; after clicking the reset input the combobox input value is "" and getAll('combobox') equals ['']. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support multiple selection")
- Given an isRequired ComboBox with selectionMode="multiple", name="combobox" and a FieldError inside a Form, when rendered, then the combobox input has required and validity.valid is false, and after form.checkValidity() the input has aria-describedby and .react-aria-ComboBox has data-invalid. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support isRequired with multiple selection")
- Given that isRequired multi-select ComboBox, when the first option is clicked and the input is blurred, then the required attribute is removed, validity.valid is true, data-invalid is gone and exactly 1 hidden input exists with name="combobox" and value="1". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support isRequired with multiple selection")
- Given that same ComboBox after one selection, when the first option is clicked again (deselecting it) and the input blurred, then required returns, validity.valid is false, aria-describedby is present again and the single hidden input has name="combobox" with value="". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support isRequired with multiple selection")
- Given a desktop ComboBox with a `name` in a form, when an item is selected and the form is reset, then the value returns to its initial state. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should support form reset")
- Given a React 19 form action and `defaultSelectedKey` bound to that state, when the form submits, then the visible input shows the new item's text and the hidden named input holds the key. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "resets to defaultSelectedKey when submitting form action")
- Given `name="test"` with `selectedKey="2"` on desktop, when rendered, then the visible input carries the name and the item's text; switching to `formValue="key"` removes the name from the visible input and submits the key instead. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should support formValue")
- Given `isRequired` with `validationBehavior="native"` on desktop, when the form validates, then the field is natively invalid and described by the error, clearing once a valid selection is committed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "supports isRequired")
- Given a `validate` function with native validation, when the form validates, then the custom message is described. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "supports validate function")
- Given server `validationErrors` with native validation, when the form submits, then the server error shows and clears after the value changes. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "supports server validation")
- Given a custom native `errorMessage` function, when validation fails, then the custom text is used. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "supports customizing native error messages")
- Given a required native-validation ComboBox, when it is focused and blurred with no change, then no error is shown. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "only commits on blur if the value changed")
- Given a `validate` function under aria validation, when rendered, then the field is aria-invalid and described by the message until the value becomes valid. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "supports validate function")
- Given server validation errors under aria validation, when rendered, then the field is aria-invalid and described by the error. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "supports server validation")
- Given a mobile ComboBox with `name="test"` in a form, when an item is selected in the tray and the form is reset, then the visible trigger has no name attribute, a hidden input named test carries the value, and reset empties it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should support form reset")
- Given a React 19 form action on mobile, when submitted, then the hidden input takes the new default selected key. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "resets to defaultSelectedKey when submitting form action")
- Given `name="test"` with `selectedKey="2"` on mobile, when rendered, then a `type="hidden"` input carries the name and the item's text, and `formValue="key"` switches its value to the key. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should support formValue")
- Given the mobile validation suite under native validation, when the form validates, then isRequired, a validate function, server errors, and custom native messages all surface on the tray trigger. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "supports isRequired")
- Given mobile native validation with a `validate` function, when the form validates, then the custom message is described on the trigger. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "supports validate function")
- Given mobile native validation with server errors, when the form submits, then the error is described and clears after a change. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "supports server validation")
- Given mobile native validation with a custom error message function, when validation fails, then the custom text is used. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "supports customizing native error messages")
- Given mobile aria validation with a `validate` function, when rendered, then the trigger is marked invalid and described. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "supports validate function")
- Given mobile aria validation with server errors, when rendered, then the trigger is described by the error. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "supports server validation")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given an open ComboBox listbox, when a scroll event is fired on document.body, then the listbox is removed from the document. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should close on scroll")
- Given an open ComboBox listbox with the input focused, when a scroll event is fired on the combobox input itself (simulating cursor placement in long overflowing text), then the listbox stays in the document. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should not close on input scrolling for cursor placement")
- Given a ComboBox mounted inside a scrollable light DOM ancestor with its listbox portalled into document.body (non-modal Popover registering useCloseOnScroll), when a 'scroll' Event is dispatched on the scrollable ancestor, then the listbox is removed (getListbox() returns null). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.browser.test.tsx: "overlay closes when a scrollable light DOM ancestor scrolls")
- Given enableShadowDOM() is turned on and a ComboBox mounted inside a scrollable container attached to an open shadow root, when a 'scroll' Event (composed: false, so never seen by document) is dispatched on that container, then the listbox portalled into document.body is still closed by the shadow root scroll listener. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.browser.test.tsx: "overlay closes when a scrollable shadow DOM ancestor scrolls")
- Given a mobile ComboBox, when rendered, then a trigger button renders in place of the input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should render a button to open the tray")
- Given a readonly mobile ComboBox, when the button is pressed, then no tray opens. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "readonly combobox should not open on press")
- Given a mobile ComboBox, when the button is pressed, then the tray opens and its input is autofocused. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "opening the tray autofocuses the tray input")
- Given an open tray, when it closes, then focus returns to the trigger button. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "closing the tray autofocuses the button")
- Given an open tray, when the item count changes, then the tray height stays fixed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "height of the tray remains fixed even if the number of items changes")
- Given an open tray, when arrow keys are pressed, then aria-activedescendant traverses the tray items. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "up/down arrows still traverse the items in the tray")
- Given an open tray, when text is typed in the tray input, then the options filter. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "user can filter the menu options by typing in the tray input")
- Given text in the tray input, when the clear button is pressed, then the input empties and focus stays in it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "tray input can be cleared using a clear button")
- Given a tray filter that matches nothing, when it is applied, then a "No results" placeholder shows. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "\"No results\" placeholder is shown if user types something that doesnt match any of the available options")
- Given an open tray, when an option is pressed, then it is selected and the tray closes. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "user can select options by pressing them")
- Given an open tray, when an option is focused and Enter pressed, then it is selected and the tray closes. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "user can select options by focusing them and hitting enter")
- Given an open tray with the input focused, when the listbox is scrolled with touch, then the tray input is blurred so the on-screen keyboard dismisses. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "input is blurred when the user scrolls the listbox with touch")
- Given a mobile ComboBox, when the tray input value changes, then the trigger button's visible value mirrors it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "value of the button mirrors the tray input")
- Given a mobile ComboBox with no items, when the button is pressed, then the tray still opens. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "user can open the tray even if there aren't any items to show")
- Given an open tray, when the tray input is blurred, then the tray stays open. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "combobox tray remains open on blur")
- Given an open tray, when a dismiss button is pressed, then the tray closes. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "combobox tray can be closed using the dismiss buttons")
- Given an open tray, when the tray input receives a virtual click, then the tray does not close. This pins a screen reader quirk. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "combobox tray doesn't close when tray input is virtually clicked")
- Given `menuTrigger="focus"` on mobile, when the tray closes, then it does not immediately reopen. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "menutrigger=focus doesn't reopen the tray on close")
- Given a controlled mobile ComboBox, when the controlled input value updates while closed, then the tray does not open. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "combobox tray doesn't open when controlled input value is updated")
- Given previously typed filter text on mobile, when the tray is opened, then all items are shown. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "shows all items when opening the tray")
- Given `autoFocus` on mobile, when rendered, then the trigger button is focused. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "combobox button is focused when autoFocus is true")
- Given a mobile ComboBox, when the visible label is clicked, then the trigger button is focused. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should focus the button when clicking on the label")
- Given refs on a mobile ComboBox, when rendered, then the ref points at the label wrapper (or the button's wrapper with no label) and `focus()` focuses the button. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "attaches a ref to the label wrapper")
- Given a mobile ComboBox with no label, when rendered, then the ref points at the wrapper. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "attaches a ref to the wrapper if no label")
- Given a mobile ref, when focus() is called, then the button gains focus. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "calling focus() on the ref focuses the button")

### Animation and presence

- Given a closed menu and a loading state, when rendered, then no loading circle appears. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "combobox should not render a loading circle if menu is not open")
- Given `menuTrigger="manual"` with the menu closed, when 500ms pass, then the loading circle renders in the field. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "combobox should render a loading circle if menu is not open but menuTrigger is \"manual\"")
- Given `loadingState="loading"`, when only part of the 500ms delay has elapsed, then no spinner shows; after the full delay it appears. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "combobox should not render a loading circle until a delay of 500ms passes (loadingState: loading)")
- Given `loadingState="filtering"`, when 500ms pass with the menu closed, then no spinner shows until the menu opens. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "combobox should not render a loading circle until a delay of 500ms passes and the menu is open (loadingState: filtering)")
- Given a visible spinner, when loadingState becomes a non-loading value, then it is removed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "combobox should hide the loading circle when loadingState changes to a non-loading state")
- Given a visible spinner with the menu open, when the menu closes, then the spinner is removed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "combobox should hide the loading circle when if the menu closes")
- Given loading that finishes inside the 500ms window, when timers run, then no spinner ever appears. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "combobox cancels the 500ms progress circle delay timer if the loading finishes first")
- Given loadingState changing from loading to filtering mid-delay, when the rest of the delay elapses, then the spinner appears on the original schedule. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "combobox should not reset the 500ms progress circle delay timer when loadingState changes from loading to filtering")
- Given a pending delay, when the input text changes, then the 500ms timer restarts. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "combobox should reset the 500ms progress circle delay timer when input text changes")
- Given each loadingState in a parameterized table, when rendered and opened, then the spinner placement and aria-label match that state. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "$Name")
- Given `loadingState="loadingMore"`, when the menu opens, then a loading swirl renders inside the listbox. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should render the loading swirl in the listbox when loadingState=\"loadingMore\"")
- Given `loadingState="loading"` with no items, when the menu opens, then a "Loading..." placeholder renders in the menu. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should render \"Loading...\" placeholder in menu when loadingState=\"loading\" and no items present")
- Given `loadingState="filtering"` on mobile, when the tray opens, then the tray input renders a spinner after the 500ms delay. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "tray input should render a loading circle after a delay of 500ms if loadingState=\"filtering\"")
- Given a tray spinner, when loadingState stops being filtering, then it is hidden. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "tray input should hide the loading circle if loadingState is no longer \"filtering\"")
- Given an open tray, when the input value changes, then the spinner delay timer restarts. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "tray input loading circle timer should reset on input value change")
- Given each loadingState in the mobile table, when the tray opens, then the spinner and icon layout match that state. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "$Name")
- Given `loadingState="loadingMore"` on mobile, when the tray opens, then the loading swirl renders in the listbox. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should render the loading swirl in the listbox when loadingState=\"loadingMore\"")
- Given an async list, when the menu is first opened, then `onLoadMore` fires once and the loader was already called once for the initial load. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "onLoadMore is called on initial open")
- Given an async list that has been opened once, when the menu is closed and reopened, then onLoadMore is not called again and the loader count stays put. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "onLoadMore is not called on when previously opened")
- Given a mobile ComboBox backed by `useAsyncList`, when the tray is used, then async loading works end to end. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "async combobox works with useAsyncList")

### RTL and i18n (locale-aware parsing, number formats, RTL arrow keys)

- Given a mobile ComboBox with only an external `aria-labelledby`, when rendered, then the trigger button is labelled by it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "button should be labelled by external label")
- Given only `aria-label` on mobile, when rendered, then the button carries that label. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "button should be labelled by aria-label")
- Given both an external label and the built-in label on mobile, when rendered, then the button's aria-labelledby lists both. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "button should be labelled by external label and builtin label")
- Given an open tray, when inspected, then the tray input's label matches the trigger button's label. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "label of the tray input should match label of button")
- Given an external label on mobile, when the tray opens, then the tray input receives the same aria-labelledby as the button. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "tray input should recieve the same aria-labelledby as the button if an external label is provided")
- Given `validationState="invalid"` on mobile, when rendered, then the trigger's label includes the localized invalid text. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should include invalid in label when validationState=\"invalid\"")

### SSR and hydration

- Given a ComboBox with defaultSelectedKey="dog" server rendered inside React.StrictMode, when the server HTML is inspected and again after hydration, then the combobox input value is "Dog" in both cases. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.ssr.test.js: "should render text of default selected key")
- Given a ComboBox with defaultSelectedKey="dog" wrapping a ref'd div with role="group" and a useLayoutEffect recording ref.current?.outerHTML, when server rendered, then the combobox input value is "Dog" and the first recorded trigger text is "null"; after hydration the input value is still "Dog", clicking the second button updates its text to "1" and the second recorded outerHTML equals the current outerHTML of the role="group" element, so the ref points at the right node. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.ssr.test.js: "should point ref correctly after hydration")
- Given a ComboBox rendered on the server, when hydrated and opened, then all three items are present. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "works with SSR")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given an open menu with a virtually focused option, when ArrowLeft or ArrowRight is pressed, then aria-activedescendant is cleared. This exists as an NVDA fix. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "clears aria-activedescendant when user presses left/right arrow (NVDA fix)")
- Given an open menu, when the user arrows through options, then each option's text is announced. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should announce items when navigating with the arrow keys")
- Given a selected option, when navigation reaches it, then the announcement is "Two, selected". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should announce when navigating to the selected item")
- Given sections, when navigation enters a multi-item section, then the announcement names the section and its item count; moving within it announces only the item. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should announce when navigating into a section with multiple items")
- Given a single-item section, when navigation enters it, then the announcement names the section and that item. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should announce when navigating into a section with a single item")
- Given a section containing the selected item, when navigation enters it, then the announcement includes the section, the item, and its selected state. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should announce when navigating into a section with a selected item")
- Given typing that narrows the list, when filtering runs, then the announcer reports "2 options available." then "1 option available." with correct pluralization. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should announce the number of options available when filtering")
- Given the menu opening, when it opens, then the full option count is announced. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should announce the number of options available when opening the menu")
- Given a virtually focused option, when it is selected, then the announcement is "One, selected". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should announce when a selection occurs")
- Given content outside the ComboBox, when the menu opens, then it is marked `aria-hidden` so screen reader users stay inside the widget. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should hide elements outside the combobox with aria-hidden")
- Given an outside element nested in a container, when the menu opens, then the container is hidden rather than traversed into. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should not traverse into a hidden container")
- Given the real live announcer, when the menu opens, then the announcer element itself is not hidden. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should not hide the live announcer element")
- Given an open menu, when a new element is added outside, then it is hidden too. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should handle when a new element is added outside while open")
- Given an already hidden container, when a new element is added inside it, then the container stays hidden and the child is not marked individually. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should handle when a new element is added to an already hidden container")
- Given an open menu, when a new option is added inside the listbox, then it is not hidden. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "should handle when a new element is added inside the listbox")
- Given a `placeholder`, when rendered, then it appears and a console warning says placeholders are deprecated for accessibility. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "renders with placeholder text and shows warning")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a ComboBox whose Popover also contains a Label, Button, Input and Text alongside the ListBox, when opened, then the contexts are cleared inside the popover: the Label has no for attribute, the Button has no aria-expanded, the Input has no role and the Text has no id. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should clear contexts inside popover")
- Given a ComboBox whose Popover wraps a Virtualizer with ListLayout and layoutOptions {rowHeight: 25} over 50 items, with clientWidth and clientHeight mocked to 100 and scrollTop mocking restored, when opened with interactionType mouse, then only 7 options are rendered. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should support virtualizer")
- Given a ComboBox with isInvalid and a Text slot="errorMessage" rendered inside a Dialog, when rendered, then no error is thrown. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should not throw when rendered inside a Dialog with a Text errorMessage slot")
- Given a ComboBox with isInvalid and a Text slot="errorMessage" rendered inside a Dialog with role="alertdialog", when rendered, then no error is thrown. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ComboBox.test.js: "should not throw when rendered inside an alertdialog with a Text errorMessage slot")
- Given items with hrefs, when an item is activated with the mouse or the keyboard, then the link is followed instead of selection changing. Run as `it.each(['mouse', 'keyboard'])`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "supports links on items with %s")
- Given a Provider with a client router, when a link item is activated, then navigate is called with the item's href and routerOptions. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/combobox/ComboBox.test.js: "supports RouterProvider")
- Given a ComboBox whose `children` is an inline arrow function (a new function identity every render) together with allowsCustomValue and menuTrigger focus, when the hooks run, then rendering settles without an infinite loop and inputProps.role is still "combobox". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/combobox/useComboBox.test.js: "should not infinite loop when children is an inline function")

## autocomplete

### Roles and attributes

- Given the shared suite's standard renderer (an Autocomplete wrapping a SearchField and a collection of Foo, Bar, Baz), when rendered, then the searchbox input has aria-controls, aria-autocomplete="list", autoCorrect="off", spellCheck="false" and enterkeyhint="go", and the wrapped collection element (role menu, listbox or grid depending on ariaPattern) has an id equal to the input's aria-controls. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "has default behavior (input field renders with expected attributes)")
- Given the noVirtualFocus renderer (a collection that does not support virtual focus, such as Table, GridList or TagGroup), when rendered, then the searchbox still has aria-controls, aria-autocomplete="list", autoCorrect="off", spellCheck="false" and enterkeyhint="go", never has aria-activedescendant, and the collection's id equals aria-controls. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should not support virtual focus navigation from the input")
- Given the sections renderer, when rendered, then the collection contains 2 groups with text "Section 1" and "Section 2", one element with role separator, and 3 items in each group. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should properly skip over sections when keyboard navigating")
- Given the links renderer, when its third item is inspected, then that item's tagName is "A" and it has href="https://google.com". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should trigger the link option when hitting Enter")
- Given the submenus renderer, when rendered, then the second menuitem has aria-haspopup="menu". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should open a submenu when pressing the autocomplete wrapped submenu trigger")
- Given the subdialogs renderer, when rendered, then the second menuitem of the outer menu has aria-haspopup="menu". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should open a subdialog when pressing the autocomplete wrapped subdialog triggers")
- Given the disabledItems renderer (item with key 2 disabled), when rendered, then the second item has aria-disabled="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should properly skip over disabled items")
- Given an Autocomplete wrapping a SearchField whose Button clears the field, when rendered, then that button has aria-label="Clear search". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should clear the input field when clicking on the clear button")
- Given a Spectrum SearchAutocomplete, when rendered, then the input has `autoCorrect="off"`, `spellCheck="false"`, `autoComplete="off"` and the label is visible. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "renders correctly")
- Given an open SearchAutocomplete listbox, when inspected, then the listbox is visible with `aria-label="Suggestions"`, the input has `aria-controls` pointing at it plus `aria-expanded="true"`, the options render in order, and neither the listbox nor its options carry a tabIndex (focus stays on the input). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "renders correctly")
- Given a custom `icon`, when rendered, then that icon appears. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should support custom icons")
- Given `icon={null}`, when rendered, then no search icon renders. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should support no icons")
- Given `data-testid`, when rendered, then the attribute lands on the input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "supports custom data attributes")
- Given `validationState="invalid"`, when rendered, then the input has `aria-invalid="true"`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should have aria-invalid when validationState=\"invalid\"")
- Given a closed SearchAutocomplete, when rendered, then the input has `aria-autocomplete="list"` and no `aria-controls` or `aria-activedescendant` until the menu opens, and the default behavior is completionMode suggest with menuTrigger input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "features default behavior of completionMode suggest and menuTrigger input")
- Given `useSearchAutocomplete` with a label and a combobox state, when the hook runs, then labelProps has an id and an htmlFor matching inputProps.id, the input gets `role="combobox"` with `aria-autocomplete="list"` and aria-labelledby pointing at the label, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant are absent while closed, and listBoxProps has an aria-labelledby of "<listboxId> <labelId>". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/autocomplete/useSearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should return default props for all the elements")

### Keyboard

- Given the standard renderer with focus in the input, when ArrowDown is pressed three times then ArrowUp once, then aria-activedescendant on the input moves to options[0], options[1], options[2] and back to options[1], and document.activeElement remains the input the whole time. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should support keyboard navigation")
- Given the standard renderer with options[0] virtually focused, when ArrowRight is pressed, then aria-activedescendant is removed, but a following ArrowDown moves to options[1] because the focused key is preserved internally; ArrowLeft clears aria-activedescendant again with real focus still on the input, and ArrowUp then returns to options[0]. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should clear the focused key when using ArrowLeft and ArrowRight but preserves it internally for future keyboard operations")
- Given the standard renderer after typing "B" so aria-activedescendant points at "Bar", when Backspace is pressed, then aria-activedescendant is removed and the internal focused key is fully cleared: the next ArrowDown sets aria-activedescendant to the new options[0] ("Foo"), an id different from the previous active descendant. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should completely clear the focused key when Backspacing")
- Given the standard renderer after typing "B" so aria-activedescendant is set, when "az" is pasted into the input, then aria-activedescendant is removed and the focused key is fully cleared: the next ArrowDown sets aria-activedescendant to the new options[0] ("Baz"), a different id. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should completely clear the focused key when pasting")
- Given the standard renderer, when "a" is typed, then aria-activedescendant is not set immediately and only appears after advancing timers by 500ms, at which point it equals options[0].id. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should delay the aria-activedescendant being set when autofocusing the first option")
- Given the standard renderer where "a" was typed and the 500ms autofocus delay has not elapsed, when ArrowDown is pressed and timers run, then aria-activedescendant is options[1].id, so the newest user-moved focus wins over the delayed autofocus of the first option. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should maintain the newest focused item as the activescendant if set after autofocusing the first option")
- Given the standard renderer after typing "Bar" (input.selectionStart is 3) and pressing ArrowLeft (selectionStart 2), when Home, End, ArrowDown and ArrowUp are each pressed, then input.selectionStart stays at 2 for every one of them, so collection navigation keys do not move the text cursor. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should not move the text input cursor when using Home/End/ArrowUp/ArrowDown")
- Given the noVirtualFocus renderer with the input focused, when ArrowDown is pressed and then "Foo" typed, then aria-activedescendant is never set and the input value is "Foo". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should not support virtual focus navigation from the input")
- Given the itemActions renderer (menu ariaPattern only), when ArrowDown virtually focuses options[0] and Enter is pressed, then the collection's action listener is called once with ('1', undefined), and a further ArrowDown plus Enter brings it to 2 calls, last called with ('2', undefined). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should trigger the wrapped element's actionListener when hitting Enter")
- Given the standard renderer (this item actions test renders renderers.standard) with options[0] virtually focused, when [Space] is pressed, then the action listener is called 0 times and the space character is typed into the input instead, filtering the collection down to 0 items. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should not trigger the wrapped element's actionListener when hitting Space")
- Given the multipleSelection renderer (items exposed as menuitemcheckbox for the menu pattern or option for the listbox pattern), when ArrowDown plus Enter is pressed, then the selection listener is called once with Set(['1']); a further ArrowDown plus Enter gives Set(['1','2']); an ArrowUp plus Enter gives Set(['2']), for 3 calls total. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should trigger the wrapped element's onSelectionChange when hitting Enter")
- Given the multipleSelection renderer after selecting items 1 and 2, when Escape is pressed, then the selection listener is called a third time with an empty set, clearing the wrapped collection's selection. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should clear the wrapped element's selection when hitting Escape")
- Given the disabledItems renderer, when ArrowDown is pressed twice, then aria-activedescendant goes from options[0] to options[2], skipping the aria-disabled item; typing "Bar" then leaves a single disabled option and no aria-activedescendant. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should properly skip over disabled items")
- Given the disabledItems renderer after typing "r" so only the single disabled item remains and no aria-activedescendant is set, when Backspace is pressed, then aria-activedescendant is still not set (the first item is not autofocused), and a following ArrowDown sets it to options[0]. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should not autofocus the first item if backspacing from a list state where there are only disabled items")
- Given the sections renderer with focus in the input, when ArrowDown is pressed once per item across both sections in order, then aria-activedescendant equals each item's id in turn, never a section header. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should properly skip over sections when keyboard navigating")
- Given the links renderer with a window click listener installed via mockClickDefault({capture: true}), when ArrowDown is pressed three times to reach the anchor item and Enter is pressed, then the click handler is called, navigating the link (the recorded call count differs between the menu and listbox patterns because useSelectableItem prevents default on one of them). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should trigger the link option when hitting Enter")
- Given the submenus renderer with options[1] (aria-haspopup="menu") virtually focused via two ArrowDowns and showing data-focused plus data-focus-visible, when ArrowRight is pressed, then the submenu opens (2 menus), aria-activedescendant still points at options[1] while that item loses data-focused and data-focus-visible, and real DOM focus is inside the second menu. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should not clear the focused key when using arrowRight to open a submenu")
- Given that open submenu, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then only 1 menu remains, aria-activedescendant is still options[1] with data-focused and data-focus-visible restored, and a following ArrowDown moves to options[2] with those attributes. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should not clear the focused key when using arrowRight to open a submenu")
- Given the submenus renderer with two levels of submenu open (3 menus, real focus in the deepest), when Escape is pressed, then only one level closes: 2 menus remain and document.activeElement is the second menu's second menuitem; a second Escape leaves 1 menu and returns real focus to the autocomplete input. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should only close a single level when hitting Escape and focus should be moved back to the input")
- Given the subdialogs renderer with two nested subdialogs open (each an Autocomplete with an autoFocus SearchField that holds real focus), when Escape is pressed, then one level closes: 1 dialog remains, focus returns to the first subdialog's searchbox and that searchbox's aria-activedescendant points at its second menuitem; a second Escape closes all dialogs and returns focus to the outer input. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should only close a single level when hitting Escape and focus should be moved back to the input")
- Given the subdialogAndMenu renderer (autocomplete subdialog containing a real submenu containing another autocomplete subdialog), when ArrowDown twice then ArrowRight is pressed on options[1], then a subdialog opens with real focus on its searchbox; ArrowDown plus ArrowRight from there opens a real submenu (3 menus, real focus inside menus[2]); ArrowDown plus ArrowRight again opens a third subdialog with real focus on its searchbox. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should allow opening a subdialog from menu and vice versa")
- Given that mixed stack fully open, when Escape is pressed, then 2 dialogs remain and real focus returns to the submenu item; ArrowLeft then leaves 2 menus with focus on the first subdialog's searchbox whose aria-activedescendant is its second menuitem; a final Escape closes all dialogs and puts real focus back on the outer input with aria-activedescendant still options[1]. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should allow opening a subdialog from menu and vice versa")
- Given an Autocomplete wrapping a Menu inside a div with an onKeyDown handler, when ArrowDown is pressed in the input, then the outer onKeyDown is not called. (skipped in repo, the comment says arrow keys still leak out of useSelectableCollection) (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should prevent key presses from leaking out of the Autocomplete")
- Given an Autocomplete with disableAutoFocusFirst, when "Foo" is typed, then the input has no aria-activedescendant, and pressing ArrowDown then sets aria-activedescendant to options[0].id. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should not auto focus first item when disableAutoFocusFirst is true")
- Given a closed SearchAutocomplete, when ArrowDown is pressed, then onOpenChange fires once with `(true, 'manual')`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "opens the menu on down arrow press")
- Given a closed SearchAutocomplete, when ArrowUp is pressed, then onOpenChange fires once with `(true, 'manual')`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "opens the menu on up arrow press")
- Given a closed SearchAutocomplete, when the user types "Two", then onOpenChange fires once with `(true, 'input')`, the listbox shows the single matching option, focus stays on the input, and no aria-activedescendant is set yet. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "opens the menu on user typing")
- Given an open menu, when ArrowDown then ArrowDown then ArrowUp are pressed, then aria-activedescendant moves to the first, second, and back to the first option while real focus stays on the input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "allows the user to navigate the menu via arrow keys")
- Given an open menu with the first option virtually focused, when Enter is pressed, then the listbox closes and the input value becomes that option's text. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "allows the user to select an item via Enter")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given the standard renderer, when the first collection item is clicked, then document.activeElement becomes the searchbox input. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should focus the input when clicking on an item")

(react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should update the aria-activedescendant when hovering over an item")

- Given the submenus renderer, when the second menuitem is clicked, then 2 menus are present. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should open a submenu when pressing the autocomplete wrapped submenu trigger")
- Given the submenus renderer with installPointerEvent and a submenu open (2 menus), when options[2] of the parent list is hovered, then the submenu closes and only 1 menu remains. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should close the menu when hovering an adjacent menu item in the virtual focus list")
- Given the subdialogs renderer, when the second menuitem is clicked, then 1 dialog opens, and clicking the second menuitem inside it opens a second dialog. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should open a subdialog when pressing the autocomplete wrapped subdialog triggers")
- Given the subdialogs renderer with document.elementFromPoint mocked to return its argument and one subdialog open, when the second menuitem inside it is hovered, then a second dialog opens; hovering the first menuitem instead collapses back to 1 dialog. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should close the subdialog when hovering an adjacent menu item in the virtual focus list")
- Given an Autocomplete wrapping a Menu with installPointerEvent active, when the first menuitem is tapped via touch (user.pointer with keys '[TouchA]'), then document.activeElement is not the searchbox input. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should not move focus to the input field if tapping on a menu item via touch")
- Given an Autocomplete wrapping a Menu with installPointerEvent active, when the first menuitem is clicked via mouse (user.pointer with keys '[MouseLeft]'), then document.activeElement is the searchbox input. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should move focus to the input field if clicking on a menu item via mouse")
- Given an Autocomplete wrapping a SearchField with a clear Button, when the user types "Foo" and clicks the clear button, then the input value becomes "". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should clear the input field when clicking on the clear button")
- Given an open menu, when an option is clicked, then it is selected and the input takes its text. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "can select by mouse")
- Given `menuTrigger="focus"`, when the input is focused, then onOpenChange fires once with `(true, 'focus')`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "opens menu when searchAutocomplete is focused")

### Focus management

- Given an Autocomplete wrapping a Menu, when the user tabs into the searchbox, then the input has data-focus-visible and no aria-activedescendant; after ArrowDown the input's aria-activedescendant equals options[0].id, options[0] has data-focus-visible and the input has neither data-focus-visible nor data-focused, so the focus ring moves to the virtually focused item. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should apply focusVisible/focused to virtually focused menu items when keyboard navigating")
- Given that Autocomplete after clicking the input (mouse modality), when options[1] is hovered, then options[1] has data-focused but not data-focus-visible and the input has no data-focused. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should apply focusVisible/focused to virtually focused menu items when keyboard navigating")
- Given that Autocomplete with keyboard modality restored, when "Bar" is typed and timers run, then aria-activedescendant is options[0].id, options[0] has data-focus-visible and the input has no data-focused; pressing ArrowLeft removes aria-activedescendant and returns data-focus-visible to the input. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should apply focusVisible/focused to virtually focused menu items when keyboard navigating")
- Given that Autocomplete with options[0] virtually focused, when Backspace is pressed and timers run, then aria-activedescendant is removed and the input regains data-focus-visible. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should apply focusVisible/focused to virtually focused menu items when keyboard navigating")
- Given an Autocomplete whose input was clicked (data-focused on the input) and then options[1] hovered so options[1] has data-focused, the input loses data-focused and aria-activedescendant is options[1].id, when the input is clicked again, then document.activeElement is the input, the input has data-focused but not data-focus-visible, aria-activedescendant is removed and options[1] no longer has data-focused. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should restore focused styles to the input when clicking it after hovering an option")
- Given an Autocomplete next to an outside button, with options[1] hovered so aria-activedescendant is set and options[1] has data-focused, when the outside button is clicked, then that button is document.activeElement and the input has neither data-focused nor data-focus-visible; clicking back into the input gives it focus and data-focused with no data-focus-visible, clears aria-activedescendant and removes data-focused from options[1]. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should restore the input state after clicking outside the autocomplete and then back into the input")
- Given an Autocomplete where ArrowDown put data-focus-visible on options[0] with aria-activedescendant set and the input not data-focused, when the input is clicked, then document.activeElement is the input, the input has data-focused without data-focus-visible, aria-activedescendant is removed and options[0] has neither data-focused nor data-focus-visible. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should restore focused styles to the input when clicking it after keyboard focusing an option")
- Given an Autocomplete between two plain inputs with options[0] virtually focused (aria-activedescendant set, options[0] data-focus-visible, input neither data-focus-visible nor data-focused), when the user tabs away, then options[0] loses data-focused and data-focus-visible and the input has neither; shift-tabbing back restores data-focused and data-focus-visible on options[0] while the input still has neither. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should not display focus in the virtually focused menu if focus isn't in the autocomplete input")
- Given an Autocomplete over a Menu with disabledKeys ['2'] where typing "Ba" virtually focused "Baz", when "r" is typed so the only match is the disabled "Bar", then aria-activedescendant is removed, "Bar" has no data-focus-visible and the input regains data-focused and data-focus-visible. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should restore focus visible styles back to the input when typing forward results in only disabled items")
- Given an Autocomplete over a Menu with the input keyboard focused, when "Q" is typed so 0 menuitems match, then the input keeps data-focused and data-focus-visible and has no aria-activedescendant. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should maintain focus styles on the input if typing forward results in an completely empty collection")
- Given an Autocomplete over a Menu where "F" was typed and only 300ms advanced (less than the 500ms activedescendant delay), when the state is inspected, then aria-activedescendant is not yet set even though "Foo" already has data-focus-visible and the input has neither data-focused nor data-focus-visible. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should restore focus visible styles back to the input if the user types forward and backspaces in quick succession")
- Given that same in-flight state, when Backspace is pressed and all timers run, then the input has data-focused and data-focus-visible, has no aria-activedescendant, and "Foo" no longer has data-focus-visible. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should restore focus visible styles back to the input if the user types forward and backspaces in quick succession")
- Given a Select whose Popover contains an Autocomplete with an autoFocus SearchField and a ListBox, when Enter opens the Select, then the searchbox is document.activeElement, 3 options render, the searchbox's aria-activedescendant is options[0].id and options[0] has data-focus-visible; ArrowDown moves it to options[1]; typing "b" filters to 2 options with aria-activedescendant on the new options[0]; Enter closes the listbox, returns focus to the Select trigger button and sets its text to "Bar". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should work inside a Select")
- Given a Dialog whose FocusScope contains two Buttons followed by an Autocomplete with an autoFocus TextField, when the dialog opens then Tab, Shift+Tab and Shift+Tab again are pressed, then focus goes input, First button, input, Second button (tab order wraps within the scope and the collection items are skipped). - Given a Dialog whose FocusScope contains an Autocomplete with an autoFocus TextField followed by two Buttons, when the dialog opens then Tab, Shift+Tab and Shift+Tab again are pressed, then focus goes input, First button, input, Second button. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Autocomplete.test.tsx: "should be able to tab inside a focus scope that contains with buttons after the autocomplete")
- Given the subdialogs renderer with a subdialog opened via ArrowDown ArrowDown ArrowRight so real focus is on the subdialog's searchbox, when Tab and then Shift+Tab are pressed, then document.activeElement stays that subdialog searchbox, so focus is contained even under virtual focus. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should contain focus even for virtual focus")
- Given a ref on a labelled SearchAutocomplete, when rendered, then `ref.current.UNSAFE_getDOMNode()` is the label's parent wrapper. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "attaches a ref to the label wrapper")
- Given a ref with no visible label, when rendered, then the ref points at the SearchAutocomplete wrapper. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "attaches a ref to the searchAutocomplete wrapper if no label")
- Given a ref, when `ref.current.focus()` is called, then the combobox input receives focus. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "calling focus() on the ref focuses the input field")
- Given a focused SearchAutocomplete with an open menu and typed text, when the user clicks outside to blur, then the menu closes with onOpenChange `(false, undefined)`, onInputChange's last call is the typed text, and the input keeps that value. - Given typed text that is not an item, when the field is blurred, then the custom value is committed and the menu closes. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "closes and commits custom value")
- Given a selected key whose text matches the input, when the field is blurred, then the selected key is retained. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "retains selected key on blur if input value matches")
- Given an onBlur on the component and another on a wrapping element, when focus leaves, then both fire once: the blur event propagates out of the component. ### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given the standard renderer (also run against the controlled renderer under the "controlled text value" describe), when the input starts empty with 3 items, the user tabs in and types "F", then exactly 1 item remains with text "Foo", the input value is "F", aria-activedescendant equals that option's id and document.activeElement is still the input; Backspace restores 3 items, removes aria-activedescendant and keeps real focus on the input. - Given the sections renderer, when "F" is typed, then 1 group remains whose aria-labelledby resolves to "Section 1" with 1 item and 0 separators, and ArrowDown sets aria-activedescendant to that item ("Foo"). - Given the sections renderer filtered to "F", when Backspace returns the unfiltered view, then 2 groups, 6 items and 1 separator are present, aria-activedescendant is unset, and ArrowDown selects "Foo". - Given the sections renderer, when "e" is typed, then 1 group remains labelled "Section 2" with 1 item and 0 separators, and ArrowDown sets aria-activedescendant to "Paste". - Given the sections renderer, when "a" is typed so both sections match, then 2 groups with 3 items total (2 in the first, 1 in the second) and 1 separator render, aria-activedescendant is auto-set to "Bar", ArrowDown moves to "Baz", another ArrowDown moves to "Paste" in the second section, and for ariaPattern "menu" one more ArrowDown wraps back to "Bar". - Given an Autocomplete with a filter that inspects the collection node (returning true for any node whose parentKey is 'sec1') over a Menu with two sections, when "Copy" is typed, then 4 menuitems remain in 2 groups: section 1 keeps Foo, Bar and Baz and section 2 keeps only Copy. - Given an Autocomplete with a controlled inputValue driving an externally filtered Collection plus a ListBoxLoadMoreItem, when "o" is typed, then 3 options render with aria-activedescendant on options[0]; typing a second "o" leaves 0 options and removes aria-activedescendant; Backspace brings 3 options back, and no keyboard interaction throws or is blocked by a stale active descendant. - Given an Autocomplete over a multiple selection ListBox with defaultSelectedKeys="all" (3 options all aria-selected="true"), when the filter is set to "Ba" leaving 2 selected options and ArrowDown plus Enter deselects "Baz", then onSelectionChange is called once with a set equal to {'1','2'}, and clearing the input shows 3 options with Foo and Bar aria-selected="true" and Baz aria-selected="false". - Given an Autocomplete over a multiple selection ListBox with defaultSelectedKeys="all", when the filter is narrowed to "Foo" (1 option, still aria-selected="true") and then cleared without toggling anything, then all 3 options are aria-selected="true" again. - Given the submenus renderer with a submenu and its nested submenu open (3 menus), when document.body is clicked, then all submenus close and 1 menu remains. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should close all menus when clicking on the body")

- Given the subdialogs renderer with a subdialog open, when the second of the 2 hidden dismiss buttons inside its .react-aria-Popover is virtual clicked (pointerType mouse, width 1, height 1, detail 0), then no dialogs remain and document.activeElement is options[1]. (skipped in repo, the comment questions the use of fireEvent breaking other tests) (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx: "should close the current subdialog when clicking the dismiss button")
