- Given a mobile SearchAutocomplete, when the button is pressed, then a tray opens containing a dialog whose aria-labelledby matches the tray input's, the tray input has `role="searchbox"` with `aria-expanded="true"`, `aria-controls` to the listbox and `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, all three options render, and the tray input is focused. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "opening the tray autofocuses the tray input")
- Given an open tray, when Escape is pressed, then the tray is removed and focus returns to the trigger button. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "closing the tray autofocuses the button")
- Given a readonly mobile SearchAutocomplete, when the button is pressed, then `aria-expanded` stays "false" and no tray opens. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "readonly searchAutocomplete should not open on press")
- Given an open tray, when the option list is filtered down, then the tray's inline style (its height) is unchanged, so the sheet does not resize under the user's finger. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "height of the tray remains fixed even if the number of items changes")
- Given an open tray, when ArrowDown and ArrowUp are pressed, then aria-activedescendant walks the tray options while focus stays in the tray input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "up/down arrows still traverse the items in the tray")
- Given an open tray, when text is typed in the tray input, then the options filter down, and clearing the text restores all three. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "user can filter the menu options by typing in the tray input")
- Given an open tray with no text, when text is typed, then a Clear affordance appears; it is a DIV with no tabIndex, clicking it calls onClear once, empties the tray input, and leaves focus in the tray input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "tray input can be cleared using a clear button")
- Given an open tray, when text matching nothing is typed, then a "No results" placeholder shows as the only list entry, and clearing the text brings back the three options. - Given an open tray, when an option is pressed, then onInputChange fires once with its text, onOpenChange fires `(false, undefined)`, the tray is removed, and reopening shows that option selected with `aria-selected="true"`, the tray input pointing at it via aria-activedescendant and holding its text. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "user can select options by pressing them")
- Given an open tray, when an option is reached with ArrowUp and Enter is pressed, then the same selection, close, and reopen behavior holds. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "user can select options by focusing them and hitting enter")
- Given an open tray with the tray input focused, when a touch scroll starts on the listbox, then the tray input is blurred so the on-screen keyboard dismisses while scrolling. - Given a mobile SearchAutocomplete with no items, when the button is pressed, then the tray still opens and shows the placeholder entry. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "user can open the tray even if there aren't any items to show")
- Given an open tray with a default input value, when the tray input is blurred, then the tray stays open and the input value is not reset. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "searchAutocomplete tray remains open on blur")
- Given an open tray, when inspected, then there are two `aria-label="Dismiss"` buttons (one before and one after the content), and clicking the first closes the tray. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "searchAutocomplete tray can be closed using the dismiss buttons")
- Given an open tray, when the tray input receives a virtual click (a touchEnd with screen reader style coordinates), then the tray does not close. This pins a VoiceOver or TalkBack quirk. - Given `menuTrigger="focus"` on mobile, when the tray is closed by clicking outside, then it does not immediately reopen from the refocused trigger. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "menutrigger=focus doesn't reopen the tray on close")
- Given a controlled mobile SearchAutocomplete, when the controlled input value is updated programmatically while closed, then the tray does not open. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "searchAutocomplete tray doesn't open when controlled input value is updated")

### Positioning

- Given an open tray, when the item count changes, then the tray keeps its original inline height style. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "height of the tray remains fixed even if the number of items changes")

### Animation and presence

- Given `loadingState="loading"` with the menu closed, when 500ms have not yet elapsed, then no progressbar renders; after the full 500ms the spinner appears inside the field and stays while typing. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "searchAutocomplete should not render a loading circle until a delay of 500ms passes (loadingState: loading)")
- Given `loadingState="filtering"` with the menu closed, when 500ms pass, then no spinner shows until the menu is open (filtering only matters while showing results). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "searchAutocomplete should not render a loading circle until a delay of 500ms passes and the menu is open (loadingState: filtering)")
- Given a closed menu and a loading state, when rendered, then no loading circle appears at all. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "searchAutocomplete should not render a loading circle if menu is not open")
- Given `menuTrigger="manual"` with the menu closed, when 500ms pass, then the loading circle does render inside the field. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "searchAutocomplete should render a loading circle if menu is not open but menuTrigger is \"manual\"")
- Given a visible loading circle, when loadingState changes to a non-loading value, then the spinner is removed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "searchAutocomplete should hide the loading circle when loadingState changes to a non-loading state")
- Given a visible loading circle with the menu open, when the menu closes, then the spinner is removed too. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "searchAutocomplete should hide the loading circle when if the menu closes")
- Given loading finishes before 500ms elapse, when the timers run out, then no spinner ever appears (the delay timer is canceled). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "searchAutocomplete cancels the 500ms progress circle delay timer if the loading finishes first")
- Given loadingState changes from "loading" to "filtering" partway through the delay, when the remaining time elapses, then the spinner appears on the original schedule: the timer is not restarted. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "searchAutocomplete should not reset the 500ms progress circle delay timer when loadingState changes from loading to filtering")
- Given a pending 500ms delay, when the input text changes, then the timer restarts so the spinner appears 500ms after the latest keystroke. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "searchAutocomplete should reset the 500ms progress circle delay timer when input text changes")
- Given each loadingState value in a parameterized table, when the field renders and the menu opens, then the spinner's placement and `aria-label` ("Loading..." or "Loading more…") match that state, the invalid icon is suppressed while loading, and listbox spinners appear only for the loadingMore case. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "$Name")
- Given `loadingState="loadingMore"`, when the menu opens, then a progressbar with `aria-label="Loading more…"` renders inside the listbox. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should render the loading swirl in the listbox when loadingState=\"loadingMore\"")
- Given `loadingState="filtering"` on mobile, when the tray opens, then after the 500ms delay a single progressbar renders in the tray (moving from the listbox into the tray input area). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "tray input should render a loading circle after a delay of 500ms if loadingState=\"filtering\"")
- Given a tray spinner, when loadingState stops being "filtering", then the spinner is removed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "tray input should hide the loading circle if loadingState is no longer \"filtering\"")
- Given an open tray, when the tray input value changes, then the 500ms spinner timer restarts. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "tray input loading circle timer should reset on input value change")
- Given each loadingState in the mobile parameterized table, when the tray opens, then the tray spinner's aria-label, the clear button, the listbox spinner, the invalid state on the tray input, and the number of icons rendered all match that state. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "$Name")
- Given `loadingState="loadingMore"` on mobile, when the tray opens, then exactly one progressbar renders with `aria-label="Loading more…"`, three icons are present, and the clear button contains the third icon. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should render the loading swirl in the listbox when loadingState=\"loadingMore\"")

### RTL and i18n (locale-aware parsing, number formats, RTL arrow keys)

- Given a mobile SearchAutocomplete with only an external `aria-labelledby`, when rendered, then the trigger button's aria-labelledby is composed from that external label. - Given only `aria-label`, when rendered on mobile, then the button carries that aria-label plus a composed aria-labelledby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "button should be labelled by aria-label")
- Given both an external label and the built-in label, when rendered on mobile, then the button's aria-labelledby lists both. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "button should be labelled by external label and builtin label")
- Given an open tray, when inspected, then the tray input's aria-labelledby points at the tray's own label element, which matches the button's label. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "label of the tray input should match label of button")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given an open menu with a virtually focused option, when ArrowLeft or ArrowRight is pressed, then aria-activedescendant is cleared (so the caret movement is not announced as option navigation), and ArrowDown restores it. This exists specifically as an NVDA fix. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "clears aria-activedescendant when user presses left/right arrow (NVDA fix)")
- Given an open menu, when the user arrows through options, then each option's text is announced through the live announcer. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should announce items when navigating with the arrow keys")
- Given sections in the list, when navigation enters a section with several items, then the announcement includes the section name and item count, while moving within the section announces just the item. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should announce when navigating into a section with multiple items")
- Given a section with a single item, when navigation enters it, then the announcement names the section and that one item. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should announce when navigating into a section with a single item")
- Given typing that narrows the list, when filtering runs, then the announcer says "2 options available." and then "1 option available." with correct pluralization. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should announce the number of options available when filtering")
- Given typing that opens the menu, when it opens, then the option count is announced. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should announce the number of options available when opening the menu")
- Given a virtually focused option, when Enter selects it, then the announcement is "One, selected". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should announce when a selection occurs")
- Given content outside the SearchAutocomplete, when the menu opens, then those outside elements get `aria-hidden="true"` so screen reader users cannot reach them, and the combobox stays visible. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should hide elements outside the searchAutocomplete with aria-hidden")
- Given an outside element nested in a container, when the menu opens, then the container is hidden rather than each descendant, so the walker does not traverse into it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should not traverse into a hidden container")
- Given the real live announcer implementation, when the menu opens, then the announcer element itself is not hidden and both announcements ("3 options available." then "One") are delivered. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should not hide the live announcer element")
- Given an open menu, when a new element is added outside the component, then it also becomes aria-hidden and the combobox and listbox stay visible. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should handle when a new element is added outside while open")
- Given an open menu and an already hidden outer container, when a new element is added inside that container, then the container stays hidden and the new child is not individually marked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should handle when a new element is added to an already hidden container")
- Given an open menu, when a new option is added inside the listbox, then it is not hidden and both the combobox and listbox remain visible. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should handle when a new element is added inside the listbox")
- Given a `placeholder`, when rendered, then it appears on the input and a console warning says placeholders are deprecated for accessibility. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "renders with placeholder text and shows warning")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a mobile SearchAutocomplete, when the visible label is clicked, then focus moves to the trigger button. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "should focus the button when clicking on the label")
- Given `autoFocus` on mobile, when rendered, then the trigger button is focused. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "searchAutocomplete button is focused when autoFocus is true")
- Given a ref on a mobile SearchAutocomplete with a label, when rendered, then the ref points at the label's parent; without a label it points at the button's parent, and `ref.current.focus()` focuses the button. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "attaches a ref to the label wrapper")
- Given a ref on a mobile SearchAutocomplete with no label, when rendered, then it points at the button's parent element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "attaches a ref to wrapper if no label")
- Given a ref on mobile, when focus() is called, then the trigger button receives focus. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/autocomplete/SearchAutocomplete.test.js: "calling focus() on the ref focuses the button")

## selection

### Roles and attributes

- Given a Table with selectionMode="multiple" and selectionBehavior="replace", when rendered, then no row contains a checkbox, and the first body row has aria-selected="false" before interaction. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not render checkboxes for selection with selectionBehavior=replace")
- Given selectionMode="single" with selectionBehavior="replace" (describe.each(['mouse', 'keyboard', 'touch'])), when rendered, then every row has no checkbox, aria-selected="false", no data-selected attribute, and data-selection-mode="single". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should perform selection with single selection")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with selectionBehavior="replace" (describe.each(['mouse', 'keyboard', 'touch'])), when rendered, then every row has no checkbox, aria-selected="false", no data-selected attribute, and data-selection-mode="multiple". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should perform toggle selection in highlight mode when using modifier keys")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with selectionBehavior="replace" (describe.each(['mouse', 'keyboard', 'touch'])), when rendered, then every row has no checkbox, aria-selected="false", no data-selected attribute, and data-selection-mode="multiple". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should perform replace selection in highlight mode when not using modifier keys")

### Keyboard

- Given a Menu with selectionMode="multiple" and escapeKeyBehavior="none" where the first menuitemcheckbox has been clicked so it is aria-checked="true", when Escape is pressed, then the item stays aria-checked="true" instead of the selection being cleared. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Menu.test.tsx: "should prevent Esc from clearing selection if escapeKeyBehavior is "none"")
- Given a Spectrum ListBox with selectionMode="multiple" and escapeKeyBehavior="none", when two options are clicked to select them and then Escape is pressed, then onSelectionChange stays at 2 calls and the selection is not cleared. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "should prevent Esc from clearing selection if escapeKeyBehavior is "none"")
- Given a react-aria-components ListBox with selectionMode="multiple" and escapeKeyBehavior="none", when an option is selected and Escape is pressed, then the option keeps aria-selected="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should prevent Esc from clearing selection if escapeKeyBehavior is "none"")
- Given a ListBox with selectionMode="multiple" and selectionBehavior="replace" whose item ids are the falsy-looking strings "0", "1" and "2", when item 1 is clicked and Shift+ArrowUp pressed, then items 0 and 1 are aria-selected="true" and item 2 is "false"; a following Shift+ArrowDown collapses the range so only item 1 stays selected and item 0 becomes aria-selected="false". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should deselect item 0 when navigating back in replace selection mode")
- Given that same falsy-key ListBox, when item 0 is clicked and Shift+ArrowDown pressed twice, then the range grows to items 0 and 1 and then to items 0, 1 and 2, all aria-selected="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should correctly handle starting selection at item 0 and extending to item 2")
- Given selectionMode="none" on a Mac (navigator.platform mocked to "Mac"), when ArrowDown moves focus to the second option and then Meta+ArrowDown, Meta+ArrowUp and Control+Home are pressed, then focus stays on the second option, so unsupported modifier combinations do not navigate. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should not navigate when using unsupported modifier keys")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with selectionBehavior="replace" on Mac, when Tab then ArrowDown are pressed, then focus is on the second option and onSelectionChange was last called with new Selection(['dog'], 'dog', 'dog'), so focus movement replaces the selection. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "replaces selection as focus moves with arrow keys")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with selectionBehavior="replace" on Mac, when Alt+ArrowDown is pressed after Tab, then focus moves to the second option and onSelectionChange is not called, so Alt gives non-contiguous navigation without selecting. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "navigates focus without changing selection when Alt is held (non-contiguous)")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with selectionBehavior="replace" on Mac, when Shift+ArrowDown is pressed after Tab, then focus is on the second option and onSelectionChange was last called with new Selection(['cat', 'dog'], 'cat', 'dog'), so Shift extends from the anchor. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "extends selection when Shift is held")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with selectionBehavior="replace" on Mac, when End then Home are pressed after Tab, then focus moves to the last and then the first option and onSelectionChange was last called with new Selection(['kangaroo'], 'kangaroo', 'kangaroo') and then new Selection(['cat'], 'cat', 'cat'). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "replaces selection with Home and End")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" on Mac, when Meta+a is pressed after Tab, then onSelectionChange was last called with the string 'all'. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "selects all with Mod+A (Meta) in multiple selection mode")
- Given selectionMode="single" on Mac, when Meta+a is pressed after Tab, then onSelectionChange is never called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "does not select all with Mod+A when selection mode is single")
- Given selectionMode="none" on Windows (navigator.platform mocked to "Win32"), when ArrowDown moves focus to the second option and Meta+ArrowDown is pressed, then focus stays on the second option. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should not navigate when using unsupported modifier keys")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" on Windows, when Control+ArrowDown is pressed after Tab, then focus moves to the second option and onSelectionChange is not called, so Control gives non-contiguous navigation. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "navigates focus when Control is held (non-contiguous)")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with defaultSelectedKeys=['cat'] on Windows, when Control+Shift+End is pressed, then focus is on the last option and onSelectionChange was last called with new Selection(['cat', 'kangaroo'], 'kangaroo', 'kangaroo'), so extendSelection adds to rather than replaces the existing selection; a following Control+Shift+Home moves focus to the first option and yields new Selection(['cat', 'dog', 'kangaroo'], 'kangaroo', 'cat'). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "extends selection with Control+Shift+End and Control+Shift+Home")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" on Windows, when Control+a is pressed after Tab, then onSelectionChange was last called with the string 'all'. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "selects all with Mod+A (Control) in multiple selection mode")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="multiple" and the tester having selected row 0 (Set(['foo']), announce "Foo selected.", 1 selected row), when Ctrl+A is pressed, then onSelectionChange is called once with 'all', announce says "All items selected.", and all 3 rows report as selected. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should support select all and clear all via keyboard")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="multiple" and all items selected, when Escape keydown/keyup is fired on row 0, then onSelectionChange is called once with an empty selection, announce says "No items selected.", and no rows report as selected. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should support select all and clear all via keyboard")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="multiple" and escapeKeyBehavior="none" with rows Bar and Baz selected via their checkboxes, when Escape is pressed, then onSelectionChange is not called and both rows stay aria-selected="true". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should prevent Esc from clearing selection if escapeKeyBehavior is "none"")
- Given a ListView with selectionStyle="highlight" and selectionMode="multiple" and row 0 clicked (selection Set(['foo']), announce "Foo selected."), when ArrowDown is pressed, then selection follows focus to Set(['bar']) with announce "Bar selected."; ArrowUp returns to Set(['foo']) with "Foo selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move selection when using the arrow keys")
- Given a ListView with selectionStyle="highlight" and selectionMode="multiple" with Foo selected, when Shift+ArrowDown is pressed, then the selection extends to Set(['foo','bar']) and announce says "Bar selected. 2 items selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move selection when using the arrow keys")
- Given a ListView with selectionStyle="highlight" and selectionMode="multiple" where Foo and Bar are selected via Shift+ArrowDown, when a plain ArrowDown is pressed, then the range collapses to Set(['baz']) and announce says "Baz selected. 1 item selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should announce the new row when moving with the keyboard after multi select")
- Given a ListView with selectionStyle="highlight" and selectionMode="multiple" with Foo selected, when Ctrl+ArrowDown is pressed twice, then onSelectionChange is not called and no new announcements occur while focus moves to row Bar and then row Baz, so Ctrl+arrow moves focus without changing selection. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should support non-contiguous selection with the keyboard")
- Given focus on row Baz with only Foo selected in a highlight ListView, when Ctrl+Space is pressed, then the selection becomes Set(['foo','baz']) and announce says "Baz selected. 2 items selected."; pressing plain Space then replaces the selection with Set(['baz']) and announces "Baz selected. 1 item selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should support non-contiguous selection with the keyboard")
- Given a ListView with selectionStyle="highlight", selectionMode="multiple" and onAction with row 0 selected by mouse, when Ctrl+A selects all (announce "All items selected.") and then ArrowDown is pressed, then the selection collapses to Set(['bar']) and announce says "Bar selected. 1 item selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should announce the current selection when moving from all to one item")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with navigator.platform mocked to "MacIntel", when Tab focuses the table and Meta+A is pressed, then onSelectionChange is called once with the string 'all'. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support select all with Mod+A")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with navigator.platform mocked to "Win32", when Tab focuses the table and Control+A is pressed, then onSelectionChange is called once with the string 'all'. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support select all with Mod+A (Control) on Windows")
- Given selectionMode="single" with navigator.platform mocked to "MacIntel", when Tab focuses the table and Meta+A is pressed, then onSelectionChange is never called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not select all with Mod+A when selection mode is single")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with escapeKeyBehavior="none" and two rows selected via their checkboxes, when Escape is pressed, then onSelectionChange stays at 2 calls and both checkboxes remain checked. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should prevent Esc from clearing selection if escapeKeyBehavior is "none"")
- Given a TableView with selectionMode="multiple" and escapeKeyBehavior="none", driven through the @react-aria/test-utils Table tester with interaction type keyboard, when rows 0 and 1 are toggled selected and Escape is pressed, then both rows stay selected (getSelectedRows length 2) and onSelectionChange is still at two calls, so Escape does not clear the selection. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should prevent Esc from clearing selection if escapeKeyBehavior is "none"")
- Given a 25-row table with selectionMode="multiple" and row "Foo 10" already selected via Space on a cell, when Shift + ArrowDown is pressed, then onSelectionChange is called once with {'Foo 10', 'Foo 11'} and only row 11 (plus the anchor) shows aria-selected "true". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should extend a selection with Shift + ArrowDown")
- Given a 25-row table with row "Foo 10" already selected, when Shift + ArrowUp is pressed, then onSelectionChange is called once with {'Foo 9', 'Foo 10'} and rows 1 through 8 stay unselected. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should extend a selection with Shift + ArrowUp")
- Given a 25-row table with row "Foo 10" already selected, when Shift + Ctrl + Home is pressed, then onSelectionChange is called once with Foo 1 through Foo 10 and rows 1 to 10 show aria-selected "true" while rows past 10 stay false. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should extend a selection with Ctrl + Shift + Home")
- Given a 25-row table with row "Foo 10" already selected, when Shift + Ctrl + End is pressed, then onSelectionChange is called once with Foo 10 through Foo 25. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should extend a selection with Ctrl + Shift + End")
- Given a 25-row table with row "Foo 10" already selected, when Shift + PageDown is pressed, then onSelectionChange is called once with Foo 10 through Foo 25. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should extend a selection with Shift + PageDown")
- Given a 25-row table with row "Foo 10" already selected, when Shift + PageUp is pressed, then onSelectionChange is called once with Foo 1 through Foo 10 and rows 1 to 10 show aria-selected "true". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should extend a selection with Shift + PageUp")
- Given a 25-row table with selectionStyle="highlight" and onAction, when keyboard navigation moves the focused (and therefore selected) row to "Foo 10" then back up five rows to "Foo 5" and Enter is pressed, then onSelectionChange is not called, announce is not called and onAction fires once with 'Foo 5'. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support Enter to perform onAction with keyboard")
- Given selectionStyle="highlight" with row "Foo 5" selected by mouse click, when ArrowDown is pressed, then selection moves to {'Foo 6'} and announce says "Foo 6 selected."; ArrowUp returns to {'Foo 5'} announcing "Foo 5 selected."; Shift + ArrowDown then yields {'Foo 5', 'Foo 6'} announcing "Foo 6 selected. 2 items selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should move selection when using the arrow keys")
- Given selectionStyle="highlight" with rows Foo 5 and Foo 6 selected via Shift + ArrowDown, when a plain ArrowDown is pressed, then selection collapses to {'Foo 7'} and announce says "Foo 7 selected. 1 item selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should announce the new row when moving with the keyboard after multi select")
- Given selectionStyle="highlight" with row "Foo 5" selected, when Ctrl + ArrowDown is pressed twice, then neither announce nor onSelectionChange fires and focus moves to "Baz 6" then "Baz 7", so Ctrl plus arrow moves focus without changing selection. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support non-contiguous selection with the keyboard")
- Given focus has been moved to "Baz 7" with Ctrl + ArrowDown while "Foo 5" stays selected, when Ctrl + Space is pressed, then announce says "Foo 7 selected. 2 items selected." and onSelectionChange receives {'Foo 5', 'Foo 7'}; a plain Space then collapses to {'Foo 7'} announcing "Foo 7 selected. 1 item selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support non-contiguous selection with the keyboard")
- Given selectionStyle="highlight" with onAction and the focused row "Foo 10" already selected by arrow navigation, when Space is pressed then Enter, then onSelectionChange stays at one call (Space on an already selected row does not fire it again) and onAction fires once with 'Foo 10'. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should not call onSelectionChange when hitting Space/Enter on the currently selected row")
- Given selectionStyle="highlight" with row "Foo 5" selected, when Ctrl + A selects all (onSelectionChange called with 'all', announce "All items selected.") and then ArrowDown is pressed, then selection collapses to {'Foo 6'} and announce says "Foo 6 selected. 1 item selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should announce the current selection when moving from all to one item")
- Given a single-selection list built on useSelectableCollection with selectOnFocus, when Tab moves focus into it, then the first option is focused and gets `aria-selected="true"`, so focus and selection move together. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/selection/useSelectableCollection.test.js: "selects the first item it focuses if selectOnFocus")
- Given a multiple-selection list with `selectionBehavior="replace"` (highlight selection) after Tab selected the first item, when Ctrl+ArrowDown is pressed twice, then focus moves down each time while the original selection stays on item 1 and no other item becomes selected. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/selection/useSelectableCollection.test.js: "can navigate without replacing the selection in multiple selection selectOnFocus")
- Given the same list with focus moved to the third item by Ctrl+ArrowDown, when Space is pressed, then selection replaces the old one and only the focused third item is selected. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/selection/useSelectableCollection.test.js: "can navigate without replacing the selection in multiple selection selectOnFocus")
- Given a list with `shouldFocusWrap`, when ArrowUp is pressed on the first item, then focus wraps to the last item, and ArrowDown from the last wraps back to the first. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/selection/useSelectableCollection.test.js: "wraps focus with ArrowUp and ArrowDown when shouldFocusWrap is set")
- Given a three item list with focus on the first item, when PageDown is pressed, then focus moves to the last item, and PageUp returns to the first. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/selection/useSelectableCollection.test.js: "navigates by page with PageDown and PageUp")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given a ListBox with selectionMode="multiple", selectionBehavior="replace" and falsy-looking string ids, when item 1 is clicked then item 0 then item 1 again, then each click leaves exactly the clicked item aria-selected="true" and the previous one aria-selected="false". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should deselect item 0 when clicking another item in replace selection mode")
- Given that same falsy-key replace-mode ListBox, when item 0 is clicked and then item 2, then item 0 becomes aria-selected="false" and item 2 aria-selected="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should correctly handle mouse selection starting at item 0 and extending to item 2")
- Given a GridList with selectionMode="single" and selectionBehavior="replace" and no checkboxes, when the tester selects row "Kangaroo" with a modifier (selectionBehavior "replace" path) using mouse, keyboard or touch (describe.each over 'mouse', 'keyboard', 'touch'), then that row becomes aria-selected="true" with data-selected="true", the last onSelectionChange argument is Set(['kangaroo']) and exactly one row reports selected; the keyboard case has onSelectionChange called twice rather than once because initial keyboard focus selects the first row. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should perform selection with single selection")
- Given that single selection replace GridList with Kangaroo selected, when row "Dog" is selected, then Dog becomes aria-selected="true" with data-selected="true" and Kangaroo drops to aria-selected="false" with no data-selected, the last onSelectionChange argument is Set(['dog']) and one row is selected. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should perform selection with single selection")
- Given that single selection replace GridList with Dog selected, when Dog is toggled again with the modifier, then it becomes aria-selected="false" with no data-selected, the last onSelectionChange argument is an empty Set and no rows report selected, so single selection allows emptying. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should perform selection with single selection")
- Given a GridList with selectionMode="multiple", selectionBehavior="replace" and no checkboxes, when the tester selects Kangaroo with a modifier key using mouse or touch, then only Kangaroo is selected (last onSelectionChange argument Set(['kangaroo']), one selected row); with keyboard, onSelectionChange has fired twice and the selection is Set(['cat','kangaroo']) because initial keyboard focus selected the first row. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should perform toggle selection in highlight mode when using modifier keys")
- Given that highlight multiple GridList, when Dog is then selected with a modifier, then both Dog and Kangaroo are aria-selected="true" with data-selected="true"; the mouse and touch cases report Set(['dog','kangaroo']) with two selected rows, the keyboard case reports Set(['cat','dog','kangaroo']) with three. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should perform toggle selection in highlight mode when using modifier keys")
- Given that highlight multiple GridList with Dog and Kangaroo selected, when Dog is pressed again with the modifier key, then Dog becomes aria-selected="false" with no data-selected while Kangaroo stays selected, so modifier press deselects; mouse and touch end at Set(['kangaroo']) with one selected row and keyboard ends at Set(['cat','kangaroo']) with two. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should perform toggle selection in highlight mode when using modifier keys")
- Given a GridList with selectionMode="multiple", selectionBehavior="replace" and no checkboxes, when Kangaroo is selected without modifier keys, then it is aria-selected="true" with data-selected="true" and the last onSelectionChange argument is Set(['kangaroo']) with one selected row; onSelectionChange fired once for mouse and touch but three times for keyboard because selection changes on each focus move while arrowing down. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should perform replace selection in highlight mode when not using modifier keys")
- Given that replace-mode GridList with Kangaroo selected, when Dog is pressed without modifier keys using mouse or keyboard, then Dog becomes aria-selected="true" and Kangaroo drops to aria-selected="false" with no data-selected, the last onSelectionChange argument is Set(['dog']) and one row is selected; pressing Dog again without a modifier does not deselect it and does not fire onSelectionChange again. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should perform replace selection in highlight mode when not using modifier keys")
- Given that replace-mode GridList with Kangaroo selected and interaction type touch, when Dog is tapped, then touch always behaves as toggle so both Dog and Kangaroo are aria-selected="true" with onSelectionChange call 2 giving Set(['dog','kangaroo']) and two selected rows; tapping Dog again deselects it, giving call 3 Set(['kangaroo']) and one selected row. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should perform replace selection in highlight mode when not using modifier keys")
- Given a GridList with selectionMode="multiple", selectionBehavior="replace" and selection checkboxes, when row 0 then row 1 are clicked, then selection replaces so only row 1 is aria-selected="true" and rows 0 and 2 are "false"; clicking row 2's checkbox then adds it so rows 1 and 2 are both aria-selected="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support selectionMode="replace" with checkboxes")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="multiple" and row 0 clicked (selection Set(['foo'])), when Shift+click hits row 2, then the range Set(['foo','bar','baz']) is selected and announce says "3 items selected." on its second call. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should support range selection")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="multiple" and the full range selected, when Shift+click hits row 0 again, then the selection shrinks to Set(['foo']) and announce says "1 item selected." on its third call. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should support range selection")
- Given a ListView with selectionStyle="highlight", selectionMode="multiple" and navigator.platform mocked to 'Mac', when Meta+click hits row Bar, then only Bar is selected (Set(['bar']), aria-selected="true") and announce says "Bar selected."; Meta+click on Baz adds it giving Set(['bar','baz']) and "Baz selected. 2 items selected."; a third Meta+click on Bar deselects it giving Set(['baz']) with Bar aria-selected="false" and announce "Baz selected. 1 item selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should toggle items in selection highlight with meta-click on Mac")
- Given a ListView with selectionStyle="highlight", selectionMode="multiple" and navigator.userAgent mocked to 'Windows', when Ctrl+click hits row Foo then row Baz, then the selection grows from Set(['foo']) to Set(['foo','baz']) with rows 0 and 2 aria-selected="true", row 1 "false", and announce reporting "Foo selected." then "Baz selected. 2 items selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should allow multiple items to be selected in selection highlight with ctrl-click on Windows")
- Given a ListView with selectionStyle="highlight", selectionMode="multiple" and navigator.userAgent mocked to 'Windows', when Ctrl+click hits Bar then Baz then Bar again, then the selection goes Set(['bar']), Set(['bar','baz']), Set(['baz']) with Bar ending aria-selected="false" and Baz "true", and announce reporting "Bar selected.", "Baz selected. 2 items selected." and "Baz selected. 1 item selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should toggle items in selection highlight with ctrl-click on Windows")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" and escapeKeyBehavior="none", when the first row checkbox is clicked then the second, then each becomes checked and onSelectionChange receives the sets {'1'} then {'1', '2'}. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should prevent Esc from clearing selection if escapeKeyBehavior is "none"")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with selectionBehavior="replace", when the first body row is clicked, then its aria-selected changes from "false" to "true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not render checkboxes for selection with selectionBehavior=replace")
- Given a DraggableTable with selectionMode="multiple" and isDisabled on the drag hooks, when rendered then every row checkbox is unchecked and the first has aria-label "Select All", and when that checkbox is clicked then every row's checkbox becomes checked, so selection still works with drag and drop disabled. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should allow selection even when drag and drop is disabled")
- Given selectionMode="multiple", selectionBehavior="replace" and onRowAction with installPointerEvent, when the first body row receives a touch long press, then that row gets aria-selected="true" and checkboxes appear in every row (they were absent before the long press); long press for grid rows is strictly touch only. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should show checkboxes on long press")
- Given selectionMode="single" with no shouldSelectOnPressUp, when MouseLeft is pressed down on a row, then onSelectionChange is called once, and releasing the button does not call it again. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should select an item on pressing down when shouldSelectOnPressUp is not provided")
- Given selectionMode="single" with shouldSelectOnPressUp={false}, when MouseLeft is pressed down on a row, then onSelectionChange is called once, and releasing the button does not call it again. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should select an item on pressing down when shouldSelectOnPressUp is false")
- Given selectionMode="single" with shouldSelectOnPressUp={true}, when MouseLeft is pressed down on a row, then onSelectionChange is not called, and it is called once only on release. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should select an item on pressing up when shouldSelectOnPressUp is true")
- Given a 25-row table with selectionMode="multiple", when the "Baz 1" cell is clicked and then the "Baz 20" cell is clicked with ShiftLeft held, then onSelectionChange is called once with Foo 1 through Foo 20, rows 1 to 20 show aria-selected "true" and rows past 20 stay false. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support selecting a range with a pointer")
- Given a 25-row table where "Baz 10" was clicked first, when "Baz 20" is shift clicked then "Baz 1" is shift clicked, then the first shift click yields Foo 10 through Foo 20 and the second yields Foo 1 through Foo 10, so the anchor stays at row 10 rather than moving to the last shift-clicked row. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should anchor range selections with a pointer")
- Given a 25-row table with disabledKeys ['Foo 3', 'Foo 16'], when "Baz 1" is clicked and "Baz 20" is shift clicked, then onSelectionChange receives Foo 1 to Foo 20 minus Foo 3 and Foo 16, and those two rows keep aria-selected "false" while their neighbours are true. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should not include disabled rows within a range selection")
- Given a 25-row table with selectionStyle="highlight", when "Baz 10" is clicked, then no "Select All" checkbox exists at all, announce is called once with "Foo 10 selected."; shift clicking "Baz 20" announces "11 items selected." (second call); clicking "Foo 5" plainly replaces the whole selection with {'Foo 5'} and announces "Foo 5 selected. 1 item selected."; shift clicking "Foo 10" then yields {'Foo 5' ... 'Foo 10'} and announces "6 items selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "will replace the current selection with the new selection")
- Given a 25-row table with selectionStyle="highlight" and navigator.platform mocked to 'Mac', when "Baz 10" is clicked, "Baz 20" shift clicked, and then "Foo 5" clicked with MetaLeft held, then onSelectionChange receives Foo 5 plus Foo 10 through Foo 20, so the command key adds to the existing highlight selection rather than replacing it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "will add to the current selection if the command key is pressed")
- Given a 25-row table with selectionStyle="highlight" and PointerEvent installed, driven by the test-utils Table tester in touch interaction mode, when rows "Baz 5" and "Foo 10" are toggled, then there is no "Select All" checkbox, announce says "Foo 5 selected." then "Foo 10 selected. 2 items selected.", and onSelectionChange ends with {'Foo 5', 'Foo 10'}, so touch toggles rather than replaces. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should toggle selection with touch")
- Given a 25-row table with selectionStyle="highlight" and onAction and PointerEvent installed, when the "Baz 5" cell receives a single TouchA tap, then announce is never called, onSelectionChange is never called and onAction is called once with 'Foo 5'. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support single tap to perform onAction with touch")
- Given a 25-row table with selectionStyle="highlight" and onAction, when the test-utils tester toggles row "Foo 5" (single click selects, announcing "Foo 5 selected.") and then triggers the row action with needsDoubleClick, then the double click fires onAction once with 'Foo 5' while announce and onSelectionChange stay untouched. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support double click to perform onAction with mouse")
- Given a 25-row table with selectionStyle="highlight", no onAction, navigator.userAgent mocked to 'Android' and PointerEvent installed, when a zero-width touch pointerdown/pointerup/click sequence hits "Baz 5", then onSelectionChange receives {'Foo 5'}; a virtual mouse pointer sequence with pressure 0 and detail 0 on "Foo 8" adds Foo 8; repeating that sequence on "Foo 10" (the Android TalkBack double tap path) adds Foo 10, so a screen reader single tap selects the row. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support single tap to perform row selection with screen reader if onAction isn't provided")
- Given a 25-row table with selectionStyle="highlight", onAction, navigator.userAgent mocked to 'Android' and PointerEvent installed, when a click with detail 0 hits "Baz 5", then announce and onSelectionChange are untouched and onAction fires once with 'Foo 5'; the Android TalkBack virtual pointer sequence on "Foo 10" fires onAction a second time with 'Foo 10' and still no selection change. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support single tap to perform onAction with screen reader")
- Given a 25-row table with selectionStyle="highlight", onAction, window.ontouchstart stubbed and PointerEvent installed, when a touch pointerdown lands on the "Baz 5" cell, then the grid's aria-describedby contains the id of a hidden "Long press to enter selection mode." description, announce, onSelectionChange and onAction are all untouched and no "Select All" checkbox exists yet. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support long press to enter selection mode on touch")
- Given the touch press is held on "Baz 5", when timers advance by 800 ms, then announce says "Foo 5 selected." (one call), onSelectionChange receives {'Foo 5'}, onAction is not called and a "Select All" checkbox now exists because the table entered selection mode. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support long press to enter selection mode on touch")
- Given selection mode has been entered by long press, when the "Foo 10" cell is tapped with pointerType touch, then announce says "Foo 10 selected. 2 items selected." and onSelectionChange receives {'Foo 5', 'Foo 10'} without a further long press. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support long press to enter selection mode on touch")
- Given two rows selected by touch in highlight mode, when both are toggled off, then announce says "Foo 10 not selected. 1 item selected." then "Foo 5 not selected.", onSelectionChange ends with an empty set, onAction was never called, and the "Select All" checkbox disappears because the table leaves selection mode. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support long press to enter selection mode on touch")
- Given a table with selectionMode="none" and onAction, when the "Baz 10" cell is clicked with pointerType mouse, then announce and onSelectionChange stay untouched and onAction fires once with 'Foo 10'. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should perform onAction on single click with selectionMode: none")
- Given a mobile viewport and a `selectionBehavior="replace"` multiple-selection list, when items are activated with VoiceOver style virtual pointer events (pointerDown/pointerUp with `pointerType: 'virtual'` then a click with detail 1), then each press adds to the selection instead of replacing it, so highlight selection falls back to toggle behavior for screen reader and touch users. Run under `describe.each` for "VO Events". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/selection/useSelectableCollection.test.js: "uses toggle mode when the interaction is touch")
- Given the same list driven by touch pointer events (`pointerType: 'touch'` with a pointerId then a click), then presses also toggle rather than replace the selection. Run under `describe.each` for "Touch Pointer Events". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/selection/useSelectableCollection.test.js: "uses toggle mode when the interaction is touch")

### Focus management

- Given `autoFocus="first"` or `autoFocus="last"` with selectOnFocus, when rendered, then the corresponding option is focused and selected. Run as `it.each` over first/index 0 and last/index 2. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/selection/useSelectableCollection.test.js: "selects the autofocused item if selectOnFocus with autoFocus=$autoFocus")
- Given `autoFocus="first"` with `defaultSelectedKeys` already containing the third item, when rendered, then the existing selection is kept and the first item does not become selected. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/selection/useSelectableCollection.test.js: "does not change the selection when autofocusing an already selected collection")
- Given two highlight-selection lists that each start with items 2 and 3 selected and a button between them, when Tab moves forward into the second list, then focus lands on its first selected option ("Vicente Amigo"); when Shift+Tab moves backward into the first list, focus lands on its last selected option ("Gerardo Nunez"); neither list fires onSelectionChange. Run twice under the pointer-event `describe.each`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/selection/useSelectableCollection.test.js: "focuses first/last selected item on focus enter and does not change the selection")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given selectionMode="single" with selectionBehavior="replace" and installPointerEvent, when toggleOptionSelection with selectionBehavior "replace" selects "Kangaroo", then that option has aria-selected="true" and data-selected="true", it is the single selected option, and onSelectionChange was last called with a set equal to {'kangaroo'}; for keyboard the call count is 2 because initial keyboard focus selects the first option, and 1 for mouse and touch. Parameterized over %s mouse, keyboard and touch. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should perform selection with single selection")
- Given that single-selection replace ListBox, when the second option is then toggled with modifier, then it becomes aria-selected="true" with data-selected="true" while the previously selected option goes to aria-selected="false" with no data-selected, only one option is selected, and onSelectionChange was last called with {'dog'}. Parameterized over %s mouse, keyboard and touch. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should perform selection with single selection")
- Given that single-selection replace ListBox with the second option selected, when it is toggled again with modifier, then it becomes aria-selected="false" with no data-selected, no option is selected, and onSelectionChange was last called with an empty set. Parameterized over %s mouse, keyboard and touch. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should perform selection with single selection")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with selectionBehavior="replace", when toggleOptionSelection with selectionBehavior "replace" selects "Kangaroo", then for mouse and touch onSelectionChange fires once with {'kangaroo'} and one option is selected, while for keyboard it fires twice with {'cat','kangaroo'} and two options are selected because the initial keyboard focus selected the first option. Parameterized over %s mouse, keyboard and touch. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should perform toggle selection in highlight mode when using modifier keys")
- Given that multiple-selection replace ListBox, when the second option is toggled with modifier, then it and Kangaroo are both aria-selected="true" and data-selected="true", giving {'dog','kangaroo'} and 2 selected for mouse and touch, or {'cat','dog','kangaroo'} and 3 selected for keyboard. Parameterized over %s mouse, keyboard and touch. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should perform toggle selection in highlight mode when using modifier keys")
- Given that multiple-selection replace ListBox with the second option selected, when it is toggled with modifier again, then it becomes aria-selected="false" with no data-selected while Kangaroo stays selected, so with a modifier key the same option can be deselected in highlight mode. Parameterized over %s mouse, keyboard and touch. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should perform toggle selection in highlight mode when using modifier keys")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with selectionBehavior="replace", when toggleOptionSelection selects "Kangaroo" without a modifier, then it is the only selected option with aria-selected="true" and data-selected="true", and onSelectionChange was last called with {'kangaroo'}, fired once for mouse and touch but 3 times for keyboard because selection changes on each option focus while arrowing down. Parameterized over %s mouse, keyboard and touch. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should perform replace selection in highlight mode when not using modifier keys")
- Given that ListBox with Kangaroo selected, when the second option is pressed without a modifier using mouse or keyboard, then it replaces the selection ({'dog'}, one selected option, Kangaroo aria-selected="false"), and pressing it again without a modifier does not deselect it (call count unchanged, still one selected). Parameterized over %s mouse and keyboard. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should perform replace selection in highlight mode when not using modifier keys")
- Given that ListBox with Kangaroo selected, when the second option is tapped without a modifier on touch, then touch always behaves as toggle so both options end aria-selected="true" with onSelectionChange called with {'dog','kangaroo'}, and tapping it again deselects it leaving {'kangaroo'}. Parameterized over %s touch. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should perform replace selection in highlight mode when not using modifier keys")
- Given selectionMode="single" and selectionBehavior="replace" (describe.each(['mouse', 'keyboard', 'touch'])), when row 2 is toggled with selectionBehavior "replace" then row 1 then row 1 again, then row 2 becomes aria-selected="true" with data-selected="true" and the change payload is the set {'3'}; selecting row 1 replaces it so row 1 is selected, row 2 is deselected and loses data-selected, and the payload is {'2'}; toggling row 1 again deselects it and the payload is the empty set, with getSelectedRows() reporting 1, 1 then 0 rows. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should perform selection with single selection")
- Given the same single selection replace table, when interactionType is keyboard, then onSelectionChange fires one extra time up front because initial keyboard focus selects the first row, giving call counts 2, 3 and 4 instead of the pointer counts 1, 2 and 3. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should perform selection with single selection")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" and selectionBehavior="replace" (describe.each(['mouse', 'keyboard', 'touch'])), when row 2 then row 1 are toggled with modifier keys, then both rows end up aria-selected="true" with data-selected="true"; for mouse and touch the payloads are {'3'} then {'2', '3'} with 1 then 2 calls, and toggling row 1 a third time deselects only row 1 leaving payload {'3'} and 2 selected rows before it, 1 after. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should perform toggle selection in highlight mode when using modifier keys")
- Given the same multiple replace table with interactionType keyboard, then initial focus selects row 1 first, so payloads are {'1', '3'}, {'1', '2', '3'} and {'1', '3'} with call counts 2, 3 and 4 and selected row counts 2, 3 and 2. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should perform toggle selection in highlight mode when using modifier keys")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" and selectionBehavior="replace" (describe.each(['mouse', 'keyboard', 'touch'])), when row 2 is toggled without modifier keys, then it becomes aria-selected="true" with data-selected="true" and the payload is {'3'}; call counts are 1 for mouse and 3 for keyboard because selection follows focus as arrow keys move down. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should perform replace selection in highlight mode when not using modifier keys")
- Given the same table with interactionType mouse or keyboard, when row 1 is then toggled without modifiers, then the selection is replaced so row 1 is selected, row 2 is deselected and loses data-selected, the payload is {'2'}, and pressing row 1 again without modifiers does not deselect it (call count and 1 selected row stay unchanged). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should perform replace selection in highlight mode when not using modifier keys")
- Given the same table with interactionType touch, when row 1 is toggled after row 2, then touch always behaves as toggle so both rows are aria-selected="true" with payload {'2', '3'} after 2 calls, and toggling row 1 again deselects it leaving payload {'3'} and row 2 as the only selected row. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should perform replace selection in highlight mode when not using modifier keys")

## typeahead

### Keyboard

- Given a sectioned Menu with autoFocus="first" and items Foo, Bar, Baz, Blah, Bleh, when the keys B, L then E are pressed in rapid succession on the menu, then focus moves to Bar (index 1), then Blah (index 3), then Bleh (index 4), so the accumulated search string matches item text across sections. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/Menu.test.js: "$Name supports focusing items by typing letters in rapid succession")
- Given the same Menu, when B is pressed to focus Bar and all jest timers are then run to expire the typeahead buffer, then pressing B again keeps focus on Bar rather than advancing to the next B match, so the search text resets after the timeout. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/Menu.test.js: "$Name resets the search text after a timeout")
- Given the same Menu with focus moved to Bleh by typing B, L, E, when the timers are run and B is pressed again, then focus stays on Bleh, so the search wraps around and finds the nearest match when no item past the current one matches. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/menu/Menu.test.js: "$Name wraps around when no items past the current one match")
- Given a Spectrum ListBox with 7 options across sections and autoFocus="first", when the keys B, L then E are pressed in rapid succession on the listbox, then focus moves to option 1 (Bar), then option 3 (Blah), then option 4 (Bleh), matching the accumulated search string. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports focusing items by typing letters in rapid succession")
- Given the same ListBox with autoFocus="first", when F, O, O are typed (focus stays on option 0 "Foo") and then a space is pressed, then the space is treated as part of the search and focus moves to option 5 ("Foo Bar"), and continuing with B, A, Z moves focus to option 6 ("Foo Baz"). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports the space character in a search")
- Given autoFocus="first" and selectionMode="single", when F, O, O and then space are typed, then focus moves to option 5 but no selection is made: the active option has aria-selected="false", it has no checkmark image, the listbox has zero checkmark images, and onSelectionChange is not called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports item selection using the Spacebar after search times out")
- Given that same search is continued with B (focus stays on option 5), when the typeahead timers are run out and Space is then pressed, then the focused option becomes aria-selected="true" with a checkmark, the listbox has exactly one checkmark, and onSelectionChange is called once with a set containing "Foo Bar". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "supports item selection using the Spacebar after search times out")
- Given autoFocus="first", when B is pressed moving focus to option 1, the typeahead timers are run out, and B is pressed again, then focus stays on option 1 rather than advancing, so the search text resets after the timeout. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "resets the search text after a timeout")
- Given autoFocus="first", when B, L, E move focus to option 4 (Bleh), the timers are run out, and B is pressed again, then focus stays on option 4, so the search wraps around and finds the current item when nothing past it matches. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "wraps around when no items past the current one match")
- Given a Picker opened with ArrowDown so the first option is focused, when "t" then "h" are typed on the listbox, then focus moves to "Two" and then to "Three" as the search buffer accumulates, and Enter selects "three" (onSelectionChange called once with "three"), closing the listbox and restoring focus to the trigger which shows "Three". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports type to select")
- Given the same Picker after advancing timers by 500ms and reopening with ArrowDown (focus on the previously selected third option), when "n" is typed and Enter pressed, then the item with key="" and text "None" is selected, onSelectionChange was called a second time with the empty string and the trigger shows "None". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports type to select")
- Given a closed Picker with the trigger focused, when "t" then "h" are typed in rapid succession on the trigger, then the menu never opens and the selection itself changes: onSelectionChange is called with "two" then "three" and the trigger text goes "Two" then "Three". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "supports focusing items by typing letters in rapid succession without opening the menu")
- Given a closed Picker where typing "t" already selected "two", when all timers run so the typeahead buffer resets and then "h" is typed, then onSelectionChange is still at one call and the trigger still shows "Two", because "h" alone matches nothing. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "resets the search text after a timeout")
- Given a closed Picker where typing "t" selected "two" and the buffer then timed out, when "o" is typed, then onSelectionChange has been called twice and the trigger shows "One", so the search wraps around to an earlier item when nothing past the current one matches. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/picker/Picker.test.js: "wraps around when no items past the current one match")
- Given a RAC Select with Australian state options, when the trigger is focused with Tab and "Northern Terr" is typed (under jest fake timers), then the trigger shows "Northern Territory" and has no data-pressed attribute, so typeahead on a closed trigger selects without opening the popover. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Select.test.js: "can select an option via typeahead")
- Given a ListView with rows Foo, Bar and Baz and focus moved into the list by Tab, when keydown "B", keydown "A" and keydown "Z" are fired on the grid (the first keyup is deliberately fired as "Enter"), then focus lands on row Baz. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "focuses the correct cell when typing")
- Given a GridList with rows "Apple" and "Banana" where the Apple row contains a text input, and either keyboardNavigationBehavior="tab" or layout="grid", when focus is moved into the input and "b" is typed, then focus stays on the input and its value becomes "b", so typeahead does not jump to the Banana row. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should not trigger typeahead when typing in a text input child (%s)")
- Given a dynamic Table whose rows are Games, Program Files, bootmgr and log.txt, when Tab focuses the first body row and the characters "boo" are typed, then focus moves to the "bootmgr" row (rowElements[3]). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support columnHeader typeahead")
- Given rows whose visible names are prefixed ("1. Games", "3. bootmgr") but whose Row textValue props are the unprefixed names, when Tab focuses the first body row and "boo" is typed, then focus moves to the row with textValue "bootmgr" (rowElements[3]), so textValue overrides the rendered text for typeahead matching. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support textValue overriding typeahead")
- Given a Table with keyboardNavigationBehavior="tab" and focus moved into the "Games notes" text input inside a cell, when "Games" is typed into the input, then the input value becomes "Games" and focus stays on the input rather than typeahead moving row focus. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not trigger typeahead when typing in a text input child")
- Given a TableView with selectionMode="none", two isRowHeader columns (First Name, Last Name) and a non-row-header Birthday column, with focus on the "Sam" cell, when J then o then h are typed in rapid succession, then focus moves to the "Julia" cell, then the "Jones" cell, then the "John" cell, so typeahead on a cell moves focus cell by cell across matching row header cells. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "focuses cell by typing letters in rapid succession")
- Given the same table with focus on the "Sam" cell, when D is typed, then focus moves to the "Doe" cell, so typeahead matches text in any row header column, not only the first. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "matches against all row header cells")
- Given the same table with focus on the "Sam" cell, when F is typed (matching only the non-row-header "February 10" birthday cell), then focus stays on the "Sam" cell, so non row header columns are excluded from the typeahead text. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "non row header columns don't match")
- Given the same table with focus on the first body row element, when J then o then h are typed in rapid succession, then focus goes to the second row, stays on the second row for "Jo", then moves to the third row for "Joh". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "focuses row by typing letters in rapid succession")
- Given the same table with focus on the first body row element, when D is typed, then focus moves to the third row (whose last name is Doe), so row-level typeahead also matches every row header cell. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "matches row against all row header cells")
- Given typeahead has already matched "J" and moved focus to the "Julia" cell, when all timers run so the search buffer times out and J is typed again, then focus stays on the "Julia" cell instead of advancing, so the buffer resets to a single letter search. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "resets the search text after a timeout")
- Given typeahead has walked J, o, h to reach the "John" cell and the search buffer has timed out, when J is typed then u, then focus stays on "John" for the J and moves to the "Julia" cell for "Ju", so the search wraps around past the end of the collection. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "wraps around when reaching the end of the collection")
- Given focus is on the "Julia" cell after typing J and the buffer has timed out, when S is typed, then focus wraps backwards to the "Sam" cell because no item past the current one matches. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "wraps around when no items past the current one match")
- Given the TypeaheadWithDialog story where a dialog trigger inside the table opens a dialog containing a text field labelled "Enter a J", when the trigger is clicked and J is typed into the focused text field, then the text field keeps DOM focus and the table's typeahead does not steal it; pressing Escape afterwards closes the dialog. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "does not pick up typeahead from a dialog")

## collections

### Roles and attributes

- Given a Spectrum ListBox whose items use falsy ids (a section with id 0 and a section with id ''), when rendered, then both sections render as groups and each contains its two options with the expected text, so falsy keys are not dropped from the collection. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "renders with falsy id")
- Given Spectrum Items rendered with an explicit id prop equal to the item name, when rendered, then the option's DOM id is not "Foo", so a custom id does not override the generated item id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "item id should not get overridden by custom id")

### Keyboard

- Given a tree built with `useTreeState`, when the user navigates with the keyboard, then focus moves through the tree rows. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/tree/useTreeState.test.js: "should be keyboard navigable")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a Spectrum ListBox with two sections where "Foo 1" starts in Section 1, when rerendered with "Foo 1" moved into Section 2's children, then the option is found inside the second section group (the one labelled "Section 2") instead of the first. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/listbox/ListBox.test.js: "should handle when an item changes sections")
- Given a react-aria-components ListBox with items={[{id:1,'Cat'},{id:2,'Dog'}]} and a render function, when the items array is rerendered with an appended item, an item inserted in the middle, an item's name changed, two items swapped, and finally an item removed, then the rendered option texts are in turn [Cat, Dog], [Cat, Dog, Mouse], [Cat, Kangaroo, Dog, Mouse], [Cat, Kangaroo, Doggy, Mouse], [Cat, Kangaroo, Mouse, Doggy] and [Cat, Kangaroo, Mouse]. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support dynamic collections")
- Given a ListBox whose children come from a descendant component holding local state, when that descendant toggles a second ListBoxItem on and off and then changes the first item's text, then the option texts go [One], [One, Two], [One] and [Hi], so the collection updates when descendants update. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should update collection when descendants update")
- Given two ListBoxSections with three items each, when rerendered with "Ham" moved from the meats section into the veggies section, then the first group has 4 options and the second has 2.
