(react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should update collection when moving item to a different section")
- Given a ListBox with items={['Foo','Bar','Baz']} (plain strings, not objects), when rendered, then there are 3 options with those texts, and rerendering with ['Foo','Baz'] leaves 2 options with texts Foo and Baz. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should support dynamic collection with non-object entries")
- Given a ListBox over the same items array, when only the render function changes to add textValue="Updated" and prefix the text, then the 3 options rerender with texts "Updated: Foo", "Updated: Bar" and "Updated: Baz". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "should update collection if render function changes")
- Given a GridList with an items array of {id, name} and a render function returning GridListItem, then the rows inside the grid have text content ['Cat', 'Dog']. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support dynamic collections")
- Given a GridList with two GridListSections of three items each, then each rowgroup contains three role="gridcell" elements; after rerendering with the "ham" item moved from the Meats section into the Veggies section, the first rowgroup has four gridcells and the second has two. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should update collection when moving item to a different section")
- Given a ListView whose items use falsy ids (id 0 and id 1), then the grid is visible with two rows and the first row has exactly one gridcell with text content "Foo", so id 0 is not treated as missing. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "renders a falsy ids")
- Given a Table whose TableHeader and TableBody use items render functions over 3 columns and 4 rows, when rendered, then 5 rows exist (header row plus 4 body rows). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support dynamic collections")
- Given dynamic rows whose ids are 1, 0 and 2 so one key is falsy, when rendered, then 4 rows exist and the body rows keep their declared order with text content "One", "Zero" and "Two". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support rows with a falsy key")
- Given a Row whose children is a render function over columns, when rendered, then the function is called at least once (once in React 19, twice in React 18, 17 and 16) and every call receives the column object itself as its only argument, never a state object. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support row render function and not call it with state")
- Given a dynamic table rendered with 3 columns, when rerendered with only the first and third columns (and matching TableBody dependencies and Row columns), then the number of columnheaders drops from 3 to 2. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support updating columns")
- Given a dynamic table whose rowheaders read Games, Program Files, bootmgr and log.txt, when rerendered with the first two items swapped and the first item's name changed to "XYZ", then the rowheaders read Program Files, XYZ, bootmgr and log.txt. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support updating and reordering a row at the same time")
- Given a Table containing a nested TagGroup collection inside a cell where tag ids collide with row ids, when rendered, then every element with a data-key attribute has a unique data-collection plus data-key pair. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support nested collections with colliding keys")
- Given a table whose columns can be hidden by a toggle button, using static Rows, when the button is clicked to hide the columns and clicked again to show them, then the button label cycles "Hide Columns", "Show Columns", "Hide Columns" without error. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "supports removing a column and adding it back static")
- Given the same hiding columns example using a dynamic TableBody with dependencies, when the toggle button is clicked twice, then the button label cycles "Hide Columns", "Show Columns", "Hide Columns" without error. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "supports removing a column and adding it back dynamic")
- Given a TableWithSuspense story in React 19 (the test returns early when React.use is missing), when the render suspends, then 2 rows show with the second reading "Loading..."; after timers run 3 rows show FalconSat and DemoSat; clicking the load button suspends again back to a single "Loading..." row; and after the promise resolves 5 rows show FalconSat, DemoSat, Trailblazer and RatSat. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support React Suspense without transitions")
- Given TableWithSuspense with reactTransition in React 19, when the initial render suspends then resolves, then rows go from a "Loading..." row to FalconSat and DemoSat; clicking the "Load more" button changes its text to "Loading" while the existing 3 rows stay visible, and after the promise resolves the button reads "Load more" again and 5 rows show FalconSat, DemoSat, Trailblazer and RatSat. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support React Suspense with transitions")
- Given TableWithSuspense with reactTransition in React 19 and real timers, when the initial promise resolves, then the mocked useSyncExternalStore subscriber has fired 2 collection updates, and clicking the load button brings it to exactly 3, so a transition does not cause excessive collection re-renders. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not render excessively in React Suspense with transitions")
- Given a CollectionBuilder whose content renders no items, when rendered, then the resulting collection is still marked `frozen: true`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/collections/CollectionBuilder.test.js: "should be frozen even in case of empty initial collection")
- Given a collection with one item that is then rerendered with none, when the update flushes, then the collection is frozen and both firstKey and lastKey are null. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/collections/CollectionBuilder.test.js: "should have correct firstKey, lastKey and should be frozen after all items are deleted")
- Given components created with the older string form of `createLeafComponent('item', ...)` and `createBranchComponent('section', ...)`, when a section with one item is rendered, then the collection is frozen, firstKey is the generated section key, the section node's type is "section" with a firstChildKey pointing at the item, and that child node's type is "item"; the string node-class API still works. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/collections/CollectionBuilder.test.js: "should still support using strings for the collection node class in createLeafComponent/createBranchComponent")
- Given `useControlledState` with a defaultValue, when setValue is called with a new value, then the state updates and onChange fires with it; calling setValue again with the same value updates nothing and does not fire onChange, while setting a value that was used earlier but not immediately before does fire onChange again. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/utils/useControlledState.test.tsx: "can handle default setValue behavior, wont invoke onChange for the same value twice in a row")
- Given a null initial value, when setValue(NaN) is called twice, then the value becomes NaN and onChange fires exactly once, because NaN is compared by value rather than by `===`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/utils/useControlledState.test.tsx: "using NaN will only trigger onChange once")
- Given an uncontrolled state, when setValue is called with an updater function, then the function receives the previous value and onChange fires with the computed result. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/utils/useControlledState.test.tsx: "can handle callback setValue behavior")
- Given a component using useControlledState, when it mounts and updates, then the render count stays at the minimum (1 then 2), so the hook does not double render. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/utils/useControlledState.test.tsx: "does not trigger too many renders")
- Given a controlled value, when setValue is called, then the rendered value stays at the prop value while onChange reports the attempted one; calling setValue with the current prop value fires nothing. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/utils/useControlledState.test.tsx: "can handle controlled setValue behavior")
- Given a controlled value, when setValue is called with an updater function, then the updater sees the controlled value and onChange receives the result. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/utils/useControlledState.test.tsx: "can handle controlled callback setValue behavior")
- Given a controlled value, when setValue is called several times inside one `act`, then each updater sees the value produced by the previous call rather than a stale prop. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/utils/useControlledState.test.tsx: "can handle controlled callback setValue behavior called multiple times within a single act")
- Given a controlled value that changes by prop, when setValue's updater runs afterwards, then it sees the new prop value. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/utils/useControlledState.test.tsx: "can handle controlled callback setValue behavior after prop change")
- Given a controlled component, when it rerenders with the value prop removed, then a console warning fires about switching from controlled to uncontrolled. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/utils/useControlledState.test.tsx: "will console warn if the programmer tries to switch from controlled to uncontrolled")
- Given an uncontrolled component, when it rerenders with a value prop added, then a console warning fires about switching from uncontrolled to controlled. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/utils/useControlledState.test.tsx: "will console warn if the programmer tries to switch from uncontrolled to controlled")
- Given a controlled useControlledState inside a Suspense boundary that suspends on update, when values are set across suspensions, then onChange fires once per distinct value with the right payloads and no duplicates. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/utils/useControlledState.test.tsx: "should work with suspense when controlled")
- Given the same controlled setup driven by function set state, when values are set across suspensions, then onChange still fires once per distinct value. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/utils/useControlledState.test.tsx: "should work with suspense when controlled with function set state")
- Given an uncontrolled useControlledState with Suspense, when values are set across suspensions, then onChange fires for each committed value including the repeat that a suspended render produces. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/utils/useControlledState.test.tsx: "should work with suspense when uncontrolled")
- Given the uncontrolled Suspense setup driven by function set state, when values are set, then the same onChange sequence results. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/utils/useControlledState.test.tsx: "should work with suspense when uncontrolled with function set state")

### Positioning

- Given a scrollable document root with a border, when `scrollIntoView` scrolls an element to the start, then the root's border width is excluded from the computed scroll port so the element is not left under the border. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/utils/scrollIntoView.test.ts: "excludes root border from scroll port when scrolling to start")
- Given the same setup, when scrolling an element to the end, then the root border is likewise excluded. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/utils/scrollIntoView.test.ts: "excludes root border from scroll port when scrolling to end")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a ListBox with 5 ListBoxItems wrapped in React.Activity whose mode is toggled by a button (React 19 only, the test is skipped on older React via a version check), when the mode starts as "hidden", then there are 0 options; clicking the button to "visible" renders 5 options and clicking again returns to 0. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "supports Activity")
- Given a page component rendered inside React.Activity and reading mode from context, memoized so the route element identity is stable (React 19 only), when mode is "visible" 5 options are rendered, and after rerendering through mode "hidden" with a changed pathname and back to "visible", then 5 options are rendered again. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/ListBox.test.js: "supports Activity into a portal")
- Given a Table whose Rows are written statically without id props but whose Cells are produced by a render function over columns, when rendered, then it throws "No id detected for the Row element. The Row element requires a id to be provided to it when the cells are rendered dynamically.". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should throw a warning if the rows are rendered staticly without ids but the cells are rendered dynamically")

## slider

### Roles and attributes

- Given `useSlider` with a `label`, when the hook runs, then groupProps.role is "group" and labelProps.htmlFor is undefined, deliberately, because Safari misreports a label pointing at a range input (WebKit bug 172464). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSlider.test.js: "should have the right labels when setting label")
- Given `useSlider` with only `aria-label`, when the hook runs, then labelProps is an empty object and the aria-label moves onto the group. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSlider.test.js: "should have the right labels when setting aria-label")
- Given a slider-level label with minValue 10, maxValue 200, step 2 and value 50, when useSliderThumb runs, then inputProps is `type: 'range'`, step 2, value 50, min 10, max 200, and aria-labelledby points at the slider label id. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSliderThumb.test.js: "should have the right labels with Slider-level label")
- Given a thumb-level `label` under a slider with an aria-label, when the hook runs, then the input's aria-labelledby is "<thumbLabelId> <groupId>" and the input id equals the thumb label's htmlFor. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSliderThumb.test.js: "should have the right labels with Slider thumb label")
- Given two thumbs with their own aria-labels and values 50 and 70, when the hooks run, then thumb 0 gets min 10 and max 70 while thumb 1 gets min 50 and max 200 (each thumb is bounded by its neighbor), and each input's aria-labelledby is "<ownId> <groupId>". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSliderThumb.test.js: "should have the right labels with Slider thumb aria-label")
- Given a Spectrum Slider with only `aria-label`, when rendered, then the group carries the aria-label, renders no visible text, and the slider input has `aria-valuetext="0"`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "supports aria-label")
- Given a Spectrum Slider with a `label`, when rendered, then the group's aria-labelledby and the slider's aria-labelledby both point at the label, the label has no `for` attribute (WebKit bug 172464), and an `output` element with role status shows the value, has `for` pointing at the slider id, no aria-labelledby, and `aria-live="off"`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "supports label")
- Given `showValueLabel={false}`, when rendered, then the group text is just the label and no status element exists, while the slider still has aria-valuetext. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "supports showValueLabel: false")
- Given a Spectrum RangeSlider with a label, when rendered, then the two inputs get localized `aria-label` values "Minimum" and "Maximum", each with aria-labelledby of "<ownId> <groupLabelId>", and the output shows "0 – 100" with a `for` listing both slider ids and `aria-live="off"`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "supports label")
- Given a RangeSlider with only `aria-label`, when rendered, then the group has the aria-label and no visible text. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "supports aria-label")
- Given `showValueLabel={false}` on a RangeSlider, when rendered, then the group text is just the label and no status element renders. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "supports showValueLabel: false")
- Given a RAC Slider with Label, SliderOutput, SliderTrack, SliderFill, and SliderThumb, when rendered, then the group has class `react-aria-Slider` with aria-labelledby pointing at the label text, the status output reads "0", and the track, thumb, and fill elements each render with their default classes. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should render a slider with default class")
- Given a custom className on the RAC Slider, when rendered, then it replaces the default class. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should render a slider with custom class")
- Given data props on Slider, SliderThumb, SliderTrack, and SliderOutput, when rendered, then each element carries its own. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support DOM props")
- Given a SliderContext "test" slot with an aria-label, when `slot="test"` is used, then the group has both the slot attribute and the aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support slot")
- Given `isDisabled` on a RAC Slider, when rendered, then the input is disabled and both the group and the thumb get `data-disabled="true"` plus their disabled render-prop classes. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support disabled state")
- Given `orientation="vertical"`, when rendered, then the group has `data-orientation="vertical"` with the orientation class and the input has `aria-orientation="vertical"`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support orientation")
- Given a RAC Slider with `defaultValue={[30, 60]}` and thumbs mapped from `state.values`, when rendered, then there are two slider inputs with values 30 and 60 and the output reads "30–60". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support two thumbs")
- Given `defaultValue={[30, 60, 80]}`, when rendered, then three inputs exist and the output reads "30, 60, 80" (a list rather than a range). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support three thumbs")

### Keyboard

- Given a horizontal slider at 10, when ArrowRight then ArrowLeft are pressed, then the value goes to 11 and back to 10, with onChange and onChangeEnd each firing once per key press (keyboard changes commit immediately). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSliderThumb.test.js: "can be moved with keys")
- Given a slider already at its minimum 0, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then onChangeEnd still fires with 0 and no value change happens; ArrowRight then moves to 1. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSliderThumb.test.js: "can be moved with keys at the beginning of the slider")
- Given a slider at its maximum 100, when ArrowRight is pressed, then onChangeEnd fires with 100 with no change, and ArrowLeft moves to 99. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSliderThumb.test.js: "can be moved with keys at the end of the slider")
- Given a vertical slider at 10, when ArrowRight, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, and ArrowLeft are pressed, then the value goes 11, 12, 11, 10, so both axes of arrows work on a vertical slider. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSliderThumb.test.js: "can be moved with keys (vertical)")
- Given a vertical slider at 0, when ArrowDown is pressed, then onChangeEnd fires with 0 and nothing moves; ArrowUp raises it to 1. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSliderThumb.test.js: "can be moved with keys (vertical) at the bottom of the slider")
- Given a vertical slider at 100, when ArrowUp is pressed, then onChangeEnd fires with 100 and nothing moves; ArrowDown lowers it to 99. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSliderThumb.test.js: "can be moved with keys (vertical) at the top of the slider")
- Given a Spectrum Slider at 50 in a de-DE (LTR) locale, when ArrowRight then ArrowLeft are pressed, then the value moves +1 then -1. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "$Name moves the slider in the correct direction")
- Given the same slider in an ar-AE (RTL) locale, when ArrowRight is pressed, then the value moves -1 and ArrowLeft moves +1 (horizontal arrows are mirrored in RTL). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "$Name moves the slider in the correct direction")
- Given a disabled Slider, when ArrowRight or ArrowLeft is pressed, then the value does not change. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "$Name moves the slider in the correct direction")
- Given a Slider in either de-DE or ar-AE, when ArrowUp or ArrowDown is pressed, then the value moves +1 or -1 regardless of direction (vertical arrows are never mirrored). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "$Name moves the slider in the correct direction")
- Given a 0-100 Slider in either locale, when PageUp or PageDown is pressed, then the value moves by the default page size of 10 and is not mirrored in RTL. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "$Name moves the slider in the correct direction")
- Given a 0-100 Slider at 50 in either locale, when Home then End are pressed, then the value jumps to the minimum then the maximum, unaffected by RTL. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "$Name moves the slider in the correct direction")
- Given `orientation="vertical"` on a Spectrum Slider, when the same arrow, page, and Home/End keys are pressed in de-DE and ar-AE, then the values move exactly as in the horizontal case, including RTL mirroring of left and right arrows. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "$Name moves the slider in the correct direction orientation vertical")
- Given `step={20}` with value 40, when arrows or Page keys are pressed, then each press moves a full step of 20 in the direction appropriate to the locale. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "$Name respects the step size")
- Given minValue 0, maxValue 230, step 10, when arrows move by 10, then PageUp and PageDown move by 20, because the computed page size 230/10 = 23 is snapped down to the nearest multiple of the step. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "$Name sets page size to a multiple of step")
- Given minValue 50, maxValue 75, step 2, when Page keys are pressed, then the page size is 2 because 25/10 = 2.5 snaps to 2, meaning page movement never falls below one step. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "$Name sets page size to a multiple of step (scenario: step is less than min)")
- Given minValue -50, maxValue -15, step 2, when Page keys are pressed, then the page size is 4 because 35/10 = 3.5 snaps to 4. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "$Name sets page size to a multiple of step (scenario: step is greater than max)")
- Given minValue -1, maxValue 1, value 0, when the decreasing arrow is pressed twice, then the value stops at -1 and the second press changes nothing, in both LTR and RTL with the appropriate key. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "$Name is clamped by min/max")
- Given a RangeSlider at start 20 end 50 in de-DE, when arrows are pressed on each thumb, then each thumb moves +1 or -1 independently; in ar-AE the horizontal direction is mirrored; when disabled neither thumb moves. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "$Name moves the slider in the correct direction")
- Given a RangeSlider with `step={10}`, when arrows are pressed on either thumb, then each press moves 10 in the locale-appropriate direction. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "$Name respects the step size")
- Given a RangeSlider with minValue -5, maxValue 5, start -4, end 4, when the start thumb is driven toward the minimum and the end thumb toward the maximum, then each stops at its limit and further presses do nothing, mirrored appropriately in RTL. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "$Name is clamped by min/max")
- Given a RAC Slider at 20 with the default page size of 10, when PageUp is held for three keydown events, then the value reaches 50, and holding PageDown for three returns it to 20, so repeat keydowns each apply. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support repeat keydown events when holding Page Up/Page Down")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given a two-thumb slider at [10, 80] on a 100px track, when the track is clicked at x 20, then the nearest thumb moves there and both onChange and onChangeEnd fire with [20, 80]; clicking at 90 moves the other thumb. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSlider.test.js: "should allow you to set value of closest thumb by clicking on track")
- Given the same slider, when the track is pressed and dragged with mouse events, then onChange fires on every move while onChangeEnd fires only on mouseUp with the final value. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSlider.test.js: "should allow you to set value of closest thumb by dragging on track")
- Given a disabled slider, when the track is pressed, dragged, and released, then neither onChange nor onChangeEnd fires and the values stay put. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSlider.test.js: "should not allow you to set value if disabled")
- Given `orientation="vertical"` on a 100px tall track, when the track is dragged with decreasing clientY, then the value increases (y is inverted) and onChangeEnd fires on release. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSlider.test.js: "should allow you to set value of closest thumb by dragging on track (vertical)")
- Given pointer events installed, when the track is clicked at two positions, then the nearest thumb moves each time with onChange and onChangeEnd, matching the mouse-event behavior. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSlider.test.js: "should allow you to set value of closest thumb by clicking on track")
- Given pointer events installed, when the track is pressed and dragged, then onChange fires per move and onChangeEnd only on pointerUp. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSlider.test.js: "should allow you to set value of closest thumb by dragging on track")
- Given two thumbs stacked at [40, 40], when the track is pressed before them at x 20, then the first (lower index) thumb is the one that moves. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSlider.test.js: "should allow you to set value of before thumbs when thumbs stacked")
- Given two thumbs stacked at [40, 40], when the track is pressed after them at x 60, then the second thumb moves. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSlider.test.js: "should allow you to set value of after thumbs when thumbs stacked")
- Given five thumbs at [25, 25, 50, 75, 75], when the track is pressed at 70 then at 20, then the fourth thumb takes 70 and the first takes 20, so stacked groups resolve to the correct edge thumb. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSlider.test.js: "should allow you to set value of before thumbs when many thumbs and stacked")
- Given the same five thumbs, when the track is pressed at 80 then at 30, then the last thumb takes 80 and the second takes 30. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSlider.test.js: "should allow you to set value of after thumbs when many thumbs and stacked")
- Given a disabled slider with pointer events, when the track is pressed, moved, and released, then nothing changes. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSlider.test.js: "should not allow you to set value if disabled")
- Given two thumbs rendered outside the track element, when thumb 0 is dragged with pointer events, then pointerDown alone fires nothing, each pointerMove fires onChange, and pointerUp fires onChangeEnd; dragging thumb 1 down past thumb 0 clamps it at thumb 0's value (40) so thumbs never cross. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSliderThumb.test.js: "can be moved by dragging")
- Given the same setup driven by mouse events, when thumb 0 is dragged and then thumb 1 is dragged past it, then the same values and clamping apply. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSliderThumb.test.js: "can be moved by dragging")
- Given a single thumb inside the track, when dragged with pointer events, then onChange fires per move, onChangeEnd fires exactly once on release. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSliderThumb.test.js: "can be moved by dragging")
- Given a single thumb inside the track, when dragged with mouse events, then the same holds. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSliderThumb.test.js: "can be moved by dragging")
- Given a vertical single-thumb slider, when the thumb is dragged upward (decreasing pageY), then the value increases and onChangeEnd fires once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/slider/useSliderThumb.test.js: "can be moved by dragging (vertical)")
- Given a Spectrum Slider at 50 on a 100px track, when the thumb is pressed then dragged, then pressing focuses the input without firing onChange, each move fires onChange with the clamped value (10, then 0 for a negative page X, then 100 past the end), and mouseUp fires nothing more. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "can click and drag handle")
- Given a disabled Spectrum Slider, when the thumb is pressed and dragged, then the input never receives focus and onChange never fires. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "cannot click and drag handle when disabled")
- Given a Spectrum Slider, when the left or right portion of the track is pressed, then the input gains focus and onChange fires once with the position value. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "can click on track to move handle")
- Given a disabled Spectrum Slider, when either track half is pressed, then no focus and no onChange. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "cannot click on track to move handle when disabled")
- Given a Spectrum Slider with a label, when the label is clicked, then the thumb input receives focus. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "clicking on the label should focus the first thumb")
- Given a Spectrum Slider being dragged by touch identifier 1, when a second touch starts, moves, and ends on the track, then onChange is not called for the second touch, and continuing to move the original touch still updates the value: a slider tracks only its first touch point. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "doesn't jump to second touch on track while already dragging")
- Given a RangeSlider at [20, 50], when the start thumb is dragged, then it focuses on press, updates per move, clamps at 0 below the minimum, and clamps at the other thumb's value (50) when dragged past it; the end thumb behaves symmetrically, clamping at 50 below and 100 above. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "can click and drag handle")
- Given a disabled RangeSlider, when either thumb is dragged, then no focus and no onChange. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "cannot click and drag handle when disabled")
- Given a RangeSlider at [40, 70], when the left track, the middle track near the left thumb, the middle track near the right thumb, or the right track is pressed, then the nearest thumb takes that value and gains focus, one onChange per press. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "can click on track to move nearest handle")
- Given a disabled RangeSlider, when any track region is pressed, then no focus and no onChange. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "cannot click on track to move nearest handle when disabled")
- Given a RangeSlider with a label, when the label is clicked, then the first thumb is focused. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "clicking on the label should focus the first thumb")
- Given a RAC SliderThumb with an isDragging className, when the mouse goes down on it and then up, then `data-dragging="true"` and the dragging class appear and clear. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support dragging state")
- Given hover callbacks on both the RAC thumb and track, when each is hovered and unhovered, then `data-hovered` toggles on the right element and the hover callbacks fire in order for the thumb then the track. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support hover state")
- Given a RAC Slider with onChange, when the track is clicked at x 20 with the left mouse button, then onChange fires. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support clicking on the track to move the thumb")

### Focus management

- Given a disabled Spectrum Slider between two buttons, when Tab is pressed twice, then focus skips the slider entirely and goes from the first to the second button. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "supports disabled")
- Given an enabled Spectrum Slider between two buttons, when the slider is focused and Tab or Shift+Tab pressed, then focus moves out to the following button and back to the preceding one. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "can be focused")
- Given a disabled RangeSlider between buttons, when Tab is pressed, then both slider inputs are disabled and focus goes button to button. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "supports disabled")
- Given an enabled RangeSlider between buttons, when Tab is pressed repeatedly, then focus goes button A, start thumb, end thumb, button B, and Shift+Tab walks back the same way: both thumbs are separate tab stops. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "can be focused")
- Given a RAC SliderThumb with an isFocusVisible className, when tabbed to, then the input is focused and the thumb gets `data-focus-visible="true"` plus the focus class, cleared when focus leaves. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support focus ring")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given `useSliderState` with defaultValue [50], min 10, max 200, step 10 and a USD currency formatter, when values are read, then getThumbValue is 50, getThumbPercent and getValuePercent are 40/190, and getThumbValueLabel is "$50.00"; setting 500 clamps to 200, setting 0 or 7 clamps to 10, and setThumbPercent(0.13) snaps to 30. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/slider/useSliderState.test.js: "should allow setting and reading values, percentages, and labels")
- Given three thumbs at [50, 70, 90] within 10-200, when the per-thumb bounds are read, then each thumb's min and max are its neighbors' values (or the slider bounds at the ends), and moving thumb 1 to 100 clamps it to 90 while updating thumb 2's minimum. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/slider/useSliderState.test.js: "should enforce maxValue and minValue for multiple thumbs")
- Given min 1, max 15, step 2.5 with defaultValue [1, 13], when the state initializes, then values snap to [1, 13.5], and later setThumbValue calls snap to the step grid while respecting neighbor bounds. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/slider/useSliderState.test.js: "should round values to nearest step with two thumbs")
- Given the same step grid with three thumbs [1, 6, 13], when values are set, then each snaps to the nearest step and the neighbor min and max values update accordingly, including collapsing two thumbs to the same value. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/slider/useSliderState.test.js: "should round values to nearest step with three thumbs")
- Given onChange and onChangeEnd, when a thumb is marked dragging, moved several times, and then marked not dragging, then onChange fires on every value change while onChangeEnd fires only when dragging ends, and `isThumbDragging` reports the drag state. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/slider/useSliderState.test.js: "should call onChange and onChangeEnd appropriately")
- Given a thumb already at 0, when setThumbValue(0, 0) is called, then neither onChange nor onChangeEnd fires. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/slider/useSliderState.test.js: "should not call onChange and onChangeEnd if not being moved")
- Given `defaultValue={20}` on a Spectrum Slider, when the native input value changes to 40, then the input value, aria-valuetext, and the status output all update. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "supports defaultValue")
- Given value or defaultValue outside the allowed range, with or without a step, when rendered, then the input value, aria-valuetext, and output text are all the clamped and step-snapped value (for example defaultValue 20 with maxValue 10 and step 3 renders 9). Run as `it.each` over eight combinations. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "clamps value & defaultValue to the allowed range $Name")
- Given a controlled Spectrum Slider, when the input changes to 55, then the value, aria-valuetext, and output update and onChange received exactly [55]. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "can be controlled")
- Given a custom `getValueLabel`, when the value changes, then the output text uses the custom format while aria-valuetext stays the plain formatted number (the file notes this as an open question). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "supports a custom getValueLabel")
- Given a RangeSlider with defaultValue {start: 20, end: 40}, when each input changes, then both the values and the combined output text update. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "supports defaultValue")
- Given a controlled RangeSlider, when each thumb changes, then onChange receives the full `{start, end}` object each time and the output plus aria-valuetext follow. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "can be controlled")
- Given a custom `getValueLabel` on a RangeSlider, when either thumb changes, then the output uses the custom string while each thumb's aria-valuetext stays its own formatted number. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "supports a custom valueLabel")
- Given a RAC Slider whose children are a render function of `{orientation}`, when rendered vertical, then the wrapper gets the orientation-derived class. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support render props")
- Given `render` props on Slider, thumb, track, and output, when rendered, then each uses the custom element with `data-custom`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support custom render function")
- Given a controlled two-thumb RAC Slider with an external reset button, when reset sets [0, 100] and then arrows move a thumb, then the controlled values update, and a second reset restores [0, 100] so the parent stays authoritative. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support multiple thumbs (controlled)")
- Given an `inputRef` on a RAC SliderThumb, when rendered, then the ref points at the thumb's hidden input element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support input ref")

### Forms (name, value, validation, form reset, hidden inputs, autofill)

- Given `name="cookies"` and `form="test"` on a Spectrum Slider with value 10, when rendered, then the range input carries the name, the form attribute, and the value. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "supports form name")
- Given a controlled Slider inside a form with a reset input, when the value is changed and reset is clicked, then the value returns to the original 10. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "supports form reset")
- Given a React 19 form action returning 50 with the Slider's defaultValue bound to that state, when the form is submitted, then the input value becomes 50. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/Slider.test.tsx: "resets to defaultValue when submitting form action")
- Given `startName` and `endName` plus `form` on a RangeSlider, when rendered, then each input carries its own name, the shared form attribute, and its value. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "supports form name")
- Given a controlled RangeSlider in a form, when both thumbs are changed and reset is clicked, then both return to their original values. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "supports form reset")
- Given a React 19 form action returning `{start: 0, end: 100}`, when submitted, then both inputs take the new default values. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/slider/RangeSlider.test.tsx: "resets to defaultValue when submitting form action")
- Given `form="test"` on a RAC SliderThumb, when rendered, then the input has the form attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support form prop")

### Positioning

(react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support horizontal SliderFill")
- Given a horizontal SliderFill with `offset={50}`, when the value is 30 then 80, then the fill spans from the value to the offset (start 30% width 20%) and then from the offset to the value (start 50% width 30%). - Given a vertical SliderFill with `offset={50}`, when the value is 30 then 80, then the fill spans bottom 30% height 20% and then bottom 50% height 30%. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Slider.test.js: "should support vertical SliderFill with offset")

### RTL and i18n (locale-aware parsing, number formats, RTL arrow keys)

## number-field

### Roles and attributes

- Given a Spectrum NumberField, when rendered, then the wrapper has `role="group"`, the input is `type="text"` with `inputMode="numeric"`, and both stepper buttons exist with `tabIndex="-1"` so they are not tab stops. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name has correct aria and props")
- Given `useNumberField({})` with no props, when the hook runs, then inputProps.type is "text", disabled and readOnly are falsy, aria-invalid and aria-required are undefined, all four aria-value* props are null (the input is deliberately not a spinbutton for screen readers), and a console warning fires about the missing label. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/numberfield/useNumberField.test.ts: "with default numberField props if no props are provided")
- Given a `placeholder`, when the hook runs, then it passes through to inputProps. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/numberfield/useNumberField.test.ts: "with appropriate props if placeholder is defined")
- Given a NumberField with readOnly, disabled, required, an id, min, max, and a currency format, when rendered, then the input has aria-readonly, aria-required, and aria-disabled true, carries the given id, has no `role`, and does NOT expose aria-valuenow, aria-valuetext, aria-valuemin, or aria-valuemax; each stepper button has `aria-controls` pointing at the input id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name has proper aria attributes")
- Given `hideStepper`, when rendered, then neither stepper button renders. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name can hide step buttons")
- Given `scale="large"` (the mobile scale), when rendered, then both stepper buttons still render. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name step buttons show for mobile")
- Given `isQuiet` at the large scale, when rendered, then both stepper buttons still render. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name step buttons show for mobile quiet")
- Given `validationState="invalid"`, when rendered, then the group wrapper has `aria-invalid="true"`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name can be invalid")
- Given a `label`, when rendered, then the input is reachable by that label text and carries `aria-roledescription="Number field"`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name supports labels")
- Given `data-testid` on the NumberField, when rendered, then the attribute lands on the input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "adds data attributes to textField")
- Given a RAC NumberField with Label, Group, decrement and increment Buttons, Input, and description plus errorMessage Text slots, when rendered, then the group has class `react-aria-Group`, the wrapper carries data props, the input shows the grouped value "1,024", aria-labelledby points at the Label, aria-describedby resolves to "Description Error", and the two buttons get `aria-label` "Decrease" and "Increase" automatically. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/NumberField.test.js: "provides slots")
- Given a NumberFieldContext "test" slot, when `slot="test"` is used, then the wrapper has the slot attribute and the input gets the slot aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/NumberField.test.js: "should support slot")
- Given `isReadOnly` toggled on a RAC NumberField, when rerendered, then the wrapper gains `data-readonly`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/NumberField.test.js: "should support read-only state")
- Given `data-testid` on a RAC NumberField, when rendered, then exactly one element has it and it is the outer `react-aria-NumberField` wrapper. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/NumberField.test.js: "should render data- attributes only on the outer element")
- Given `useSpinButton({value: 2, textValue: '2 items', minValue: 1, maxValue: 3})`, when rendered, then the element has `role="spinbutton"`, aria-valuenow 2, aria-valuemin 1, aria-valuemax 3, aria-valuetext "2 items", and no aria-disabled or aria-readonly. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/spinbutton/useSpinButton.test.js: "should have role=\"spinbutton\" and aria props")
- Given `isDisabled` on useSpinButton, when rendered, then the element has `aria-disabled="true"`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/spinbutton/useSpinButton.test.js: "should have aria-disabled if isDisabled is set")
- Given `isReadOnly` on useSpinButton, when rendered, then the element has `aria-readonly="true"`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/spinbutton/useSpinButton.test.js: "should have aria-readonly if isReadOnly is set")
- Given a negative value with a textValue of "-2 items", when rendered, then aria-valuenow keeps the ASCII hyphen while aria-valuetext substitutes the Unicode minus sign "−2 items", and announcements use the minus sign too (screen readers read the hyphen as a dash otherwise). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/spinbutton/useSpinButton.test.js: "should substitute a minus sign for hyphen in the textValue for negative values")
- Given `isReadOnly` with a value, when rendered, then both stepper buttons have `aria-disabled` but are not natively `disabled`, so they stay discoverable. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name isReadOnly cannot be stepped")

### Keyboard

- Given a NumberField at 10 with a currency format, when ArrowUp then two ArrowDowns are pressed, then the value steps to 11 then 9 in the locale's format, blurring keeps the formatted value, and the user's onKeyDown and onKeyUp handlers fire once per key (3 each). Parameterized over en-US, fr-FR, and ar-AE Euros. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name pressing up arrow & down arrow keeps focus state formatting")
- Given a percent-formatted NumberField with "5.2" typed, when Enter is pressed, then the value commits and displays as "52%" and onChange receives 0.52, so Enter commits like blur. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name sets number value on enter")
- Given a NumberField at 10 with maxValue 521, when End is pressed, then the value jumps to 521 and onChange fires once. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "goes to valid max on `end`")
- Given step 10 and maxValue 521, when End is pressed, then the value goes to 520, the largest value on the step grid. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "goes to valid step max on `end`")
- Given minValue -521, when Home is pressed, then the value jumps to -521. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "goes to valid min on `home`")
- Given step 10 and minValue -521 with a defaultValue that snaps to 9, when Home is pressed, then the value goes to -521. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "goes to valid step min on `home`")
- Given an empty NumberField with various min and max combinations, when ArrowUp or ArrowDown is pressed, then the first step lands on a documented starting point per combination (unbounded starts at 0 both ways; min -5 gives -5 up and 0 down; min 5 gives 5 both ways; max 5 gives 0 up and 5 down; max -5 gives -5 both ways; -5..5 gives -5 up and 5 down; -15..-5 gives -15 up and -5 down; 5..15 gives 5 up and 15 down), and onBlur, onKeyUp, and onKeyDown each fire once. Run as `it.each` over 16 rows. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$direction $Name starts from the right place")
- Given the same combinations with `step: 3`, when an arrow key is pressed from empty, then the first value is snapped onto the step grid within the bounds (for example min -5 down gives 1, max 5 down gives 3, max -5 up gives -6, 5..15 down gives 14). Run as `it.each` over 16 rows. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$direction $Name step 3 starts from the right place")
- Given useSpinButton with onIncrement, when ArrowUp is pressed on the focused element, then onIncrement fires once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/spinbutton/useSpinButton.test.js: "should trigger onIncrement on arrow up")
- Given onDecrement, when ArrowDown is pressed, then onDecrement fires once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/spinbutton/useSpinButton.test.js: "should trigger onDecrement on arrow down")
- Given onIncrementPage, when PageUp is pressed, then onIncrementPage fires once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/spinbutton/useSpinButton.test.js: "should trigger onIncrementPage on page up")
- Given only onIncrement and no onIncrementPage, when PageUp is pressed, then onIncrement is called instead. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/spinbutton/useSpinButton.test.js: "should fall back to onIncrement on page up if onIncrementPage is not available")
- Given onDecrementPage, when PageDown is pressed, then onDecrementPage fires once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/spinbutton/useSpinButton.test.js: "should trigger onDecrementPage on page up")
- Given only onDecrement, when PageDown is pressed, then onDecrement is called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/spinbutton/useSpinButton.test.js: "should fall back to onDecrement on page up if onDecrementPage is not available")
- Given onDecrementToMin and a minValue, when Home is pressed, then onDecrementToMin fires once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/spinbutton/useSpinButton.test.js: "should trigger onDecrementToMin on home key")
- Given onIncrementToMax and a maxValue, when End is pressed, then onIncrementToMax fires once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/spinbutton/useSpinButton.test.js: "should trigger onIncrementToMax on end key")
- Given a RAC NumberField at 1024, when ArrowUp is held for three keydown events, then the value reaches 1,027 and holding ArrowDown three times returns it to 1,024, so repeats apply one step each. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/NumberField.test.js: "should support repeat keydown events when holding an arrow key")
- Given a RAC NumberField at 1024 with grouping on, when the caret is moved to just after the leading "1" and Backspace is pressed, then the input shows ",024" while editing and commits to 24 on Enter, so a leading digit next to a group separator can be deleted. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/NumberField.test.js: "should allow you to delete the first digit in a number if it is followed by a group separator")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given defaultValue 0, when the increment button is clicked, then onChange receives 1. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name increment value by one when increment button is pressed")
- Given defaultValue 0, when the decrement button is clicked, then onChange receives -1. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name decrement value by one when increment button is pressed")
- Given defaultValue 0 with step 10, when decrement then increment are clicked, then onChange receives -10 then 0. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name use step for increasing and decreasing value")
- Given a focused NumberField at 0, when a wheel event with `deltaY: -10` fires, then onChange receives -1 and onBlur is not triggered by the wheel. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name decrement value when scrolling downwards or left in LTR")
- Given an unfocused NumberField, when a wheel event fires, then onChange is never called, so scrolling the page cannot change the value. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name cannot scroll to step when not focused")
- Given a focused NumberField, when a wheel event with positive deltaY fires, then the value increments. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name increment value when scrolling upwards")
- Given an ar-AE locale, when a wheel event with negative deltaY fires on the focused field, then the value still decrements. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name decrement value when scrolling down")
- Given a focused NumberField, when a wheel event carries `ctrlKey: true` (a pinch-zoom gesture in browsers), then onChange is never called in either direction. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name should not fire increment or decrement if it is a zoom event")
- Given a controlled value equal to minValue, when decrement is clicked, then onChange is never called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name onChange is not called when controlled at minValue and decrement is pressed")
- Given a controlled value equal to maxValue, when increment is clicked, then onChange is never called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name onChange is not called when controlled at maxValue and increment is pressed")
- Given a NumberField at 10, when the increment button is held down, then the first step fires immediately, nothing more happens until 400ms have passed, and after that a step fires every 60ms (11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16); releasing stops it, and holding the decrement button steps back down the same way. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "advances automatically if the arrows are held down")
- Given minValue 0, maxValue 20 and value 10, when a stepper is held down past the limit, then auto-stepping stops at the boundary and fires no further onChange calls. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "advances automatically to the limit and not beyond")
- Given an empty NumberField, when the increment button is held, then the first value is 0 and auto-repeat continues from there (reaching 2 after two repeats). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "advances increment starting from undefined")
- Given an empty NumberField with minValue 20, when the increment button is held, then the first value is 20 and repeats continue to 22. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "advances increment starting from undefined where min is defined")
- Given an empty NumberField, when the decrement button is held, then the values go 0, -1, -2. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "advances decrement starting from undefined")
- Given step 0.001 and an uncommitted "1" typed, when increment is clicked repeatedly, then onChange receives 1.001, 1.002, 1.003, 1.004 without floating point drift. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name handles input change with custom decimal step number")
- Given step 5 and an uncommitted typed "2", when the increment button is clicked, then the uncommitted text is committed and snapped first so onChange receives 5; clearing the field fires onChange with NaN, and typing "3" then incrementing again gives 5. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name will start with uncommitted value when stepper buttons are pressed")
- Given an uncommitted typed "2", when increment is clicked, then the displayed value becomes 3 and onChange fires with 3; repeating the same edit produces the same displayed 3 without a second onChange, because the resulting number did not change. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name adjust the text field value if the resulting number is the same - inc")
- Given the same setup with the decrement button, when repeated, then the display becomes 1 and onChange only fires when the number actually changes. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name adjust the text field value if the resulting number is the same - dec")
- Given a RAC NumberField, when the increment or decrement stepper is activated by a programmatic `element.click()` with no pointer events (the screen reader and automation path), then onChange still fires with 1025 then 1024. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/NumberField.test.js: "should trigger onChange via programmatic click() on stepper buttons")
- Given a controlled RAC NumberField whose decrement button becomes disabled once the value hits 4, when the decrement button is pressed and timers run out, then the button is disabled and the value stays 4: auto-spinning stops when its button disables. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/NumberField.test.js: "stops spinning if the associated button is disabled")
- Given a RAC NumberField group with hover callbacks, when the group is hovered and unhovered, then `data-hovered` and the hover class toggle on the group. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/NumberField.test.js: "should support hover state")

### Focus management

- Given a ref on a Spectrum NumberField without a label, when `ref.current.focus()` is called, then the ref's DOM node is the group's parent and focus lands on the input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "attaches a user provided ref to the outer div")
- Given a ref on a labelled NumberField, when focus() is called, then the ref points at the labelled root wrapper and focus still goes to the input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "attaches a user provided ref to the outer div with a label")
- Given onChange and onBlur, when a value is typed and Tab leaves the field, then onChange is invoked before onBlur. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name fires state change then blur")
- Given clicking the increment or decrement button, when it fires, then onBlur is not triggered, so stepping does not look like leaving the field. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name starting from empty field, will start at the 0 if neither min or max are defined")
- Given a RAC NumberField with an isFocusVisible group className, when Tab focuses the input, then the group gets `data-focus-visible="true"` and the class, cleared when focus leaves. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/NumberField.test.js: "should support focus visible state")
- Given defaultValue 100, when the field is focused, then the existing text should be selected so the first keystroke replaces it; the repo leaves this off because jsdom does not implement text selection. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name selects input text on focus") (skipped in repo)

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given onChange and a typed "5", when the field is blurred, then onChange receives the number 5 (commit happens on blur, not per keystroke). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name handles input change")
- Given an empty field, when only a minus sign is typed and the field is blurred, then onChange is never called and the input is left empty. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name handles just typing a minus sign from empty")
- Given an empty field, when ".5" is typed and blurred, then onChange receives 0.5. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name handles starting a number with a decimal input change")
- Given an empty field, when "1acd" is typed, then only "1" appears, onChange has not fired yet, and blurring fires onChange once with 1. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "cannot type random letter after a number")
- Given step 5, when "2" is typed and blurred, then onChange receives 0 (snapped down), and a later increment click gives 5; typing "3" and blurring does not fire onChange because the snapped value is unchanged, while the next increment gives 10. onBlur fires once per blur. - Given value or defaultValue outside the range, with or without a step, when rendered, then the displayed value is clamped and snapped (defaultValue 20 with maxValue 10 and step 3 renders "9"). - Given minValue 0, when a minus sign then "1" are typed, then the minus is rejected outright, the field stays valid (no aria-invalid on the group), and blurring commits 1. - Given minValue 10 with `commitBehavior="validate"`, when "5" is typed and the field blurred, then the text stays "5", onChange fires with 5, and the group gains `aria-invalid="true"` instead of the value being clamped. - Given minValue 20 and maxValue 50, when "32" is typed and blurred, then it is kept as is and onChange fires once with 32. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name will allow typing of a number between min and max")
- Given maxValue 1 and defaultValue 0, when "2" is typed and blurred, then the value clamps to 1, onChange fires with 1, and the group stays valid; typing the same "1" again fires no onChange. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name will not allow typing of a number greater than the max")
- Given maxValue 1 with `commitBehavior="validate"`, when "2" is typed and blurred, then the value stays 2 with `aria-invalid="true"`, and appending another 2 commits 22 while still invalid. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name will allow typing of a number greater than the max when value snapping is disabled")
- Given minValue 0.1, maxValue 24, step 0.1, when "24" is typed and the field blurred, then the displayed value is exactly "24" with no floating point drift. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "does not lose precision")
- Given an empty field with no min or max, when increment is clicked, then the value becomes 0 and onChange fires with 0; clearing the field fires onChange with NaN; clicking decrement then returns to 0. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name starting from empty field, will start at the 0 if neither min or max are defined")
- Given an empty field with minValue 3, when increment is clicked, then the value starts at 3; clearing fires NaN; decrement from empty also gives 3. ### Forms (name, value, validation, form reset, hidden inputs, autofill)

- Given `name="age"`, `form="test"` and value 30 on a Spectrum NumberField, when rendered, then the visible input has no `name`, a hidden input carries the name, the form attribute, and the value "30", and setting the value to null empties the hidden input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "supports form value")
- Given a controlled NumberField inside a form with a reset input, when the value is edited and reset clicked, then the value returns to 10. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "supports form reset")
- Given a React 19 form action returning 33 and the field's defaultValue bound to that state, when the form submits, then the input shows 33. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "resets to defaultValue when submitting form action")
- Given `isRequired` with `validationBehavior="native"`, when the form's checkValidity runs, then the input has `required` and not aria-required, becomes invalid, gains aria-describedby with "Constraints not satisfied", and is focused; typing a digit makes it valid and blurring clears the message. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "supports isRequired")
- Given a required native-validation NumberField showing an error, when the increment button is pressed, then the error clears and validity becomes true, so stepping commits a validation change. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "commits validation changes when pressing increment/decrement buttons")
- Given a `validate` function requiring 4 with step 2 and defaultValue 2 under native validation, when checkValidity runs, then the error "Invalid value" is described and focused; typing 3 keeps it invalid until blur snaps the value to 4, at which point it becomes valid and the message clears. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "supports validate function")
- Given a Form whose onSubmit sets `validationErrors`, when submit is pressed, then the field is described by "Invalid value." and invalid; Shift+Tab back, typing a new value, and tabbing away clears it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "supports server validation")
- Given an `errorMessage` render function reading `e.validationDetails.valueMissing`, when checkValidity runs, then the described text is the custom "Please enter a value". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "supports customizing native error messages")
- Given a required native-validation field, when it is focused and blurred without editing, then no validation message appears; only checkValidity surfaces one, and later edits behave normally. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "only commits on blur if the value changed")
- Given a `validate` function under aria validation with defaultValue 2, when rendered, then the field already has aria-invalid and an aria-describedby error while `input.validity.valid` stays true, and typing a valid value clears both. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "supports validate function")
- Given a Form with `validationErrors={{value: 'Invalid value'}}` under aria validation, when rendered, then the named field is aria-invalid and described by the error; editing and blurring clears it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "supports server validation")
- Given `name`, `form`, and value 25 with a currency format on a RAC NumberField, when rendered, then a hidden input named "test" holds the raw "25" with the form attribute, and setting the value to null empties it. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/NumberField.test.js: "should support form value")
- Given `isDisabled` with a form value, when rendered, then the hidden form input is also disabled so it is excluded from submission. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/NumberField.test.js: "should support disabled when having a form value")
- Given a RAC NumberField with `isRequired` and a FieldError in a form, when checkValidity runs, then the wrapper gains `data-invalid`, the input is described by "Constraints not satisfied" and focused, and typing then blurring clears both. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/NumberField.test.js: "supports validation errors")
- Given a RAC Form with a server `validationErrors` entry and defaultValue 5, when the input is focused and blurred without editing, then the invalid state and the error message survive the blur. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/NumberField.test.js: "should not reset validation errors on blur when value has not changed")
- Given a required RAC NumberField with min 10, max 50, step 10 and `commitBehavior="validate"`, when out-of-range or off-step values are typed and committed by blur, then the typed text is preserved verbatim, `data-invalid` and aria-invalid are set, `input.validity.valid` is false with the native message described, the announcement reads the typed value, and checkValidity moves focus back; typing a valid on-step value clears everything, and an empty value is also invalid. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/NumberField.test.js: "should not change the edited input value when value snapping is disabled")

### RTL and i18n (locale-aware parsing, number formats, RTL arrow keys)

- Given a NumberField on iPhone Safari, when rendered with no props, then `inputMode` is "text"; with maximumFractionDigits 0 still "text"; with minValue 0 it becomes "decimal"; and with both it becomes "numeric". On iPad and Mac Safari every combination is "numeric". On Android Chrome, plain and fraction-limited are "numeric", minValue 0 alone is "decimal", and both together are "numeric". This pins the iOS keyboard quirk that the numeric pad lacks a minus sign. Run as `it.each` over 16 platform and UA rows. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name uses inputMode=$inputMode on $platform $UA with $props")

- Given a JPY currency format with minValue 0, when "5.2" is typed and blurred, then inputMode is "numeric", the decimal is dropped, and the value displays as "¥52" with onChange 52. - Given a percent format, when "5.2" is typed and blurred, then inputMode is "numeric", the display becomes "52%", and onChange receives 0.52 (percent values are divided by 100). - Given an EUR format, when a lone minus is typed then deleted, then onChange is never called with NaN. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name will not call onChange with NaN before a valid input has been typed")

- Given a percent format pinned to two fraction digits, when "2.11" is typed and blurred, then the display is "2.11%" and onChange receives 0.0211. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "$Name properly formats percent for 2.11")
- Given `style: 'unit', unit: 'percent', signDisplay: 'always'` and value 10 shown as "+10%", when a digit is replaced inside the text, then editing works around the sign and unit and onChange receives 15 (unit percent is not divided by 100). - Given a JSX element as the label, when rendered, then the stepper buttons fall back to plain "Increase" and "Decrease" plus an aria-labelledby of "<ownId> <labelId>", because the label text cannot be interpolated. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "JSX label")
- Given `aria-labelledby="label-id"`, when rendered, then the steppers use "Increase"/"Decrease" with aria-labelledby "<ownId> label-id". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "aria-labelledby")
- Given `incrementAriaLabel: 'Increment'`, when rendered, then the increment button uses the custom label while the decrement button keeps "Decrease Width". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "custom incrementAriaLabel")
- Given `decrementAriaLabel: 'Decrement'`, when rendered, then only the decrement button's label changes. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "custom decrementAriaLabel")
- Given an errorMessage with `validationState="invalid"`, when rendered, then aria-describedby points at the error text element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "error message")
- Given a description, when rendered, then aria-describedby points at the description element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "description")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given copy, cut, paste, composition, select, beforeinput, and input handlers passed to useNumberField, when each corresponding inputProps handler is invoked, then the user callback fires: all events are merged onto the input rather than swallowed. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/numberfield/useNumberField.test.ts: "all events are merged into the input element")
- Given a USD currency field with `currencyDisplay: 'code'` showing "USD 12.00", when the whole "USD" prefix is selected and a delete-style beforeinput fires (deleteHardLineBackward, deleteSoftLineBackward, deleteContentBackward, deleteContentForward, deleteContent, deleteByCut, or deleteByDrag), then the event is allowed through. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "allows %s of whole currency symbol")
- Given the same field with only part of the currency code selected, when any of those delete input types fires, then the beforeinput event is canceled so a partial symbol cannot be broken. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "prevents %s of partial currency symbol")
- Given a collapsed caret inside the currency code, when deleteContentBackward or deleteContentForward fires, then the event is canceled. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "prevents %s inside currency symbol")
- Given a caret inside the numeric part, when insertText, insertFromPaste, insertFromDrop, insertFromYank, or insertReplacementText fires with a digit, then the event is allowed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "allows %s of number inside number")
- Given the whole number portion selected, when any insert input type fires with a digit, then the replacement is allowed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "allows %s replacing whole number")
- Given a caret inside the currency code, when any insert input type fires with a digit, then the event is canceled. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "prevents %s of number inside currency symbol")
- Given a formatted currency value, when a historyUndo or historyRedo beforeinput fires, then it is allowed through so browser undo keeps working. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "allows %s")
- Given a unit percent format with `signDisplay: 'always'` showing "+12%", when deleteContentForward fires with the caret before the plus sign, then the event is allowed so the sign can be removed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "allows %s of starting plusSign")
- Given "123" in the field, when an IME composition inserts "ü" in the middle (compositionStart, an uncancelable insertCompositionText beforeinput, an input event, then compositionEnd), then the composition is undone on compositionEnd: the value returns to "123" and the caret is restored to position 1. This pins IME input handling. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/numberfield/NumberField.test.js: "handles compositionend events and undoes them if invalid")

## text-field

### Roles and attributes
