- Given `useTextField({})` with no props, when the hook runs, then inputProps.type is "text", disabled and readOnly are falsy, aria-invalid and aria-required are undefined, autoFocus is falsy, an onChange function is returned, and a console warning fires about needing a visible label or aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/textfield/useTextField.test.js: "with default textfield props if no props are provided")
- Given `type: 'search'`, when the hook runs, then inputProps.type is "search". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/textfield/useTextField.test.js: "with appropriate props if type is defined")
- Given `isDisabled: true` then false, when the hook runs, then inputProps.disabled follows it. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/textfield/useTextField.test.js: "with appropriate props if isDisabled is defined")
- Given `isRequired: true` then false, when the hook runs, then aria-required is truthy then undefined (no `required` attribute in the default aria behavior). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/textfield/useTextField.test.js: "with appropriate props if isRequired is defined")
- Given `isReadOnly: true` then false, when the hook runs, then inputProps.readOnly follows it. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/textfield/useTextField.test.js: "with appropriate props if isReadOnly is defined")
- Given `validationState: 'invalid'` then 'valid', when the hook runs, then aria-invalid is truthy then undefined. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/textfield/useTextField.test.js: "with appropriate props if validationState is defined")
- Given `autoCapitalize: 'on'` then 'off', when the hook runs, then inputProps.autoCapitalize passes through unchanged (matters for mobile keyboards). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/textfield/useTextField.test.js: "with appropriate props if autoCapitalize is defined")
- Given `inputElementType: 'textarea'` with a type and pattern also passed, when the hook runs, then both type and pattern are dropped because a textarea supports neither. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/textfield/useTextField.test.js: "without type prop if inputElementType is textarea")
- Given TextField, TextArea, and SearchField, when each renders and receives typed text, then the value updates, TextField gets `type="text"`, SearchField gets `type="search"`, TextArea has no type attribute, and the tag is INPUT, INPUT, and TEXTAREA respectively. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name renders with default textfield behavior")
- Given a `name` prop on TextField, TextArea, or SearchField, when rendered, then the input has that name attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name allow custom naming")
- Given `validationState="invalid"` on TextField or TextArea, when rendered, then the input has `aria-invalid="true"` and a hidden `img` role invalid icon renders. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name has the proper aria-invalid value and renders a invalid icon if validationState=invalid")
- Given `validationState="valid"`, when rendered, then aria-invalid is absent and a hidden valid icon renders. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name has the proper aria-invalid value and renders a valid icon if validationState=valid")
- Given `validationState="invalid"` plus `aria-errormessage="error"`, when rendered, then the input keeps `aria-invalid="true"` and the aria-errormessage passes through. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name passes through aria-errormessage")
- Given `isRequired`, when rendered, then the input has `aria-required`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name supports a isRequired prop")
- Given `isReadOnly`, when rendered and clicked, then the input has the `readonly` attribute and still takes focus. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name should support isReadOnly")
- Given `isDisabled`, when rendered and clicked, then the input has `disabled` and does not become the active element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name should disable the input field if isDisabled=true")
- Given aria-activedescendant, aria-autocomplete, and aria-haspopup passed to the field, when rendered, then all three land on the input so combobox patterns can be built on it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name passes through ARIA props")
- Given `excludeFromTabOrder`, when rendered, then the input has `tabIndex="-1"`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name supports excludeFromTabOrder")
- Given a custom `icon` element on TextField or TextArea, when rendered, then the icon has `role="img"`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name allow the user to render a custom icon")
- Given `UNSAFE_className="custom-class-name"` on SearchField, when rendered, then the class lands on the root element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name supports appending custom classnames onto the root element")
- Given a RAC TextField wrapping Input or TextArea with Label plus description and errorMessage Text slots, when rendered, then the input has class `react-aria-Input` or `react-aria-TextArea`, Input has `type="text"` while TextArea has no type, the wrapper carries the data props, aria-labelledby points at the `react-aria-Label` element, and aria-describedby resolves to "Description Error" in that order. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TextField.test.js: "provides slots")
- Given a TextFieldContext with a "test" slot supplying aria-label, when a TextField uses `slot="test"`, then the wrapper has the slot attribute and the input gets the aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TextField.test.js: "should support slot")
- Given `isReadOnly` toggled on a RAC TextField, when rerendered, then the wrapper gains `data-readonly`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TextField.test.js: "should support read-only state")
- Given `isRequired` toggled on a RAC TextField, when rerendered, then the wrapper gains `data-required`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TextField.test.js: "should support required state")
- Given data attributes on a RAC TextField, when rendered, then exactly one element carries the test id and it is the outer `react-aria-TextField` wrapper, not the input. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TextField.test.js: "should render data- attributes only on the outer element")
- Given `id="name"` on a RAC TextField, when rendered, then the id lands on the input and not on the wrapper. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TextField.test.js: "should render the id attribute only on the input element")
- Given an `id` set directly on the RAC Input, when rendered, then the Label's `for` attribute matches that id and the wrapper has no id. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TextField.test.js: "should link an id on the input to the label htmlFor")
- Given `form="test"` on a RAC TextField, when rendered, then the input has the form attribute so it can associate with a form elsewhere in the document. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TextField.test.js: "should support form prop")

### Keyboard

- Given a TextField, TextArea, or SearchField, when the user tabs in and types, then the value reflects the typed text. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name renders with default textfield behavior")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given a RAC Input or TextArea with hover callbacks, when hovered then unhovered, then `data-hovered="true"` and the hover class toggle, onHoverStart and onHoverEnd fire once each, and onHoverChange fires twice. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TextField.test.js: "should support hover state")

### Focus management

- Given onFocus on the field, when the input is focused programmatically and later clicked, then onFocus fires once per focus (twice total). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name calls onFocus when the the input field is focused")
- Given `autoFocus` and onBlur, when the input is blurred, then onBlur fires once. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name calls onBlur when the input field loses focus")
- Given `autoFocus` and onFocus, when rendered, then the input is the active element and onFocus has fired once. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name automatically focuses the input field if autoFocus=true")
- Given a RAC Input or TextArea with an isFocusVisible className, when tabbed to, then it is focused with `data-focus-visible="true"` and the focus class, and tabbing away clears both. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TextField.test.js: "should support focus visible state")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given onChange, when the input's value changes, then onChange is called once with the new string value rather than the event. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name calls onChange when text changes")
- Given `useTextField({onChange})`, when inputProps.onChange receives an event, then the user callback gets `event.target.value`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/textfield/useTextField.test.js: "with an onChange that calls user specified onChange with appropriate values")
- Given `defaultValue`, when the user types four characters, then onChange fires once per character and the field manages its own value. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name is uncontrolled if defaultValue prop is provided")
- Given a `value` prop, when the user types, then the rendered value never changes while onChange still fires once per keystroke. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name is controlled if value prop is provided")
- Given a ref on the field, when rendered, then `ref.current.getInputElement()` returns the input DOM node. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name will attach a ref to the input field if provided as a prop")
- Given a RAC TextField with a `render` prop returning a div with `data-custom`, when rendered, then the wrapper is the custom element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TextField.test.js: "should support custom render function")

### Forms (name, value, validation, form reset, hidden inputs, autofill)

- Given a `label` and a ref, when rendered, then aria-labelledby points at a label element containing the text and the label's `for` matches the input id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name supports labeling")
- Given a controlled field with description, errorMessage, and a validationState derived from the value, when the value is valid then aria-describedby lists the description id followed by the valid icon id; when it becomes invalid, aria-describedby switches to the error id alone and the message text tracks whether the value is empty; when it becomes valid again, both the description and valid icon return. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name supports description or error message")
- Given errorMessage with no description, when valid then aria-describedby is just the valid icon id; after typing an invalid value the error message id replaces it, an empty value swaps in "Empty input not allowed.", and a valid digit restores the valid icon. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name supports error message")
- Given a controlled field inside a form with a reset input, when text is appended then reset is clicked, then the value returns to the original controlled value "Devon". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name supports form reset")
- Given a React 19 form action that returns a new value and a field whose defaultValue is that state, when the form is submitted, then the input shows the updated default value instead of keeping the typed one. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name resets to defaultValue when submitting form action")
- Given a RAC TextField with a defaultValue tied to `useActionState` (React 19 only), when the user types and submits the form action, then the input value becomes the submitted value. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TextField.test.js: "resets to defaultValue when submitting form action")
- Given `isRequired` with `validationBehavior="native"` inside a Form, when rendered, then the input has `required` and no aria-required, `input.validity.valid` is false, and no aria-describedby yet; after `form.checkValidity()` focus moves to the input and aria-describedby points at "Constraints not satisfied"; after typing the value becomes valid but the message stays until blur, when aria-describedby is removed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name supports isRequired")
- Given a `validate` function returning an error for the current value with native validation, when `form.checkValidity()` runs, then the input is invalid, focused, and described by "Invalid name"; typing a new value makes it valid and blurring clears the description. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name supports validate function")
- Given a Form with `validationErrors` populated in onSubmit and native validation, when submit is pressed, then the field shows "Invalid name." and is invalid; pressing submit again does not clear the server error and focus returns to the field; typing a new value and blurring clears the error and the field becomes valid. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name supports server validation")
- Given a React 19 form action that returns `{test: 'Error'}` as validationErrors, when the form action submits, then the field gains aria-describedby with "Error" and stays invalid, so server errors survive an action submit. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name retains server validation errors after form action submit")
- Given `isRequired` plus an `errorMessage` render function reading `e.validationDetails.valueMissing` with native validation, when checkValidity runs and the queued microtask flushes, then the described error text is the custom "Please enter a name". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name supports customizing native error messages")
- Given a Form whose `onInvalid` calls preventDefault with native validation, when checkValidity runs, then focus is not moved to the invalid input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name does not auto focus invalid input if default is prevented")
- Given a `validate` function under the default aria validation behavior, when rendered, then the input already has aria-invalid and aria-describedby with "Invalid name" while `input.validity.valid` stays true (no native constraint), and typing a valid value clears both. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name supports validate function")
- Given a Form with `validationErrors={{name: 'Invalid name'}}` under aria validation, when rendered, then the named field is aria-invalid and described by the error, and typing a new value then blurring clears both. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name supports server validation")
- Given a RAC TextField with `isRequired` and a FieldError inside a form, when the form's checkValidity runs, then the input has `required` and not aria-required, becomes described by "Constraints not satisfied", the wrapper gains `data-invalid`, and the input is focused; typing makes validity true and blurring removes the description and data-invalid. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TextField.test.js: "supports validation errors")
- Given a RAC TextField with `isRequired isInvalid` and an empty FieldError, when rendered, then the input has aria-invalid and data-invalid but no aria-describedby, so no empty error element is rendered. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TextField.test.js: "should not render the field error div if no error is provided and isInvalid is true")
- Given a FieldError child function reading `e.validationDetails.valueMissing`, when checkValidity runs, then the custom message "Please enter a name" is used and the input is focused; typing then blurring clears it. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TextField.test.js: "supports customizing validation errors")

### Positioning

- Given a quiet TextArea with a mocked scrollHeight of 500, when it mounts (default, controlled with value, or uncontrolled with defaultValue), then the inline height style is set to 500px so the auto-growing textarea has no internal scroller. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextArea.test.js: "$Name quiet variant automatically adjusts its vertical height on mount")
- Given a quiet TextArea whose scrollHeight grows to 1000, when the user types, then the inline height updates to 1000px. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextArea.test.js: "isQuiet can adjust after text \"grows\"")
- Given a default (non-quiet) TextArea whose scrollHeight grows, when the user types, then the inline height also updates to the new scrollHeight. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextArea.test.js: "default can adjust after text \"grows\"")
- Given a TextArea with an explicit `height` prop, when rendered and typed into, then the inline height style stays empty so the author's height wins over auto-grow. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextArea.test.js: "default does not change height when a height prop is set")

### SSR and hydration

- Given a Spectrum TextField with a label, when server rendered and hydrated, then no errors occur. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.ssr.test.js: "should render without errors")
- Given a Spectrum TextArea with a label, when server rendered and hydrated, then no errors occur. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextArea.ssr.test.js: "should render without errors")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given a `placeholder` prop, when rendered, then the placeholder appears on the input and a console warning tells the developer placeholders are deprecated for accessibility and names the component's help-text docs URL. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/textfield/TextField.test.js: "$Name renders with placeholder text and shows warning")

## search-field

### Roles and attributes

- Given `useSearchField` with a value state, when the hook runs, then inputProps.type is "search", inputProps.value mirrors state.value, and onKeyDown is a function. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/searchfield/useSearchField.test.js: "with base props and value equal to state.value")
- Given `isDisabled: true`, when the hook runs, then no onKeyDown prop is returned at all, so Enter and Escape handling is inert while disabled. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/searchfield/useSearchField.test.js: "does not return an onKeyDown prop if isDisabled is true")
- Given `defaultValue: 'ABC'`, when the hook runs, then inputProps has no defaultValue (the state owns the value, so the input stays controlled). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/searchfield/useSearchField.test.js: "does not return an defaultValue prop")
- Given a Spectrum SearchField with no value, when rendered, then the input has `type="search"` and no clear button is present. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "$Name default behavior check")
- Given a custom `icon` element, when rendered, then that icon renders. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "$Name should support custom icons")
- Given `icon=""`, when rendered, then no search icon renders. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "$Name should support no icons")
- Given `aria-label="Test"`, when rendered, then the searchbox has that aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "$Name should support aria-label")
- Given `excludeFromTabOrder`, when rendered, then the searchbox has `tabIndex="-1"`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "$Name should support excludeFromTabOrder")
- Given a RAC SearchField with Label, Input, Button, and description plus errorMessage Text slots, when rendered, then the input has role searchbox with the default value, the wrapper carries data props, aria-labelledby points at the `react-aria-Label`, aria-describedby resolves to "Description Error", and the clear Button gets `aria-label="Clear search"` automatically. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/SearchField.test.js: "provides slots")
- Given a SearchFieldContext with a "test" slot, when `slot="test"` is used, then the wrapper has the slot attribute and the searchbox gets the slot's aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/SearchField.test.js: "should support slot")
- Given `data-testid` on a RAC SearchField, when rendered, then exactly one element has it and it is the outer `react-aria-SearchField` element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/SearchField.test.js: "should render data- attributes only on the outer element")
- Given `isReadOnly` on a RAC SearchField, when rendered, then the input's parent has `data-readonly`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/SearchField.test.js: "supports readonly")
- Given `form="test"` on a RAC SearchField, when rendered, then the input has the form attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/SearchField.test.js: "should support form prop")

### Keyboard

- Given an Escape keydown, when handled by useSearchField, then neither preventDefault nor stopPropagation is called, so an enclosing overlay can still react to Escape. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/searchfield/useSearchField.test.js: "preventDefault and stopPropagation are not called for Escape")
- Given no onSubmit prop, when Enter is pressed, then preventDefault is not called so a surrounding form submits normally. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/searchfield/useSearchField.test.js: "preventDefault is not called for Enter if onSubmit is not provided")
- Given an onSubmit prop, when Enter is pressed, then onSubmit is called once with the current value. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/searchfield/useSearchField.test.js: "preventDefault and onSubmit are called for Enter if submit is provided")
- Given a non-empty value and an onClear prop, when Escape is pressed, then setValue('') and onClear each fire once; pressing Escape again with an empty value fires neither. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/searchfield/useSearchField.test.js: "pressing the Escape key sets the state value to \"\", if state.value is not empty, and calls onClear if provided and will not call onClear if escape pressed again")
- Given a user onKeyDown prop, when Enter is pressed, then the user handler is still called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/searchfield/useSearchField.test.js: "onKeyDown prop is called")
- Given a SearchField with a default value and onSubmit, when Enter is pressed, then onSubmit receives the current text; after clearing the input and pressing Enter again, onSubmit is called a second time with the empty string. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "$Name submits the textfield value when enter is pressed")
- Given a disabled SearchField with a value, when Enter is pressed, then onSubmit is never called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "$Name doesn't submit the textfield value when enter is pressed but field is disabled")
- Given an uncontrolled SearchField with a default value, when Escape is pressed, then onChange fires once with the empty string, the input clears, onClear fires once, and focus stays on the body rather than moving to the input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "$Name clears the input field if the escape key is pressed and the field is uncontrolled")
- Given a controlled SearchField, when Escape is pressed, then onChange fires with the empty string and onClear fires, but the displayed value stays unchanged because the parent owns it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "$Name doesn't clear the input field if the escape key is pressed and the field is controlled")
- Given a disabled SearchField with a value, when Escape is pressed, then neither onChange nor onClear fires and the value stays. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "$Name doesn't clear the input field if the escape key is pressed and the field is disabled")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given an uncontrolled SearchField with a value, when the clear button is clicked, then onChange fires once with the empty string, the input empties, onClear fires once, and focus moves to the input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "$Name clears the input field if the clear button is pressed and the field is uncontrolled")
- Given a controlled SearchField, when the clear button is clicked, then onChange and onClear fire but the value stays and focus still moves to the input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "$Name doesn't clear the input field if the clear button is pressed and the field is controlled")
- Given a disabled SearchField, when the clear button is clicked, then neither onChange nor onClear fires and the value is unchanged. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "$Name doesn't clear the input field if the clear button is pressed and the field is disabled")
- Given clearButtonProps from useSearchField, when onPressStart then onPress run, then setValue('') is called once and the input ref's focus() is called once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/searchfield/useSearchField.test.js: "sets the state to \"\" and focuses the search field")
- Given an onClear prop, when the clear button is pressed, then setValue(''), the input focus, and onClear (called with no arguments) all happen. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/searchfield/useSearchField.test.js: "calls the user provided onClear if provided")

### Focus management

- Given clearButtonProps, when inspected, then `excludeFromTabOrder` is true so the clear button is not a tab stop. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/searchfield/useSearchField.test.js: "clear button should not be tabbable")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a SearchField with a default value, when the value is emptied then retyped, then the clear button is removed while empty and reappears once there is text. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "$Name should display the clear button icon only if text is present")
- Given `isReadOnly` with a value, when rendered, then no clear button renders. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "SearchField doesn't show clear button if isReadOnly is true")
- Given `useSearchFieldState({value, onChange})`, when setValue is called, then the rendered value stays at the prop value and onChange fires once with the new value. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/searchfield/useSearchFieldState.test.js: "should be controlled if props.value is defined")
- Given `defaultValue` only, when setValue is called, then the state value updates and onChange fires once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/searchfield/useSearchFieldState.test.js: "should start with value = props.defaultValue if props.value is not defined and props.defaultValue is defined")
- Given neither value nor defaultValue, when the hook runs, then the value starts as the empty string and setValue updates it. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/searchfield/useSearchFieldState.test.js: "should default to uncontrolled with value = \"\" if defaultValue and value aren't defined")
- Given `defaultValue: 13`, when the hook runs, then the value is the string "13". (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/searchfield/useSearchFieldState.test.js: "should convert numeric values to strings (uncontrolled)")
- Given `defaultValue: ['hi','this','is','me']`, when the hook runs, then the value is the array's toString form. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/searchfield/useSearchFieldState.test.js: "should convert an array of string values to a string (uncontrolled)")
- Given `value: 13`, when the hook runs, then the controlled value is coerced to "13". (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/searchfield/useSearchFieldState.test.js: "should convert numeric values to strings (controlled)")
- Given `value: ['hi','this','is','me']`, when the hook runs, then the controlled value is coerced to the array's toString form. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/searchfield/useSearchFieldState.test.js: "should convert an array of string values to a string (controlled)")
- Given a RAC SearchField whose children are a function of `{state}`, when rendered with defaultValue "test", then the description reads `You are looking for "test"`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/SearchField.test.js: "should support render props")
- Given a `render` prop returning a div with `data-custom`, when rendered, then the wrapper is the custom element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/SearchField.test.js: "should support custom render function")

### Forms (name, value, validation, form reset, hidden inputs, autofill)

- Given a `description` prop, when rendered, then the help text has an id and aria-describedby points at it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "$Name should support description")
- Given `errorMessage` plus `validationState="invalid"`, when rendered, then the error text has an id and aria-describedby points at it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.test.js: "$Name should support error message")
- Given a RAC SearchField with `isRequired` and a FieldError in a form, when the form's checkValidity runs, then the input had `required` and no aria-required, becomes described by "Constraints not satisfied", is focused, and its parent has both `data-invalid` and `data-required`; typing makes validity true and blurring clears the description. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/SearchField.test.js: "supports validation errors")

### RTL and i18n (locale-aware parsing, number formats, RTL arrow keys)

- Given a de-DE locale Provider, when the hook renders, then clearButtonProps['aria-label'] is the German translation of "Clear search" from the intl messages. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/searchfield/useSearchField.test.js: "with a localized aria-label")

### SSR and hydration

- Given a Spectrum SearchField with a label, when server rendered and hydrated, then no errors occur. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/searchfield/SearchField.ssr.test.js: "should render without errors")

## form

### Roles and attributes

- Given a Form with an aria-label, when rendered, then an element with role form exists and carries the `novalidate` attribute (Spectrum Form defaults to non-native validation). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/form/Form.test.js: "should render a form")
- Given a Form with children, when rendered, then the children render inside the form element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/form/Form.test.js: "should render children inside the form")
- Given `aria-label="Test"`, when rendered, then the form element has that aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/form/Form.test.js: "supports aria-label")
- Given `aria-labelledby="test"` and a span with that id, when rendered, then the form element has aria-labelledby pointing at the span. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/form/Form.test.js: "supports aria-labelledby")
- Given `aria-describedby="test"`, when rendered, then the form element has that aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/form/Form.test.js: "supports aria-describedby")
- Given `data-testid` on Form, when rendered, then the custom data attribute lands on the form DOM element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/form/Form.test.js: "supports custom data attributes")
- Given a RAC Form, when rendered, then the form element has class `react-aria-Form`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Form.test.js: "should use validationBehavior=\"native\" by default")
- Given a RAC FieldError with `data-testid`, when rendered, then data attributes pass through to the error element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/FieldError.test.js: "supports data attributes passed as props")
- Given a RAC FieldError with no elementType, when rendered, then it renders as a SPAN. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/FieldError.test.js: "renders as span by default")
- Given `elementType="div"` on FieldError, when rendered, then it renders as a DIV. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/FieldError.test.js: "supports elementType prop")

### Focus management

- Given a native form with a required Input and a submit Button under React 19, when submit fails validation and a form library moves focus with a plain `ref.focus()` after `checkValidity()`, then the input gains focus and gets `data-focus-visible` (pins the react-hook-form `shouldFocusError` flow; skipped on React 18). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Form.test.js: "shows focus-visible when a form library moves focus to the first invalid field on submit")
- Given a Form whose `form.elements` includes an object with no `validity` property (simulating a Web Component), when the submit button is clicked, then no error is thrown and focus still moves to the first invalid input. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Form.test.js: "should not throw when form contains elements without validity property")
- Given a disabled Spectrum Form containing a Picker with contextualHelp, when the help button is clicked, Tab moves to the dialog dismiss button, and that button is clicked, then neither the help button nor the dismiss button is disabled and focus returns to the help button after timers run. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/form/Form.test.js: "contextual help should not be disabled nor should its dismiss button be disabled")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a Form that sets `necessityIndicator={undefined}` and a child TextField with `necessityIndicator="label"`, when rendered, then the child prop wins and the label reads "A text field ​(optional)". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/form/Form.test.js: "should context props should be overridden by child")
- Given a ref on Form, when rendered, then `ref.current.UNSAFE_getDOMNode()` is the form element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/form/Form.test.js: "should attach a optional user provided ref to the form")
- Given a RAC Form with a `render` prop returning a form with `data-custom`, when rendered, then the custom render output is used. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Form.test.js: "should support custom render function")

### Forms (name, value, validation, form reset, hidden inputs, autofill)

- Given a Form with action, method, target, encType, autoComplete and onSubmit plus a submit Button, when rendered, then all those attributes appear on the form element, and when the submit button is clicked onSubmit fires. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/form/Form.test.js: "supports form attributes")
- Given a Picker named "picker" with no selection inside a Form, when read via `form.elements['picker'].value`, then the value is the empty string. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/form/Form.test.js: "default value of a picker is empty")
- Given a Picker with `defaultSelectedKey="one"` inside a Form, when read via `form.elements['picker'].value`, then the value is "one". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/form/Form.test.js: "value of a picker can be set")
- Given a RAC Form with `validationErrors={{name: 'Invalid name.'}}` set from an onSubmit handler, when submit is pressed and `form.checkValidity()` runs, then the input gains aria-describedby pointing at an element with text "Invalid name.", `input.validity.valid` is false, and the input receives focus. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Form.test.js: "supports server validation errors")
- Given the same server error state, when submit is pressed a second time, then the server error is not cleared and the input stays invalid and focused. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Form.test.js: "supports server validation errors")
- Given a displayed server error, when the input is cleared, retyped with a new value, and blurred, then aria-describedby is removed and `input.validity.valid` becomes true. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Form.test.js: "supports server validation errors")
- Given a RAC Form with no validationBehavior and an `isRequired` TextField, when rendered, then the form has no `novalidate` attribute, the input has `required`, and it does not have `aria-required` (native validation is the default). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Form.test.js: "should use validationBehavior=\"native\" by default")
- Given `validationBehavior="aria"` on the Form, when rendered, then the form has `novalidate`, the input has no `required` attribute, and it has `aria-required`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Form.test.js: "supports validationBehavior=\"aria\"")
- Given a Form defaulting to native validation and a TextField with `validationBehavior="aria"`, when rendered, then the field-level prop wins: the form keeps no `novalidate` while the input uses `aria-required` and not `required`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Form.test.js: "Form element's validationBehavior=\"aria\" should override Form's default validationBehavior=\"native\"")
- Given `validationBehavior="aria"` on the Form and `validationBehavior="native"` on the TextField, when rendered, then the form has `novalidate` while the input still gets `required` and no `aria-required`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Form.test.js: "Form element's validationBehavior=\"native\" should override Form's validationBehavior=\"aria\"")
- Given `useFormReset(ref, '', onReset)` on an input inside a form with a reset button, when the reset button is clicked, then onReset is called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/utils/useFormReset.test.tsx: "should call onReset on reset")
- Given a form whose onReset handler calls `stopPropagation()`, when reset is clicked, then onReset is still called (the hook listens in a way propagation cannot block). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/utils/useFormReset.test.tsx: "should call onReset on reset even if event is stopped")
- Given two inputs each registered with useFormReset, when reset is clicked, then both onReset callbacks fire. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/utils/useFormReset.test.tsx: "should call every onReset on reset")
- Given a form whose `onResetCapture` calls `preventDefault()`, when reset is clicked, then onReset is not called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/utils/useFormReset.test.tsx: "should not call onReset if reset is cancelled in capture phase")
- Given two registered inputs and a form whose `onResetCapture` prevents default, when reset is clicked, then neither onReset fires. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/utils/useFormReset.test.tsx: "should not call any onReset if reset is cancelled")
- Given a form whose bubble-phase `onReset` calls `preventDefault()`, when reset is clicked, then onReset would ideally not be called; the repo documents that matching native cancel semantics needs a capture listener and leaves the test off. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/utils/useFormReset.test.tsx: "should not call onReset if reset is cancelled") (skipped in repo)

### SSR and hydration

- Given a Spectrum Form inside a Provider, when server rendered and hydrated, then no errors or hydration warnings occur. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/form/Form.ssr.test.js: "should render without errors")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a FieldError with `elementType="div"` and a render prop that returns a div wrapping a list, when rendered, then no "Unexpected DOM element" console warning is emitted. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/FieldError.test.js: "does not warn when render prop returns element matching elementType")
- Given a FieldError with no elementType and a render prop that returns a div, when rendered, then a console warning containing "Unexpected DOM element" is emitted because the rendered element does not match the default span. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/FieldError.test.js: "warns when render prop returns element that does not match elementType")

## label

### Roles and attributes

- Given `useLabel({label: 'Test'})`, when the hook runs, then labelProps.id and fieldProps.id are both generated and distinct, fieldProps['aria-labelledby'] equals labelProps.id, and labelProps.htmlFor equals fieldProps.id. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/label/useLabel.test.js: "should return props for visible label")
- Given a visible label plus `aria-labelledby="foo"`, when the hook runs, then fieldProps['aria-labelledby'] is "<labelId> foo" and htmlFor still points at the field id. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/label/useLabel.test.js: "should combine aria-labelledby if visible label is also provided")
- Given a visible label plus both aria-labelledby and aria-label, when the hook runs, then aria-label passes through unchanged and fieldProps['aria-labelledby'] becomes "<fieldId> <labelId> foo", so the field's own id is included to pick up its aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/label/useLabel.test.js: "should combine aria-labelledby if visible label and aria-label is also provided")
- Given only `aria-label`, when the hook runs, then labelProps has no id and no htmlFor, the field still gets an id, aria-labelledby is undefined, and aria-label passes through. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/label/useLabel.test.js: "should work without a visisble label")
- Given `aria-label` plus `aria-labelledby="foo"` and no visible label, when the hook runs, then fieldProps['aria-labelledby'] is "<fieldId> foo" and aria-label passes through. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/label/useLabel.test.js: "should work without a visible label and both aria-label and aria-labelledby")
- Given `labelElementType: 'span'` with a visible label, when the hook runs, then labelProps.htmlFor is undefined (only a real label element gets `for`) while aria-labelledby still links the two. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/label/useLabel.test.js: "should not return a `for` attribute when the label element type is not <label>")
- Given `useField({label: 'Test'})`, when the hook runs, then both labelProps.id and fieldProps.id are defined. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/label/useField.test.js: "should return label props")
- Given a Field with a label and no description, when rendered, then the labelled input exists and has no aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/label/Field.test.js: "renders correctly")
- Given a Field with contextualHelp, when rendered, then the help trigger button has `aria-label="Help"`, an id, and an aria-labelledby whose first token is the field label's id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/label/Field.test.js: "supports contextualHelp")

### Focus management

- Given a focused Field with no visible label that the user has typed into, when it rerenders with `validationState="invalid"` and an errorMessage, then the error renders and the input keeps focus (the DOM node is not recreated). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/label/Field.test.js: "does not lose focus when no visible label and validation state changes")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a Field with a ref, when rendered, then the ref points at the wrapper div containing the input. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/label/Field.test.js: "supports a ref")
- Given `labelPosition="side"` and a ref, when rendered, then the ref points at the parent of the input's wrapper div (the side layout adds a level). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/label/Field.test.js: "supports a ref")

### Forms (name, value, validation, form reset, hidden inputs, autofill)

- Given `useField({label, description, errorMessage})` with nothing rendered into the DOM, when the hook runs, then descriptionProps.id and errorMessageProps.id are undefined because `useSlotId` only assigns ids once the slots are actually rendered. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/label/useField.test.js: "should return props for description and error message if they are passed in")
- Given `useField({label})` with no description or errorMessage, when the hook runs, then descriptionProps.id and errorMessageProps.id are undefined. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/label/useField.test.js: "should not return an id for description and error message if they are not passed in")
- Given the useField "WithError" story that renders both a description and an error message, when rendered, then the input's aria-describedby contains both the description id and the error id. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/label/useField.test.js: "can render and label both the description and error message at the same time")
- Given a Field with a description, when rendered, then the help text renders and the input's aria-describedby is the help text id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/label/Field.test.js: "renders when description is provided")
- Given both description and errorMessage but validationState not invalid, when rendered, then only the description shows and aria-describedby points at it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/label/Field.test.js: "renders when description and error message are provided but validationState is not invalid")
- Given a description and `validationState="invalid"` but no errorMessage, when rendered, then the description still renders and is referenced by aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/label/Field.test.js: "renders when description is provided and validationState is invalid but no error message is provided")
- Given no description, when rendered, then the input has no aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/label/Field.test.js: "does not render when no description is provided")
- Given a description with only an aria-label and no visible label, when rendered, then the description renders and is still referenced by aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/label/Field.test.js: "renders when no visible label is provided")
- Given errorMessage plus `validationState="invalid"`, when rendered, then the error renders and aria-describedby is the error id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/label/Field.test.js: "renders when error message is provided and validationState is invalid")
- Given errorMessage with validationState not invalid, when rendered, then the error is not in the DOM and the input has no aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/label/Field.test.js: "does not render when error message is provided but validationState is not invalid")
- Given `validationState="invalid"` and no errorMessage, when rendered, then the input has no aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/label/Field.test.js: "does not render when validationState is invalid but no error message is provided")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given `useLabel({})` with neither a visible label nor aria-label nor aria-labelledby, when the hook runs, then it logs the console warning "If you do not provide a visible label, you must specify an aria-label or aria-labelledby attribute for accessibility". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/label/useLabel.test.js: "should warn if no visible label or aria labels are provided")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given contextualHelp with no visible label (only aria-label), when rendered with or without a description, then no help trigger button renders at all. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/label/Field.test.js: "does not render contextual help if there is no label")

## tag-group

### Roles and attributes

- Given a Spectrum TagGroup with one Item, when rendered, then the container has role grid, each tag is a row, and the number of rows equals the number of gridcells (one cell per row). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "has correct accessibility roles")
- Given a TagGroup with one Item, when rendered, then the tag row has `tabIndex="0"`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "has correct tab index")
- Given `aria-label="tag group"`, when rendered, then the grid element has that aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "TagGroup allows aria-label")
- Given `aria-labelledby`, when rendered, then the grid element has that aria-labelledby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "TagGroup allows aria-labelledby")
- Given Items with their own `aria-label`, when rendered, then the aria-label lands on the gridcell inside each row. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "TagGroup allows aria-label on Item")
- Given an Item with UNSAFE_className, when rendered, then the row keeps both the custom class and `spectrum-Tag`, carries `role="row"` and `tabIndex="0"`, and does not leak `icon` or `unsafe_classname` attributes to the DOM. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "TagGroup should pass className, role and tabIndex")
- Given `actionLabel="Clear"` with onAction, when rendered, then the action wrapper has role group with `aria-label="Actions"` and an aria-labelledby of "<tagGroupId> <actionGroupId>". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "action group is labelled correctly")
- Given data attributes on the TagGroup and on each Item, when rendered, then the grid and each row carry their own data attribute values. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "should support data attributes")
- Given a RAC TagGroup with TagList and Tags, when rendered, then the wrapper has class `react-aria-TagGroup`, the grid has `react-aria-TagList`, and each row has `react-aria-Tag`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should render with default classes")
- Given custom classNames on TagGroup, TagList, and Tag, when rendered, then each replaces its default class. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should render with custom classes")
- Given data props on TagGroup, TagList, and Tag, when rendered, then each element carries its own. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support DOM props")
- Given a RAC TagGroup with a Label and description plus errorMessage Text slots, when rendered, then the grid's aria-labelledby points at the `react-aria-Label` and its aria-describedby resolves to "Description Error". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "provides slots for description and error message")
- Given `selectionMode="multiple"` with `disabledKeys: ['cat']`, when rendered, then the disabled row has `aria-disabled="true"` and the isDisabled render-prop class. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support disabled state")
- Given onRemove on a RAC TagGroup, when rendered, then each row has `data-allows-removing="true"`, the allowsRemoving render prop is true, and the remove Button gets `aria-label="Remove"` automatically. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support removing items")
- Given a TagList with no items and a renderEmptyState, when rendered, then the list has `data-empty="true"`, shows the empty content, and its role changes from grid to group. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support empty state")

### Keyboard

- Given a de-DE (LTR) horizontal TagGroup, when Tab focuses the first tag, then ArrowRight moves to the second tag, ArrowLeft returns to the first, and ArrowLeft again wraps to the last. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "$Name shifts button focus in the correct direction on key press")
- Given an ar-AE (RTL) horizontal TagGroup, when Tab focuses the first tag, then ArrowLeft moves forward to the second tag and ArrowRight moves back, mirroring the LTR mapping. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "$Name shifts button focus in the correct direction on key press")
- Given a de-DE horizontal TagGroup, when ArrowDown and ArrowUp are used, then they also move forward and backward through the tags and wrap. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "$Name shifts button focus in the correct direction on key press")
- Given an ar-AE horizontal TagGroup, when ArrowUp is pressed from the first tag, then focus wraps to the last tag and ArrowDown moves forward again, so vertical arrows are not mirrored by RTL. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "$Name shifts button focus in the correct direction on key press")
- Given four tags that all start with `tabIndex="0"`, when Tab focuses the first, then that tag keeps tabIndex 0 while the rest become -1 (roving tabindex), and ArrowRight, ArrowLeft, End, Home, PageDown, and PageUp move focus to the expected tag. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "handles keyboard focus management properly")
- Given onRemove and focus on a tag, when Delete is pressed, then onRemove fires once with a Set containing that tag's key. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "Remove tag $Name")
- Given onRemove and focus on a tag, when Backspace is pressed, then onRemove fires once with that key. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "Remove tag $Name")
- Given onRemove, when Space is pressed on a tag, then onRemove is not called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "Space does not trigger removal")
- Given a keyboard-focused custom action button, when Enter is pressed, then onAction fires once with no arguments. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "can keyboard navigate to a custom action")
- Given a useTagGroup based group with three tags, when Tab enters it, then the first row is focused, and ArrowRight then ArrowLeft move between rows. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/tag/useTagGroup.test.js: "should support tabbing to tags and arrow navigation between tags")
- Given a useTagGroup group with remove buttons, when Tab is pressed twice, then focus goes from the first row to that row's remove button, and Space on the button calls onRemove with that key. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/tag/useTagGroup.test.js: "should support tabbing to remove buttons")
- Given a multiple selection useTagGroup group, when Space is pressed on the focused tag, then onSelectionChange fires, and ArrowRight then Space selects the next tag as well (two calls total). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/tag/useTagGroup.test.js: "should support keyboard selection while navigating between tags")
- Given a multiple-selection useTagGroup group with "parking" preselected, when another tag is clicked and Backspace pressed, then onRemove receives the whole selected set (parking plus pool), and after also selecting the first tag another Backspace passes all three keys. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/tag/useTagGroup.test.js: "should support selection")
- Given a RAC tag with `isDisabled` in the middle of the list, when ArrowRight is pressed from the first tag, then focus skips the disabled tag and lands on the third. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support isDisabled prop on items")
- Given a RAC TagGroup backed by useListData whose onRemove deletes the key (React 18+), when Backspace is held for three keydown events, then all three tags are removed in order (cat, dog, kangaroo) because focus shifts to the next tag after each repeat. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support repeat keydown events when holding the remove key")
- Given a RAC TagGroup with remove buttons, when Tab reaches the first remove button, then Space removes the "cat" tag, Delete on the button removes it again, Shift+Tab returns focus to the first tag, ArrowRight moves to the second, and Delete there removes "dog". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support tabbing to remove buttons")
- Given all tags disabled with onRemove, when Backspace is pressed on a focused tag, then onRemove is never called, and Shift+Tab from a later button lands focus on the grid itself. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "disabled tags should not be deletable")
- Given `onAction` with `selectionMode="none"` on a RAC TagGroup, when a tag is clicked or Enter is pressed on it, then onAction fires once per activation. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support onAction")
- Given `onAction` set on the individual Tag, when a tag is clicked or Enter pressed, then the item level onAction fires. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support onAction on the items")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given onRemove and a tag with a remove button, when the row itself is clicked then onRemove does not fire, and when the remove button is clicked onRemove fires once with that tag's key. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "should remove tag when remove button is clicked")
- Given onRemove and a tag rendered through useTag, when that row's remove button is clicked, then onRemove receives a Set containing only that key even while other tags are selected. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/tag/useTagGroup.test.js: "should support selection")
- Given a RAC TagGroup with `selectionMode="multiple"` and hover callbacks on the Tag, when a row is hovered then unhovered, then `data-hovered` and the hover class toggle, onHoverStart and onHoverEnd fire once each, and onHoverChange fires twice. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support hover")
- Given a RAC TagGroup with no selection mode, no action, and no href, when a row is hovered, then no `data-hovered` attribute and no hover callbacks fire because the tag is not interactive. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should not show hover state when item is not interactive")
- Given a Tag with an `href` and no selectionMode, when hovered, then hover state and callbacks do fire, because a link makes the tag interactive. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should show hover state when tag has an href even without selectionMode")
- Given a selectable RAC Tag with an isPressed className, when the left mouse button goes down then up, then `data-pressed="true"` appears and clears. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support press state")
- Given a non-interactive RAC Tag, when the mouse is pressed on it, then no pressed state appears. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should not show press state when not interactive")
- Given `selectionMode="multiple"`, when a row is clicked twice, then `aria-selected` and the selected class turn on then off. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support selection state")
- Given a disabled tag whose remove button is therefore disabled, when the remove button is clicked, then it carries `aria-label="Remove"` plus the `disabled` attribute and onRemove is never called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should disable the remove button if the tag is disabled")
- Given `selectionMode="single"` with no shouldSelectOnPressUp, when the mouse goes down on a tag, then onSelectionChange fires on press down and not again on release. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should select an item on pressing down when shouldSelectOnPressUp is not provided")
- Given `shouldSelectOnPressUp: false`, when the mouse goes down, then selection still happens on press down. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should select an item on pressing down when shouldSelectOnPressUp is false")
- Given `shouldSelectOnPressUp: true`, when the mouse goes down then up, then onSelectionChange fires only on release. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should select an item on pressing up when shouldSelectOnPressUp is true")
- Given press callbacks on the Tag driven through the GridList tester's `triggerRowAction`, when a row is activated by mouse or by keyboard, then onPressStart, onPressEnd, onPress, and onClick each fire once. Run as `it.each` over mouse and keyboard. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support press events on items when using $interactionType")
- Given `onAction` with `selectionMode="single"` and `selectionBehavior="replace"`, when a tag is double clicked then onAction fires; a single click selects instead without firing onAction; a later double click fires onAction and leaves nothing selected; Enter fires onAction with no selection change. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support onAction with selectionMode = single, behaviour = replace")
- Given `onAction` with `selectionMode="multiple"` and `selectionBehavior="replace"`, when a tag is double clicked onAction fires, a single click on another tag selects it without onAction, a double click back on the first fires onAction and leaves the first selected and the second not, and Enter fires onAction keeping that selection. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support onAction with selectionMode = multiple, behaviour = replace")

### Focus management

- Given buttons around a TagGroup with `disabledKeys`, when Tab enters the group and ArrowRight moves to the second tag, then Tab leaves to the following button and Shift+Tab returns to the second tag, so the group remembers its last focused item. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "should remember last focused item")
- Given buttons around a TagGroup, when Tab is pressed from the preceding button, then the first tag is focused and one more Tab leaves the whole group. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "should be focusable from Tab")
- Given focus on the button after a TagGroup, when Shift+Tab is pressed, then focus enters the group on its last tag, and another Shift+Tab reaches the button before the group. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "should be focusable from Shift + Tab")
- Given a dynamic TagGroup of six items, when Delete or Backspace removes the focused first tag, then onRemove fires with that id and focus lands on the new first tag, after which ArrowRight still works. Run as `it.each` over Delete and Backspace. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "Can move focus after removing tag $Name")
- Given a dynamic TagGroup of two items, when both are removed by Delete or Backspace, then after timers run there are no rows left and focus moves to the grid container. Run as `it.each` over Delete and Backspace. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "Should focus container after last tag is removed $Name")
- Given a RAC TagGroup whose first two tags are disabled and the third is focused, when Backspace removes the third, then focus falls back to the grid rather than getting stuck trying to focus a disabled neighbor. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "if we cannot restore focus to next, then restore to previous but do not try focusing next again")
- Given a RAC TagGroup where four items were inserted at index 0 so the newest is first, when Delete is pressed four times from the first tag, then items are removed newest first with the order preserved, and after the last removal focus moves to the TagGroup element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should maintain item order when adding new items")
- Given `selectionMode="multiple"` with focus and blur callbacks on the Tag, when Tab focuses the first row then ArrowDown moves on, then the first row gets `data-focus-visible="true"` and the focus class, loses them on move, and onFocus, onBlur, and onFocusChange fire as focus passes through each tag. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support focus ring")
- Given an empty TagGroup whose renderEmptyState includes a link, when Tab is pressed, then focus lands on the link inside the empty state. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "should allow you to tab into TagGroup if empty with link")
- Given a TagGroup with both a "Show all" button and a custom Clear action, when Tab is pressed repeatedly, then focus goes first tag, show-all button, Clear button; Enter on Clear fires onAction once; Shift+Tab walks back through the show-all button to the tag; and a mouse press on the tag does not fire onAction. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "can keyboard navigate to show all button and custom action")
- Given a TagGroup with a custom action, when Tab moves from the tags to the action and Shift+Tab returns, then focus comes back to the tag that was focused before (tag 1, then tag 2 after ArrowRight). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "can keyboard navigate to a custom action")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a TagGroup with onRemove and a Tag component, when Delete is fired on a tag row, then onRemove is called once, proving the group supplies removal context to its tags. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "provides context for Tag component")
- Given refs on TagGroup, TagList, and Tag, when rendered, then each ref points at an HTMLElement. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support refs")
- Given `render` props on TagGroup, TagList, and Tag returning divs with `data-custom`, when rendered, then each level uses the custom element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should support custom render function")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given a RAC Tag wrapped in a TooltipTrigger, when the tag is hovered and timers run, then a tooltip with the trigger's content appears. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "supports tooltips")

### Positioning

- Given `maxRows={2}` with seven tags and mocked bounding rects that only fit three, when rendered, then only three gridcells show and a button reads "Show all (7)"; clicking it expands to all seven and the label becomes "Show less", and clicking again collapses back to three. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "maxRows should limit the number of tags shown")
- Given `maxRows={2}` with two tags that fit, when rendered, then both tags show and no show-all button renders. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "maxRows should not show button if there is enough room to show all tags")

### SSR and hydration

- Given a Spectrum TagGroup with four static Items, when server rendered and hydrated, then no errors occur. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.ssr.test.js: "should render without errors")
- Given a RAC TagGroup in StrictMode whose list conditionally includes a fourth tag, when server rendered, then the HTML contains the three visible rows in order and a grid role; after hydration the same three rows remain, and clicking the button inserts the extra tag in its correct position between Middle and Right. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.ssr.test.js: "should render without errors")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given an empty Spectrum TagGroup, when rendered and the MutationObserver in useHasTabbableChild settles, then the localized empty text "None" is shown. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "should render empty state")
- Given Spectrum Items with hrefs, when rendered, then rows are not anchor elements but carry `data-href`, and clicking a row produces a native click whose target is a real HTMLAnchorElement with the expected href. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/tag/TagGroup.test.js: "should support links")
- Given RAC Tags with hrefs under selectionMode none, single, or multiple, when a link tag is activated by mouse or Enter, then the native click fires and onSelectionChange does not; activating the non-link tag selects it instead (when selection is enabled) and activating a link again never changes selection. Run as nested `describe.each(['mouse','keyboard'])` and `it.each(['none','single','multiple'])`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "with selectionMode = %s")
- Given a RouterProvider with navigate and a `useHref` that prefixes "/base", when a Tag with an href and routerOptions is activated by mouse or keyboard, then `data-href` is the prefixed path and navigate is called with the original href plus the routerOptions. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TagGroup.test.js: "should work with RouterProvider")

## grid-list

### Roles and attributes

- Given a GridList with three GridListItems and no className, then the role="grid" element has class "react-aria-GridList" and every row has class "react-aria-GridListItem". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should render with default classes")
- Given className="gridlist" on GridList and className="item" on each item, then the role="grid" element has class "gridlist" and every role="row" element has class "item". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should render with custom classes")
- Given data-foo="bar" on GridList and data-bar="foo" on each item, then the grid has data-foo="bar" and every row has data-bar="foo". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support DOM props")
- Given a GridListContext.Provider with slots {test: {'aria-label': 'test'}} and a GridList with slot="test" and aria-label undefined, then the grid has slot="test" and aria-label="test". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support slot")
- Given render functions on GridList and GridListItem that spread props onto a div with data-custom="true", then the grid and every row have data-custom="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support custom render function")
- Given two GridListSections, the first containing a GridListHeader "Favorite Animal" and the second carrying aria-label="Favorite Ice Cream", then there are exactly two role="rowgroup" elements, both with class "react-aria-GridListSection", the first has aria-labelledby pointing at an element whose text content is "Favorite Animal", and the second has aria-label="Favorite Ice Cream". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support sections")
- Given a GridList with renderEmptyState returning "No results" and an empty children array, then the .react-aria-GridList element has data-empty="true"; the test queries by class rather than role because jsdom pretends to be WebKit and so the element uses role="group" instead of role="grid". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support empty state")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" and disabledKeys=['cat'], then the first row has aria-disabled="true", has the isDisabled render-prop class "disabled", and its checkbox is disabled. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support disabled state")
- Given a GridListItem with isDisabled containing a Button, then that row has aria-disabled="true" and the nested button is disabled. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support isDisabled prop on items")
- Given a GridList with no checkboxes and selectionMode="single" or "multiple" plus selectionBehavior="replace", then no row contains a role="checkbox", every row starts with aria-selected="false" and no data-selected attribute, and every row carries data-selection-mode equal to the selection mode ("single" or "multiple"), parameterized over interaction types mouse, keyboard and touch. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should perform selection with single selection", "should perform toggle selection in highlight mode when using modifier keys", "should perform replace selection in highlight mode when not using modifier keys")
- Given a static ListView with three Items and data-testid="test", then the role="grid" element is visible with aria-label="List", data-testid="test", aria-rowcount="3" and aria-colcount="1". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "renders a static listview")
- Given a static ListView with three Items, then three rows exist with aria-rowindex "1", "2" and "3", and the first row holds exactly one role="gridcell" with text content "Foo" and aria-colindex="1". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "renders a static listview")
- Given a dynamic ListView built from three items, then the grid is visible with aria-label="List", aria-rowcount="3" and aria-colcount="1", the three rows have aria-rowindex "1", "2" and "3", and the first row has exactly one gridcell with text "Foo" and aria-colindex="1". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "renders a dynamic listview")
- Given a ListView with no selection, then each row has aria-label equal to its own text content ("Foo", "Bar", "Baz"). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should have an aria-label on the row for the row text content")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="single", then every row's checkbox has aria-labelledby set to "<checkbox id> <row id>". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should label the checkboxes with the row label")
- Given an Item containing a Text label and a Text slot="description", then the row has aria-labelledby="<row id> <description id>"; the test is named for aria-describedby but asserts aria-labelledby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should use item description text as aria-describedby")
- Given data-testid="test" on ListView, then the role="grid" element has data-testid="test". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "supports custom data attributes")
- Given ListView with disabledKeys=['foo'] and selectionMode="multiple", then row Foo has aria-disabled="true", has no aria-selected attribute at all, its checkbox has the disabled attribute, and both nested ActionButtons have the disabled attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should disable nested elements when row is disabled")
- Given ListView with disabledKeys=['foo'] and selectionMode="multiple", then the non-disabled row Bar has no aria-disabled="true", has aria-selected="false", and neither its checkbox nor its two buttons are disabled. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should disable nested elements when row is disabled")
- Given ListView with disabledKeys=['foo'], disabledBehavior="selection" and selectionMode="multiple", then row Foo has no aria-disabled attribute and no aria-selected attribute, its checkbox has the disabled attribute, but its two nested ActionButtons are not disabled. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should disable nested elements with disabledBehavior="selection"")
- Given a virtualized GridList wrapped in Virtualizer with ListLayout rowHeight 25 and clientWidth/clientHeight mocked to 100, then every rendered row carries an aria-rowindex attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support virtualizer")

### Keyboard

- Given a GridList with layout="grid" where the second item contains a Button, when Tab focuses the first row and ArrowRight is pressed twice, then focus moves row 0 to row 1 to row 2, and ArrowLeft moves back to row 1. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support grid layout")
