- Given a GridList with layout="grid" and focus on row 1 which contains a Button, when Tab is pressed, then focus moves to that Button, and a further Tab moves focus to document.body. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support grid layout")
- Given a GridList with orientation="horizontal", when Tab focuses row 0 then ArrowDown is pressed twice, then focus moves to row 1 then row 2, and ArrowUp twice moves back to row 1 then row 0. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support horizontal orientation")
- Given a GridList with orientation="horizontal" and layout="grid" where row 1 contains a Button, when Tab focuses row 0 then ArrowDown is pressed twice, then focus moves to row 1 then row 2; ArrowUp returns to row 1, Tab moves focus into the Button, and another Tab moves focus to document.body. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support horizontal orientation with grid layout")
- Given a GridList whose second item has isDisabled, when Tab focuses row 0 and ArrowDown is pressed, then focus skips the disabled row and lands on row 2. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support isDisabled prop on items")
- Given a GridList with selectionMode="multiple", escapeKeyBehavior="none" and two rows selected, when Escape is pressed, then the selected row count stays at 2. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should prevent Esc from clearing selection if escapeKeyBehavior is "none"")
- Given a virtualized GridList of 50 items showing rows Item 7 to Item 14 after scrolling, when Tab then End is pressed, then 9 rows render and the list is Item 7 through Item 14 plus Item 49, so the last item is rendered in addition to the current window. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support virtualizer")
- Given a GridListItem containing a TagGroup with three Tags (default arrow navigation), when Tab focuses row 0 and ArrowRight is pressed, then focus moves into tag 0, a second ArrowRight moves to tag 1, ArrowDown moves out to the next GridList row, and Tab from there moves focus to document.body. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support rendering a TagGroup inside a GridListItem")
- Given a GridList with keyboardNavigationBehavior="tab" whose first item contains a TagGroup with removable Tags, when Tab focuses row 0 and ArrowRight is pressed, then focus stays on row 0 because arrow keys do not enter the row in tab mode; Tab then moves focus to tag 0 and ArrowRight moves to tag 1. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support rendering a TagGroup with tabbing navigation inside a GridListItem")
- Given focus on tag 1 inside the GridListItem, when Tab is pressed then Space, then focus is on that tag's remove Button and onRemove is called once with new Set(['2']). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support rendering a TagGroup with tabbing navigation inside a GridListItem")
- Given focus on the remove Button of tag 1, when Shift+Tab is pressed, then focus returns to tag 1; a further simulated Shift+Tab (keydown plus manual focus walker plus keyup, because user.tab({shift: true}) does not reproduce the coercion of focus back into the collection) puts focus back on row 0. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support rendering a TagGroup with tabbing navigation inside a GridListItem")
- Given a GridList with either keyboardNavigationBehavior="tab" or layout="grid" whose first row contains an input, when focus is moved into the input by Tab and ArrowDown, ArrowUp, ArrowRight and ArrowLeft are pressed, then focus remains on the input for every arrow key. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should not navigate rows when arrow keys are pressed while a text input child has focus (%s)")
- Given a GridList with selectionMode="multiple" and either keyboardNavigationBehavior="tab" or layout="grid" whose first row contains an input, when Space is typed with the input focused, then the input value becomes " " and onSelectionChange is not called; a following Enter also leaves onSelectionChange uncalled. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should not trigger selection when pressing Space or Enter in a text input child (%s)")
- Given a GridList (keyboardNavigationBehavior="tab" or layout="grid") containing a row with a ComboBox, a row with a Toolbar and a row with a plain input, plus inputs before and after the list, when Tab is pressed three times then once more, then focus goes from the ComboBox straight to the input after the list rather than to the next row. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should exit the grid when tabbing from a combobox or toolbar, not focus the next row (%s)")
- Given focus on the input after the list, when Shift+Tab is pressed, then focus lands on row 0 (the test notes this returns to the GridList item rather than the ComboBox itself and flags it as something to look into); ArrowRight (grid layout) or ArrowDown moves to row 1, Tab moves into the Toolbar's Bold button, and Tab again moves to the input after the list. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should exit the grid when tabbing from a combobox or toolbar, not focus the next row (%s)")
- Given focus back on row 1 after Shift+Tab, when ArrowRight (grid layout) or ArrowDown moves to row 2 and Tab is pressed, then focus lands on that row's input, and another Tab moves to the input after the list. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should exit the grid when tabbing from a combobox or toolbar, not focus the next row (%s)")
- Given a GridList with keyboardNavigationBehavior="tab" whose items all have focusMode="child", when Tab focuses the list, then focus lands on the first item's button, and after Shift+Tab plus ArrowDown focus is on the second item's button. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "focusMode="child" auto-focuses first child when item receives focus")
- Given a GridList with keyboardNavigationBehavior="tab" whose items have focusMode="child" and allowsArrowNavigation, when Tab focuses the first item's button and ArrowDown is pressed, then focus moves to the second item's button. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "allowsArrowNavigation allows arrow key row navigation when focused on child")
- Given a GridList with default arrow navigation and three items with focusMode="child", each containing a button and an input, when Tab focuses item 1's button and ArrowDown is pressed twice, then focus moves to item 2's button then item 3's button. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "ArrowDown from child navigates to first child of next item")
- Given two items with focusMode="child" each containing a button and an input, when ArrowDown then ArrowUp are pressed from item 1's button, then focus moves to item 2's button and back to item 1's button. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "ArrowUp from child navigates to first child of previous item")
- Given one item with focusMode="child" containing two buttons, when ArrowRight is pressed from the first button, then focus goes first button to last button to the row element (wrapping); ArrowLeft from the row goes to the last button, then the first button, then the row; ArrowRight from the row re-enters the first child. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "ArrowLeft/Right cycles through children and row element")
- Given a GridList with keyboardNavigationBehavior="tab" and one item (default focusMode="row") containing two buttons, when Tab is pressed repeatedly, then focus goes row 0, then "Item 1 action" button, then "Item 1 action 2" button; Shift+Tab walks back to "Item 1 action" and then to row 0. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "Tab into list focuses row, Tab from row enters child, Shift+Tab returns to row")
- Given a draggable GridList with renderDropIndicator, when Tab, ArrowRight and Enter start a keyboard drag, then five rows render, rows 0, 2, 3 and 4 have class "react-aria-DropIndicator" with text "Test", only row 2 has data-drop-target, and their buttons have aria-labels "Insert before Cat", "Insert between Cat and Dog", "Insert between Dog and Kangaroo" and "Insert after Kangaroo". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should render drop indicators")
- Given an in-progress keyboard drag with the drop indicator between Cat and Dog active, when ArrowDown then Enter are pressed, then the active element has aria-label "Insert between Dog and Kangaroo", only row 3 has data-drop-target="true", and onReorder is called once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should render drop indicators")
- Given a draggable GridList with disabledKeys=['dog'], when a keyboard drag is started and ArrowDown pressed twice, then the drop positions visited are "Insert between Cat and Dog", "Insert between Dog and Kangaroo" and "Insert after Kangaroo", so positions around a disabled item are not skipped; Escape then cancels the drag. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should not skip drop positions before/after a disabled item")
- Given two draggable GridLists where the second accepts onItemDrop, when a keyboard drag is started from the first, then the second list shows three rows whose buttons have aria-labels "Drop on Cat", "Drop on Dog" and "Drop on Kangaroo", only the element after row 0 has data-drop-target="true", focus is on row 0's drop button, and Enter calls onItemDrop once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support dropping on rows")
- Given two draggable GridLists where the second accepts onRootDrop, when a keyboard drag is started from the first, then the second list shows a single row whose button has aria-label "Drop on", focus is on that button, the second grid has data-drop-target="true", and Enter calls onRootDrop once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support dropping on the root")
- Given a draggable GridList with orientation="horizontal" and renderDropIndicator, when a keyboard drag is started, then row 2 has data-drop-target with aria-label "Insert between Cat and Dog"; ArrowRight moves the target to row 3 ("Insert between Dog and Kangaroo"), ArrowLeft moves it back to row 2, and Enter calls onReorder once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support dropping with horizontal arrow keys when orientation is horizontal")
- Given a ListView with no focusable children and focus on row Foo, when ArrowRight is pressed, then focus stays on row Foo. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should not move focus if no focusables present")
- Given a ListView whose rows each contain two ActionButtons and focus on row Foo, when ArrowRight is pressed three times, then focus moves to button1, then button2, then back to the row itself. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move focus to next cell and back to row")
- Given a ListView with no focusable children and focus on row Foo, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then focus stays on row Foo. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should not move focus if no focusables present")
- Given a ListView whose rows contain two ActionButtons and focus on row Foo, when ArrowLeft is pressed three times, then focus moves to button2, then button1, then back to the row. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move focus to previous cell and back to row")
- Given focus on the first ListView row, when ArrowUp is pressed, then focus does not wrap and stays on row Foo. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should not wrap focus")
- Given selectionMode="single" and row Bar clicked, when ArrowUp is pressed, then focus moves to row Foo. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move focus to above row")
- Given disabledKeys=['bar'] with selectionMode="single" and row Baz clicked, when ArrowUp is pressed, then focus skips Bar and lands on row Foo. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should skip disabled rows")
- Given disabledKeys=['foo'], disabledBehavior="selection" and selectionMode="single" with row Bar clicked, when ArrowUp is pressed, then focus moves onto the disabled row Foo. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should allow focus on disabled rows with disabledBehavior="selection"")
- Given selectionMode="single" and row Baz (the last row) clicked, when ArrowDown is pressed, then focus does not wrap and stays on Baz. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should not wrap focus")
- Given selectionMode="single" and row Foo clicked, when ArrowDown is pressed, then focus moves to row Bar. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move focus to below row")
- Given disabledKeys=['bar'] with selectionMode="single" and row Foo clicked, when ArrowDown is pressed, then focus skips Bar and lands on row Baz. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should skip disabled rows")
- Given disabledKeys=['bar'], disabledBehavior="selection" and selectionMode="single" with row Foo clicked, when ArrowDown is pressed, then focus moves onto the disabled row Bar. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should allow focus on disabled rows with disabledBehavior="selection"")
- Given a ListView of 100 items with selectionMode="single" and row "Foo 25" clicked, when PageUp is pressed, then focus moves to row "Foo 1". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move focus to a row a page above when focus starts on a row")
- Given a ListView of 100 items with focus on the first ActionButton inside row "Foo 25", when PageUp is pressed, then focus moves to row "Foo 1" itself. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move focus to a row a page above when focus starts in the row cell")
- Given a ListView of 100 items with selectionMode="single" and the grid's style.overflow set to "auto" so ListKeyboardDelegate treats it as scrollable, when Tab focuses the list and PageDown is pressed twice, then focus moves to row "Foo 25" then row "Foo 49". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move focus to a row a page below when focus starts on a row")
- Given a ListView of 100 items with style.overflow="auto" and focus on the first ActionButton of row "Foo 1", when PageDown is pressed twice, then focus moves to row "Foo 25" then row "Foo 49". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move focus to a row a page below when focus starts in the row cell")
- Given a ListView of 100 items with selectionMode="single" and row "Foo 15" clicked, when Home is pressed, then focus moves to row "Foo 1". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move focus to the first row when focus starts on a row")
- Given a ListView of 100 items with focus on the first ActionButton inside row "Foo 15", when Home is pressed, then focus moves to row "Foo 1". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move focus to the first row when focus starts in the row cell")
- Given a ListView of 100 items, when Tab focuses the list and End is pressed, then focus moves to row "Foo 100". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move focus to the last row when focus starts on a row")
- Given a ListView of 100 items with focus on the first ActionButton inside row "Foo 1", when End is pressed, then focus moves to row "Foo 100". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move focus to the last row when focus starts in the row cell")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="multiple" and focus on the first row via Tab, when Space is pressed, then onSelectionChange is called once with Set(['foo']), the row becomes aria-selected="true", and announce is called once with "Foo selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should select a row by pressing the Space key on a row")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="multiple" and focus on the first row via Tab, when Enter is pressed, then onSelectionChange is called once with Set(['foo']), the row becomes aria-selected="true", and announce is called once with "Foo selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should select a row by pressing the Enter key on a row")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="multiple" and an onAction, when the GridList tester triggers a row action on row 1 with interactionType keyboard (Enter), then onSelectionChange is not called and onAction is called once with 'bar'; a subsequent keyboard selection toggle of row 2 calls onSelectionChange once with Set(['baz']) and does not call onAction. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should trigger onAction when pressing Enter")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="multiple", onAction and defaultSelectedKeys=['foo'], when Tab focuses row 0 and Space is pressed, then onSelectionChange is called once and onAction is not called, so deselecting by keyboard does not fire the action. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should not trigger action when deselecting with keyboard")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="multiple", onAction and defaultSelectedKeys=['foo'] (so the list is already in selection mode), when Tab focuses row 0 and Enter is pressed, then neither onSelectionChange nor onAction is called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should not trigger action or selection when pressing Enter while in selection mode")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given selectionMode="multiple" with onHoverStart, onHoverChange, onHoverEnd and an isHovered render-prop class, when a row is hovered, then it gets data-hovered="true" and class "hover" and onHoverStart and onHoverChange each fire once; unhovering removes both and fires onHoverEnd once with onHoverChange at two calls. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support hover")
- Given a draggable GridList with selectionMode="none" (no selection and no action), when a row is hovered then unhovered, then data-hovered="true" appears and is removed, so draggable rows still show hover state. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should show hover state on draggable rows even when not selectable/actionable")
- Given a GridList with no selection, action or drag (non-interactive items), when a row is hovered, then it never gets data-hovered or class "hover" and onHoverStart, onHoverChange and onHoverEnd are never called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should not show hover state when item is not interactive")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" and an isPressed render-prop class, when MouseLeft is pressed down on a row, then it has data-pressed="true" and class "pressed", and releasing removes both. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support press state")
- Given a non-interactive GridList, when MouseLeft is pressed down and released on a row, then data-pressed and class "pressed" are never applied. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should not show press state when not interactive")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with the selection checkbox rendered as either Checkbox or CheckboxField (parameterized over 'Checkbox' and 'CheckboxField'), when the tester toggles row 0's selection, then the row gains aria-selected="true", class "selected" and a checked checkbox; toggling again clears aria-selected="true", the class and the checked state. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support selection state with %s")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with disabledKeys=['cat'], when the tester tries to toggle row 0's selection or trigger its row action, then both promises reject and throw. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support disabled state")
- Given a GridListItem with its own onAction, when the row is clicked, then that item's onAction is called once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support onAction on items")
- Given onAction on the GridList and onAction on the first item, when that row is clicked, then the list-level onAction is called with 'cat' and the item-level action is called once, so both fire. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support onAction on list and list items")
- Given a GridList with onScroll, when a scroll event is fired on the grid, then onScroll is called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support onScroll")
- Given selectionMode="single" without shouldSelectOnPressUp, when MouseLeft is pressed down on a row, then onSelectionChange has already fired once, and releasing does not fire it again. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should select an item on pressing down when shouldSelectOnPressUp is not provided")
- Given selectionMode="single" with shouldSelectOnPressUp={false}, when MouseLeft is pressed down on a row, then onSelectionChange fires once on press down and not again on release. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should select an item on pressing down when shouldSelectOnPressUp is false")
- Given selectionMode="single" with shouldSelectOnPressUp={true}, when MouseLeft is pressed down on a row, then onSelectionChange has not been called, and it fires once only on release. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should select an item on pressing up when shouldSelectOnPressUp is true")
- Given a GridList with onAction, onPressStart, onPressEnd, onPress and onClick on items, when the tester triggers a row action with interactionType mouse or keyboard (it.each over $interactionType mouse and keyboard), then onAction, onPressStart, onPressEnd, onPress and onClick are each called exactly once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support press events on items when using $interactionType")
- Given a GridList with selectionMode="multiple" using default arrow navigation and a row containing an input, when that input is clicked, then focus lands on the input and onSelectionChange is not called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should not trigger selection when clicking on a tabbable child in arrow navigation mode")
- Given a GridList with selectionMode="multiple" and either keyboardNavigationBehavior="tab" or layout="grid" with a row containing an input, when the input is clicked, then focus lands on the input and onSelectionChange is not called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should not trigger selection when clicking on a tabbable child element (%s)")
- Given a GridList with selectionMode="multiple" and either keyboardNavigationBehavior="tab" or layout="grid" whose rows contain no tabbable children, when row 0 is clicked, then onSelectionChange is called once with Set(['item1']). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should still trigger selection when clicking on a row with no tabbable children (%s)")
- Given a ListView whose rows contain two ActionButtons, when the second button in row Foo is clicked, then that button keeps focus (focus is not pulled to the row). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should retain focus on the pressed child")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="single", when the gridcell inside row Bar is clicked, then focus lands on the row Bar element rather than the cell. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should focus the row if the cell is pressed")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="single", when row Bar is clicked, then announce is called once with "Bar selected."; clicking again announces "Bar not selected." for a total of two calls. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should announce the selected or deselected row")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="multiple", when row Bar's checkbox is clicked, then onSelectionChange fires once with Set(['bar']), the row becomes aria-selected="true", and announce is called once with "Bar selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should select an item from checkbox")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="single", when row Bar's checkbox is clicked then row Baz's checkbox, then selection replaces rather than adds: Bar goes aria-selected="false", Baz goes "true", and onSelectionChange reports Set(['baz']). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should only allow one item to be selected in single selection")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="multiple", when row Bar's checkbox then row Baz's checkbox are clicked, then both rows are aria-selected="true", onSelectionChange reports Set(['bar','baz']), and announce says "Baz selected. 2 items selected."; clicking Baz's checkbox again announces "Baz not selected. 1 item selected." for three announce calls total. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should allow multiple items to be selected in multiple selection")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="multiple" and onAction, when the tester triggers a row action on row 1 with the mouse, then onSelectionChange is not called and onAction is called once with 'bar'; afterwards toggling row 1's selection calls onSelectionChange once with Set(['bar']) and toggling row 2 gives Set(['bar','baz']). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should trigger onAction when clicking items with the mouse")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="multiple" and onAction, when a row action is triggered on row 1 and then the tester switches interactionType to touch and toggles row 2's selection, then onAction fired once with 'bar' without any selection change, and the touch toggles produce Set(['bar']) then Set(['bar','baz']). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should trigger onAction when clicking items with touch")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="multiple", onAction and checkbox selection under installPointerEvent, when pointerdown with pointerType touch is fired on row 1 and timers advance 800ms, then onSelectionChange fires with Set(['bar']) and onAction is never called; a following touch on row 2 gives Set(['bar','baz']), and deselecting both rows by touch ends with Set([]) and onAction still uncalled. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should support long press to enter selection mode on touch")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="multiple", onAction and defaultSelectedKeys=['foo'], when row 0 is clicked (deselecting it), then onSelectionChange fires once and onAction is not called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should not trigger action when deselecting with mouse")
- Given a ListView with onAction and disabledKeys=['foo'], when row 0 is clicked, then onAction is not called; clicking row 1 calls onAction once. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should not trigger actions when a row is disabled")
- Given a ListView with onAction, disabledKeys=['foo'] and disabledBehavior="selection", when the disabled row 0 is clicked, then onAction is called once, so disabledBehavior="selection" still allows actions. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should trigger actions when a disabledBehavior="selection"")
- Given a ListView with selectionStyle="highlight", selectionMode="multiple" and navigator.userAgent mocked to 'Android' (screen reader single tap), when row 1's text is clicked with pointerType touch and width/height 0, then onSelectionChange fires with Set(['bar']), the row becomes aria-selected="true", and announce says "Bar selected."; a simulated Android TalkBack double tap on row 2 (pointerdown/pointerup with pointerType mouse, pressure 0, detail 0, then click with detail 1) adds 'baz' and announces "Baz selected. 2 items selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should support single tap to perform row selection with screen reader if onAction isn't provided")
- Given the same Android-mocked highlight ListView but with onAction provided, when a zero-size touch pointerdown/mousedown/pointerup/mouseup/click sequence hits row 1, then onSelectionChange is not called and onAction is called once with 'bar'; the simulated TalkBack double tap on row 2 calls onAction with 'baz' for two calls total and announce is never called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should support single tap to perform onAction with screen reader")
- Given a ListView with selectionStyle="highlight", selectionMode="multiple" and onAction, when Ctrl+click selects row Bar, then onSelectionChange gives Set(['bar']), the row is aria-selected="true", onAction has not fired, and announce says "Bar selected."; pressing Space on the already-selected row leaves onSelectionChange at one call and onAction at zero, and pressing Enter leaves onSelectionChange at one call while calling onAction once with 'bar', with announce still at one call. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should not call onSelectionChange when hitting Space/Enter on the currently selected row")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="none", selectionStyle="highlight" and onAction, when row 0 is clicked, then announce is not called, onSelectionChange is not called, and onAction is called once with 'foo'. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should perform onAction on single click with selectionMode: none")
- Given a ListView with selectionStyle="highlight", selectionMode="multiple", onAction and window.ontouchstart defined under installPointerEvent, when pointerdown with pointerType touch is fired on row 0, then the text "Long press to enter selection mode." is rendered and the grid's aria-describedby contains that element's id, while announce, onSelectionChange and onAction have not fired. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should support long press to enter selection mode on touch")
- Given that same long press in progress, when timers advance 800ms, then announce says "Foo selected.", onSelectionChange reports Set(['foo']), onAction is not called, and a checkbox is now rendered inside row 0. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should support long press to enter selection mode on touch")
- Given selection mode entered by long press, when a TouchA tap hits row 1, then announce says "Bar selected. 2 items selected." and onSelectionChange reports Set(['foo','bar']); tapping row 0 announces "Foo not selected. 1 item selected." and tapping row 1 announces "Bar not selected.", ending with Set([]), onAction never called, and no checkbox remaining in row 0. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should support long press to enter selection mode on touch")
- Given a GridList with selectionMode="none" whose items have href, then no row is an A element and every row has a data-href attribute; when the row is activated by mouse click or by Enter keydown/keyup (describe.each over 'mouse' and 'keyboard'), then the document click handler fires once with target instanceof HTMLAnchorElement and target.href "https://google.com/". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support links with selectionMode="none"")
- Given a GridList with selectionMode "single" or "multiple" (default toggle behavior) whose items have href and a selection Checkbox, when row 0 is activated by click or Enter, then rows are not A elements but have data-href and the click handler fires once with an HTMLAnchorElement whose href is "https://google.com/"; clicking row 0's checkbox then sets aria-selected="true", and activating row 1 with Space leaves the click count at 1 while setting row 1 aria-selected="true", parameterized over mouse and keyboard. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support links with selectionBehavior="toggle" selectionMode="%s"")
- Given a GridList with selectionBehavior="replace" and selectionMode "single" or "multiple" whose items have href, when row 0 is single clicked (mouse) or Space is pressed (keyboard, twice for single selection because replace follows focus), then no navigation happens and row 0 is aria-selected="true"; a double click (mouse) or Enter (keyboard) then navigates, firing the click handler once with an HTMLAnchorElement href "https://google.com/". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support links with selectionBehavior="replace" selectionMode="%s"")
- Given a RouterProvider with navigate and useHref prefixing "/base", and a GridListItem with href="/foo" and routerOptions={{foo: 'bar'}}, then the row has data-href="/base/foo", and activating it by click or Enter calls navigate with ('/foo', {foo: 'bar'}). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should work with RouterProvider")
- Given a ListView with selectionMode="none" whose Items have href, then no row is an A element and every row has data-href; activating row 0 by click or by Enter keydown/keyup fires the document click handler once with target instanceof HTMLAnchorElement and href "https://google.com/". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should support links with selectionMode="none"")
- Given a ListView with default checkbox selection and selectionMode "single" or "multiple" whose Items have href, when row 0 is activated by click or Enter, then the click handler fires once with an HTMLAnchorElement href "https://google.com/"; clicking row 0's checkbox sets aria-selected="true", and activating row 1 with Space leaves the click count at 1 while setting row 1 aria-selected="true". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should support links with selectionStyle="checkbox" selectionMode="%s"")
- Given a ListView with selectionStyle="highlight" and selectionMode "single" or "multiple" whose Items have href, when row 0 is single clicked or Space is pressed (twice for single selection since replace follows focus), then the click handler has not fired and row 0 is aria-selected="true"; a double click or Enter then fires it once with an HTMLAnchorElement href "https://google.com/". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should support links with selectionStyle="highlight" selectionMode="%s"")
- Given a Provider with router={{navigate}} and a ListView Item with href="/one" and routerOptions={{foo: 'bar'}}, when row 0 is activated by click or Enter, then navigate is called with ('/one', {foo: 'bar'}); activating the second Item, whose href is the external "https://adobe.com", does not call navigate and instead fires the document click handler once. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "works with RouterProvider")

### Focus management

- Given autoFocus on a GridList, then document.activeElement is the role="grid" element itself. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support autoFocus")
- Given selectionMode="single", selectionBehavior="replace" and autoFocus set to "first" or "last" (it.each over autoFocus | index with 'first'|0 and 'last'|2), then the row at that index has focus and aria-selected="true", so autofocus selects with selectOnFocus. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "selects the autofocused row when selectOnFocus with autoFocus=$autoFocus")
- Given selectionMode="none", selectionBehavior="replace" and autoFocus="first", then row 0 has focus but has no aria-selected attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "does not select the autofocused row when selectionMode="none"")
- Given selectionMode="multiple", selectionBehavior="replace", defaultSelectedKeys="all" and autoFocus="first", then row 0 has focus and every row stays aria-selected="true", so autofocus does not collapse an existing "all" selection. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "does not change an existing "all" selection when autofocusing")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" and an isFocusVisible render-prop class, when Tab moves focus to row 0, then it has data-focus-visible="true" and class "focus"; tabbing away removes both. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support focus ring")
- Given the ListViewActions FocusExample where each row has a remove button and some rows are disabled, when the button in row 3 is clicked so row 3 is removed and row 4 is aria-disabled="true", then focus moves to the row now at index 4 rather than the disabled one. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move focus to the next item that is not disabled when the focused item is removed")
- Given the FocusExample with focus on the last row's button, when that row is repeatedly removed by clicking its button, then focus each time lands on the new last row; on the final removal focus lands on rows[length - 2] because the final row is aria-disabled="true". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move focus to the next item that is not disabled when the focused item is removed")
- Given a ListView with loadingState="loading" and no items (so no tabbable children), when Tab is pressed, then document.activeElement is the role="grid" element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should allow you to tab to ListView body if loading (no tabbable children)")
- Given an ActionButton followed by an empty ListView whose renderEmptyState contains a link, when Tab is pressed twice, then focus goes to the button and then into the empty state's link. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should allow you to tab into ListView body if empty with link")
- Given a 20 item ListView with selectionStyle="highlight", height 60px and clientHeight forced to 60, when Tab focuses the list and ArrowDown is pressed three times with scrollTop updated between each, then scrollIntoView (mocked module) is called with (grid, row) for Item 1, Item 2 and Item 3 in turn; three ArrowUps then call it for Item 2, Item 1 and Item 0. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should scroll to a row when it is focused")
- Given the same 20 item highlight ListView, when row "Item 1" is focused programmatically, then it is document.activeElement and scrollIntoView is called with (grid, activeElement). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should scroll to a row when it is focused")
- Given the same 20 item highlight ListView with row "Item 0" focused, when a scroll event fires on the grid body, then focus remains on that row and the row is not recycled by the virtualizer (the "Item 0" text node is still row.firstElementChild.firstElementChild.firstElementChild); a following ArrowDown focuses "Item 1" and calls scrollIntoView with (body, activeElement). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should scroll to a row when it is focused off screen")

### RTL and i18n (locale-aware parsing, number formats, RTL arrow keys)

- Given a GridList inside I18nProvider locale="ar-AE" with one item using focusMode="child" and two buttons, when ArrowLeft is pressed from the first button, then focus advances forward to the last button and then wraps to the row element, while ArrowRight from the row wraps backward to the last child. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "ArrowLeft/Right RTL cycle: ArrowLeft advances forward, ArrowRight wraps to last child")
- Given a ListView rendered with locale="ar-AE" and focus set on button2 of row Foo by clicking (a press is needed to set the interaction modality, otherwise useSelectableCollection treats it as a tab), when ArrowRight is pressed, then focus moves backward to button1. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move focus to previous cell in RTL")
- Given a ListView rendered with locale="ar-AE" and focus set on button1 of row Foo by clicking, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then focus moves forward to button2. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should move focus to next cell in RTL")

### SSR and hydration

- Given a GridList server rendered inside React.StrictMode with three GridListItems and a fourth conditional item hidden, then the server HTML contains rows with text ['Left','Middle','Right'], the hydrated DOM matches, and clicking the Show button adds the extra row so the rows become ['Left','Middle','Extra','Right']. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.ssr.test.js: "should render without errors")
- Given a ListView with three Items server rendered inside a Provider with the default theme, then testSSR completes without errors or hydration mismatches. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.ssr.test.js: "should render without errors")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given refs passed to GridList and GridListItem, then both ref.current values are instances of HTMLElement. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support refs")
- Given a GridList with selectionMode="multiple" whose first row contains a DialogTrigger opening a Modal with its own Checkbox, when the trigger button is clicked, then the dialog's checkbox is in the document, so the selection checkbox context is not propagated into other cells. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should not propagate the checkbox context from selection into other cells")
- Given a GridList with keyboardNavigationBehavior="Tab" containing an item with id "1" that itself contains a nested GridList with an item also using id "1", then every element with data-key has a unique data-collection plus data-key pair, so colliding keys across nested collections do not collide. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support nested collections with colliding keys")
- Given a virtualized GridList of 50 items with ListLayout rowHeight 25 and clientWidth/clientHeight mocked to 100, then only 7 rows render, Item 0 through Item 6. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support virtualizer")
- Given that virtualized GridList, when scrollTop is set to 200 and a scroll event fires, then 8 rows render, Item 7 through Item 14. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support virtualizer")
- Given an async GridList with a GridListLoadMoreItem and isLoading, then 4 rows render with the fourth having text content "Loading...", and the loadMoreSentinel test id's parent element has the inert attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should render the loading element when loading")
- Given an async GridList with three items and isLoading false, then only 3 rows render, no "Loading..." text exists, and the loadMoreSentinel is still in the document. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should render the sentinel but not the loading indicator when not loading")
- Given an async GridList with an empty items array and renderEmptyState, then one row renders with text "empty state", no "Loading..." text exists, and the sentinel is present. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should properly render the renderEmptyState if gridlist is empty")
- Given that empty async GridList rerendered with isLoading, then 2 rows render with the second being the "empty state" row, "Loading..." text is present, and the sentinel remains, so the loader renders even when the list is empty. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should properly render the renderEmptyState if gridlist is empty")
- Given a mocked IntersectionObserver and an async GridList with isLoading, then observe was last called with the loadMoreSentinel element and onLoadMore has not fired; triggering the observer callback with isIntersecting true calls onLoadMore once, and after rerendering without isLoading the sentinel is observed again and a second intersection calls onLoadMore a second time, so loadMore fires on intersection regardless of loading state. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should only fire loadMore when intersection is detected regardless of loading state")
- Given a virtualized async GridList of 50 items with ListLayout rowHeight 25 and loaderHeight 30 and loadingState="loadingMore", then 8 rows render, the eighth has text "Loading..." and no aria-rowindex, its parent style has top "1250px" (50 items times 25px) and height "30px", and the sentinel's parent element has the inert attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should always render the sentinel even when virtualized")
- Given the same virtualized async GridList with no loading state, then 7 rows render, no "Loading..." text exists, and the sentinel's grandparent style has top "1250px" and height "0px" with inert on the sentinel's parent, so no room is reserved for the loader. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should not reserve room for the loader if isLoading is false")
- Given that virtualized async GridList rerendered with an empty items array, then one row renders with text "empty state", no "Loading..." text exists, and the sentinel's grandparent style has top "0px" and height "0px". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should not reserve room for the loader if isLoading is false")
- Given that virtualized async GridList rerendered with an empty items array and loadingState="loading", then one row renders with text "loading" and the sentinel's grandparent style has top "0px" and height "0px". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should not reserve room for the loader if isLoading is false")
- Given a virtualized async GridList with no items and loadingState="loading", then one row renders with aria-rowindex="1" and text "loading". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should have the correct row indicies after loading more items")
- Given that list rerendered with 50 items and no loading state, then 7 rows render with no "loading" text and aria-rowindex values 1 through 7. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should have the correct row indicies after loading more items")
- Given that list rerendered with 50 items and loadingState="loadingMore", then 8 rows render, the loader row at index 7 has no aria-rowindex, and all other rows keep sequential aria-rowindex values. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should have the correct row indicies after loading more items")
- Given a draggable GridList, then the first button inside a row (slot="drag") has aria-label "Drag Cat". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.test.js: "should support drag button slot")
- Given a ListView with loadingState="loading" and no items, then the first row's parent node has style.height "1000px" (matching the mocked clientHeight) and the row contains a role="progressbar". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should display loading affordance with proper height (isLoading)")
- Given a ListView with three items and loadingState="loadingMore", then a role="progressbar" exists and its third ancestor has style.height "40px" (the mocked scrollHeight). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should display loading affordance with proper height (isLoadingMore)")
- Given a ListView with renderEmptyState and no children, then the text "No results" is rendered; the test awaits a resolved promise first to let the MutationObserver in useHasTabbableChild settle and avoid act warnings. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should render empty state")
- Given a ListView of 20 items with width 250px and height 60px but clientWidth, clientHeight and scrollHeight all mocked to 0, then rendering completes without an infinite loop and the grid's first child is an empty DOM element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/list/ListView.test.js: "should render and not infinite loop")
- Given a real browser (vitest-browser-react) GridList with layout="grid", selectionMode="single", a 3x3 CSS grid and 9 items, when the tester toggles selection on row 5, then row 5 has aria-selected="true" and is document.activeElement; the same holds after toggling row 0 and then row 8, parameterized over interactionType mouse and keyboard. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.browser.test.tsx: "selects a row via $interactionType in real browser grid layout")
- Given a virtualized GridList with GridLayout inside a container, when the container's display is toggled to none and back twice and again, then tester.getRows().length stays greater than zero each time, so the virtualizer re-measures and re-renders after display:none. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/GridList.browser.test.tsx: "virtualizer renders items after toggling display:none")

## table

### Roles and attributes

- Given a Table with a TableHeader, three Columns and three Rows, when rendered with no className, then the table has class "react-aria-Table", every row has class "react-aria-Row", there are exactly 2 rowgroups with classes "react-aria-TableHeader" and "react-aria-TableBody", every column has class "react-aria-Column", and every rowheader and gridcell has class "react-aria-Cell". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should render with default classes")
- Given className passed to Table, TableHeader, Column, TableBody, Row and Cell, when rendered, then the grid has class "table", body rows have class "row", the two rowgroups have classes "table-header" and "table-body", columnheaders have class "column", and rowheaders and gridcells have class "cell". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should render with custom classes")
- Given data-testid passed to Table, TableHeader, Column, TableBody, Row and Cell, when rendered, then each corresponding element carries that data-testid, including both rowgroups ("table-header", "table-body"), all columnheaders, all rowheaders and all gridcells. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support DOM props")
- Given a render prop on Table, TableHeader, Column, TableBody, Row and Cell that renders table, thead, th, tbody, tr and td with data-custom="true", when rendered, then the grid, both rowgroups, every body row, every columnheader, every rowheader and every gridcell have data-custom="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support custom render function")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with the selection checkbox rendered as either Checkbox or CheckboxField, when rendered, then every row (header row included) contains one unchecked checkbox and the first checkbox has aria-label "Select All". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should render checkboxes for selection using %s", it.each(['Checkbox', 'CheckboxField']))
- Given selectionMode="multiple" with disabledKeys=['2'] and disabledBehavior="all", when rendered, then the second row has aria-disabled="true", has class "disabled", and the checkbox inside it is disabled. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support disabled state")
- Given a Table with selectionMode="multiple", disabledBehavior="all" and isDisabled on the middle Row, when rendered, then that row has aria-disabled="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support isDisabled prop on rows")
- Given sortDescriptor={{column: 'name', direction: 'ascending'}} and allowsSorting on every column, when rendered, then the first columnheader has aria-sort="ascending" and text content "▲" while the other two have aria-sort="none" and no "▲". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support sorting")
- Given a TableBody with renderEmptyState={() => 'No results'} and no children, when rendered, then the body rowgroup has data-empty="true" and the single rowheader has text content "No results". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support empty state")
- Given four Columns and Cells whose children are a function of columnIndex, when rendered, then the cells render "cell index: 0" through "cell index: 3" and carry data-column-index "0" through "3". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support column index in render props")
- Given a first row whose first Cell has colSpan={2} and a second row with four plain cells, when rendered, then the first row's cells report columnIndex 0, 2, 3 with matching data-column-index, and the second row's cells report 0, 1, 2, 3 with matching data-column-index. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support colspan with cell index")
- Given the TableCellColSpanWithVariousSpansExample story, when rendered, then there are 8 rows; row 1 has 3 cells where the spanning cell has colspan="2" and no aria-colindex and the trailing cell has aria-colindex="4"; row 3 has a single cell with colspan="4" and no aria-colindex; row 5 has 2 cells where the first has colspan="3" and the second has aria-colindex="4". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should render table with colSpans")
- Given a TableFooter alongside TableHeader and TableBody, when rendered, then there are 3 rowgroups with tagNames THEAD, TBODY and TFOOT and 8 rows in total. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support table footer")
- Given three TableBody elements plus a TableFooter, when rendered, then there are 5 rowgroups (THEAD then three TBODY then the footer), 11 rows total, 3 rows in the first body, 3 in the second and 4 in the third, and tableTester.getFooterRows() returns 1 row with text content "Blah". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support multiple table bodies")
- Given a Table wrapped in Virtualizer with TableLayout and rowHeight 25 and 50 items, when rendered with clientWidth and clientHeight mocked to 100, then only 7 rows render ("FooBar" plus Foo 0 through Foo 5) and every rendered row has an aria-rowindex attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support virtualizer")
- Given a TableLoadMoreItem with isLoadingMore, when rendered, then there are 7 rows, the loader row's rowheader has colspan="3", it contains a progressbar with aria-label "loading", and the preceding sentinel row has the inert attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should render the load more element with the expected attributes")
- Given a load more table that is not loading, when rendered, then there are 6 rows, the last row (sentinel) has the inert attribute, and no progressbar is present. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should still render the sentinel, but not render the spinner if it isnt loading")
- Given a Table with a TableLoadMoreItem and isLoading, when rendered, then tableTester.getRows() returns 12 rows, the last row has text content "spinner", and the loadMoreSentinel is inside an element with the inert attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should render the loading element when loading")
- Given the same table without isLoading, when rendered, then there are 11 rows, no "spinner" text, and the loadMoreSentinel is still in the document. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should render the sentinel but not the loading indicator when not loading")
- Given a virtualized load more table with loadingState="loadingMore" and 50 items of rowHeight 25 and loaderHeight 30, when rendered, then 7 rows render, the loader row has text "spinner" and no aria-rowindex, its virtualizer wrapper has top 1250px and height 30px, and the sentinel sits inside an inert element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should always render the sentinel even when virtualized")
- Given a virtualized load more table that is not loading, when rendered with 50 items, then 6 rows render with no "spinner", and the sentinel's presentation wrapper has top 1250px and height 0px and is inert; when rerendered with no items, then 1 row renders with text "No results" and the sentinel wrapper has top 0px and height 0px; when rerendered with no items and loadingState="loading", then 1 row renders with text "loading" and the sentinel wrapper stays at top 0px and height 0px. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not reserve room for the loader if isLoading is false")
- Given a virtualized load more table starting empty with loadingState="loading", when rerendered with 50 items and then with loadingState="loadingMore", then the empty/loading row never has aria-rowindex, the 6 loaded rows get aria-rowindex 2 through 7, and after switching to loadingMore there are 7 rows where the loader row still has no aria-rowindex and the rest keep aria-rowindex index+2. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should have the correct row indicies after loading more items")
- Given an empty table rendered with isLoading, when rendered, then there are 2 rows, the body rowgroup has data-empty="true", and the loader row contains a progressbar with aria-label "loading"; when rerendered without isLoading, then there are still 2 rows, the body keeps data-empty="true", and the second row has text content "No results" instead of the spinner. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not render no results state and the loader at the same time")
- Given a load more table with items=[] and renderEmptyState, when rendered, then there are 2 rows, the second has text "No results", no "spinner" is rendered, the loadMoreSentinel is present, the body rowgroup has data-empty="true" and the select all checkbox is disabled; when rerendered with isLoading, then there are 3 rows, the third has "No results", "spinner" is present, data-empty stays "true" and select all stays disabled. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should properly render the renderEmptyState if table is empty")
- Given a DraggableTable with isDisabled, when rendered, then every button is disabled, the grid has neither data-allows-dragging="true" nor draggable="true", and no row has draggable="true". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support disabled drag and drop")
- Given a DraggableTable, when rendered, then the first button (the Button with slot="drag") has aria-label "Drag Games". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support drag button slot")
- Given useTable with data-testid="test-id" and id="table-id" on the table, when rendered, then the element found by test id has id "table-id". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/table/useTable.test.tsx: "sets the passed id")
- Given a static TableView with three Columns and two Rows, when rendered, then the container has role grid, is visible, keeps aria-label "Table" and the passed data-testid, and has aria-rowcount 3 and aria-colcount 3. - Given a static TableView with no selection, when rendered, then the body rowgroup holds two rows with aria-rowindex 2 and 3, each first cell has role rowheader with aria-colindex 1, each row has aria-labelledby pointing at the span id inside its rowheader, and the second row has no aria-selected attribute.
