- Given a table with selectionMode="single", when the first columnheader is inspected, then it does not have aria-disabled "true", its firstElementChild (a VisuallyHidden span) is visible, the inner input[type=checkbox] is not visible, that input has aria-label "Select" and the VisuallyHidden text equals that aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should contain a hidden checkbox and VisuallyHidden accessible text")
- Given a TableView with selectionMode="multiple", two columns and a TableBody with loadingState="loading" and no children, when rendered, then the table has two rows, the body row has aria-rowindex 2 and its single rowheader has aria-colspan "3" (two columns plus the checkbox column) and holds a visible progressbar with aria-label "Loading…" and no aria-valuenow; rerendering with a loaded table gives three rows and removes the spinner from the document. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should display a spinner when loading")
- Given a TableView with two columns, two rows and loadingState="loadingMore", when rendered, then there are four rows, the last has aria-rowindex 4 and its rowheader has aria-colspan "2" and holds a visible progressbar with aria-label "Loading more…" and no aria-valuenow; rerendering with a loaded table drops back to three rows and removes the spinner. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should display a spinner at the bottom when loading more")
- Given a TableView with two rows and loadingState="filtering", when rendered, then the grid contains no progressbar at all. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should not display a spinner when filtering")
- Given a TableView whose Foo and Bar Columns have allowsSorting and Baz does not, when rendered with no sortDescriptor, then Foo and Bar have aria-sort "none" and an aria-describedby pointing at an element whose text is "sortable column", while Baz has neither aria-sort nor aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should set the proper aria-describedby and aria-sort on sortable column headers")
- Given a TableView with sortDescriptor {column: 'bar', direction: 'ascending'}, when rendered, then Foo has aria-sort "none", Bar has aria-sort "ascending", Baz has none, and both sortable headers keep an aria-describedby whose target text is "sortable column". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should set the proper aria-describedby and aria-sort on an ascending sorted column header")
- Given a TableView with sortDescriptor {column: 'bar', direction: 'descending'}, when rendered, then Foo has aria-sort "none", Bar has aria-sort "descending", Baz has none, and both sortable headers keep an aria-describedby whose target text is "sortable column". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should set the proper aria-describedby and aria-sort on an descending sorted column header")
- Given the ExampleSortTable (initial ascending sort on Bar) with navigator.userAgent mocked to 'Android', when rendered, then no columnheader has aria-sort at all, the Foo header's description reads "sortable column" and the Bar header's reads "sortable column, ascending", so the direction is folded into aria-describedby instead; toggling sort on column 1 through the test-utils tester changes that text to "sortable column, descending". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should add sort direction info to the column header's aria-describedby for Android")
- Given a TableView with two columns, an empty TableBody and renderEmptyState returning an h3 "No results", when rendered (after awaiting the MutationObserver in useHasTabbableChild), then the grid has two rows, the body row has aria-rowindex 2 and its rowheader has aria-colspan "2" and holds a visible heading with text "No results"; rerendering with a populated table gives three rows and removes the heading from the document. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should display an empty state when there are no items")
- Given the EmptyStateStory table, when rendered, then the third columnheader has tabindex "-1" and the button inside it has aria-disabled "true", so keyboard navigation inside an empty table is switched off. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should disable keyboard navigation within the table")
- Given a TableView with `UNSTABLE_allowsExpandableRows` and three nested levels, when rendered, then the treegrid reports `aria-rowcount="5"` and `aria-colcount="3"`, has two rowgroups and one header row, the header row has no aria-rowindex, and each column header has a 1-based `aria-colindex`, no aria-sort, and no aria-describedby. Run as `it.each` over the static and dynamic table renderers. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "renders a $Name expandable rows table")
- Given the same expandable table, when each row is inspected, then a parent row has `aria-expanded="true"`, `aria-level`, `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize` reflecting its position among its siblings, no `aria-rowindex`, an `aria-labelledby` pointing at its row header's text span, a rowheader at `aria-colindex="1"`, and its other cells at colindex 2 and 3; a leaf row has no aria-expanded and `aria-level="3"`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "renders a $Name expandable rows table")
- Given an expandable table with multiple selection, when rendered, then the treegrid has `aria-multiselectable="true"` and `aria-colcount="4"`, the header row starts with a checkbox column whose checkbox has `aria-label="Select All"`, each row's checkbox has `aria-label="Select"` plus an aria-labelledby of "<checkboxId> <rowTextId>", and the rowheader shifts to `aria-colindex="2"`. Run as `it.each` over both renderers. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "renders a $Name expandable rows table with selection")
- Given a row whose parent is not in `expandedKeys`, when rendered, then that child row is not in the DOM at all. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "shouldn't render a child row if its parent isn't included in the expanded keys")
- Given an expandable table with selection, when a row is inspected, then the expand chevron lives inside the first rowheader cell (at `aria-colindex="2"`) with `aria-label="Collapse"` when expanded, not in its own column. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should place the chevron cell on the first row header")
- Given an empty expandable table, when rendered, then the empty state renders with the proper aria attributes. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should display an empty state with the proper aria attributes")
- Given a loading expandable table, when rendered, then a spinner row renders with the expected attributes. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should render a spinner row with the proper attributes when loading")

### Keyboard

- Given selectionMode="multiple" with disabledKeys=['2'] and disabledBehavior="all", when Tab focuses the first row and ArrowDown is fired, then focus skips the disabled row and lands on the third row, and tableTester.toggleRowSelection({row: 1}) and tableTester.triggerRowAction({row: 1}) both reject with an error. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support disabled state")
- Given a Table with disabledBehavior="all" and isDisabled on the middle Row, when Tab focuses the first body row and ArrowDown is pressed, then focus moves to the third body row, skipping the disabled one. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support isDisabled prop on rows")
- Given the colSpan example table, when navigating with ArrowRight twice then ArrowDown and ArrowUp repeatedly across rows with different colspans, then focus always lands on the cell covering the same column index, including landing on the single spanning rowheader of rows 3 and 5 and returning to gridcell index 2 of row 4 when coming up from a spanning cell. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should focus to the same colIndex when moving focus up or down")
- Given a Table with a TableFooter and 8 rows, when Tab focuses the table and ArrowDown is pressed through every row, then focus visits each row in order including the footer row, and pressing ArrowUp back through them returns focus to each row in reverse order. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support table footer")
- Given the same footer table inside a Virtualizer with TableLayout and clientWidth/clientHeight mocked to 1000, when Tab then ArrowDown walks all 8 rows and ArrowUp walks back, then focus visits every row in order and in reverse. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support table footer with virtualizer")
- Given three TableBody elements plus a TableFooter (11 rows), when Tab then ArrowDown walks all rows and ArrowUp walks back, then focus visits every row across all bodies and the footer in order and in reverse. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support multiple table bodies")
- Given a virtualized table of 50 rows, when Tab then End is pressed, then the virtualizer renders 9 rows and the last rendered row is "Foo 49Bar 49". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support virtualizer")
- Given a load more table with isLoadingMore, when Tab focuses the first row and ArrowDown is pressed three times then once more, then focus stops on the last real row (rows[4]) and never reaches the loader row, and a following ArrowUp moves to rows[3], proving the focused key never shifted to the loader. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not focus the load more row when using ArrowDown")
- Given a load more table with isLoadingMore, when Tab then End is pressed, then focus lands on the last real row (rows[4]) rather than the loader, and a following ArrowUp moves to rows[3]. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not focus the load more row when using End")
- Given a load more table with isLoadingMore, when Tab then PageDown is pressed, then focus lands on rows[4] and ArrowUp moves to rows[3]; and with a cell focused, ArrowRight focuses the rowheader of rows[3], ArrowUp focuses the rowheader of rows[2], and PageDown focuses the rowheader of rows[4]. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not focus the load more row when using PageDown")
- Given a Table with keyboardNavigationBehavior="tab" whose last cell contains an input and a button, when Tab focuses the first row, ArrowLeft moves to the last cell and Tab is pressed, then focus moves to the input labelled "Games notes" (the first tabbable child). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "Tab from a focused cell moves focus to the first tabbable child")
- Given the tab mode table between a Before and an After button, when focus is on a rowheader with no tabbable children and Tab is pressed, then focus leaves the table and lands on the After button; and when focus is on the last cell, Tab moves to the input, Tab again to the "Button next to input", and Tab again exits to the After button. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "Tab from a cell with no tabbable children or from the last child in a cell exits the table")
- Given the tab mode table with focus on the input inside the last cell, when Shift+Tab is pressed, then focus returns to that cell element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "Shift+Tab from a child returns focus to the cell")
- Given the tab mode table with focus on the "Games notes" input, when ArrowDown, ArrowUp, ArrowRight and ArrowLeft are pressed, then focus stays on the input for all four keys. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not navigate to next cell when arrow keys are pressed while a text input child has focus")
- Given the tab mode table with selectionMode="multiple" and focus on the "Games notes" input, when Space is pressed then Enter, then the input value becomes " " and onSelectionChange is never called for either key. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not trigger selection when pressing Space or Enter in a text input child")
- Given the tab mode table with focusMode="child" on the last cell, when Tab focuses the row and ArrowLeft navigates left, then focus lands directly on the "Button next to input" because ArrowLeft uses childFocusStrategy "last". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "arrow navigating to a focusMode="child" cell focuses the child directly")
- Given focusMode="child" plus allowsArrowNavigation on the last cell, when ArrowLeft focuses the "Button next to input" and ArrowDown is pressed, then focus moves to the "Program Files notes" input in the next row. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "allowsArrowNavigation allows arrow key row navigation when focused on child")
- Given focusMode="child" on the last cell with focus on the "Button next to input", when Shift+Tab is pressed, then focus moves to the "Games notes" input, and a second Shift+Tab moves focus to document.body, never returning to the cell element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "Shift+Tab from a focusMode="child" child skips the cell and does not return to it")
- Given cells containing two buttons each in default arrow navigation mode, when Tab then ArrowRight twice focuses "R1C2 first", then ArrowRight focuses "R1C2 last", ArrowRight again crosses to "R1C3 first", and ArrowLeft crosses back to "R1C2 last". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "default focusMode: ArrowRight crosses from last child to first child of next cell, ArrowLeft reverses")
- Given cells with focusMode="cell" containing two buttons each, when Tab then ArrowRight twice, then the col2 gridcell element itself is focused; ArrowRight enters "R1C2 first", ArrowRight advances to "R1C2 last", ArrowLeft retreats to "R1C2 first", ArrowLeft returns to the col2 cell element rather than the previous cell; ArrowRight three more times reaches the col3 cell element, ArrowRight enters "R1C3 first", ArrowLeft returns to the col3 cell element, and ArrowLeft then moves to the col2 cell element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "arrow navigation with focusMode="cell": cell element stays focused on navigate, arrows enter/exit children within cell")
- Given a DraggableTable with renderDropIndicator, when Tab, ArrowRight and Enter start a keyboard drag and ArrowDown moves the drop target, then the focused drop indicator button changes to aria-label "Insert between Program Files and bootmgr", rows[3] gains data-drop-target="true" while rows[0] and rows[2] lose it, and pressing Enter calls onReorder once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should render drop indicators")
- Given a draggable table where the middle row is disabled, when a keyboard drag is started with Tab, ArrowRight and Enter, then the first drop target is "Insert between Games and Program Files", ArrowDown moves to "Insert between Program Files and bootmgr", and ArrowDown again moves to "Insert after bootmgr", so positions around the disabled row are not skipped; Escape then cancels the drag. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not skip drop positions before/after a disabled item")
- Given the DndTableExample story, when a keyboard drag is started and Tab moves to the second table's "Drop on" target, then repeated ArrowDown cycles through "Insert before Pictures" through "Insert after Adobe Dreamweaver", Home returns to "Drop on", repeated ArrowUp walks the same list in reverse, End focuses "Insert after Adobe Dreamweaver", and ArrowDown from there wraps back to "Drop on". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "support drop target keyboard navigation")
- Given two DraggableTables where the second has onItemDrop, when a keyboard drag is started from the first, then the second table renders 3 rows whose buttons are labelled "Drop on Games", "Drop on Program Files" and "Drop on bootmgr", the element after the first row has data-drop-target="true", focus is on the first drop button, and Enter calls onItemDrop once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support dropping on rows")
- Given two DraggableTables where the second has onRootDrop, when a keyboard drag is started from the first, then the second table renders 1 row whose button has aria-label "Drop on", that button has focus, the grid has data-drop-target="true", and Enter calls onRootDrop once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support dropping on the root")
- Given the DndTableExample story with 7 rows and no selection in the second table, when a keyboard drag inserts an item before Pictures and the onInsert promise resolves, then the second table has 8 rows and exactly 1 selected row. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should select dropped item")
- Given a selection table with a loader row (isLoading) and drag and drop, when Tab and ArrowRight focus the drag button and Enter starts a keyboard drag, then 4 rows remain (3 drop indicators plus the dragged row), the first indicator button is labelled "Insert before Adobe Photoshop", and Escape cancels without crashing. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not crash when dragging over the loader")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given selectionMode="multiple" with the selection checkbox rendered as Checkbox or CheckboxField, when the "Select All" checkbox is clicked, then every row's checkbox becomes checked. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should render checkboxes for selection using %s", it.each(['Checkbox', 'CheckboxField']))
- Given columns with allowsSorting and a className function of isHovered, when the first columnheader is hovered, then it gains data-hovered="true" and class "hover", and unhovering removes both. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support column hover when sorting is allowed")
- Given columns without allowsSorting, when the first columnheader is hovered, then it gains neither data-hovered nor class "hover". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not show column hover state when column is not sortable")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" and hover handlers on rows, when the first body row is hovered, then it gains data-hovered="true" and class "hover" and onHoverStart and onHoverChange are each called once; unhovering removes the attribute and class and calls onHoverEnd once with onHoverChange called twice in total. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support hover")
- Given a DraggableTable with no selection or row action, when the first body row is hovered, then it gains data-hovered="true", and unhovering removes it. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should show hover state on draggable rows even when not selectable/actionable")
- Given a Table with no selection and no row action but hover handlers on rows, when the first body row is hovered, then data-hovered and class "hover" are never set and onHoverStart, onHoverChange and onHoverEnd are never called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not show hover state when item is not interactive")
- Given hover handlers and a className function on TableHeader, when the header rowgroup is hovered, then it gains data-hovered and class "hover" and onHoverStart and onHoverChange are each called once; unhovering removes them and calls onHoverEnd once with onHoverChange called twice in total. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support hover events on the TableHeader")
- Given selectionMode="multiple" and a className function of isPressed on rows, when MouseLeft is pressed down on the first body row, then it gains data-pressed="true" and class "pressed", and releasing the button removes both. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support press state")
- Given a non-interactive Table with a className function of isPressed on rows, when MouseLeft is pressed down and released on the header row, then data-pressed and class "pressed" are never set. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not show press state when not interactive")
- Given onRowAction on the Table, when MouseLeft is pressed and released on the first body row, then the row shows data-pressed="true" and class "pressed" while held, loses them on release, and onRowAction is called once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support row actions")
- Given a Table with onAction on a single Row, when tableTester.triggerRowAction({row: 0}) is used, then that row's onAction is called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support onAction on items")
- Given sortDescriptor {column: 'name', direction: 'ascending'} and sortable columns, when tableTester.toggleSort({column: 0}) is used, then onSortChange is called once with {column: 'name', direction: 'descending'}. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support sorting")
- Given rows with onAction, onPressStart, onPressEnd, onPress and onClick, when tableTester.triggerRowAction({row: 1, interactionType}) fires for interactionType mouse and for keyboard, then onAction, onPressStart, onPressEnd, onPress and onClick are each called exactly once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support press events on items when using $interactionType", it.each template with interactionType mouse and keyboard)
- Given rows with an href and selectionMode="none", when a row is triggered (describe.each(['mouse', 'keyboard']), keyboard uses Enter), then no row element is an anchor, every row has data-href, the click handler is called once, and the event target is an HTMLAnchorElement whose href is "https://google.com/". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support links with selectionMode="none"")
- Given rows with an href and selectionBehavior="toggle", when a row is triggered by mouse or keyboard Enter (describe.each(['mouse', 'keyboard']), it.each(['single', 'multiple'])), then the link navigates once with an HTMLAnchorElement target of "https://google.com/"; clicking the row's checkbox sets aria-selected="true" on it; and triggering the second row with Space selects it (aria-selected="true") without firing another link click. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support links with selectionBehavior="toggle" selectionMode="%s"")
- Given rows with an href and selectionBehavior="replace", when the first row is clicked once (or Space is pressed) under describe.each(['mouse', 'keyboard']) and it.each(['single', 'multiple']), then no link click fires and the row gets aria-selected="true"; a double click (or Enter) then fires the link click once with an HTMLAnchorElement target of "https://google.com/". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support links with selectionBehavior="replace" selectionMode="%s"")
- Given the tab mode table with selectionMode="multiple", when the "Games notes" input is clicked, then the input has focus and onSelectionChange is never called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not trigger selection when clicking on a tabbable child element")
- Given the tab mode table with selectionMode="multiple" and a nested TagGroup inside a cell, when the TagGroup's inner gridcell is clicked, then onSelectionChange is never called. - Given the tab mode table with selectionMode="multiple", when a row with no tabbable children is clicked, then onSelectionChange is called once with the set {'1'}. - Given a 25-row table with selectionMode="single", when the first row's checkbox is clicked, then onSelectionChange is called once with {'Foo 1'} and the row gets aria-selected "true". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should select a row from checkbox")
- Given a 25-row table with selectionMode="single", when the "Baz 1" cell is clicked, then onSelectionChange is called once with {'Foo 1'} and the row gets aria-selected "true". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should select a row by pressing on a cell")
- Given a 25-row table with selectionMode="single", when "Baz 1" is clicked then "Baz 2" then "Baz 2" again, then onSelectionChange receives {'Foo 1'}, then {'Foo 2'} with row 1 falling back to aria-selected "false", then an empty set on the deselecting click. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "will only select one if pointer is used to click on multiple rows")
- Given a 25-row table with selectionMode="single", when row 1's checkbox is clicked then row 2's then row 2's again, then onSelectionChange receives {'Foo 1'}, then {'Foo 2'} with row 1 deselected, then an empty set, so a single-selection checkbox behaves like a radio. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "will only select one if pointer is used to click on multiple checkboxes")
- Given selectionMode="single" with disabledKeys ['Foo 1'], when that row's checkbox is clicked, its "Baz 1" cell is clicked, and Space then Enter are pressed at several cells in the row, then the row stays aria-selected "false" and onSelectionChange is never called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should not select a disabled row from checkbox or keyboard interaction")
- Given a table with selectionMode="multiple", when a row is hovered then pressed with the left mouse button, then its className contains "is-hovered" and then "is-active"; the same holds after rerendering with selectionMode="single". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "displays pressed/hover styles when row is pressed/hovered and selection mode is not "none"")
- Given a table with selectionMode="none" and disabledBehavior="all" and no onAction, when a row is hovered then pressed, then its className contains neither "is-hovered" nor "is-active". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "doesn't show pressed/hover styles when row is pressed/hovered and selection mode is "none" and disabledBehavior="all"")
- Given a table with selectionMode="none", disabledBehavior="selection" and an onAction handler, when a row is hovered then pressed, then its className contains "is-hovered" and then "is-active". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "shows pressed/hover styles when row is pressed/hovered and selection mode is "none", disabledBehavior="selection" and has a action")
- Given a table with selectionMode="none", disabledBehavior="selection", onAction and disabledKeys ['Foo 1'], when that disabled row is hovered then pressed, then its className still contains "is-hovered" and then "is-active" because only selection is disabled. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "shows pressed/hover styles when row is pressed/hovered, disabledBehavior="selection", row is disabled and has a action")
- Given a table with selectionMode="multiple", onAction, disabledBehavior="all" and disabledKeys ['Foo 1'], when that disabled row is hovered then pressed, then its className contains neither "is-hovered" nor "is-active". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "doesn't show pressed/hover styles when row is pressed/hovered, has a action, but is disabled and disabledBehavior="all"")
- Given a TableView with two sortable columns, onSortChange and no sortDescriptor (both sortable headers aria-sort "none"), when the Foo header is clicked, then onSortChange is called once with {column: 'foo', direction: 'ascending'}. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should fire onSortChange when there is no existing sortDescriptor")
- Given a TableView with sortDescriptor {column: 'foo', direction: 'ascending'} and onSortChange, when the Foo header (aria-sort "ascending") is clicked, then onSortChange is called once with {column: 'foo', direction: 'descending'}. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should toggle the sort direction from ascending to descending")
- Given a TableView with sortDescriptor {column: 'foo', direction: 'descending'} and onSortChange, when the Foo header (aria-sort "descending") is clicked, then onSortChange is called once with {column: 'foo', direction: 'ascending'}. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should toggle the sort direction from descending to ascending")
- Given a TableView with sortDescriptor {column: 'foo', direction: 'ascending'} and onSortChange, when the Bar header (aria-sort "none") is clicked, then onSortChange is called once with {column: 'bar', direction: 'ascending'}, so switching columns starts over at ascending. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should trigger sorting on a different column")
- Given a collapsed row, when the chevron is clicked, then onExpandedChange fires once with that key, onSelectionChange does not fire, the chevron label flips to Collapse, and the child rows appear with correct level, posinset and setsize values. - Given an expanded row, when the chevron is clicked, then onExpandedChange fires with an empty set, onSelectionChange does not fire, the children are removed, and the chevron label flips to Expand. - Given a selectable expandable table, when the chevron cell (not the chevron itself) is clicked, then the row is selected. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should select a row when clicking on the chevron cell")
- Given a nested row, when it is clicked, then it becomes selected and onSelectionChange receives its key. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should select a nested row on click")
- Given the select-all checkbox, when pressed, then nested rows are selected too. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should select nested rows if select all checkbox is pressed")
- Given disabled nested rows, when they are clicked, then they are not selected. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should not allow selection of disabled nested rows")
- Given a shift-click from a top-level row to a nested row, when it happens, then the range covers every visible row between them. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should support selecting a range from a top level row to a nested row")
- Given a shift-click from a nested row back up to a top-level row, when it happens, then the same range is produced. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should support selecting a range from a nested row to a top level row")
- Given a shift-click from a top-level row to one of its own descendants, when it happens, then the descendants in between are included. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should support selecting a range from a top level row to a descendent child row")
- Given a shift-click from a nested child up to its own ancestor, when it happens, then the range includes the ancestor and the intervening rows. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should support selecting a range from a nested child row to its top level row ancestor")
- Given disabled rows inside a pointer range, when the range is selected, then they are excluded. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should not include disabled rows")
- Given `onAction` on an expandable table, when a nested row is activated with each pointer type, then onSelectionChange does not fire and onAction fires once. Run as `it.each` over the pointer types. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should trigger onAction when clicking nested rows with $Name")
- Given `selectionStyle="highlight"` on an expandable table, when rows are clicked with the mouse, then selection toggles in highlight mode. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should toggle selection with mouse")
- Given highlight selection on touch, when rows are tapped, then selection toggles. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should toggle selection with touch")
- Given highlight selection on touch with nothing selected, when a row is long pressed, then the table enters selection mode and selects it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should support long press to enter selection mode on touch")
- Given highlight selection with onAction, when a row is double clicked with the mouse, then onAction fires. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should support double click to perform onAction with mouse")
- Given highlight selection with onAction on touch, when a row is tapped once, then onAction fires (a single tap is the action on touch). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should support single tap to perform onAction with touch")

### Focus management

- Given a cell containing three DialogTriggers, when the "Open 2" button is clicked, the dialog is focused and Escape dismisses it, then the dialog is removed from the document and focus returns to the "Open 2" button. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should restore focus to the associated dialog trigger inside a cell")
- Given className functions of isFocusVisible on row, cell and column, when Tab focuses the first body row, then that row has focus with data-focus-visible="true" and class "focus"; ArrowRight moves focus to its rowheader which gains data-focus-visible="true" and class "focus" while the row loses both; ArrowUp then focuses the first columnheader which gains data-focus-visible="true" and class "focus". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support focus ring")
- Given a Column and a Cell whose children are functions of isFocused, when the columnheader is focused, then its text becomes "Name (focused)", and when the rowheader is focused its text becomes "Foo (focused)". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support cell render props")
- Given a Table, when Tab focuses the first body row, then that row has data-focus-visible-within="true"; ArrowRight moves focus to its rowheader which has data-focus-visible="true" while the row keeps data-focus-visible-within="true"; ArrowDown then removes data-focus-visible-within from the first row. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support data-focus-visible-within")
- Given a dynamic table with focus on the "Program Files" rowheader of the second row, when that row is removed by rerendering without it, then 3 rows remain and focus is on the rowheader of the new second row, which contains "bootmgr". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "supports removing rows")
- Given a dynamic table with focus on the "Program Files" rowheader, when the focused row is removed and every remaining row is disabled with disabledBehavior="all", then the rerender completes without hanging (the previous focus-restore search looped forever when no focusable row existed), 3 rows remain, and focus is no longer on the removed cell. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "does not hang restoring focus when no focusable row remains")
- Given an empty table rendered with isLoading, when Tab is pressed, then the grid element itself receives focus and the select all checkbox inside the first columnheader is disabled. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should disable the select all checkbox and column focusablity when the table is empty and loading")
- Given a table whose cells contain Switches and Links (selectionMode="multiple"), when the third switch is clicked, then that switch keeps DOM focus rather than the cell or row taking it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should retain focus on the pressed child")
- Given a table whose cells contain Switches and Links, when arrow keys are pressed starting from the "Baz 1" cell, then focus is marshalled onto the focusable child inside each cell rather than the cell: ArrowLeft reaches link 0, ArrowLeft reaches switch 0, ArrowDown reaches switch 1, ArrowRight reaches switch 2, ArrowRight reaches link 1, ArrowLeft goes back to switch 2, ArrowLeft to switch 1, ArrowLeft to checkbox 2 (the row checkbox), ArrowUp to checkbox 1, ArrowUp to checkbox 0 (the select-all checkbox in the header). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should marshall focus to the focusable element inside a cell")
- Given the first switch inside a cell has been clicked so it holds focus, when ArrowDown is pressed, then focus moves to the second switch, so grid keyboard navigation still works after pressing a focusable child. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support keyboard navigation after pressing focusable element inside a cell")
- Given an untouched table between two inputs, when focus is on the input before it and a Tab keydown is followed by focus landing on the table's first tabbable child, then the grid has tabIndex "0" and focus is redirected to the first body row element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should move focus to the first row when tabbing into the table from the start")
- Given an untouched table between two inputs, when focus is on the input after it and a Shift + Tab keydown is followed by focus landing on the table's last tabbable child, then the grid has tabIndex "0" and focus is redirected to the last body row element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should move focus to the last row when tabbing into the table from the end")
- Given the "Baz 1" cell has been focused once so the grid's tabIndex flips from "0" to "-1", when focus moves out to the preceding input and Tab brings focus back into the table, then focus is restored to the "Baz 1" cell. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should move focus to the last focused cell when tabbing into the table from the start")
- Given the "Baz 1" cell has been focused once so the grid's tabIndex is "-1", when focus moves out to the following input and Tab brings focus back into the table, then focus is restored to the "Baz 1" cell. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should move focus to the last focused cell when tabbing into the table from the end")
- Given a table with a Picker inside a cell and focus on the "Baz 1" cell, when ArrowLeft is pressed twice then ArrowRight twice, then focus goes to the Picker button, then the switch, back to the Picker button, and then out to the third gridcell, so the Picker does not trap arrow-key navigation. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should not trap focus when navigating through a cell with a picker using the arrow keys")
- Given focus on the second switch inside a cell, when Tab moves to the next tabbable node found by getFocusableTreeWalker, then focus lands on the input after the table rather than another element inside it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should move focus after the table when tabbing")
- Given focus on the last body row element, when Tab moves to the next tabbable node, then focus lands on the input after the table. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should move focus after the table when tabbing from the last row")
- Given focus on the second switch inside a cell, when Shift + Tab moves to the previous tabbable node, then focus lands on the input before the table. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should move focus before the table when shift tabbing")
- Given the InlineDeleteButtons story with selectionMode="multiple", when Tab focuses the first row, ArrowLeft focuses that row's delete button, and Enter deletes the row, then after timers run focus is on the delete button of the new first row (the row below the removed one), and a subsequent ArrowUp moves focus to the fifth columnheader in the header row. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should send focus to the appropriate key below if the focused row is removed")
- Given the InlineDeleteButtons story with selectionMode="multiple", when focus is moved to the second row's delete button via Tab, ArrowLeft and ArrowDown and Enter deletes that last row, then after timers run focus is on the delete button of the row above (now rows[1]), and a subsequent ArrowUp moves focus to the fifth columnheader. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should send focus to the appropriate key above if the focused last row is removed")
- Given focus on the "Baz 1" cell (column index 3) and a rerender that reorders the items and drops the table to two columns, then focus falls back to the first body row element because the last focused column index exceeds the new column count. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should send focus to the appropriate column and row if both the current row and column are removed")
- Given focus on the "Bar 1" cell and a rerender that leaves a single item and a single column, then focus falls back to the first body row element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should send focus to the appropriate column and row if both the current row and column are removed")
- Given focus on the "Foo 2" cell and a rerender whose items no longer contain that row key but keep all columns, then focus moves to the "Foo 1" cell. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should send focus to the appropriate column and row if both the current row and column are removed")
- Given a 25-row table, when the "Baz 25" cell is focused and timers run, then the mocked scrollIntoView was last called with the table body element and document.activeElement. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should scroll to a cell when it is focused")
- Given a 20-column 25-row table with the "Foo 5 5" cell focused, when the body is scrolled to scrollTop 1000 and scrollLeft 1000, then the scroll position sticks, the focused cell keeps DOM focus, and its text node is still its firstElementChild because the virtualizer does not recycle focused items. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should scroll to a cell when it is focused off screen")
- Given the focused "Foo 5 5" cell has been scrolled out of view, when its row is inspected, then the row has ten gridcells and one rowheader ordered as the checkbox cell at aria-colindex 1, the rowheader at aria-colindex 2, the persisted focused cell at aria-colindex 6, and the first visible cell at aria-colindex 14. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should scroll to a cell when it is focused off screen")
- Given the focused cell is scrolled out of view, when ArrowLeft is pressed, then focus moves to the "Foo 5 4" cell and scrollIntoView was last called with the body and the newly focused element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should scroll to a cell when it is focused off screen")
- Given a 25-row table with the "Baz 5" cell focused and the body scrolled to scrollTop 1000, when the "Bar" column header is focused, then the active element has role columnheader with text "Bar" and scrollIntoView was last called with the body and that header (the assertion records that the header itself is passed through scrollIntoView rather than causing a body scroll). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should not scroll when a column header receives focus")
- Given an empty TableView with selectionMode="multiple", renderEmptyState and an input after it, when Tab is pressed, then focus lands on the grid itself; a second Tab skips the select-all checkbox, which carries the disabled attribute, and onSelectionChange is never reachable. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "empty table select all should be disabled")
- Given the EmptyStateStory table (a toggle button before it and a link in the empty state), when Tab is pressed twice, then focus goes to the toggle button and then into the table body's link, so the empty state content is tabbable. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should allow the user to tab into the table body")
- Given the ColumnHeaderFocusRingTable story with three rows and focus on the "Height" column header, when Enter triggers a sort that empties the table and timers advance 500 ms, then focus has shifted to the grid element itself, and after all timers and transitions run the table is down to two rows. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should shift focus to the table if table becomes empty via column sort")
- Given the EmptyStateStory table with focus on the toggle button before it, when the button inside the third columnheader is clicked, then focus stays on the toggle button, no menuitem appears, and hovering that header with the timers run produces no slider, so press interactions on column headers are disabled while the table is empty. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should disable press interactions with the column headers")
- Given the EmptyStateStory table, when the toggle button loads items into the table, then the select-all checkbox loses its disabled attribute, clicking it checks it and leaves it focused, hovering the third header yields a resizer slider, the third header's button opens a menu whose Escape returns focus to that button, ArrowLeft then moves focus to the second header's button, and toggling the items back off re-disables select all, makes header clicks leave focus on the toggle button and gives the grid tabIndex "0" again. (skipped in repo) (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should re-enable functionality when the table recieves items")
- Given a grid in cell focus mode with child cell focus where the second switch inside a cell was last focused, when the cell element itself is focused programmatically and timers run, then focus is restored to that second switch rather than the first child. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/grid/useGrid.test.js: "should restore focus to the child that was last focused within a cell, not the first child")
- Given a focused cell, when focus moves, then the mocked `scrollIntoView` is called with the table body and the active element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should scroll to a cell when it is focused")
- Given a nested row cell that is off screen, when it is focused, then scrollIntoView is called with it, the cell keeps focus after a scroll event, and its cells report the expected `aria-colindex` values with the rowheader at colindex 2 in a selectable table. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TreeGridTable.test.tsx: "should scroll to a nested row cell when it is focused off screen")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a Table with onScroll, when a scroll event fires on the grid, then onScroll is called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support onScroll")
- Given a load more table with onLoadMore and a mocked IntersectionObserver, when the sentinel is observed and the intersection callback fires with isIntersecting true, then observe was last called with the sentinel div (whose parent is a TD inside a TR) and onLoadMore is called once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should fire onLoadMore when intersecting with the sentinel")
- Given a load more table rendered with isLoading, when the intersection callback fires while loading and again after rerendering without isLoading, then onLoadMore is called once each time (twice total), so loading state does not gate the callback but each intersection does. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should only fire loadMore when intersection is detected regardless of loading state")
- Given scrollHeight and clientHeight both mocked to 100 so the table is not scrollable, when the table rerenders from isLoading to not loading and the intersection callback fires, then onLoadMore is called once. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should automatically fire onLoadMore if there aren't enough items to fill the Table")
- Given a Table passed a user defined scrollRef on TableBody with scrollHeight 100 and clientHeight 25, when the grid is scrolled then onLoadMore is not called, and when the body rowgroup is scrolled to 76 then onLoadMore is called once. (skipped in repo) (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "accepts a user defined scrollRef")
- Given a 25-row table with selectionMode="multiple" driven through the @react-aria/test-utils Table tester in keyboard interaction mode, when toggleSelectAll runs, then every row is reported selected, onSelectionChange was called once with the string 'all', all rows have aria-selected "true" and the select-all checkbox is checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support selecting all via the checkbox")
- Given a 25-row table with selectionMode="multiple", when Tab plus ArrowRight puts focus in the table and Ctrl + A is pressed, then onSelectionChange is called once with 'all', every row is aria-selected "true" and select-all is checked; pressing Ctrl + A a second time does not fire onSelectionChange again and leaves everything selected. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support selecting all via ctrl + A")
- Given select all is active via the select-all checkbox, when the fourth row is clicked, then onSelectionChange is called once with Foo 1 through Foo 25 except Foo 4 and that row shows aria-selected "false". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should deselect an item after selecting all")
- Given select all is active via the select-all checkbox, when the fourth row is shift clicked, then onSelectionChange is called once with just {'Foo 4'} and only that row keeps aria-selected "true" while every other row is false. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should shift click on an item after selecting all")
- Given the select-all checkbox has been clicked so it is checked, when it is clicked again, then onSelectionChange is called once with an empty set, all rows become aria-selected "false" and the checkbox is unchecked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support clearing selection via checkbox")
- Given one row selected by clicking "Baz 1" so select-all is indeterminate, when ArrowLeft then Escape are pressed, then onSelectionChange is called once with an empty set, all rows become aria-selected "false" and select-all is unchecked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support clearing selection via Escape")
- Given an empty selection, when Tab plus ArrowRight focus the table and Escape is pressed, then onSelectionChange is never called; after select all is clicked (onSelectionChange last called with 'all') and ArrowDown plus two ArrowRights move focus, Escape then calls onSelectionChange with an empty set. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should only call onSelectionChange if there are selections to clear")
- Given select all is active (selection state 'all') on a 25-row table, when the table is rerendered with an extra item "Foo 0" prepended, then the new "Foo 0" cell is visible and all rows remain aria-selected "true", so new items join the selection automatically. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should automatically select new items when select all is active")
- Given a two-row table where both rows were clicked individually so the select-all checkbox reads checked (indeterminate after the first click), when the table is rerendered with an extra item "Foo 0" prepended, then the new row has aria-selected "false", the previously selected rows stay true and the select-all checkbox falls back to indeterminate. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "manually selecting all should not auto select new items")
- Given a 25-row table with disabledKeys ['Foo 3'], when the select-all checkbox is clicked, then onSelectionChange is called once with 'all' but the disabled row keeps aria-selected "false" while every other row is true. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should not included disabled rows when selecting all")
- Given the CRUDExample story with two rows (aria-rowindex 2 and 3), when the "Add item" button opens the dialog, Devon, Govett and Feb 3 are typed across three fields and Create is clicked, then the dialog is removed from the document, the table has four rows with aria-rowindex 2, 3 and 4, the new first row's two rowheaders read Devon and Govett and its second gridcell reads "Feb 3", so the new row is inserted at the top. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "can add items")

- Given a 25-row table, when rows 1 and 2 are clicked in turn, then announce was last called with "Foo 2 selected. 2 items selected."; clicking row 2 again announces "Foo 2 not selected. 1 item selected.". - Given a 25-row table, when row 1 is clicked and row 3 is shift clicked, then announce was last called with "3 items selected." with no row name; shift clicking back on row 1 announces "1 item selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should announce only the number of selected items when multiple are selected at once")
- Given a 25-row table, when the select-all checkbox is clicked, then announce was last called with "All items selected."; clicking it again announces "No items selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should announce select all")
- Given a table with two isRowHeader columns (First Name, Last Name), when the first row is clicked, then announce was last called with "Sam Smith selected." joining both row header values; clicking again announces "Sam Smith not selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should announce all row header columns")
- Given the ExampleSortTable with Foo and Bar sortable and an initial ascending sort on Bar, when the Bar header is clicked twice and the Foo header is clicked twice, then announce is called with "sorted by column Bar in descending order", then "sorted by column Bar in ascending order", then "sorted by column Foo in ascending order", then "sorted by column Foo in descending order", each with politeness 'assertive' and a 500 ms timeout. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should announce changes in sort order")
- Given the WithBreadcrumbNavigation story with selectionMode="multiple", when row 2 is selected (announcing "File B selected.") and the second breadcrumb link is clicked so the whole item set is swapped out, then announce was last called with "No items selected." and has been called exactly twice. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "can announce deselect even when items are swapped out completely")
- Given the WithBreadcrumbNavigation story where the second link has been followed and a row selected (announcing "File C selected.", two announce calls total), when the root breadcrumb link is clicked, then announce is still at two calls because focus is not on the table, so the resulting deselection is not announced. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "will not announce deselect caused by breadcrumb navigation")
- Given the WithBreadcrumbNavigation story with a row selected (two announce calls) and focus moved to the collapsed breadcrumb menu button, when the root is chosen from the breadcrumb menu (a menuitemradio), then announce stays at two calls because focus is off the table; following the second link again brings the total to three with the last call "No items selected.". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "updates even if not focused")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given refs on Table, TableHeader, Column, TableBody, Row and Cell, when rendered, then the refs are instances of HTMLTableElement, HTMLTableSectionElement, HTMLTableCellElement, HTMLTableSectionElement, HTMLTableRowElement and HTMLTableCellElement. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support refs")
- Given a Table with style={{width: 200}}, when rendered, then the grid's style attribute contains "width: 200px". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support overriding table style")
- Given four columns and a row whose cells (one with colSpan={2}) total five columns, when rendered, then render throws "Cell count must match column count. Found 5 cells and 4 columns."; and given two columns with a row containing one cell, render throws "Cell count must match column count. Found 1 cells and 2 columns.". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should throw error if number of cells do not match column count")
- Given a virtualized table of 50 rows with clientHeight 100, when the grid is scrolled to scrollTop 200, then 8 rows render showing Foo 7 through Foo 13. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should support virtualizer")
- Given a table with a loader row (isLoading) and selectionMode multiple, when the "Select All" checkbox is clicked, then onSelectionChange is called with 'all'; clicking an individual row checkbox afterwards calls it with the set {'1'}, so the loader row is never part of the selection. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not include the loader in the selection when selecting all/deselecting all")
- Given a Table with selectionMode="multiple" and a cell containing a DialogTrigger whose Dialog holds its own Checkbox, when the dialog is opened, then the Checkbox inside the dialog renders (the row selection checkbox context does not leak into other cells). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Table.test.js: "should not propagate the checkbox context from selection into other cells")
- Given a TableView with 100 items, onLoadMore and scrollHeight mocked to 4100, when rendered, then the body renders 34 rows (41 px per row in a 1000 px tall table gives 25 visible rows plus one third overscan), and scrolling the body to scrollTop 250, then 1500, then 2800 with timers run between calls onLoadMore exactly once. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should fire onLoadMore when scrolling near the bottom")
- Given a TableView with a single item, onLoadMore and scrollHeight mocked to 1000 (the handler then raises the mock to 2000), when the table renders and timers run, then onLoadMore was called once without any scrolling because the content does not fill the table. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should automatically fire onLoadMore if there aren't enough items to fill the Table")
- Given a TableView with no selection whose Rows carry href props, parameterized by describe.each over 'mouse' and 'keyboard' (keyboard triggers with Enter), when a row is triggered, then the row element's tagName is not A but it has a data-href attribute, and the document click handler fires once with an event whose target is an HTMLAnchorElement with href "https://google.com/". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support links with selectionMode="none"")
- Given a TableView with checkbox selection and href Rows, parameterized by describe.each over 'mouse' and 'keyboard' and by it.each over selectionMode 'single' and 'multiple', when the first row is triggered, then rows are not anchor tags but have data-href and the click handler fires once with an HTMLAnchorElement target whose href is "https://google.com/". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support links with selectionStyle="checkbox" selectionMode="%s"")
- Given the same checkbox-selection link table, when the first row's checkbox is clicked it becomes aria-selected "true", and when the second row is triggered with Space, then the click handler is still at one call while the second row becomes aria-selected "true", so Space selects without navigating. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support links with selectionStyle="checkbox" selectionMode="%s"")
- Given a TableView with selectionStyle="highlight" and href Rows, parameterized by describe.each over 'mouse' and 'keyboard' and by it.each over selectionMode 'single' and 'multiple', when the first row is triggered with Space, then no navigation click fires and the row becomes aria-selected "true". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support links with selectionStyle="highlight" selectionMode="%s"")
- Given the highlight-selection link table with the first row selected, when it is double clicked (mouse) or Enter is pressed on it (keyboard), then the click handler fires once with an HTMLAnchorElement target whose href is "https://google.com/". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should support links with selectionStyle="highlight" selectionMode="%s"")
- Given a Provider with a router whose navigate is mocked and a table whose first Row has href "/one" and routerOptions {foo: 'bar'}, parameterized by describe.each over 'mouse' and 'keyboard', when the first row is triggered, then navigate was called with '/one' and {foo: 'bar'}; triggering the second row (href "https://adobe.com") leaves navigate uncalled and fires a real document click once, so external links bypass the client router. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js: "should work with RouterProvider")
- Given the Spectrum TableView suite, when run, then the bulk of its cases come from the shared `tableTests()` generator in packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/TableTests.js, invoked once by Table.test.js and again by TableNestedRows.test.js with the `enableTableNestedRows` flag on, so every shared behavior is asserted twice. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/table/Table.test.js: "success")

## calendar

### Roles and attributes

- Given a calendar with no props, when it renders, then the outer element has role application and is visible, a role heading element has the current month and year text from Intl.DateTimeFormat({month: 'long', year: 'numeric'}), and the role grid element has no tabIndex attribute. - Given a calendar with no props, when it renders, then the cell for today has aria-label "Today, <weekday, month day, year>", tabIndex 0, and its parent has role gridcell. - Given a calendar with no props, when it renders, then a button labeled Previous and a button labeled Next are visible, the number of gridcells that are not aria-disabled="true" equals GregorianCalendar.getDaysInMonth(today()), and every such gridcell's first child element has an aria-label. ### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given defaultValue 2019-06-05, when the Next button is clicked then the heading becomes "July 2019", the count of non-disabled gridcells becomes 31, no cell has an aria-label containing "selected", and the Next button keeps focus; clicking Previous returns the heading to "June 2019" with 30 cells, a selected cell present again, and focus on the Previous button. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/CalendarBase.test.js: "$Name should change the month when previous or next buttons are clicked")

(react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/CalendarBase.test.js: "$Name should change the month when previous or next buttons are clicked and multiple months are visible")

- Given a RangeCalendar inside a shadow root (the file pins that pointer tracking still resolves targets through the shadow boundary), when pointerDown on 17 is followed by pointerLeave/pointerEnter across 20 and 23 and then pointerUp plus click on 23, then 17 has data-selection-start="true", 23 has data-selection-end="true", and onChange fires once with start June 17 2019 and end June 23 2019. - Given a RangeCalendar inside a shadow root mid selection anchored on June 17 2019 (the file pins that the calendar can still tell its own navigation buttons from outside targets inside a shadow root), when the Next button inside the shadow root is clicked, then onChange has not fired, and clicking 5 in July commits once with start June 17 2019 and end July 5 2019. - Given a RangeCalendar inside a shadow root with commitBehavior="clear" and defaultValue June 10 to June 20 2019 (shadow root focus and target resolution under test), when 17 is clicked then 23 is clicked, then the click lands as a normal range commit rather than a clear, and onChange fires once with start June 17 2019 and end June 23 2019. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/RangeCalendar.shadow.test.tsx: "should not clear the selection when clicking a date with commitBehavior=\"clear\"")
- Given a RangeCalendar rendered in a shadow root that is itself inside another shadow root (nested boundaries, which is the point of this file), when 17 then 23 are clicked, then onChange fires once with start June 17 2019 and end June 23 2019. - Given a drag started inside a RangeCalendar in a shadow root and dragged to 23 (this file pins that pointerup outside the shadow root still resolves), when pointerUp fires on document.body, then onChange fires once with start June 17 2019 and end June 23 2019. ### Focus management

- Given autoFocus and no selected value, when the calendar mounts, then the cell for today has DOM focus and its parent has role gridcell. Parameterized over v3 Calendar and v3 RangeCalendar. - Given defaultValue 2019-03-10 with minValue 2019-02-03 and maxValue 2019-04-20, when the Previous button is clicked and becomes disabled, then focus moves off the button into the grid onto the cell whose aria-label starts with "Sunday, February 10, 2019"; clicking Next while it stays enabled leaves focus on the Next button, and clicking Next again so it becomes disabled moves focus to the cell starting with "Wednesday, April 10, 2019". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/CalendarBase.test.js: "$Name should move focus when the previous or next buttons become disabled")

- Given controlled focusedValue 2019-06-05 with autoFocus, when the calendar mounts, then the focused element's aria-label starts with "Wednesday, June 5, 2019". - Given defaultFocusedValue 2019-06-05 with minValue 2019-07-05 and autoFocus, when the calendar mounts, then the grid has aria-label "July 2019" and focus is on the cell whose aria-label starts with "Friday, July 5, 2019", so the focused date is clamped into the valid range. - Given controlled focusedValue 2019-06-05 with minValue 2019-07-05 and autoFocus, when the calendar mounts, then the grid has aria-label "July 2019" and focus is on the cell whose aria-label starts with "Friday, July 5, 2019". - Given a ref on the calendar, then ref.current has a focus property, and when ref.current.focus() is called the active element has role button and its parent has role gridcell. - Given value 2019-02-03 and autoFocus on a v3 Calendar, when it mounts, then the selected cell has DOM focus, its parent gridcell has role gridcell and aria-selected="true", and the grid has no aria-activedescendant, so focus is real rather than virtual. - Given defaultValue 2019-06-05 with autoFocus so the selected date holds focus, when ArrowRight is pressed and all timers run, then the cell labeled "Thursday, June 6, 2019" has DOM focus. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/Calendar.test.js: "ensures that the active descendant is announced when the focused date changes")
- Given a RangeCalendar with value February 3 to February 18 2019 and autoFocus, when it mounts, then the first selected cell has real DOM focus, its parent has role="gridcell" and aria-selected="true", and the grid has no aria-activedescendant. - Given a RangeCalendar with value June 20 to July 10 2019, when the Next button is clicked and later the Previous button, then focus stays on the button that was pressed rather than moving into the grid. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/RangeCalendar.test.js: "should show selected dates across multiple months")
- Given a RangeCalendar with allowsNonContiguousRanges, weekends unavailable and a selection anchored on March 9 2022, when PageDown moves focus to Saturday April 9 2022 (which has aria-disabled="true" and a parent without aria-selected) and the cell is then blurred, then onChange is called with start March 9 2022 and end April 8 2022, the nearest available date. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/RangeCalendar.test.js: "selects the nearest available date when blurring the calendar")
- Given a RangeCalendar with defaultValue June 5 to June 10 2019 and autoFocus, when ArrowRight is pressed, then the second selected cell takes real DOM focus (the component uses real focus, not aria-activedescendant). ### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given useCalendarState with isDateUnavailable provided and defaultFocusedValue 2026-04-15, when focusNextPage() moves the visible range past that date and selectDate(2026-04-15) is called, then state.value is not null and equals 2026-04-15, so selecting before the visible range still works. - Given useCalendarState with isDateUnavailable provided and defaultFocusedValue 2026-04-15, when focusPreviousPage() moves the visible range before that date and selectDate(2026-04-15) is called, then state.value is not null and equals 2026-04-15. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/calendar/useCalendarState.test.ts: "selects a date after the visible range when isDateUnavailable is provided")
- Given useCalendarState with isDateUnavailable returning true for day 15 and defaultFocusedValue 2026-04-20, when selectDate(2026-04-15) is called, then state.value becomes 2026-04-14, the nearest earlier available date. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/calendar/useCalendarState.test.ts: "selects the nearest earlier available date when the selected date is unavailable")
- Given useCalendarState with isDateUnavailable returning true for every day up to and including 15 and defaultFocusedValue 2026-04-20, when selectDate(2026-04-15) is called, then state.value stays null because no available date exists between the target and the start of the visible range. (react-spectrum: packages/react-stately/test/calendar/useCalendarState.test.ts: "returns null when there is no available date between the selected date and the start of the visible range")
- Given a react-aria-components Calendar with defaultValue March 3 2020 and a footer Button that calls setValue(null) from CalendarStateContext, when a cell is clicked (gaining data-selected="true" and class 'selected') and then the reset button is pressed, then the cell loses data-selected and the 'selected' class, so setValue accepts null. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Calendar.test.js: "should support setting \"null\" for method setValue")
- Given a react-aria-components Calendar with defaultFocusedValue April 15 2026 and isDateUnavailable returning false, when the Next button moves the visible range past the focused date and state.selectDate is called with the focused date and with one month before it, then the rendered value becomes 2026-04-15 and then 2026-03-15, so selectDate works for dates before the visible range. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Calendar.test.js: "selects a date before the visible range when isDateUnavailable is provided")
- Given a react-aria-components Calendar with defaultFocusedValue April 15 2026 and isDateUnavailable returning false, when the Previous button moves the visible range before the focused date and state.selectDate is called with the focused date and with one month after it, then the value becomes 2026-04-15 and then 2026-05-15. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Calendar.test.js: "selects a date after the visible range when isDateUnavailable is provided")
- Given a react-aria-components Calendar where isDateUnavailable marks only day 15 unavailable and the focused date is April 15 2026, when state.selectDate is called with that focused date, then the value becomes 2026-04-14, the nearest earlier available date. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Calendar.test.js: "selects the nearest earlier available date when the focused date is unavailable")
- Given a react-aria-components Calendar where every day up to and including the focused April 15 2026 is unavailable, when state.selectDate is called with the focused date, then the value stays 'none' because no earlier available date exists in the visible range. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Calendar.test.js: "does not select anything when the focused date is unavailable and no earlier date in the visible range is available")
- Given a react-aria-components Calendar with visibleDuration={{weeks: 1}} and defaultFocusedValue April 7 2026 whose heading reads 'April 5 - 11, 2026', when it is rerendered with visibleDuration={{months: 1}}, then the heading updates to 'April 2026'. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Calendar.test.js: "should handle changing the visible duration")

### Forms (name, value, validation, form reset, hidden inputs, autofill)

- Given defaultValue 2022-03-11 and isInvalid, when the calendar renders, then the day button "Friday, March 11, 2022 selected" has aria-invalid="true", its parent gridcell has aria-selected="true" and aria-invalid="true", and the text of its aria-describedby targets reads "Selected date unavailable.".
