(react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/Calendar.test.js: "should support a custom errorMessage")
- Given defaultValue 2022-03-11 and an errorMessage but no isInvalid, when the calendar renders, then the selected day button does not have aria-invalid="true" and its parent gridcell has aria-selected="true" without aria-invalid. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/Calendar.test.js: "does not show error message without isInvalid")
- Given defaultValue 2022-03-05 (a Saturday), isDateUnavailable based on isWeekend for the current locale and allowsNonContiguousRanges, when the calendar renders, then the selected day button has aria-invalid="true", its parent gridcell has aria-selected="true" and aria-invalid="true", and the aria-describedby text reads "Selected date unavailable.", so an unavailable selection is marked invalid without an explicit isInvalid prop. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/Calendar.test.js: "automatically marks selection as invalid using isDateUnavailable")
- Given a RangeCalendar with isInvalid and defaultValue March 10 to 12 2022, when it renders, then the March 11 cell has aria-invalid="true", its parent gridcell has both aria-selected="true" and aria-invalid="true", and the joined aria-describedby text is 'Selected dates unavailable.'. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/RangeCalendar.test.js: "should support invalid state")
- Given an isInvalid RangeCalendar, when a selected cell is focused, then its joined aria-describedby text becomes 'Selected dates unavailable. Click to start selecting date range'. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/RangeCalendar.test.js: "should support invalid state")
- Given a RangeCalendar with isInvalid and errorMessage="Selection dates cannot include weekends.", when it renders, then the selected cell has aria-invalid="true", its parent has aria-selected="true" and aria-invalid="true", and the described text is exactly the custom error message; focusing the cell appends ' Click to start selecting date range'. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/RangeCalendar.test.js: "should support a custom errorMessage")
- Given a RangeCalendar with an errorMessage but no isInvalid, when it renders, then the selected cell has no aria-invalid="true", its parent has aria-selected="true" without aria-invalid, and it has no aria-describedby at all until focused, at which point the description is only 'Click to start selecting date range'. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/RangeCalendar.test.js: "does not show error message without isInvalid")
- Given a RangeCalendar with allowsNonContiguousRanges, weekends marked unavailable via isDateUnavailable and defaultValue March 1 to March 5 2022 spanning a weekend, when it renders, then the March 4 cell has aria-invalid="true", its parent has aria-selected="true" and aria-invalid="true", and the description is 'Selected dates unavailable.' (or with ' Click to start selecting date range' appended when focused), so an unavailable date inside the range marks the whole selection invalid without isInvalid being passed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/RangeCalendar.test.js: "automatically marks selection as invalid using isDateUnavailable")
- Given DatePicker with defaultValue CalendarDate(2021, 10, 3) or DateRangePicker with a 2021-10-03 to 2021-10-04 range, plus errorMessage="Selected dates cannot include weekends." and validationState="invalid" (it.each over Name/Component/props), when the trigger button is clicked, then the first cell in the dialog's grid labelled "selected" has an aria-describedby whose concatenated text starts with "Selected dates cannot include weekends.", so validationState and errorMessage reach the calendar cells. - Given a RangeCalendar with value December 14 1 BC to January 22 1 AD, when it renders, then the first selected cell's aria-label is 'Selected Range: Thursday, December 14, 1 BC to Monday, January 22, 1 AD, Thursday, December 14, 1 BC selected', so era is included on both ends. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/RangeCalendar.test.js: "should show era for BC dates")
- Given a RangeCalendar with a BC defaultValue, when a range is selected by clicking 17 then 23, then announce is called once with 'Selected Range: Saturday, February 17 to Friday, February 23, 5 BC', 'polite', 4000. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/RangeCalendar.test.js: "includes era in BC dates")
- Given a RangeCalendar showing February 5 BC, when the first Next button is clicked, then announce is called once with 'March 5 BC'. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/RangeCalendar.test.js: "includes era in BC dates")
- Given a react-aria-components Calendar with defaultFocusedValue February 3 2022 and createCalendar returning a Custom454Calendar, when it renders, then the CalendarHeading reads 'February 2022' via getFormattableMonth. - Given a react-aria-components Calendar with createCalendar returning a Custom454Calendar and defaultFocusedValue January 30 2022 (month 1, day 1 of fiscal year 2022), when the CalendarMonthPicker rendered as a Select is opened, then its trigger reads 'Feb' and the listbox options are ['Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec', 'Jan'], since the fiscal year starts in Gregorian February. ### SSR and hydration

- Given a Calendar rendered through testSSR, when it is server rendered and hydrated, then no errors or hydration mismatches are thrown. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/calendar/Calendar.ssr.test.js: "should render a Calendar without errors")

### Accessibility tooling

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a RangeCalendar with value February 3 to February 10 2019, minValue February 1 2019 and visibleMonths={3}, when it renders, then 3 grids exist and every selected cell lives in the first grid, because minValue constrains the visible region. - Given a react-aria-components RangeCalendar with defaultFocusedValue April 1 2026 and CalendarMonthPicker/CalendarYearPicker rendered as native selects, when it renders, then the grid aria-label is 'Appointment date, April 2026', the month select value is '4' with options Jan through Dec, and the year select value is '10' with options 2016 through 2035. ## date-field

### Roles and attributes

- Given a DateField with label "Date", when rendered, then the first role=group element has aria-labelledby equal to the label element's id, and every role=spinbutton segment has an id plus aria-labelledby="{segmentId} {labelId}". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should support labeling")
- Given a DateField with aria-label="Birth date" and no visible label, when rendered, then the role=group element has aria-label="Birth date" and an id, and every spinbutton segment has an id, an aria-label ending in " Birth date", and no aria-labelledby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should support labeling with aria-label")
- Given a DateField with aria-labelledby="foo", when rendered, then the role=group element has no aria-label and has aria-labelledby="foo", and every spinbutton segment has an id plus aria-labelledby="{segmentId} foo". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should support labeling with aria-labelledby")
- Given a DateField with description="Help text", when rendered, then the group has aria-describedby pointing at an element whose text content is "Help text", only the first segment carries aria-describedby equal to the group's value, and the remaining segments have no aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should support help text description")
- Given a DateField with errorMessage="Error message" and validationState="invalid", when rendered, then the group has aria-describedby pointing at an element with text "Error message", and every spinbutton segment has aria-describedby equal to the group's value (not only the first). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should support error message")
- Given a DateField with errorMessage="Error message" but no validationState, when rendered, then the group has no aria-describedby and no segment has aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should not display error message if not invalid")
- Given a DateField with description="Help text" and value CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3), when rendered, then the group's aria-describedby ids resolve in order to "Selected Date: February 3, 2020 Help text", only the first segment carries the same aria-describedby, and the rest have none. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should support help text with a value")
- Given a DateField with errorMessage="Error message", validationState="invalid" and value CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3), when rendered, then the group's aria-describedby ids resolve to "Selected Date: February 3, 2020 Error message" and every segment has aria-describedby equal to the group's value. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should support error message with a value")
- Given a DateField with showFormatHelpText, when rendered, then neither the group nor any segment has aria-describedby, because each segment already has its own label and repeating the format would be duplicative. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should support format help text")
- Given a DateField with data-testid="foo", when rendered, then the element carrying that test id has role="group". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should pass through data attributes")
- Given a DateField inside a Provider with isDisabled, when rendered, then every spinbutton segment has aria-disabled="true". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should respond to provider props")
- Given a TimeField with label "Date" and value Time(8, 45), when rendered, then the group's aria-describedby ids resolve to "Selected Time: 8:45 AM", only the first segment carries aria-describedby equal to the group's value, and the remaining segments have none. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "should include a selected value description")
- Given a TimeField with data-testid="foo", when rendered, then the element carrying that test id has role="group". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "should pass through data attributes")
- Given a TimeField inside a Provider with isDisabled, when rendered, then every spinbutton segment has aria-disabled="true". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "should respond to provider props")
- Given a TimeField with defaultValue parseZonedDateTime('2023-07-01T00:45-07:00[America/Los_Angeles]'), when rendered, then a role=textbox element exists for the time zone with aria-label "time zone, " and text content "PDT" (the time zone is not a spinbutton). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "should have a timeZone when set by defaultValue")
- Given a RAC DateField with Label, DateInput rendering DateSegments, and description plus errorMessage Text slots, when rendered, then the DateInput has `role="group"` with class `react-aria-DateInput` and text "mm/dd/yyyy", the outer wrapper carries the DateField data props, aria-labelledby points at the `react-aria-Label`, aria-describedby resolves to "Description Error", and every segment has class `react-aria-DateSegment`, `data-placeholder="true"`, a `data-type`, forwarded data props, and no `data-readonly`; literal separators also have no data-readonly. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "provides slots")
- Given custom classNames on DateField, DateInput, and a function className on DateSegment, when rendered, then the group uses the DateInput class, the wrapper matches the DateField class, and every segment gets "segment placeholder" from the isPlaceholder render prop. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "supports custom class names")
- Given a DateFieldContext "test" slot with an aria-label, when `slot="test"` is used, then the wrapper has the slot attribute and the group gets the aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should support slot")
- Given `isDisabled` on a DateField with a function className, when rendered, then the group has `data-disabled` and the disabled class, and every segment and every literal separator also gets `data-disabled` but not `data-readonly`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should support disabled state")
- Given both `isReadOnly` and `isDisabled`, when rendered, then the group, every segment, and every literal carry both `data-readonly` and `data-disabled`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should support readonly with disabled state")
- Given `isReadOnly` alone, when rendered, then the group, segments, and literals have `data-readonly` and no `data-disabled`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should support readonly state")
- Given `isRequired` toggled on, when rerendered, then the outer `react-aria-DateField` gains `data-required`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should support required state")
- Given `data-testid` on a DateField, when rendered, then exactly one element carries it and it is the outer `react-aria-DateField` wrapper. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should render data- attributes only on the outer element")
- Given a RAC TimeField with slots, when rendered, then the group's text is "––:–– AM" once bidi isolate characters are stripped, the wrapper carries the TimeField data props, aria-labelledby and aria-describedby wire up the Label and the description plus error, and each segment gets `data-placeholder="true"` with a `data-type`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TimeField.test.js: "provides slots")
- Given custom classNames on a TimeField, when rendered, then the DateInput class replaces the default and segments use the isPlaceholder-derived class. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TimeField.test.js: "supports custom class names")
- Given a TimeFieldContext "test" slot, when `slot="test"` is used, then the wrapper has the slot and the group gets the aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TimeField.test.js: "should support slot")
- Given `isRequired` toggled on a TimeField, when rerendered, then the outer `react-aria-TimeField` gains `data-required`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TimeField.test.js: "should support required state")

### Keyboard

- Given a DateField with onKeyDown and onKeyUp handlers, when the field is tabbed into, then onKeyDown has not been called and onKeyUp has been called once (the Tab keyup lands on the segment). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should trigger right arrow key event for segment navigation")
- Given focus on the first segment of a DateField, when ArrowRight is pressed, then focus moves to the second segment, onKeyDown has been called once and onKeyUp twice. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should trigger right arrow key event for segment navigation")
- Given a DateField with isDateUnavailable marking Jan 1 to Jan 8 1980 unavailable and errorMessage "Date unavailable.", when the field is tabbed into and "01011980" typed, then the text "Date unavailable." is rendered. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "Shows as invalid if an unavailable date is given")
- Given a TimeField with onKeyDown and onKeyUp handlers, when the field is tabbed into, then onKeyDown has not been called and onKeyUp has been called once. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "should trigger right arrow key event for segment navigation")
- Given focus on the first segment of a TimeField, when ArrowRight keyDown and keyUp are fired with fireEvent, then focus moves to the second segment, onKeyDown has been called once and onKeyUp twice. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "should trigger right arrow key event for segment navigation")
- Given a TimeField with defaultValue parseTime('20:24') and focus on the hour segment (aria-valuetext "8 PM"), when Backspace is pressed, then the hour segment's aria-valuetext becomes "Empty" while the AM/PM segment keeps aria-label "AM/PM, " and still renders the text "PM". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "should keep dayPeriod the same when hour segment that has a value >= 12 is cleared")
- Given a TimeField with a zoned defaultValue of 01:05 America/Los_Angeles and focus moved to the minute segment (aria-valuetext "05"), when Backspace is pressed, then the minute segment's aria-valuetext becomes "Empty" and the time zone textbox keeps aria-label "time zone, " with text "PDT". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "should keep timeZone from defaultValue when minute segment cleared")
- Given a TimeField with a zoned defaultValue of 01:05 America/Los_Angeles whose minute segment was cleared with Backspace to "Empty", when ArrowUp is pressed, then the minute segment's aria-valuetext becomes "00", the minute segment keeps focus, and the time zone textbox still shows "PDT". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "should keep timeZone from defaultValue when minute segment cleared then set")
- Given a TimeField with placeholderValue parseZonedDateTime('2021-11-07T01:45:00-07:00[America/Los_Angeles]') where both hour and minute start with aria-valuetext "Empty", when the hour segment is focused and ArrowUp pressed four times then ArrowDown pressed three times, then the hour text goes 1, 1, 2 on the way up and 1, 1, 12 on the way down, so the repeated hour of the DST fall back transition is visited twice in each direction and the first ArrowUp only commits the placeholder hour. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "should support cycling through DST fall back transitions with ZonedDateTime placeholder")
- Given a TimeField with defaultValue parseZonedDateTime('2021-11-07T01:45:00-07:00[America/Los_Angeles]') and focus on the hour segment, when ArrowUp is pressed twice then ArrowDown three times, then onChange is called five times with, in order, 01:45-08:00, 02:45-08:00, 01:45-08:00, 01:45-07:00 and 00:45-07:00, all America/Los_Angeles, so stepping the hour crosses the DST offset change without changing the wall clock hour. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "should support cycling through DST fall back transitions with ZonedDateTime defaultValue")
- Given a DateField with the value 12/31/2024 and focus on the year segment, when Backspace is pressed four times, then the year empties while focus stays on it, and a fifth Backspace moves focus to the previous (day) segment; the same pattern repeats from day to month. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should focus previous segment when backspacing on an empty date segment")
- Given an empty DateField with focus on the third segment, when Backspace is held for two keydown events, then focus walks back two segments to the first. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should support repeat keydown events when holding backspace across empty segments")
- Given a filled DateField with focus on the first segment, when ArrowRight is held for two keydown events, then focus moves two segments to the right. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should support repeat keydown events when holding an arrow key to navigate segments")
- Given a focused segment, when Enter is pressed, then nothing happens and focus stays on that segment (so Enter can submit an enclosing form). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should do nothing when pressing enter")
- Given an empty DateField where the month segment was filled with "11", when it is clicked and Backspace pressed twice, then the month returns to its "mm" placeholder and the day and year segments still show "dd" and "yyyy". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should reset to placeholders when deleting a partially filled DateField")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given hover callbacks on the DateInput and on each DateSegment, when the group then a segment is hovered and unhovered, then `data-hovered` and the hover class toggle on each, with onHoverStart and onHoverEnd firing once and onHoverChange twice for the segment. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should support hover state")

### Focus management

- Given a DateField with a ref, when ref.current.focus() is called, then ref.current exposes a focus method and document.activeElement is the first spinbutton segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should support focusing via a ref")
- Given a DateField with autoFocus, when rendered, then document.activeElement is the first spinbutton segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should support autoFocus")
- Given a DateField with a ref, when ref.current.UNSAFE_getDOMNode() is called, then it returns the outermost wrapper element, which is in the document and contains both the label text "Date" and the first spinbutton segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should return the outer most DOM element from the ref")
- Given a DateField with onBlur, onFocus and onFocusChange, when Tab focuses the first segment and Tab again moves to the second segment, then focus follows the segments while onFocus and onFocusChange stay at one call each and onBlur is never called, so moving between segments does not blur the field. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should focus field and switching segments via tab does not change focus")
- Given a DateField with three segments and its hidden input given tabIndex -1 to work around a userEvent.tab() bug where hidden inputs are not focusable, when Tab is pressed four times, then the first three tabs land on segments 0, 1 and 2 with onBlur still at zero calls, and the fourth tab leaves the field with onBlur called once, onFocusChange twice and onFocus once. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "should call blur when focus leaves")
- Given a TimeField with a ref, when ref.current.focus() is called, then ref.current exposes a focus method and document.activeElement is the first spinbutton segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "should support focusing via a ref")
- Given a TimeField with autoFocus, when rendered, then document.activeElement is the first spinbutton segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "should support autoFocus")
- Given a TimeField with a ref, when ref.current.UNSAFE_getDOMNode() is called, then it returns the outermost wrapper element containing the label text "Time" and the first spinbutton segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "should return the outer most DOM element from the ref")
- Given a TimeField with onBlur, onFocus and onFocusChange, when Tab focuses the first segment and Tab again moves to the second, then onFocus and onFocusChange remain at one call each and onBlur is never called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "should focus field and switching segments via tab does not change focus")
- Given a TimeField with hour, minute and AM/PM segments and its hidden input given tabIndex -1 to work around the userEvent.tab() bug, when Tab is pressed four times, then the first three tabs walk segments 0, 1 and 2 with onBlur at zero, and the fourth tab leaves the field with onBlur called once, onFocusChange twice and onFocus once. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "should call blur when focus leaves")
- Given isFocusVisible classNames on the DateInput and segments, when Tab focuses the field, then focus lands on the first segment and both the group and that segment get `data-focus-visible="true"` plus the focus class; Shift+Tab away clears both. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should support focus visible state")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a useDateField built on an empty useDateFieldState (no value, no defaultValue) rendering its segments' text, when a sibling button calls state.setValue(parseDate('2020-01-01')), then the field's text content changes from "mm/dd/yyyy" to include "2020", so a programmatic setValue commits immediately even when no segment has been entered. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/datepicker/useDatePicker.test.tsx: "should commit programmatically setValue when field is empty")
- Given a DateField whose children are a render function of `{isInvalid}` with a minValue above the value and `validationBehavior="aria"`, when rendered, then the group gets `data-validation-state="invalid"`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should support render props")
- Given a render function of `{isDisabled}` with `isDisabled`, when rendered, then the group reflects the disabled render prop. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should support disabled render prop")
- Given a render function of `{isRequired}` with `isRequired`, when rendered, then the group reflects the required render prop. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should support required render prop")
- Given `render` props on DateField, Label, DateInput, and DateSegment, when rendered, then every level uses the custom element with `data-custom`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should support custom render function")
- Given a TimeField with a `{isInvalid}` render function, a minValue of 06:00 and a value of 05:00 under aria validation, when rendered, then the group is marked invalid. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TimeField.test.js: "should support render props")
- Given a TimeField with a `{isDisabled}` render function and `isDisabled`, when rendered, then the group reflects it. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TimeField.test.js: "should support disabled render prop")
- Given a TimeField with a `{isRequired}` render function and `isRequired`, when rendered, then the group reflects it. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TimeField.test.js: "should support required render prop")
- Given `render` props on TimeField, Label, DateInput, and DateSegment, when rendered, then each uses the custom element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TimeField.test.js: "should support custom render function")

### Forms (name, value, validation, form reset, hidden inputs, autofill)

- Given a DateField with name="date", when the value is a CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3), then the hidden input named date has value "2020-02-03"; when rerendered with CalendarDateTime(2020, 2, 3, 8, 30) it has "2020-02-03T08:30:00"; when rerendered with ZonedDateTime(2020, 2, 3, 'America/Los_Angeles', -28800000, 12, 24, 45) it has "2020-02-03T12:24:45-08:00[America/Los_Angeles]". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "supports form values")
- Given a controlled DateField named date inside a form with a reset input, when the month is stepped up with ArrowUp the description becomes "Selected Date: March 3, 2020" and the hidden input "2020-03-03", and when the reset input is clicked the description returns to "Selected Date: February 3, 2020" and the hidden input to "2020-02-03". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "supports form reset")
- Given a DateField named date whose defaultValue comes from React.useActionState with initial CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3) and an action returning CalendarDate(2025, 2, 3) (test only defined when parseInt(React.version, 10) >= 19), when the submit input is clicked, then the hidden input changes from "2020-02-03" to "2025-02-03". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "resets to defaultValue when submitting form action")
- Given a DateField with isRequired and validationBehavior="native" inside a Form, when rendered, then the hidden input has the required attribute, input.validity.valid is false, and the group has no aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "supports isRequired")
- Given that same required native DateField, when form.checkValidity() is called, then the group gains an aria-describedby whose text contains "Constraints not satisfied" and document.activeElement becomes the first spinbutton in the group. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "supports isRequired")
- Given the required native DateField showing "Constraints not satisfied", when the keyboard sequence [ArrowUp][Tab][ArrowUp][Tab][ArrowUp] fills all three segments, then the description still contains "Constraints not satisfied" while input.validity.valid is already true, and only after tabbing out of the field does the message disappear. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "supports isRequired")
- Given a native DateField with minValue CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3), maxValue CalendarDate(2024, 2, 3) and defaultValue CalendarDate(2019, 2, 3), when rendered, then input.validity.valid is false but the description does not yet contain "Value must be 2/3/2020 or later."; after form.checkValidity() the group has aria-describedby containing that message and the first spinbutton is focused. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "supports minValue and maxValue")
- Given that native min/max DateField showing the minimum error, when [Tab][Tab][ArrowUp] raises the year to 2020, then the message is still shown even though input.validity.valid is true, and it clears on tabbing out of the field. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "supports minValue and maxValue")
- Given the same native DateField, when shift+Tab returns to the year and "2025" is typed, then the description does not yet contain "Value must be 2/3/2024 or earlier." and input.validity.valid is false; after tabbing out and calling form.checkValidity() the description contains that message and the first spinbutton is focused; [Tab][Tab][ArrowDown] makes validity valid while the message persists until the next tab out. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "supports minValue and maxValue")
- Given a native DateField with defaultValue CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3) and validate returning "Invalid value" when year < 2022, when rendered the description does not contain "Invalid value" and input.validity.valid is false; after form.checkValidity() the group's description contains "Invalid value" and the first spinbutton is focused; typing [ArrowRight][ArrowRight]2024 makes validity valid while the message persists, and tabbing out clears it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "supports validate function")
- Given a native DateField inside a Form whose onSubmit sets validationErrors {date: 'Invalid value'}, when the submit Button is clicked, then the group's description contains "Invalid value" and input.validity.valid is false; after shift+Tab and typing "2024[ArrowLeft]2[ArrowLeft]2" then blurring the active element, the message is gone and validity is valid. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "supports server validation")
- Given a native required DateField with errorMessage as a function returning "Please enter a value" when e.validationDetails.valueMissing, when form.checkValidity() is called, then the group's aria-describedby element has text content "Please enter a value". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "supports customizing native error messages")
- Given a native required DateField whose description contains "Constraints not satisfied" after form.checkValidity(), when the reset Button is clicked, then the group no longer has aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "clears validation on form reset")
- Given a native required DateField, when the field is tabbed into and immediately shift+Tab out without editing, then the group still has no aria-describedby, so blur alone does not commit validation; after form.checkValidity() the message appears and the first spinbutton is focused, typing "232023" makes validity valid while the message remains, and the next tab clears it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "only commits on blur if the value changed")
- Given a DateField with default validationBehavior (aria), minValue CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3), maxValue CalendarDate(2024, 2, 3) and defaultValue CalendarDate(2019, 2, 3), when rendered the description already contains "Value must be 2/3/2020 or later." with no checkValidity call; [Tab][Tab][Tab][ArrowUp] clears it live, five more ArrowUp presses produce "Value must be 2/3/2024 or earlier.", and one ArrowDown clears that. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "supports minValue and maxValue")
- Given an aria-validated DateField with defaultValue CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3) and validate returning "Invalid value" for year < 2022, when rendered the group has aria-describedby containing "Invalid value", and typing [Tab][ArrowRight][ArrowRight]2024 clears the message without leaving the field. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "supports validate function")
- Given an aria-validated DateField named value inside a Form with validationErrors {value: 'Invalid value'}, when rendered the group has aria-describedby containing "Invalid value", and typing [Tab][ArrowRight][ArrowRight]2024[Tab] clears it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "supports server validation")
- Given a controlled TimeField named time inside a form with a reset input, when rendered the description is "Selected Time: 8:30 AM" and the hidden input has value "08:30:00" and name "time"; firing ArrowUp keyDown/keyUp on the hour makes the description "Selected Time: 9:30 AM" and the input "09:30:00"; clicking reset restores "Selected Time: 8:30 AM" and "08:30:00". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "supports form reset")
- Given a TimeField named time whose defaultValue comes from React.useActionState with initial Time(8, 30) and an action returning Time(10, 30) (test only defined when parseInt(React.version, 10) >= 19), when submit is clicked, then the hidden input changes from "08:30:00" to "10:30:00". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "resets to defaultValue when submitting form action")
- Given a TimeField with isRequired and validationBehavior="native" inside a Form, when rendered the hidden input has required and validity.valid false and the group has no aria-describedby; after form.checkValidity() the description contains "Constraints not satisfied" and the first spinbutton is focused; [ArrowUp][Tab][ArrowUp][Tab][ArrowUp] makes validity valid while the message persists, and tabbing out clears it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "supports isRequired")
- Given a native TimeField with minValue Time(9), maxValue Time(17) and defaultValue Time(8), when rendered validity.valid is false and the description lacks "Value must be 9:00 AM or later."; after form.checkValidity() the description contains it and the first spinbutton is focused; a single ArrowUp makes validity valid while the message persists, and shift+Tab out of the field clears it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "supports minValue and maxValue")
- Given that same native TimeField, when "6[Tab][ArrowUp]" sets 6 PM, then validity.valid is false; after tabbing out and calling form.checkValidity() the description contains "Value must be 5:00 PM or earlier." and the first spinbutton is focused; ArrowDown makes validity valid while the message persists, and blurring the active element clears it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "supports minValue and maxValue")
- Given a native TimeField with defaultValue Time(8) and validate returning "Invalid value" when hour < 9, when rendered the description lacks "Invalid value" and validity.valid is false; after form.checkValidity() the description contains it and the first spinbutton is focused; typing "10" makes validity valid while the message persists, and blurring the active element clears it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "supports validate function")
- Given a native TimeField with defaultValue Time(9) inside a Form whose onSubmit sets validationErrors {date: 'Invalid value'}, when submit is clicked the description contains "Invalid value" and validity.valid is false; after shift+Tab then [ArrowUp][Tab], the message is gone and validity is valid. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "supports server validation")
- Given a native required TimeField with errorMessage as a function returning "Please enter a value" for e.validationDetails.valueMissing, when form.checkValidity() is called, then the group's aria-describedby element has text content "Please enter a value". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "supports customizing native error messages")
- Given a native required TimeField whose description contains "Constraints not satisfied" after form.checkValidity(), when the reset Button is clicked, then the group no longer has aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "clears validation on form reset")
- Given an aria-validated TimeField with minValue Time(9), maxValue Time(17) and defaultValue Time(8), when rendered the description already contains "Value must be 9:00 AM or later."; [Tab][ArrowUp] clears it, "6[Tab][ArrowUp]" produces "Value must be 5:00 PM or earlier", and [Tab][Tab][ArrowDown] clears that. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "supports minValue and maxValue")
- Given an aria-validated TimeField with defaultValue Time(8) and validate returning "Invalid value" for hour < 9, when rendered the group has aria-describedby containing "Invalid value", and typing [Tab]10 clears it without leaving the field. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "supports validate function")
- Given an aria-validated TimeField named value with defaultValue Time(9) inside a Form with validationErrors {value: 'Invalid value'}, when rendered the group has aria-describedby containing "Invalid value", and [Tab][ArrowUp][Tab][Tab][Tab] clears it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/TimeField.test.js: "supports server validation")
- Given `name="birthday"`, `form="test"` and the value 2020-02-03, when rendered, then a hidden input named birthday holds the ISO string "2020-02-03" and carries the form attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should support form value")
- Given a required DateField with a FieldError inside a form, when the form's checkValidity runs and the microtask flushes, then the hidden input has `required` and is invalid, the group gains aria-describedby containing "Constraints not satisfied" plus `data-invalid`, and focus moves to the first segment; filling all three segments makes the hidden input valid while the message stays until blur, when both the description and data-invalid clear. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "supports validation errors")
- Given a required DateField with `isInvalid={false}` explicitly controlled, when checkValidity runs, then the hidden input is still natively invalid but the group gets no aria-describedby and no `data-invalid`: the controlled prop wins over computed validation. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should use controlled validation first")
- Given a DateField with an empty value, when the browser autofills the hidden `input[type=date]` with "2000-05-30", then the visible segments show "5/30/2000". This pins browser autofill support. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "should support autofill")
- Given a HiddenDateInput driven by useDateFieldState, when the hidden `input[type=date]` receives a typed value (the autofill path), then onChange is called with the parsed CalendarDate for 2000-05-30. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/HiddenDateInput.test.js: "should trigger onChange when input onchange is triggered (autofill)")
- Given a HiddenDateInput with autoComplete and a name, when rendered, then its container has `data-a11y-ignore="aria-hidden-focus"` so accessibility linters do not flag the focusable hidden input. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/HiddenDateInput.test.js: "should always add a data attribute data-a11y-ignore=\"aria-hidden-focus\"")
- Given the same, when rendered, then the container also has `data-react-aria-prevent-focus` so focus management skips it. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/HiddenDateInput.test.js: "should always add a data attribute data-react-aria-prevent-focus")
- Given `name="time"`, `form="test"` and the value 08:30, when a TimeField renders, then the hidden input holds "08:30:00" with the form attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TimeField.test.js: "should support form value")
- Given a required TimeField with a FieldError in a form, when checkValidity runs, then the group is described by "Constraints not satisfied", focus moves to the first segment, filling the segments makes the hidden input valid, and blurring clears the message. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/TimeField.test.js: "supports validation errors")

### RTL and i18n (locale-aware parsing, number formats, RTL arrow keys)

- Given a DateField with showFormatHelpText inside a Provider with locale="zh-CN-u-ca-chinese", when rendered, then the segments carrying data-testid inside the group are exactly ['year', 'month', 'day'] in that order and rendering does not crash on segment types the component does not recognize. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateField.test.js: "does not crash on unknown segment types")
- Given a `zh-CN-u-ca-chinese` locale (a calendar whose formatter yields segment types the component does not model), when a DateField renders, then it does not crash and the rendered segment types are year, literal, month, day in that order. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "does not crash on unknown segment types")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a button focused next to a DateField whose last segment still holds a stale selection anchor, when a `selectionchange` event fires and `window.getSelection()` reports that anchor, then the component does not call `collapse`, so focus is not stolen back into the segment. This is a regression test for a Firefox stale-selection quirk (issue 10259). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateField.test.js: "does not collapse the selection onto a segment while another element is focused")

## date-picker

### Roles and attributes

- Given a DatePicker with value={new CalendarDate(2019, 2, 3)}, when rendered, then the first element with role="group" is visible and has neither aria-disabled nor aria-invalid. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should render a datepicker with a specified date")
- Given a DatePicker with value={new CalendarDate(2019, 2, 3)}, when rendered, then there are exactly 3 role="spinbutton" segments: month with text "2", aria-label "month, ", aria-valuenow "2", aria-valuetext "2 – February", aria-valuemin "1", aria-valuemax "12"; day with text "3", aria-label "day, ", aria-valuenow "3", aria-valuetext "3", aria-valuemin "1", aria-valuemax "31"; year with text "2019", aria-label "year, ", aria-valuenow "2019", aria-valuetext "2019", aria-valuemin "1", aria-valuemax "9999". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should render a datepicker with a specified date")
- Given a DatePicker with value={new CalendarDateTime(2019, 2, 3)} and granularity="second", when rendered, then the group is visible with no aria-disabled and no aria-invalid, and there are exactly 7 spinbutton segments. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should render a datepicker with granularity=\"second\"")
- Given a DatePicker with granularity="second", when rendered, then the hour segment has text "12", aria-label "hour, ", aria-valuenow "12", aria-valuetext "12 AM", aria-valuemin "1", aria-valuemax "12"; minute has text "00", aria-label "minute, ", aria-valuenow "0", aria-valuetext "00", aria-valuemin "0", aria-valuemax "59"; second has text "00", aria-label "second, ", aria-valuenow "0", aria-valuetext "00", aria-valuemin "0", aria-valuemax "59"; the day period segment has text "AM", aria-label "AM/PM, " and aria-valuetext "AM". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should render a datepicker with granularity=\"second\"")
- Given a DatePicker with data-testid="foo", when rendered, then the element found by that test id has role="group", so arbitrary data attributes land on the group. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should pass through data attributes")
- Given a DatePicker with label="Date", when rendered, then the group has aria-labelledby pointing at the label element's id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support labeling")
- Given a DatePicker with label="Date", when rendered, then the calendar trigger button has aria-label "Calendar", an id, and aria-labelledby "<buttonId> <labelId>". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support labeling")
- Given a DatePicker with label="Date", when rendered, then every spinbutton segment has an id and aria-labelledby "<segmentId> <labelId>". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support labeling")
- Given a DatePicker with aria-label="Birth date" and no label, when rendered, then the group has an id and aria-label "Birth date", the inner date field (data-testid "date-field") has role="presentation" and no aria-label, the button has aria-label "Calendar" and aria-labelledby "<buttonId> <groupId>", and each segment's aria-label ends with " Birth date" with no aria-labelledby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support labeling with aria-label")
- Given a DatePicker with aria-labelledby="foo", when rendered, then the group has no aria-label and aria-labelledby "foo", the date field has role="presentation" and no aria-labelledby, the button has aria-label "Calendar" and aria-labelledby "<buttonId> foo", and every segment has aria-labelledby "<segmentId> foo". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support labeling with aria-labelledby")
- Given a DatePicker with description="Help text" and no value, when rendered, then the group has aria-describedby pointing at an element whose text is "Help text", the inner date field has no aria-describedby, only the first segment has aria-describedby equal to that description id, and the remaining segments have no aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support help text description")
- Given a DatePicker with errorMessage="Error message" and validationState="invalid", when rendered, then the group has aria-describedby pointing at an element whose text is "Error message", the inner date field has no aria-describedby, and every segment has aria-describedby equal to the group's aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support error message")
- Given a DatePicker with errorMessage="Error message" but no validationState, when rendered, then neither the group, nor the inner date field, nor any segment has aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should not display error message if not invalid")
- Given a DatePicker with description="Help text" and value={new CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3)}, when rendered, then the group's aria-describedby ids concatenate to "Selected Date: February 3, 2020 Help text", the inner date field has no aria-describedby, only the first segment carries the full aria-describedby and later segments have none. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support help text with a value")
- Given a DatePicker with errorMessage="Error message", validationState="invalid" and value={new CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3)}, when rendered, then the group's aria-describedby ids concatenate to "Selected Date: February 3, 2020 Error message" and every segment has aria-describedby equal to the group's. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support error message with a value")
- Given a DatePicker with showFormatHelpText, when rendered, then the group, the inner date field, and every segment all lack aria-describedby, because each segment already has a label and the format text would be duplicative. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support format help text")
- Given a DatePicker with value={new CalendarDate('BC', 5, 2, 3)}, when rendered, then the group's aria-describedby text is "Selected Date: February 3, 5 BC" and the fourth spinbutton segment has text content "BC". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should include era for BC dates")
- Given DatePicker (3 segments) or DateRangePicker (6 segments) with label="Date" via it.each over Name/Component/numSegments, when rendered, then the group is visible with no aria-disabled and no aria-invalid, the segment count matches numSegments, each segment has no aria-disabled, contentEditable="true", inputMode="numeric" and is not aria-readonly="true", and the first button is visible with tabindex "0". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePickerBase.test.js: "$Name should render a default datepicker")
- Given DatePicker or DateRangePicker with isDisabled (it.each over Name/Component), when rendered, then the group has aria-disabled="true", every segment has aria-disabled="true" and lacks contentEditable="true" and inputMode="numeric", and the first button has the disabled attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePickerBase.test.js: "$Name should set aria-disabled when isDisabled")
- Given DatePicker or DateRangePicker with isReadOnly (it.each over Name/Component), when rendered, then the group does not have aria-readonly="true", every segment has aria-readonly="true", and the first button has the disabled attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePickerBase.test.js: "$Name should set aria-readonly when isReadOnly")
- Given DatePicker or DateRangePicker with isRequired (it.each over Name/Component), when rendered, then the group does not have aria-required="true" but every segment has aria-required="true". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePickerBase.test.js: "$Name should set aria-required when isRequired")
- Given DatePicker or DateRangePicker with validationState="invalid" (it.each over Name/Component), when rendered, then the group does not have aria-invalid="true" but every segment has aria-invalid="true". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePickerBase.test.js: "$Name should set aria-invalid when validationState=\"invalid\"")
- Given DatePicker or DateRangePicker with placeholderValue={parseZonedDateTime('2021-11-07T00:45-07:00[America/Los_Angeles]')} (it.each over Name/Component), when rendered, then every element with data-testid "timeZoneName" has role="textbox", aria-readonly="true", text content "PDT", and no contenteditable attribute. - Given a Provider with isDisabled wrapping DatePicker or DateRangePicker with isDisabled (it.each over Name/Component), when rendered, then the group has aria-disabled="true", every segment has aria-disabled="true", and the first button has the disabled attribute. - Given DatePicker with defaultValue CalendarDate(2019, 7, 5) or DateRangePicker with a 2019-07-05 to 2019-07-08 range plus shouldForceLeadingZeros (it.each over Name/Component/props), when rendered, then the literal text nodes of every segment except the one with data-testid "year" start with "0". - Given DatePicker or DateRangePicker (it.each over Name/Component), when rendered closed, then the group has neither aria-haspopup="dialog" nor aria-owns, every segment has neither aria-expanded nor aria-controls, and the trigger button has aria-haspopup="dialog", aria-expanded="false" and no aria-controls. - Given that same DateRangePicker, when the end field segments are inspected, then segment 3 shows "5" with aria-label "month, End Date, ", aria-valuenow "5", aria-valuetext "5 – May", aria-valuemin "1" and aria-valuemax "12"; segment 4 shows "6" with aria-label "day, End Date, ", aria-valuenow "6", aria-valuetext "6", aria-valuemin "1" and aria-valuemax "31"; segment 5 shows "2019" with aria-label "year, End Date, ", aria-valuenow "2019", aria-valuetext "2019", aria-valuemin "1" and aria-valuemax "9999". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should render a DateRangePicker with a specified date range")
- Given a DateRangePicker with granularity="second" and CalendarDateTime start and end values, when rendered, then the first group is visible with no aria-disabled and no aria-invalid and there are exactly 14 spinbutton segments, seven per field. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should render a DateRangePicker granularity="second"")
- Given that granularity="second" DateRangePicker, when the start field's time segments are inspected, then the hour shows "12" with aria-label "hour, Start Date, ", aria-valuenow "12", aria-valuetext "12 AM", aria-valuemin "1" and aria-valuemax "12"; the minute shows "00" with aria-label "minute, Start Date, ", aria-valuenow "0", aria-valuetext "00", aria-valuemin "0" and aria-valuemax "59"; the second shows "00" with aria-label "second, Start Date, ", aria-valuenow "0", aria-valuetext "00", aria-valuemin "0" and aria-valuemax "59"; the day period shows "AM" with aria-label "AM/PM, Start Date, " and aria-valuetext "AM" and no aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin or aria-valuemax assertions. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should render a DateRangePicker granularity="second"")
- Given that granularity="second" DateRangePicker, when the end field's segments are inspected, then segments 7 to 13 mirror the start field with aria-labels "month, End Date, ", "day, End Date, ", "year, End Date, ", "hour, End Date, ", "minute, End Date, ", "second, End Date, " and "AM/PM, End Date, ", with values 5 ("5 – May"), 6, 2019, 12 ("12 AM"), 00, 00 and AM. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should render a DateRangePicker granularity="second"")
- Given a DateRangePicker with data-testid="foo", when rendered, then the element carrying that test id has role="group". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should pass through data attributes")
- Given a DateRangePicker with label "Date range", when rendered, then the first group has aria-labelledby equal to the label's id, the start-date and end-date wrappers both have role="presentation" and no aria-labelledby, and the calendar trigger button has aria-label "Calendar", an id, and aria-labelledby="{buttonId} {labelId}". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support labeling")
- Given that labeled DateRangePicker, when the segments are inspected, then every spinbutton in the start-date wrapper has an id, an aria-label ending in " Start Date, " and aria-labelledby="{segmentId} {labelId}", and every spinbutton in the end-date wrapper has an id, an aria-label ending in " End Date, " and the same aria-labelledby shape. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support labeling")
- Given a DateRangePicker with aria-label="Birth date" and no visible label, when rendered, then the first group has aria-label "Birth date" and an id, start-date and end-date wrappers have role="presentation" with no aria-labelledby, the trigger button has aria-label "Calendar" and aria-labelledby="{buttonId} {fieldId}", and each segment has aria-labelledby="{segmentId} {fieldId}" with an aria-label ending in " Start Date, " or " End Date, ". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support labeling with aria-label")
- Given a DateRangePicker with aria-labelledby="foo", when rendered, then the first group has aria-labelledby "foo", the start-date and end-date wrappers have role="presentation" with no aria-labelledby, the trigger button has aria-label "Calendar" and aria-labelledby="{buttonId} foo", and each segment has aria-labelledby="{segmentId} foo" with an aria-label ending in " Start Date, " or " End Date, ". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support labeling with aria-labelledby")
- Given a DateRangePicker with description="Help text", when rendered, then the group has aria-describedby pointing at an element with text "Help text", and within each of the start and end fields only the first segment carries aria-describedby equal to the group's value while the remaining segments have none. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support help text description")
- Given a DateRangePicker with errorMessage="Error message" and validationState="invalid", when rendered, then the group has aria-describedby pointing at an element with text "Error message" and every one of the six segments has aria-describedby equal to the group's value. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support error message")
- Given a DateRangePicker with errorMessage but no validationState, when rendered, then neither the group nor the start-date wrapper nor the end-date wrapper nor any segment has aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should not display error message if not invalid")
- Given a DateRangePicker with description="Help text" and value Feb 3 2020 to Feb 10 2020, when rendered, then the group's aria-describedby ids resolve to "Selected Range: February 3 to 10, 2020 Help text", the start-date and end-date wrappers have no aria-describedby, the first segment of each field resolves to the same combined description, and the later segments of each field have none. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support help text with a value")
- Given a DateRangePicker with errorMessage="Error message", validationState="invalid" and value Feb 3 2020 to Feb 10 2020, when rendered, then the group's description resolves to "Selected Range: February 3 to 10, 2020 Error message" and every segment in both the start and end fields resolves to that same combined description. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support error message with a value")
- Given a DateRangePicker with value CalendarDateTime(2020, 2, 3, 8) to CalendarDateTime(2020, 2, 10, 10), when rendered, then the group's description resolves to "Selected Range: February 3, 2020 at 8:00 AM to February 10, 2020 at 10:00 AM" and the start-date and end-date wrappers have no aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should have selected range description with a time")
- Given a DateRangePicker whose start and end are the identical CalendarDateTime(2020, 2, 3, 8), when rendered, then the group's description still spells both endpoints out as "Selected Range: February 3, 2020 at 8:00 AM to February 3, 2020 at 8:00 AM" rather than collapsing them. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should handle selected range description when start and end dates are the same")
- Given a DateRangePicker with showFormatHelpText, when rendered, then neither the group nor the start-date wrapper nor the end-date wrapper nor any segment has aria-describedby, because each segment already carries its own label. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support format help text")
- Given a DateRangePicker with value {start: CalendarDate('BC', 1, 12, 3), end: CalendarDate(1, 1, 10)}, when rendered, then the group's description resolves to "Selected Range: December 3, 1 BC to January 10, 1 AD" and segment index 3 has text content "BC", so an era segment is added to the start field. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should include era for BC dates")
- Given a RAC DatePicker with Label, a Group containing a DateInput and a Button, description and errorMessage Text slots, and a Popover with a Dialog and Calendar, when rendered, then the DateInput text is "mm/dd/yyyy", the trigger Button gets `aria-label="Calendar"` automatically, the outer wrapper carries the DatePicker data props, the group's aria-labelledby points at the `react-aria-Label`, its aria-describedby resolves to "Description Error", and every segment has class `react-aria-DateSegment` with `data-placeholder="true"` and a `data-type`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "provides slots")
- Given the same DatePicker, when the trigger button is clicked, then a Dialog with class `react-aria-Dialog` opens whose aria-labelledby includes the field label id, it sits inside a `react-aria-Popover` carrying `data-trigger="DatePicker"`, and the calendar grid has class `react-aria-CalendarGrid`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "provides slots")
- Given a DatePickerContext "test" slot with an aria-label, when `slot="test"` is used, then the wrapper has the slot attribute and the group gets the aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "should support the slot prop")
- Given `isRequired` toggled on a DatePicker, when rerendered, then the outer `react-aria-DatePicker` gains `data-required`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "should support required state")
- Given `data-testid` on a DatePicker, when rendered, then exactly one element has it and it is the outer `react-aria-DatePicker` wrapper. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "should render data- attributes only on the outer element")
- Given `isDisabled` on a DatePicker, when rendered, then the trigger button is natively disabled, the group has `aria-disabled="true"`, every segment has `aria-disabled="true"`, and the hidden form input carries the `disabled` attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "should disable button and date input when DatePicker is disabled")
- Given a RAC DateRangePicker with start and end DateInput slots, a Button, and a RangeCalendar in a Popover, when rendered, then both inputs show "mm/dd/yyyy", the button gets `aria-label="Calendar"`, the wrapper carries the data props, the group's aria-labelledby points at the Label and aria-describedby resolves to "Description Error", and every segment has the DateSegment class with `data-placeholder` and `data-type`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "provides slots")
- Given the same DateRangePicker, when the trigger opens, then the Dialog's aria-labelledby includes the field label id and the Popover has `data-trigger="DateRangePicker"`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "provides slots")
- Given a DateRangePickerContext "test" slot, when `slot="test"` is used, then the wrapper has the slot and the group gets the aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support the slot prop")
- Given `isRequired` toggled on a DateRangePicker, when rerendered, then the wrapper gains `data-required`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support required state")
- Given `data-testid` on a DateRangePicker, when rendered, then only the outer wrapper carries it. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should render data- attributes only on the outer element")
- Given `isDisabled` on a DateRangePicker, when rendered, then the button is disabled, the group and every segment are `aria-disabled="true"`, and the hidden inputs are disabled. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should disable button and date input when DatePicker is disabled")

### Keyboard

- Given a focused DatePicker with onKeyDown and onKeyUp handlers, when Tab moves focus into the first segment, then onKeyDown has not been called and onKeyUp has been called once; pressing ArrowRight then moves focus to the second segment with onKeyDown called once and onKeyUp called twice. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should trigger right arrow key event for segment navigation")
- Given an open calendar popover on a DatePicker with onKeyDown, onKeyUp, onFocus, onFocusChange and onBlur, when ArrowRight is pressed inside the dialog, then onKeyDown and onKeyUp are called 0 times, onBlur is not called, and onFocus and onFocusChange stay at 1 call each. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should trigger key event in popover and focus/blur/key events are not called")
- Given DatePicker or DateRangePicker (it.each over Name/Component) with the first segment focused, when ArrowRight is pressed repeatedly, then focus walks through every segment in order and then lands on the trigger button; pressing ArrowLeft from the button walks back through the segments in reverse. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePickerBase.test.js: "$Name should support arrow keys to move between segments")
- Given a closed DatePicker or DateRangePicker (it.each over Name/Component), when keyDown with key "ArrowDown" and altKey true is fired on the group, then a role="dialog" is visible with an id, the button gets aria-expanded="true" and aria-controls equal to the dialog id, and focus lands on an element whose parent has role="gridcell". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePickerBase.test.js: "$Name should open a calendar popover pressing Alt + ArrowDown on the keyboard")
- Given a focused month segment, when ArrowUp and ArrowDown are pressed, then onChange fires with the month incremented and decremented by 1; in controlled mode the segment text does not change, in uncontrolled mode it does, and with isReadOnly onChange is never called and the text never changes (all five modes are exercised by the shared testArrows helper). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the arrow keys to increment and decrement the month")
- Given a focused month segment at December or January, when ArrowUp or ArrowDown is pressed, then the month wraps to January or December respectively without changing the year; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should wrap around when incrementing and decrementing the month")
- Given a focused month segment, when PageUp or PageDown is pressed, then the month moves by 2 and wraps within the year (January becomes March or November, February becomes April or December); controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the page up and down keys to increment and decrement the month by 2")
- Given a focused month segment, when End or Home is pressed, then the month jumps to the maximum (December) or minimum (January); controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the home and end keys to jump to the min and max month")
- Given a focused day segment, when ArrowUp and ArrowDown are pressed, then onChange fires with the day incremented and decremented by 1; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the arrow keys to increment and decrement the day")
- Given a focused day segment on the last or first day of a 31 day month, when ArrowUp or ArrowDown is pressed, then the day wraps within the month (31 becomes 1, 1 becomes 31) without changing the month; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should wrap around when incrementing and decrementing the day")
- Given a focused day segment, when PageUp or PageDown is pressed, then the day moves by 7 and wraps within the month; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the page up and down keys to increment and decrement the day by 7")
- Given a focused day segment, when End or Home is pressed, then the day jumps to the last or first day of that month; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the home and end keys to jump to the min and max day")
- Given a focused year segment, when ArrowUp and ArrowDown are pressed, then onChange fires with the year incremented and decremented by 1; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the arrow keys to increment and decrement the year")
- Given a focused year segment at 2019, when PageUp or PageDown is pressed, then the year moves to the nearest multiple of 5 (2020 up, 2015 down); controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the page up and down keys to increment and decrement the year to the nearest 5")
- Given a focused hour segment, when ArrowUp and ArrowDown are pressed, then onChange fires with the hour incremented and decremented by 1; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the arrow keys to increment and decrement the hour")
- Given a focused hour segment in 12 hour time, when ArrowUp or ArrowDown crosses the end of the half day, then the hour wraps inside that half day only: 11 becomes 0 going up and 10 going down, 0 becomes 1 going up and 11 going down, 23 becomes 12 going up and 22 going down, 12 becomes 13 going up and 23 going down; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should wrap around when incrementing and decrementing the hour in 12 hour time")
- Given a focused hour segment with hourCycle={24}, when ArrowUp or ArrowDown crosses midnight, then the hour wraps across the whole day: 23 becomes 0 going up and 22 going down, 0 becomes 1 going up and 23 going down; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should wrap around when incrementing and decrementing the hour in 24 hour time")
- Given a focused hour segment, when PageUp or PageDown is pressed, then the hour moves by 2; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the page up and down keys to increment and decrement the hour by 2")
- Given a focused hour segment in 12 hour time, when End or Home is pressed, then the hour jumps to the max or min of the current half day: 8 goes to 11 or 0, and 16 goes to 23 or 12; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the home and end keys to jump to the min and max hour in 12 hour time")
- Given a focused hour segment with hourCycle={24}, when End or Home is pressed, then the hour jumps to 23 or 0; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the home and end keys to jump to the min and max hour in 24 hour time")
- Given a focused minute segment, when ArrowUp and ArrowDown are pressed, then onChange fires with the minute incremented and decremented by 1; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the arrow keys to increment and decrement the minute")
- Given a focused minute segment at 59 or 0, when ArrowUp or ArrowDown is pressed, then the minute wraps to 0 or 59 without changing the hour; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should wrap around when incrementing and decrementing the minute")
- Given a focused minute segment at 22, when PageUp or PageDown is pressed, then the minute moves to the nearest multiple of 15 (30 up, 15 down); controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the page up and down keys to increment and decrement the minute to the nearest 15")
- Given a focused minute segment with hourCycle={24}, when End or Home is pressed, then the minute jumps to 59 or 0; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the home and end keys to jump to the min and max minute")
- Given a focused second segment with granularity="second", when ArrowUp and ArrowDown are pressed, then onChange fires with the second incremented and decremented by 1; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the arrow keys to increment and decrement the second")
- Given a focused second segment with granularity="second" at 59 or 0, when ArrowUp or ArrowDown is pressed, then the second wraps to 0 or 59 without changing the minute; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should wrap around when incrementing and decrementing the second")
- Given a focused second segment with granularity="second" at 22, when PageUp or PageDown is pressed, then the second moves to the nearest multiple of 15 (30 up, 15 down); controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the page up and down keys to increment and decrement the second to the nearest 15")
- Given a focused second segment with granularity="second" and hourCycle={24}, when End or Home is pressed, then the second jumps to 59 or 0; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the home and end keys to jump to the min and max second")
- Given a focused AM/PM segment, when either ArrowUp or ArrowDown is pressed, then the day period toggles and onChange fires with the hour shifted by 12 in both directions (8 becomes 20 for both keys, 20 becomes 8 for both keys); controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the arrow keys to increment and decrement the day period")
