- Given a DatePicker whose year segment is empty, when a "1" beforeinput is dispatched on the year segment and then ArrowDown is pressed on it, then an era segment (data-testid "era") appears; pressing ArrowDown on that era segment removes it again. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should show and hide the era field as needed")
- Given a DatePicker with defaultValue CalendarDate(2026, 2, 28), when the day segment is reached by two Tabs and ArrowUp is pressed twice to reach 2/30/2026, then onChange is not called while the value is out of range and the field shows "2/30/2026"; tabbing three times out of the field then still leaves onChange uncalled and the field shows the constrained "2/28/2026" (in describe "editing > arrow keys"). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should allow entering invalid dates, and constrain on blur")
- Given a focused month segment with value 2/3/2019, when digits are dispatched as beforeinput events, then "1" sets month 1 and keeps focus, "01" sets month 1 and advances focus to the next segment, "12" sets month 12 and advances, and "4" sets month 4 and advances; in controlled mode the segment text never changes while onChange fires, in uncontrolled mode it does, and with isReadOnly onChange never fires and focus stays put. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support typing into the month segment")
- Given a focused month segment, when "0" or "00" is typed, then onChange is not called, the segment shows "0" while focused, and on blur the segment falls back to "1". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support typing into the month segment")
- Given a focused day segment with value 2/3/2019, when digits are typed, then "1" sets day 1 without moving focus, "01" sets day 1 and advances, "12" sets day 12 and advances, "4" sets day 4 and advances, and "0" or "00" is ignored (segment shows "0" then falls back to "1" on blur); controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support typing into the day segment")
- Given a focused year segment, when "1993" is typed into a date-only DatePicker, then the year becomes 1993 and focus stays on the year segment because it is last; with a CalendarDateTime value the same typing advances focus to the next segment; typing "0" is ignored and the segment falls back to "1" on blur. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support typing into the year segment")
- Given a focused hour segment in 12 hour time with an AM value of 8, when digits are typed, then "1" sets hour 1 without advancing, "01" sets hour 1 and advances, "11" sets hour 11 and advances, "12" sets hour 0 and advances, "4" sets hour 4 and advances, and "0" is ignored with the segment falling back to "12" on blur. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support typing into the hour segment in 12 hour time")
- Given a focused hour segment in 12 hour time with a PM value of 20, when digits are typed, then "1" sets hour 13 without advancing, "01" sets 13 and advances, "11" sets 23 and advances, "12" sets 12 and advances, "4" sets 16 and advances, and "0" is ignored with the segment falling back to "12" on blur, so the PM half day is preserved. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support typing into the hour segment in 12 hour time")
- Given a focused hour segment with hourCycle={24} and value 8, when digits are typed, then "0" sets hour 0 without advancing, "00" sets hour 0 and advances, "1" sets 1 without advancing, "01" sets 1 and advances, "11" sets 11 and advances, and "23" sets 23 and advances, so zero is a valid leading digit in 24 hour time. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support typing into the hour segment in 24 hour time")
- Given a focused minute segment with value 8, when digits are typed, then "0" and "1" and "2" set 0, 1 and 2 without advancing, "00", "01" and "02" set the same values and advance, "5" sets 5 without advancing, "6" sets 6 and advances because no second digit can follow, and "59" sets 59 and advances. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support typing into the minute segment")
- Given a focused second segment with granularity="second" and value 8, when digits are typed, then "0", "1", "2" and "5" set those values without advancing, "00" and "01" set 0 and 1 and advance, "6" sets 6 and advances, and "59" sets 59 and advances. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support typing into the second segment")
- Given a focused AM/PM segment, when "p" is typed on an 8 AM value then the hour becomes 20, and when "a" is typed on a 20 value then the hour becomes 8, and focus does not move either way. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support typing into the day period segment")
- Given a focused year segment with value 2019, when the Arabic-Indic digits "٢٠٢٤" are typed, then onChange fires with year 2024 and focus stays on the year segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support entering arabic digits")
- Given a focused era segment in the Japanese calendar (locale en-US-u-ca-japanese), when "h" is typed on a reiwa value the era becomes heisei, "s" makes it showa, and "r" on a showa value makes it reiwa, with focus staying on the era segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support typing into the era segment")
- Given a focused era segment in the Ethiopic calendar (locale en-US-u-ca-ethiopic), when "A" is typed on an AM value the era becomes AA, and "M" typed on an AA value makes it AM. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support typing into the era segment")
- Given an empty DatePicker, when "02", "31" and "2026" are typed, then onChange has not been called and the group reads "2/31/2026"; tabbing out then calls onChange once with new CalendarDate(2026, 2, 28) and the group reads "2/28/2026" (in describe "editing > text input"). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should allow entering invalid dates, and constrain on blur")
- Given a DatePicker with placeholderValue parseZonedDateTime('2024-09-21T00:00:00[America/Los_Angeles]'), when "3", "8", "2026", "02" and "45" are typed to produce 3/8/2026 2:45 AM PDT, a time that does not exist during the DST spring forward transition, then onChange has not been called and the group shows "3/8/2026, 2:45 AM PDT"; tabbing out twice calls onChange once with parseZonedDateTime('2026-03-08T03:45:00[America/Los_Angeles]') and the group shows "3/8/2026, 3:45 AM PDT". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should allow entering invalid times, and constrain on blur")
- Given a focused month segment, when Backspace is pressed on single digit months 2 and 6, then the segment becomes aria-valuetext "Empty"; on month 12 it drops the last digit and onChange fires with month 1 (controlled keeps the old text, uncontrolled updates it). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support backspace in the month segment")
- Given a focused day segment, when Backspace is pressed on day 3, then the segment becomes aria-valuetext "Empty"; on day 20 it becomes day 2 via onChange. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support backspace in the day segment")
- Given a focused year segment, when Backspace is pressed on 2019, then onChange fires with year 201; on a single digit year 2 the segment becomes aria-valuetext "Empty". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support backspace in the year segment")
- Given a focused hour segment in 12 hour time, when Backspace is pressed on 8 AM or 4 PM (hour 16, shown as a single digit), then the segment becomes aria-valuetext "Empty"; on 11 AM it becomes hour 1 and on 11 PM (hour 23) it becomes hour 13, keeping the day period. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support backspace in the hour segment in 12 hour time")
- Given a focused hour segment with hourCycle={24}, when Backspace is pressed on hour 8, then the segment becomes aria-valuetext "Empty"; on 11 it becomes 1, on 16 it becomes 1, and on 23 it becomes 2. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support backspace in the hour segment in 24 hour time")
- Given a focused AM/PM segment with either an AM or a PM value, when Backspace is pressed, then onChange is not called and the segment is cleared (the helper skips the "Empty" valuetext assertion for the AM/PM label). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support backspace in the am/pm field")
- Given a focused minute segment, when Backspace is pressed on minute 8, then the segment becomes aria-valuetext "Empty"; on 25 it becomes 2 and on 59 it becomes 5. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support backspace in the minute segment")
- Given a focused second segment with granularity="second", when Backspace is pressed on second 8, then the segment becomes aria-valuetext "Empty"; on 25 it becomes 2 and on 59 it becomes 5. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support second in the minute segment")
- Given a DatePicker with defaultValue CalendarDate(2019, 2, 3), when the year segment is reached with two shift+Tabs and five Backspaces are pressed, then onChange has fired 3 times and the group reads "2/3/yyyy"; two more Backspaces clear the day with no further onChange and the group reads "2/dd/yyyy"; two more clear the month, the group reads "mm/dd/yyyy" and onChange is called once with null. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should trigger onChange with null when all segments are cleared")
- Given a DateRangePicker with onKeyDown and onKeyUp handlers, when the picker is tabbed into, then onKeyDown has not been called and onKeyUp has been called once; firing ArrowRight keyDown and keyUp then moves focus to the second segment with onKeyDown called once and onKeyUp twice. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should trigger right arrow key event for segment navigation")
- Given an open calendar popover on a DateRangePicker with onKeyDown, onKeyUp, onBlur, onFocus and onFocusChange, when ArrowRight is fired on the active element inside the dialog, then onKeyDown and onKeyUp are both still at zero calls and onFocus and onFocusChange stay at one call each with onBlur never called, so key events inside the popover do not reach the picker's handlers. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should trigger key event in popover and focus/blur/key events are not called")
- Given an uncontrolled DateRangePicker with defaultValue Feb 3 2019 to May 6 2019, when the start month segment is focused and ArrowDown is fired, then the segment text becomes "1" and onChange is called once with {start: CalendarDate(2019, 1, 3), end: CalendarDate(2019, 5, 6)}; focusing the end year and firing ArrowUp then makes it "2020" and calls onChange a second time with {start: CalendarDate(2019, 1, 3), end: CalendarDate(2020, 5, 6)}. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should edit a date range with the arrow keys (uncontrolled)")
- Given a controlled DateRangePicker with value Feb 3 2019 to May 6 2019, when the start month segment is focused and ArrowDown is fired, then the displayed text stays "2" while onChange is called with {start: CalendarDate(2019, 1, 3), end: CalendarDate(2019, 5, 6)}; firing ArrowUp on the end year leaves it at "2019" while onChange is called a second time with {start: CalendarDate(2019, 2, 3), end: CalendarDate(2020, 5, 6)}, computed from the unchanged controlled value. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should edit a date range with the arrow keys (controlled)")
- Given an uncontrolled DateRangePicker with defaultValue Feb 3 2019 to May 6 2019, when a beforeinput event with data "8" is dispatched on the start month (jsdom does not support beforeinput, so the test constructs an InputEvent with inputType insertText), then the month shows "8", onChange is called once with start CalendarDate(2019, 8, 3), and focus advances to the "day, Start Date," segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should edit a date range by entering text (uncontrolled)")
- Given that same uncontrolled picker, when "2", "0", "2", "2" are typed into the end year via beforeinput, then the year shows "2022" and onChange has been called five times in total, the last with {start: CalendarDate(2019, 8, 3), end: CalendarDate(2022, 5, 6)}, so each digit fires onChange. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should edit a date range by entering text (uncontrolled)")
- Given a controlled DateRangePicker with value Feb 3 2019 to May 6 2019, when "8" is typed into the start month via beforeinput, then the displayed month stays "2", onChange is called once with start CalendarDate(2019, 8, 3), and focus still advances to the "day, Start Date," segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should edit a date range by entering text (controlled)")
- Given that same controlled picker, when "4" is typed into the end day (currently "6"), then the display stays "6" and onChange is called a second time with {start: CalendarDate(2019, 2, 3), end: CalendarDate(2019, 5, 4)}. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should edit a date range by entering text (controlled)")
- Given an uncontrolled DateRangePicker with defaultValue ending in year 2019, when Backspace is fired on the focused end year segment, then the text becomes "201" and onChange is called once with end CalendarDate(201, 5, 6), so Backspace drops the last typed digit rather than clearing the segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support backspace (uncontrolled)")
- Given a controlled DateRangePicker with value ending in year 2019, when Backspace is fired on the focused end year segment, then the display stays "2019" while onChange is called once with end CalendarDate(201, 5, 6). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support backspace (controlled)")
- Given an uncontrolled granularity="minute" DateRangePicker with an open popover, when the hour segment of a time field is focused and ArrowRight fired, then focus moves to a segment with aria-label "minute, " and aria-valuetext "Empty", and another ArrowRight moves to a segment with aria-label "AM/PM, " and aria-valuetext "AM", so the popover time fields support arrow navigation between their own segments. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should not fire onChange until both date range and time range are selected")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given an empty DatePicker, when the inner date field (data-testid "date-field") is clicked, then the first segment receives focus. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should focus the first segment on mouse down in the field")
- Given an empty DatePicker whose first segment has been filled with ArrowUp, when the date field is clicked, then focus goes to the second segment, the first unfilled one. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should focus the first unfilled segment on mouse down in the field")
- Given a DatePicker with value={new CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3)}, when the date field is clicked, then focus goes to the last (third) segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should focus the last segment on mouse down in the field with a value")
- Given DatePicker or DateRangePicker (it.each over Name/Component) with installPointerEvent active, when a pointerdown with pointerType "mouse" is fired on the first literal "/" element, then the segment before it (the first segment) receives focus. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePickerBase.test.js: "$Name should focus the previous segment on mouse down on a literal segment")
- Given DatePicker or DateRangePicker (it.each over Name/Component), when the trigger button is clicked, then the calendar dialog opens and focus lands on an element whose parentElement has role="gridcell". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePickerBase.test.js: "$Name should open a calendar popover when clicking the button")
- Given DatePicker or DateRangePicker (it.each over Name/Component), when touchStart and touchEnd are fired on the group to simulate a tap on the date field with a touch device, then the calendar dialog opens, the button gets aria-expanded="true" and aria-controls pointing at the dialog, and focus lands inside a gridcell. (skipped in repo) (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePickerBase.test.js: "$Name should open a calendar popover when tapping on the date field with a touch device")
- Given an uncontrolled DateRangePicker with defaultValue Feb 3 2019 to May 6 2019, when the trigger button is clicked, then a role=dialog is visible, the selected gridcell's child has aria-label "Selected Range: Sunday, February 3 to Monday, May 6, 2019, Sunday, February 3, 2019 selected", and the start and end fields read "2/3/2019" and "5/6/2019". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should emit onChange when selecting a date range in the calendar in uncontrolled mode")
- Given that open calendar, when February 10 then February 17 2019 are clicked, then the dialog is removed from the document, onChange is called exactly once with {start: CalendarDate(2019, 2, 10), end: CalendarDate(2019, 2, 17)}, and the uncontrolled fields update to "2/10/2019" and "2/17/2019". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should emit onChange when selecting a date range in the calendar in uncontrolled mode")
- Given a DateRangePicker whose defaultValue uses CalendarDateTime (Feb 3 2019 8:45 AM to May 6 2019 10:45 AM), when rendered, then the start field reads "2/3/2019, 8:45 AM", the end field reads "5/6/2019, 10:45 AM", and opening the popover shows a "Start time" field reading "8:45 AM" and an "End time" field reading "10:45 AM". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should display time fields when a CalendarDateTime value is used")
- Given that open popover with time fields, when February 10 then February 17 are clicked, then the dialog stays visible (selecting a date does not close it when time fields are present), onChange is called once with {start: CalendarDateTime(2019, 2, 10, 8, 45), end: CalendarDateTime(2019, 2, 17, 10, 45)}, and the fields read "2/10/2019, 8:45 AM" and "2/17/2019, 10:45 AM". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should display time fields when a CalendarDateTime value is used")
- Given that same popover, when the start time field's hour (role spinbutton, aria-valuetext "8 AM") is focused and ArrowUp fired, then its aria-valuetext becomes "9 AM", the dialog stays visible, onChange is called a second time with start CalendarDateTime(2019, 2, 10, 9, 45), and the start field reads "2/10/2019, 9:45 AM". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should display time fields when a CalendarDateTime value is used")
- Given that same popover, when the end time field's hour (aria-valuetext "10 AM") is focused and ArrowUp fired, then its aria-valuetext becomes "11 AM", onChange is called a third time with end CalendarDateTime(2019, 2, 17, 11, 45), and the end field reads "2/17/2019, 11:45 AM". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should display time fields when a CalendarDateTime value is used")
- Given an empty granularity="minute" DateRangePicker, when the popover is opened, then no gridcell has aria-selected="true", both fields show the placeholder "mm/dd/yyyy, ––:–– AM", and the "Start time" and "End time" fields both show "––:–– AM". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should not fire onChange until both date range and time range are selected")
- Given that empty granularity="minute" picker with the popover open, when the first two enabled gridcells are clicked, then the dialog stays visible, onChange has not been called, and both fields still show the full placeholder, so a date range alone does not commit a value. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should not fire onChange until both date range and time range are selected")
- Given that picker with a date range selected in the popover, when the start time field's hour and minute are stepped up with ArrowUp (hour goes from "Empty" to "12 AM", minute from "Empty" to "00"), then onChange is still not called and both fields keep the placeholder, because only the start time is complete. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should not fire onChange until both date range and time range are selected")
- Given that picker with the start time complete, when the end time field's hour and minute are stepped up the same way, then onChange is called exactly once with {start, end} equal to today's month and year with day 1 and day 2 at 12:00 AM as CalendarDateTime values, the dialog stays visible, and both fields render the values formatted by Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US') with the narrow no-break space from formatToParts normalized to a plain space (a Node whitespace difference, nodejs/node#49222). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should not fire onChange until both date range and time range are selected")
- Given an empty granularity="minute" DateRangePicker whose popover has a date range selected but no times entered, when the user clicks document.body to dismiss, then the dialog is removed and onChange is called once with the selected days at 12:00 AM, so the time placeholders are confirmed on blur. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should confirm time placeholders on blur if date range is selected")
- Given an empty granularity="minute" DateRangePicker whose popover has only a start hour entered (aria-valuetext "12 AM") and no date range, when the user clicks document.body, then the dialog is removed and onChange is never called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should not confirm on blur if date range is not selected")
- Given a DatePicker with a value, when the trigger is clicked and the day after the selected date is clicked, then the selected cell's inner element had `aria-label="Sunday, February 3, 2019 selected"` and the dialog closes after selection. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "should support close on select = true")
- Given `shouldCloseOnSelect={false}`, when a date is clicked in the popover, then the dialog stays open. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "should support close on select = false")
- Given a DateRangePicker with a value, when both ends of a new range are clicked, then the selected cell's aria-label reads "Selected Range: Tuesday, January 10 to Friday, January 20, 2023, Tuesday, January 10, 2023 selected" and the dialog closes after the second click. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support close on select = true")
- Given `shouldCloseOnSelect={false}` on a DateRangePicker, when a range is selected, then the dialog stays open. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support close on select = false")
- Given a DateRangePicker with `granularity="second"` and a focusedValue, when a range is picked in the calendar and the popover closes, then both fields show the picked dates with a placeholder time filled in, matching `new Date(...).toLocaleString('en-US')`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should set a placeholder time when closing")

### Focus management

- Given a DatePicker with a ref, when ref.current.focus() is called, then the first spinbutton segment has focus, and the ref exposes a focus method. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support focusing via a ref")
- Given a DatePicker with autoFocus, when rendered, then the first spinbutton segment already has focus. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support autoFocus")
- Given DatePicker or DateRangePicker with autoFocus (it.each over Name/Component), when rendered, then the first segment has focus. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePickerBase.test.js: "$Name should focus the first segment by default if autoFocus is set")
- Given DatePicker or DateRangePicker with isDisabled (it.each over Name/Component), when rendered, then no segment has a tabIndex attribute, so none is focusable. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePickerBase.test.js: "$Name should not be focusable when isDisabled")
- Given a DatePicker with onFocus, onBlur and onFocusChange, when Tab focuses the first segment, then onFocus and onFocusChange have each been called once and onBlur not at all; a second Tab to the next segment leaves all three counts unchanged; clicking the trigger button then opens a visible dialog while onBlur is still not called and onFocus and onFocusChange stay at 1. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should focus field, move a segment, and open popover and does not blur")
- Given a focused DatePicker segment, when document.body is clicked, then body has focus, onBlur has been called once, onFocusChange has been called twice, and onFocus stays at 1. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should focus field and leave to blur")
- Given a DatePicker that has never been focused, when the trigger button is clicked, then the dialog is visible and onFocus and onFocusChange have each been called once while onBlur has not been called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should open popover and call picker onFocus")
- Given an open calendar popover opened from the trigger button, when Escape closes it and the exit animation and raf callbacks run, then focus returns to the trigger button, onBlur has not been called, and onFocus and onFocusChange stay at 1; a following Tab moves focus to document.body and only then does onBlur fire once with onFocusChange reaching 2. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should open and close popover and only call blur when focus leaves picker")
- Given a DatePicker with defaultValue CalendarDate('BC', 2020, 2, 3) whose era segment is the last spinbutton, when the era segment is focused and ArrowUp removes the era, then the era element (data-testid "era") is gone and focus moves to the new last spinbutton, the previous segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should focus the previous segment when the era is removed")
- Given locale "lv-LV" where the era segment is the field's first child, when the era segment is focused and ArrowUp removes the era, then the era element is gone and focus moves forward to the segment whose text is "3". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should focus the next segment when the era is removed and is the first segment")
- Given a DatePicker whose era segment has focus, when the whole picker is replaced by rerendering <div />, then the era element is removed and document.activeElement is document.body with no error thrown. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "does not try to shift focus when the entire datepicker is unmounted while focused")
- Given a DateRangePicker with a ref, when ref.current.focus() is called, then ref.current exposes a focus method and document.activeElement is the first spinbutton segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support focusing via a ref")
- Given a DateRangePicker with autoFocus, when rendered, then document.activeElement is the first spinbutton segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support autoFocus")
- Given a DateRangePicker with a ref, when ref.current.UNSAFE_getDOMNode() is called, then it returns the outermost wrapper element containing the label text "Date" and the first spinbutton segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should return the outer most DOM element from the ref")
- Given a DateRangePicker with onBlur, onFocus and onFocusChange, when Tab focuses the first segment, Tab again moves to the second segment, and then the calendar button is clicked, then the dialog becomes visible while onFocus and onFocusChange stay at one call each and onBlur is never called, so neither segment movement nor opening the popover blurs the picker. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should focus field, move a segment, and open popover and does not blur")
- Given a DateRangePicker focused on its first segment, when document.body is clicked, then document.body has focus, onBlur has been called once, onFocusChange twice and onFocus once. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should focus field and leave to blur")
- Given an unfocused DateRangePicker, when the calendar trigger button is clicked, then the dialog is visible and onFocus and onFocusChange have each been called once with onBlur never called, so opening the popover counts as focusing the picker. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should open popover and call picker onFocus")
- Given an open DateRangePicker popover, when Escape is pressed and the exit animation and timers run, then the dialog is removed from the document, document.activeElement is the trigger button, and onBlur is still not called while onFocus and onFocusChange remain at one call each. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should open and close popover and only call blur when focus leaves picker")
- Given a DateRangePicker whose popover was just closed with focus restored to the trigger button, when Tab moves focus to document.body, then onBlur has been called once, onFocusChange twice and onFocus once. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should open and close popover and only call blur when focus leaves picker")
- Given a DateRangePicker, when the start-date wrapper is clicked, then the first segment of the start field has focus; after blurring, clicking the end-date wrapper focuses the first segment of the end field. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should focus the first segment of each field on mouse down")
- Given a DateRangePicker, when a pointerdown (pointerType mouse, pointerId 1) is dispatched on the element with test id date-range-dash and then it is clicked, then the first segment of the start field has focus, despite the test name saying the end date. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should focus the first segment of the end date on mouse down on the dash")
- Given a DatePicker trigger button, when the popover is open, then the button has `data-pressed`, and it has none while closed. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "should apply isPressed state to button when expanded")
- Given a DateRangePicker trigger button, when expanded, then it gets `data-pressed`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should apply isPressed state to button when expanded")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a controlled DatePicker with value={new CalendarDate(2019, 2, 3)}, when the day after the selected cell is clicked in the open calendar, then the dialog closes, onChange is called once with new CalendarDate(2019, 2, 4), and the group still reads "2/3/2019" because the value is controlled. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should emit onChange when selecting a date in the calendar in controlled mode")
- Given an uncontrolled DatePicker with defaultValue CalendarDate(2019, 2, 3), when the day after the selected cell is clicked in the open calendar, then the dialog closes, onChange is called once with new CalendarDate(2019, 2, 4), and the group reads "2/4/2019". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should emit onChange when selecting a date in the calendar in uncontrolled mode")
- Given a DatePicker with defaultValue CalendarDateTime(2019, 2, 3, 8, 45), when the popover is opened, then the group reads "2/3/2019, 8:45 AM", a field labelled "Time" inside the dialog reads "8:45 AM", and clicking the next day keeps the dialog visible while onChange fires once with CalendarDateTime(2019, 2, 4, 8, 45) and the group reads "2/4/2019, 8:45 AM". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should display a time field when a CalendarDateTime value is used")
- Given the time field inside an open popover, when the hour segment (role spinbutton, aria-valuetext "8 AM") is focused and ArrowUp is pressed, then its aria-valuetext becomes "9 AM", the dialog stays visible, onChange has fired twice with CalendarDateTime(2019, 2, 4, 9, 45), and the group reads "2/4/2019, 9:45 AM". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should display a time field when a CalendarDateTime value is used")
- Given a DatePicker with defaultValue CalendarDateTime(2019, 2, 3, 10, 45) and an open popover, when Backspace is pressed on the time field hour segment showing "10 AM", then its aria-valuetext becomes "1 AM" with onChange fired for CalendarDateTime(2019, 2, 4, 1, 45); a second Backspace makes the aria-valuetext "Empty" without throwing and without a further onChange, and the dialog stays visible. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should not throw error when deleting values from time field when CalendarDateTime value is used")
- Given an empty DatePicker with granularity="minute", when the popover is opened, then no gridcell is aria-selected, the group shows placeholder "mm/dd/yyyy, ––:–– AM", and the time field shows "––:–– AM". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should fire onChange until both date and time are selected")
- Given an empty DatePicker with granularity="minute" and an open popover, when today's cell is clicked, then that cell gets aria-selected="true", the dialog stays visible, onChange has not been called, and the group still shows the full placeholder. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should fire onChange until both date and time are selected")
- Given a date has been picked but the time is still empty, when ArrowUp sets the hour to aria-valuetext "12 AM", then onChange is still not called and the group still shows "mm/dd/yyyy, ––:–– AM"; ArrowRight then moves to the segment with aria-label "minute, " and aria-valuetext "Empty", and one ArrowUp there sets aria-valuetext "00" and finally fires onChange once with toCalendarDateTime(today(getLocalTimeZone())), with the group showing today's date and "12:00 AM". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should fire onChange until both date and time are selected")
- Given the minute has just been set, when ArrowRight moves to the segment with aria-label "AM/PM, ", then its aria-valuetext is "AM", the dialog is still visible and onChange is still at 1 call. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should fire onChange until both date and time are selected")
- Given an empty DatePicker with granularity="minute" where only a calendar date has been picked, when document.body is clicked to blur and close the dialog, then the dialog is removed and onChange is called once with toCalendarDateTime(today(getLocalTimeZone())), so the placeholder time is confirmed on blur. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should confirm time placeholder on blur if date is selected")
- Given an empty DatePicker with granularity="minute" where only the hour has been set to "12 AM" and no date is selected, when document.body is clicked, then the dialog is removed and onChange is never called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should not confirm on blur if date is not selected")
- Given an empty DatePicker with granularity="minute" where today's cell is selected, the hour is set to "12 AM" and the minute stepped twice to "01", when document.body is clicked to close the dialog, then the dialog is removed, onChange has been called twice in total, and the group reads today's date followed by "12:01 AM". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should confirm valid date time on dialog close")
- Given a controlled DatePicker with granularity="minute" whose state has been filled to today's date at 12:00 AM through the popover, when a sibling button sets the controlled value back to null, then the group shows the placeholder "mm/dd/yyyy, ––:–– AM" again; reopening the popover shows no aria-selected gridcell and the time field back at "––:–– AM". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should clear date and time when controlled value is set to null")
- Given a DatePicker with no value, when rendered, then the group shows the placeholder "mm/dd/yyyy". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should display a placeholder if no value is provided")
- Given a DatePicker with value={null}, when rendered, then the group shows the placeholder "mm/dd/yyyy". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should display a placeholder if the value prop is null")
- Given a DatePicker with placeholderValue={new CalendarDate(1980, 1, 1)}, when rendered, then the group still shows the literal placeholder text "mm/dd/yyyy" rather than 1980 values. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should use the placeholderValue prop if provided")
- Given an uncontrolled empty DatePicker, when ArrowUp fills the month and ArrowRight moves on, then focus is on the second segment, onChange has not been called, and the group reads "<today's month>/dd/yyyy"; repeating for the day gives "<month>/<day>/yyyy" with still no onChange; the final ArrowUp on the year calls onChange once with today(getLocalTimeZone()) and the group shows the fully formatted date. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should use arrow keys to modify placeholder (uncontrolled)")
- Given a controlled DatePicker with value={null}, when the same ArrowUp and ArrowRight sequence fills month, day and year, then onChange is called once with today(getLocalTimeZone()) but the group still shows "mm/dd/yyyy"; rerendering with value set to that date makes the group show the formatted date. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should use arrow keys to modify placeholder (controlled)")
- Given an uncontrolled empty DatePicker, when "4" is typed into the month, then focus advances to the day, onChange has not been called and the group reads "4/dd/yyyy"; typing "5" advances to the year with still no onChange and the group reads "4/5/yyyy"; typing "2", "0", "2", "0" into the year fires onChange after each digit for 4 calls total, the last with new CalendarDate(2020, 4, 5), focus stays on the year segment, and the group shows the formatted date. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should enter a date to modify placeholder (uncontrolled)")
- Given a controlled DatePicker with value={null}, when "4" and "5" are typed for month and day and then "2" into the year, then onChange is called once with new CalendarDate(2, 4, 5), focus stays on the year segment and the group still shows "mm/dd/yyyy"; rerendering with value new CalendarDate(2020, 4, 5) makes the group show the formatted date. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should enter a date to modify placeholder (controlled)")
- Given an empty DatePicker with granularity="minute", when the first segment is focused and blurred with nothing entered, then onChange is not called; blurring after each of month "4", day "5", year "2022", hour "5" and minute "45" also leaves onChange uncalled until the minute blur, at which point onChange is called with new CalendarDateTime(2022, 4, 5, 5, 45), confirming the un-entered AM/PM placeholder. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should confirm the placeholder on blur and only AM/PM is un-entered")
- Given a DateRangePicker with no value, when rendered, then both the start-date and end-date fields show the placeholder "mm/dd/yyyy". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should display a placeholder if no value is provided")
- Given a DateRangePicker with value={null}, when rendered, then both fields show the placeholder "mm/dd/yyyy". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should display a placeholder if the value prop is null")
- Given a DateRangePicker with placeholderValue CalendarDate(1980, 1, 1), when rendered, then both fields still show "mm/dd/yyyy" rather than 1/1/1980, so placeholderValue does not change the rendered placeholder text. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should use the placeholderValue prop if provided")
- Given an empty DateRangePicker focused on the first segment, when "2" then "4" then "2020" are typed via beforeinput, then the start field shows "2/dd/yyyy", then "2/4/yyyy", then "2/4/2020", focus advances segment by segment to the end field's first segment, and onChange has still not been called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should not fire onChange until both start and end dates have been entered")
- Given that same picker with the start date complete, when "4" and "8" are typed into the end month and day, then the end field shows "4/dd/yyyy" then "4/8/yyyy", focus advances to the end year, and onChange is still not called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should not fire onChange until both start and end dates have been entered")
- Given that same picker with only the end year left, when "2", "0", "2", "2" are typed, then onChange fires on each of those four digits (1, 2, 3 then 4 calls) and the final call is {start: CalendarDate(2020, 2, 4), end: CalendarDate(2022, 4, 8)}. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should not fire onChange until both start and end dates have been entered")
- Given a controlled DateRangePicker with value Feb 3 2020 to Apr 8 2022 rendering both dates via Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US'), when it is rerendered with value={null}, then both fields fall back to the placeholder "mm/dd/yyyy". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should reset to the placeholder if controlled value is set to null")
- Given a controlled granularity="minute" DateRangePicker whose state starts null, when a date range and both times are entered in the popover and the popover is dismissed by clicking document.body, then both fields render the committed day 1 and day 2 values at 12:00 AM. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should clear date and time when controlled value is set to null")
- Given that controlled picker with a committed value, when a separate Clear button sets the controlled value back to null, then both fields show "mm/dd/yyyy, ––:–– AM", and reopening the popover shows no gridcell with aria-selected="true" and both the Start time and End time fields back at "––:–– AM". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should clear date and time when controlled value is set to null")
- Given a DatePicker whose children are a render function of `{isInvalid}` with a minValue above the value under aria validation, when rendered, then the Group gets `data-validation-state="invalid"`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "should support render props")
- Given a `{isRequired}` render function with `isRequired`, when rendered, then the Group reflects the required render prop. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "should support required render prop")
- Given a `render` prop returning a div with `data-custom`, when rendered, then the DatePicker wrapper is the custom element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "should support custom render function")
- Given the same three render-prop cases on a DateRangePicker, when rendered, then the Group reflects isInvalid and isRequired and the wrapper honors a custom `render` function. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support render props")
- Given a `{isRequired}` render function on a DateRangePicker, when rendered, then the Group reflects it. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support required render prop")
- Given a `render` prop on a DateRangePicker, when rendered, then the wrapper uses the custom element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support custom render function")

### Forms (name, value, validation, form reset, hidden inputs, autofill)

- Given a DatePicker with name="date" and a controlled value of CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3) inside a form, when rendered, then a hidden input[name=date] exists with value "2020-02-03" and the group's description reads "Selected Date: February 3, 2020". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports form reset")
- Given that same form, when Tab focuses the month and ArrowUp increments it, then the description becomes "Selected Date: March 3, 2020" and the hidden input value becomes "2020-03-03"; clicking the input[type=reset] restores "Selected Date: February 3, 2020" and "2020-02-03". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports form reset")
- Given React 19 or newer (the test is wrapped in a version check) and a DatePicker with name="date" whose defaultValue comes from React.useActionState, when the submit input is clicked and the form action returns CalendarDate(2025, 2, 3), then the hidden input[name=date] value goes from "2020-02-03" to "2025-02-03". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "resets to defaultValue when submitting form action")
- Given a DatePicker with name="date", isRequired and validationBehavior="native" inside a Form, when rendered, then the hidden input has the required attribute, input.validity.valid is false, and the group has no aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports isRequired")
- Given that required native DatePicker, when form.checkValidity() runs, then the group gains an aria-describedby whose text contains "Constraints not satisfied" and focus moves to the first spinbutton segment of the group. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports isRequired")
- Given a native validation error is showing, when the keyboard sequence [ArrowUp][Tab][ArrowUp][Tab][ArrowUp] fills the value, then input.validity.valid becomes true but the description still contains "Constraints not satisfied"; only after tabbing out of the field does the message disappear. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports isRequired")
- Given a DatePicker with validationBehavior="native", minValue CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3), maxValue CalendarDate(2024, 2, 3) and defaultValue CalendarDate(2019, 2, 3), when rendered, then input.validity.valid is false and the description does not yet contain "Value must be 2/3/2020 or later."; after form.checkValidity() the group has aria-describedby containing that message and focus moves to the first segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports minValue and maxValue")
- Given that native min/max error is showing, when [Tab][Tab][ArrowUp] raises the year into range, then input.validity.valid becomes true while the message stays until the field is tabbed away from, at which point it is removed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports minValue and maxValue")
- Given the same native DatePicker, when shift+Tab returns to the year and "2025" is typed to exceed maxValue, then input.validity.valid is false but the description does not yet contain "Value must be 2/3/2024 or earlier."; after tabbing out and calling form.checkValidity() the message appears and focus moves to the first segment; [Tab][Tab][ArrowDown] makes validity valid again and the message clears once focus leaves the field. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports minValue and maxValue")
- Given a DatePicker with validationBehavior="native", defaultValue CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3) and validate={v => v.year < 2022 ? 'Invalid value' : null}, when rendered, then input.validity.valid is false and the description does not contain "Invalid value"; after form.checkValidity() the group has aria-describedby containing "Invalid value" and focus moves to the first segment. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports validate function")
- Given that validate error is showing, when [ArrowRight][ArrowRight]2024 sets a passing year, then input.validity.valid becomes true while "Invalid value" remains until the field is tabbed away from, after which the message is gone and validity is still valid. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports validate function")
- Given a Form whose onSubmit sets validationErrors={{date: 'Invalid value'}} and a DatePicker with name="date" and validationBehavior="native", when rendered, then the group has no aria-describedby; after clicking the submit button the description contains "Invalid value" and input.validity.valid is false. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports server validation")
- Given a server validation error is showing, when two shift+Tabs move back into the field and "2024[ArrowLeft]2[ArrowLeft]2" is typed and the active element is blurred, then the description no longer contains "Invalid value" and input.validity.valid is true. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports server validation")
- Given a DatePicker with isRequired, validationBehavior="native" and errorMessage={e => e.validationDetails.valueMissing ? 'Please enter a value' : null}, when form.checkValidity() runs, then the group gains aria-describedby and the referenced element has text content "Please enter a value". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports customizing native error messages")
- Given a DatePicker with isRequired and validationBehavior="native" whose native error is showing after form.checkValidity(), when the reset Button is clicked, then the group no longer has aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "clears validation on form reset")
- Given a DatePicker with isRequired and validationBehavior="native" whose description contains "Constraints not satisfied", when the calendar trigger button is clicked and the focused calendar cell is clicked, then input.validity.valid becomes true and the description no longer contains "Constraints not satisfied". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "updates when selecting a date with the calendar")
- Given a DatePicker inside a Form with default validationBehavior=aria, minValue CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3), maxValue CalendarDate(2024, 2, 3) and defaultValue CalendarDate(2019, 2, 3), when rendered, then the description already contains "Value must be 2/3/2020 or later." with no checkValidity call needed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports minValue and maxValue")
- Given that aria validation DatePicker, when [Tab][Tab][Tab][ArrowUp] raises the year into range, then the min message disappears immediately; five more ArrowUps push past maxValue so the description contains "Value must be 2/3/2024 or earlier."; one ArrowDown clears it again. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports minValue and maxValue")
- Given a DatePicker inside a Form with defaultValue CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3) and validate={v => v.year < 2022 ? 'Invalid value' : null} using aria validation, when rendered, then the group has aria-describedby containing "Invalid value"; typing [Tab][ArrowRight][ArrowRight]2024 removes the message live without a blur. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports validate function")
- Given a Form with validationErrors={{value: 'Invalid value'}} and a DatePicker with name="value" and defaultValue CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3) using aria validation, when rendered, then the group has aria-describedby containing "Invalid value"; typing [Tab][ArrowRight][ArrowRight]2024[Tab] clears it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "supports server validation")
- Given a controlled DatePicker with value CalendarDate(1980, 1, 1) and minValue CalendarDate(1985, 1, 1), when rendered, then the element with data-testid "invalid-icon" is visible. - Given an uncontrolled DatePicker with defaultValue and minValue both CalendarDate(1985, 1, 1), when rendered there is no invalid-icon; focusing the year segment and pressing ArrowDown makes the invalid-icon visible, and pressing ArrowUp removes it again. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should display an error icon when date is less than the minimum (uncontrolled)")
- Given a controlled DatePicker with value CalendarDate(1990, 1, 1) and maxValue CalendarDate(1985, 1, 1), when rendered, then the invalid-icon is visible. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should display an error icon when date is greater than the maximum (controlled)")
- Given an uncontrolled DatePicker with defaultValue and maxValue both CalendarDate(1985, 1, 1), when rendered there is no invalid-icon; focusing the year segment and pressing ArrowUp makes the invalid-icon visible, and pressing ArrowDown removes it again. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should display an error icon when date is greater than the maximum (uncontrolled)")
- Given DatePicker or DateRangePicker with validationState="invalid" (it.each over Name/Component), when rendered, then the element with data-testid "invalid-icon" is visible. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePickerBase.test.js: "$Name should display an error icon when validationState=\"invalid\"")
- Given DatePicker or DateRangePicker with validationState="valid" (it.each over Name/Component), when rendered, then the element with data-testid "valid-icon" is visible. - Given a DateRangePicker with value start CalendarDate(1980, 1, 1) and minValue CalendarDate(1985, 1, 1), when rendered, then the element with test id invalid-icon is visible. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should display an error icon when the start date is less than the minimum (controlled)")
- Given an uncontrolled DateRangePicker with defaultValue start exactly at minValue CalendarDate(1985, 1, 1), when rendered no invalid-icon exists, firing ArrowDown on the "year, Start Date," segment makes the invalid-icon visible, and firing ArrowUp removes it again. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should display an error icon when the start date is less than the minimum (uncontrolled)")
- Given a DateRangePicker with value start CalendarDate(1990, 1, 1) and maxValue CalendarDate(1985, 1, 1), when rendered, then the invalid-icon is visible. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should display an error icon when the start date is greater than the maximum (controlled)")
- Given an uncontrolled DateRangePicker with defaultValue Feb 1 1984 to Feb 3 1984 and maxValue CalendarDate(1985, 1, 1), when rendered no invalid-icon exists, firing ArrowUp on the start year makes it visible, and ArrowDown removes it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should display an error icon when the start date is greater than the maximum (uncontrolled)")
- Given a DateRangePicker with value Jan 1 1980 to Feb 3 1999 and maxValue CalendarDate(1985, 1, 1), when rendered, then the invalid-icon is visible because the end date exceeds the maximum. - Given an uncontrolled DateRangePicker with defaultValue Feb 1 1980 to Feb 3 1984 and maxValue CalendarDate(1985, 1, 1), when rendered no invalid-icon exists, firing ArrowUp on the "year, End Date," segment makes it visible, and ArrowDown removes it. - Given a DateRangePicker with value start Jan 1 1990 and end Feb 3 1980 and no min or max, when rendered, then the invalid-icon is visible because the end is before the start. - Given an uncontrolled DateRangePicker with defaultValue Feb 1 1980 to Feb 3 1980, when rendered no invalid-icon exists, firing ArrowDown on the end year (making the end precede the start) makes it visible, and ArrowUp removes it. - Given a controlled DateRangePicker with startName="start" and endName="end" inside a form with a reset input, when rendered, then the group's description is "Selected Range: February 3, 2020 to April 8, 2022", the hidden input named start has value "2020-02-03" and the one named end has "2022-04-08". - Given that form, when ArrowUp is fired on the first segment the description becomes "Selected Range: March 3, 2020 to April 8, 2022" with start input "2020-03-03" and end unchanged, and when the reset input is clicked both the description and both hidden inputs return to their original values. - Given a DateRangePicker with isRequired and validationBehavior="native" inside a Form, when rendered, then both the start and end hidden inputs have the required attribute and validity.valid false, and the group has no aria-describedby. - Given that required native DateRangePicker, when form.checkValidity() is called, then the group gains an aria-describedby whose text contains "Constraints not satisfied" and document.activeElement is the first spinbutton in the group; filling all six segments with [ArrowUp][Tab] sequences makes both inputs valid while the message persists, and only tabbing out of the picker clears it. - Given a native DateRangePicker with minValue CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3), maxValue CalendarDate(2024, 2, 3) and defaultValue Feb 3 2019 to Feb 3 2025, when form.checkValidity() is called, then the description contains "Value must be 2/3/2020 or later. Value must be 2/3/2024 or earlier." (both messages at once) and the first spinbutton is focused. - Given that native min/max range picker, when [Tab][Tab][ArrowUp] fixes the start year, then both messages are still shown and both inputs are still invalid; tabbing out drops the minimum message but keeps "Value must be 2/3/2024 or earlier."; [Tab][Tab][ArrowDown] on the end year then makes both inputs valid while the message persists until the next tab out. - Given a native DateRangePicker with defaultValue Feb 3 2020 to Feb 3 2021 and validate returning "Invalid value" when either endpoint's year is below 2022, when form.checkValidity() is called the description contains "Invalid value", the first spinbutton is focused, and both inputs are invalid; typing [ArrowRight][ArrowRight]2024 fixes only the start so both inputs remain invalid; typing [ArrowRight][ArrowRight]2026 makes both valid while the message persists; tabbing out clears it. - Given a native required DateRangePicker with errorMessage as a function returning "Please enter a value" for e.validationDetails.valueMissing, when form.checkValidity() is called, then the group's aria-describedby element has text content "Please enter a value". - Given a native required DateRangePicker whose description contains "Constraints not satisfied" after form.checkValidity(), when the reset Button is clicked, then the group no longer has aria-describedby. - Given a native required DateRangePicker showing "Constraints not satisfied", when the calendar button is clicked and the focused cell is clicked twice to pick a start and end date, then the start input's validity.valid becomes true and the description no longer contains "Constraints not satisfied", so selecting in the calendar clears native validation without a blur.
