- Given a DateRangePicker with default validationBehavior (aria), minValue CalendarDate(2020, 2, 3), maxValue CalendarDate(2024, 2, 3) and defaultValue Feb 3 2019 to Feb 3 2025, when rendered the description already contains "Value must be 2/3/2020 or later. Value must be 2/3/2024 or earlier." with no checkValidity call; [Tab][Tab][Tab][ArrowUp] drops the minimum message while keeping the maximum one, and another [Tab][Tab][Tab][ArrowDown] clears the maximum message. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "supports minValue and maxValue")
- Given an aria-validated DateRangePicker with defaultValue Feb 3 2019 to Feb 3 2025 and validate returning "Invalid value" when the start year is below 2022, when rendered the group has aria-describedby containing "Invalid value", and typing [Tab][ArrowRight][ArrowRight]2024 clears it live. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "supports validate function")
- Given an aria-validated DateRangePicker with startName, endName and defaultValue Feb 3 2019 to Feb 3 2025 inside a Form with validationErrors {start: 'Invalid start date.', end: 'Invalid end date.'}, when rendered the description contains "Invalid start date. Invalid end date.", and typing [Tab][ArrowRight][ArrowRight]2024[Tab] clears it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "supports server validation")
- Given `name="birthday"`, `form="test"` and the value 2020-02-03, when a DatePicker renders, then a hidden input named birthday holds "2020-02-03" and carries the form attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "should support form value")
- Given a required DatePicker with a FieldError inside a form, when checkValidity runs, then the hidden input is required and invalid, the group gains aria-describedby containing "Constraints not satisfied", the wrapper gains `data-invalid`, and focus moves to the first segment; filling the segments makes the hidden input valid while the message stays until blur, when both clear. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "supports validation errors")
- Given an empty DatePicker, when the browser autofills the hidden `input[type=date]` with "2000-05-30", then the visible DateInput shows "5/30/2000". This pins browser autofill. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "should support autofill")
- Given `startName`, `endName`, `form` and a value range, when a DateRangePicker renders, then two hidden inputs hold "2023-01-10" and "2023-01-20" and both carry the form attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support form value")
- Given a required DateRangePicker with a FieldError in a form, when checkValidity runs, then both hidden inputs are required and invalid, the group is described by "Constraints not satisfied" with `data-invalid` on the wrapper, focus goes to the first segment, filling all six segments makes both inputs valid, and blurring clears the error. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "supports validation errors")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given an open calendar popover, when Escape is pressed and timers plus the exit animation run, then the dialog is removed from the document. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should open and close popover and only call blur when focus leaves picker")
- Given an open calendar popover on a DatePicker with granularity="minute", when document.body is clicked and timers run, then the dialog is removed from the document. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should confirm time placeholder on blur if date is selected")
- Given an open calendar popover where only the hour has been edited, when document.body is clicked and timers run, then the dialog is removed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should not confirm on blur if date is not selected")
- Given an open calendar popover where a date and time have been set, when document.body is clicked and timers run, then the dialog is removed. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should confirm valid date time on dialog close")
- Given a DatePicker with a CalendarDateTime value and an open popover, when a calendar cell is clicked, then the dialog stays visible instead of closing, because a time still has to be entered. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should display a time field when a CalendarDateTime value is used")
- Given a DatePicker with a date-only value and an open popover, when a calendar cell is clicked, then the dialog is removed from the document. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should emit onChange when selecting a date in the calendar in controlled mode")
- Given an uncontrolled date-only DatePicker with an open popover, when a calendar cell is clicked, then the dialog is removed from the document. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should emit onChange when selecting a date in the calendar in uncontrolled mode")
- Given an open DateRangePicker popover, when Escape keyDown and keyUp are fired on the active element and timers run, then the dialog is removed from the document after the exit animation, waited on with waitFor, and focus returns to the trigger button. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should open and close popover and only call blur when focus leaves picker")
- Given an open DateRangePicker popover with no time fields, when a complete date range is clicked in the calendar, then the popover closes on its own (the dialog is removed from the document). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should emit onChange when selecting a date range in the calendar in uncontrolled mode")
- Given an open DateRangePicker popover that includes time fields, when a complete date range is clicked, then the dialog stays visible so the user can still edit the times. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should display time fields when a CalendarDateTime value is used")
- Given an open granularity="minute" DateRangePicker popover, when document.body is clicked and timers run, then the dialog is removed from the document. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should confirm time placeholders on blur if date range is selected")
- Given a DatePicker, when the popover opens, then the outer `react-aria-DatePicker` element gains `data-open`, and it has none while closed. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "should support data-open state")
- Given a DateRangePicker, when the popover opens, then the wrapper gains `data-open`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should support data-open state")

### RTL and i18n (locale-aware parsing, number formats, RTL arrow keys)

- Given a DatePicker with granularity="minute" in locale "ar-EG" with getBoundingClientRect mocked so segment x positions reflect the Arabic visual order (DayPeriod Hour:Minute Year/Month/Day), when the first segment is focused and ArrowLeft is pressed repeatedly, then focus follows the visual order given by segment index order [0, 1, 2, 4, 3, 5] and then lands on the trigger button; ArrowRight from the button walks back through that same order in reverse. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePickerBase.test.js: "DatePicker should support arrow keys to move between segments in an RTL locale")
- Given a DateRangePicker with granularity="minute" in locale "ar-EG" with the same getBoundingClientRect mock, when ArrowLeft is pressed repeatedly from the first segment, then focus follows segment index order [0, 1, 2, 4, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 9, 11] across both the start and end dates and then reaches the trigger button, with ArrowRight reversing the walk. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePickerBase.test.js: "DateRangePicker should support arrow keys to move between segments in an RTL locale")
- Given a DatePicker in locale "ar-EG" with defaultValue CalendarDate(2019, 2, 3), when the year segment (found by aria-label "السنة,") showing "٢٠١٩" is focused and Backspace is pressed, then onChange fires once with new CalendarDate(201, 2, 3) and the segment shows the Arabic-Indic digits "٢٠١". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support backspace with arabic digits")
- Given a focused era segment in locale "en-US-u-ca-japanese" with a heisei value, when ArrowUp and ArrowDown are pressed, then the era becomes reiwa and showa respectively; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support using the arrow keys to increment and decrement the era")
- Given a focused year segment in locale "en-US-u-ca-japanese" at reiwa year 1, when ArrowUp and ArrowDown are pressed, then the year becomes reiwa 2 going up and crosses the era boundary to heisei 30 going down; controlled, uncontrolled and isReadOnly modes are each checked. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support cycling year across era boundaries")
- Given a DatePicker with defaultValue parseZonedDateTime('2024-09-21T00:00:00[America/Los_Angeles]'), when every segment is cleared with Backspace while tabbing forward, then the group shows "mm/dd/yyyy, ––:–– AM" followed by the short time zone name for America/Los_Angeles, so the zone from defaultValue survives clearing. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should keep timeZone from defaultValue when date and time are cleared")
- Given a DatePicker with defaultValue parseZonedDateTime('2024-09-21T00:00:00[Greenwich]') that reads "9/21/2024, 12:00 AM GMT", when all segments are cleared with Backspace the group shows "mm/dd/yyyy, ––:–– AM GMT"; opening the popover then shows no aria-selected cell, clicking today's cell selects it, and clicking document.body closes the dialog and leaves the group reading today's Greenwich date and time plus " GMT". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should keep timeZone from defaultValue when date and time are cleared then set")

### SSR and hydration

- Given a DatePicker with label="Date" inside a Provider with the default theme, when rendered through testSSR, then server rendering and hydration complete without errors or hydration mismatches. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.ssr.test.js: "should render a DatePicker without errors")
- Given a DateRangePicker with label="Date range" inside a Provider, when rendered through testSSR, then server rendering and hydration complete without errors. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.ssr.test.js: "should render a DateRangePicker without errors")
- Given a DateField with label="Date" inside a Provider, when rendered through testSSR, then server rendering and hydration complete without errors. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.ssr.test.js: "should render a DateField without errors")
- Given a TimeField with label="Time" inside a Provider, when rendered through testSSR, then server rendering and hydration complete without errors. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.ssr.test.js: "should render a TimeField without errors")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a DatePicker with a ref, when ref.current.UNSAFE_getDOMNode() is called, then it returns an element that is in the document and that contains both the "Date" label text and the spinbutton segments, so the ref points at the outermost wrapper. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should return the outer most DOM element from the ref")
- Given a DatePicker with defaultValue parseZonedDateTime('2021-11-07T00:45:00-07:00[America/Los_Angeles]') and the hour segment focused, when ArrowUp is pressed three times, then onChange fires with 01:45 at -07:00, then 01:45 at -08:00 (the repeated hour of the DST fall back), then 02:45 at -08:00; three ArrowDowns retrace the same offsets back to 00:45 at -07:00, at which point the segment text is "12" rather than "0", and one more ArrowDown wraps to 11:45 at -08:00. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support cycling through DST fall back transitions")
- Given the same 2021-11-07 Los Angeles value with the minute segment cleared to aria-valuetext "Empty" by two Backspaces (the first leaves "04"), when ArrowLeft moves to the hour and ArrowUp is pressed three times, then the hour text goes 1, 1, 2 as it passes through the doubled DST hour; three ArrowDowns give 1, 1, 12 and a fourth gives 11. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DatePicker.test.js: "should support cycling through DST fall back transitions even if the minutes are undefined")
- Given the range dash element (test id date-range-dash) between the two fields, when it receives a mouse pointerdown and click, then focus lands on the start field's first segment, which contradicts the test's own name about the end date. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should focus the first segment of the end date on mouse down on the dash")
- Given placeholder text read back from the DOM, when the test compares it, then it strips Unicode isolate characters U+2066 to U+2069 from text nodes and treats a placeholder span as empty unless its parent carries the is-placeholder class, so bidi isolation marks around segments are expected in the rendered output. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/datepicker/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should display a placeholder if no value is provided")
- Given a DatePicker whose Popover contains its own Label, Group, Button, and Text, when the popover opens, then none of those inherit the field's contexts: the Label has no id, the Button has no aria-expanded, and the Group and Text have no ids, so nested components are not accidentally wired to the outer field. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DatePicker.test.js: "should clear contexts inside popover")
- Given the same setup on a DateRangePicker, when the popover opens, then the nested Label, Group, Button, and Text likewise get no inherited ids or aria state. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/DateRangePicker.test.js: "should clear contexts inside popover")

## link

### Roles and attributes

- Given `useLink({children})` with no elementType, when the hook runs, then linkProps.role is undefined (a native anchor needs none), tabIndex is 0, and an onKeyDown handler is returned. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/link/useLink.test.js: "handles defaults")
- Given `useLink({elementType: 'div'})`, when the hook runs, then linkProps.role is "link" and tabIndex is 0. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/link/useLink.test.js: "handles custom element type")
- Given `useLink({elementType: 'span', isDisabled: true})`, when the hook runs, then role is "link", `aria-disabled` is true, tabIndex is undefined so it drops out of the tab order, and an onKeyDown handler is still returned. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/link/useLink.test.js: "handles isDisabled")
- Given a Spectrum Link with a string child, when rendered, then the element is a SPAN with role link and `tabIndex="0"`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/link/Link.test.js: "Wraps string to span")
- Given `href="https://adobe.com"`, when rendered, then the element is an A with that resolved href. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/link/Link.test.js: "supports href")
- Given `data-testid` on Link, when rendered, then the data attribute lands on the link element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/link/Link.test.js: "supports custom data attributes")
- Given a RAC Link with no href, when rendered, then the element is a SPAN with class `react-aria-Link`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Link.test.js: "should render a link with default class")
- Given a RAC Link with an href, when rendered, then the element is an A with class `react-aria-Link`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Link.test.js: "should render a link with <a> element")
- Given `className="test"`, when rendered, then the default class is replaced by "test". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Link.test.js: "should render a link with custom class")
- Given `data-foo="bar"`, when rendered, then the DOM prop is forwarded. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Link.test.js: "should support DOM props")
- Given `id="my-link-id"`, when rendered, then the id is forwarded. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Link.test.js: "should support id prop")
- Given `aria-current="page"`, when rendered, then the accessibility prop is forwarded. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Link.test.js: "should support accessibility props")
- Given a LinkContext providing `slots: {test: {'aria-label': 'test'}}` and `<Link slot="test">`, when rendered, then the link has both `slot="test"` and the slot's aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Link.test.js: "should support slot")
- Given `isDisabled` on a RAC Link, when rendered, then it has `aria-disabled="true"` and the isDisabled render-prop class is applied. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Link.test.js: "should support disabled state")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given a Spectrum Link with onPress, when clicked, then onPress fires exactly once (run through `it.each` over the Link component). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/link/Link.test.js: "$Name handles defaults")
- Given a Link wrapping a custom `<a href="#only-hash-in-jsdom">` child with a ref, when rendered and clicked, then the rendered element is that A, the ref points at it, UNSAFE_className is merged onto it, the href is preserved, and onPress fires once. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/link/Link.test.js: "Wraps custom child element")
- Given a RAC Link with hover callbacks and a function className, when hovered then unhovered, then `data-hovered="true"` and the hover class appear and are removed, onHoverStart and onHoverEnd fire once each, and onHoverChange fires twice. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Link.test.js: "should support hover")
- Given a RAC Link with press callbacks, when the left mouse button goes down then up, then `data-pressed="true"` appears and clears, onPressStart, onPressEnd, onPress, onClick and onClickCapture each fire once, and onPressChange fires twice. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Link.test.js: "should support press state")

### Focus management

- Given `autoFocus` on a Spectrum Link, when rendered and timers run, then the link is the active element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/link/Link.test.js: "supports autofocus")
- Given a RAC Link with an isFocusVisible className, when tabbed to, then it is the active element with `data-focus-visible="true"` and the focus class, and tabbing away removes both. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Link.test.js: "should support focus ring")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a RAC Link whose children are a render function of `{isHovered}`, when hovered, then the text changes from "Test" to "Hovered". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Link.test.js: "should support render props")
- Given a RAC Link with an href and a `render` prop returning an anchor with `data-custom`, when rendered, then the custom element is used. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Link.test.js: "should support custom render function")
- Given a RAC Link with no href and a `render` prop returning a span, when rendered, then the custom span is used and still exposes role link. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Link.test.js: "should support custom render function without href")
- Given `UNSAFE_className="test-class"`, when rendered, then the class list contains it (run through `it.each`). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/link/Link.test.js: "$Name supports UNSAFE_className")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given a Spectrum Link inside a TooltipTrigger, when the link is tabbed to, then onOpenChange fires with true and the tooltip becomes visible; when focus moves away, onOpenChange fires with false, no further calls happen after timers run, and the tooltip is removed from the DOM. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/link/Link.test.js: "supports a wrapping tooltip trigger")

### SSR and hydration

- Given a Spectrum Link, when server rendered and hydrated, then no errors occur. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/link/Link.ssr.test.js: "should render without errors")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a Provider configured with a client router (`navigate`, `useHref` prefixing "/base") and `<Link href="/foo" routerOptions={{foo: 'bar'}}>`, when clicked, then the rendered href is "/base/foo" and navigate is called with ("/foo", {foo: 'bar'}) instead of a real page load. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/link/Link.test.js: "supports RouterProvider")
- Given a RAC RouterProvider with navigate and useHref and a Link with routerOptions, when clicked, then href is "/base/foo" and navigate receives ("/foo", {foo: 'bar'}). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Link.test.js: "should work with RouterProvider")
- Given a disabled RAC Link with an href inside a RouterProvider, when clicked, then the href still renders but neither navigate nor onClick is called. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Link.test.js: "should not navigate if disabled")

## breadcrumbs

### Roles and attributes

- Given `useBreadcrumbs({})`, when the hook runs, then navProps['aria-label'] defaults to the localized string "Breadcrumbs". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/breadcrumbs/useBreadcrumbs.test.js: "handles defaults")
- Given `useBreadcrumbs({'aria-label': 'test-label'})`, when the hook runs, then the provided aria-label wins. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/breadcrumbs/useBreadcrumbs.test.js: "handles custom aria label")
- Given `useBreadcrumbItem({elementType: 'span'})`, when the hook runs, then itemProps has tabIndex 0, role "link", no aria-disabled, and an onKeyDown handler. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/breadcrumbs/useBreadcrumbItem.test.js: "handles span elements")
- Given `useBreadcrumbItem({elementType: 'span', isCurrent: true})`, when the hook runs, then tabIndex is undefined, role is "link", and `aria-current` is "page". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/breadcrumbs/useBreadcrumbItem.test.js: "handles isCurrent")
- Given `useBreadcrumbItem({elementType: 'span', isDisabled: true})`, when the hook runs, then tabIndex is undefined, role is "link", and aria-disabled is true. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/breadcrumbs/useBreadcrumbItem.test.js: "handles isDisabled")
- Given a breadcrumb item whose child is a real `<a href>`, when the hook runs, then tabIndex is 0 and role is undefined because the native anchor already exposes link semantics. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/breadcrumbs/useBreadcrumbItem.test.js: "handles descendant link with href")
- Given a Spectrum BreadcrumbItem with a string child, when rendered, then it has a generated id and tabIndex 0. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/BreadcrumbItem.test.js: "Handles defaults")
- Given `isCurrent` on BreadcrumbItem, when rendered, then tabIndex is -1 and `aria-current="page"` is set. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/BreadcrumbItem.test.js: "Handles current")
- Given a BreadcrumbItem wrapping an `<a href>`, when rendered, then the item has an id, tabIndex 0, and the href is preserved. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/BreadcrumbItem.test.js: "Handles custom element type")
- Given Breadcrumbs with `id` and `aria-label`, when rendered, then the labelled element carries the given id. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "$Name handles defaults")
- Given three Items, when rendered, then the first two have tabIndex 0 with no aria-current and the last has tabIndex -1 with `aria-current="page"`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "Handles multiple items")
- Given a single Item with `showRoot`, when rendered, then that item renders and has tabIndex -1 since it is also the current page. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "Handles single item and showRoot")
- Given `isDisabled` on Breadcrumbs, when rendered, then every item gets `aria-disabled="true"`. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "Handles isDisabled")
- Given `aria-label="Test"`, when rendered, then the element with role navigation has that aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "supports aria-label")
- Given `aria-labelledby="test"`, when rendered, then the navigation element has that aria-labelledby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "supports aria-labelledby")
- Given `aria-describedby="test"`, when rendered, then the navigation element has that aria-describedby. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "supports aria-describedby")
- Given `data-testid` on Breadcrumbs, when rendered, then the navigation element carries it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "supports custom props")
- Given RAC Breadcrumbs with three Breadcrumb children wrapping Links, when rendered, then the container has role list with class `react-aria-Breadcrumbs`, each item has role listitem with class `react-aria-Breadcrumb`, the first link has no aria-current, and the last link has `aria-current="page"`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "should render with default class")
- Given className on Breadcrumbs and Breadcrumb, when rendered, then the custom classes replace the defaults. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "should render with custom class")
- Given data and aria props on both Breadcrumbs and each Breadcrumb, when rendered, then all are forwarded to the list and listitem elements. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "should support DOM props")
- Given a BreadcrumbsContext with a "test" slot providing aria-label and `<Breadcrumbs slot="test">`, when rendered, then the list has both the slot attribute and the slot's aria-label. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "should support slot")
- Given `size="S"`, when rendered, then the list class contains "--small". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "Handles size=\"S\"")
- Given `size="M"`, when rendered, then the list class contains "--medium". (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "Handles size=\"M\"")
- Given `UNSAFE_className="test-class"`, when rendered, then the list class list contains it. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "Handles UNSAFE_className")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given a BreadcrumbItem with onPress, when clicked, then onPress fires once. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/BreadcrumbItem.test.js: "Handles onPress")
- Given a disabled BreadcrumbItem with onPress, when clicked, then tabIndex is -1, aria-disabled is true, and onPress never fires. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/BreadcrumbItem.test.js: "Handles disabled")
- Given collapsed Breadcrumbs with showRoot and onAction, when the collapse menu button is clicked, then a menu opens containing one `menuitemradio` per breadcrumb (5), and clicking either the visible root link or its menu item calls onAction with "Folder 1"; the first click on the root closes the menu and the second triggers the action. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "can open the menu")
- Given the collapse menu open, when the menu item for the current folder (aria-checked true, last item) is clicked, then onAction is not called. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "clicking on current folder does not trigger onAction")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given a forwarded ref through a wrapper component, when rendered, then `ref.current.UNSAFE_getDOMNode()` is the breadcrumbs element. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "Should handle forward ref")
- Given RAC Breadcrumbs and Breadcrumb with refs, when rendered, then the refs point at the list and listitem elements. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "should support refs")
- Given RAC Breadcrumbs with an `items` array and a child render function, when rendered, then one listitem renders per item in order. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "should support dynamic collections")
- Given a Breadcrumb whose children are a render function of `{isCurrent}`, when rendered, then only the last item shows "Current". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "should support render props")
- Given `render` props on Breadcrumbs and Breadcrumb returning `ol` and `li` with `data-custom`, when rendered, then the custom elements are used. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "should support custom render function")

### Positioning

- Given four items in a 500px wide list where each item measures 100px, when rendered, then no collapse menu button appears and all four items are visible. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "shows four items with no menu")
- Given five items that do not all fit, when rendered, then a collapse menu button renders in the first slot, the first two items are removed from the DOM, and the last three remain (a maximum of four visible slots). (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "shows a maximum of 4 items")
- Given five items with `showRoot`, when rendered, then the root item stays visible, the collapse menu button sits in the second slot, and the middle items are dropped. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "shows a maximum of 4 items with showRoot")
- Given a 300px list with 100px items, when rendered, then only the last item plus the collapse menu button remain visible. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "shows less than 4 items if they do not fit")
- Given `showRoot` and a 300px list that cannot fit the root, when rendered, then the root item is dropped too and the menu button takes the first slot. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "collapses root item if it does not fit")
- Given `showRoot` with a 200px wide root item inside a 500px list, when rendered, then only the root and the last item are shown with the collapse button between them, so per-item widths drive how many fit. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "Handles showRoot and folders of different widths")

### SSR and hydration

- Given Spectrum Breadcrumbs with one Item, when server rendered and hydrated, then no errors occur. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.ssr.test.js: "should render without errors")
- Given RAC Breadcrumbs with three Breadcrumbs inside StrictMode, when server rendered, then the HTML already contains the three listitems with text One, Two, Three, and the same three survive hydration unchanged. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria-components/test/Breadcrumbs.ssr.test.js: "should render without errors")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given five Items that each have an href, when rendered, then only three render as links (the rest collapse) with the deepest three hrefs, and opening the collapse menu shows five `menuitemradio` items whose elements are real anchors carrying their hrefs. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "should support links")
- Given a Provider with a client router (navigate plus useHref prefixing "/base") and Items with hrefs and routerOptions, when a visible link is clicked, then the href is the prefixed one and navigate receives the unprefixed href plus that item's routerOptions; the same holds for links inside the collapse menu, each passing its own routerOptions. (react-spectrum: packages/@adobe/react-spectrum/test/breadcrumbs/Breadcrumbs.test.js: "should support RouterProvider")

## landmark

### Keyboard

- Given a nav landmark with links and a main landmark with a text field, when Tab is pressed, then focus goes to the first link rather than to the landmark element, so landmarks never join the tab order. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "can tab into a landmark region")
- Given a navigation and a main landmark, when F6 is pressed twice, then focus moves to the navigation element and then to the main element in DOM order. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "can F6 to a landmark region")
- Given a single main landmark, when F6 is pressed, then focus moves to it. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "can F6 to a landmark region when there is only one landmark")
- Given a region nested as the first child of main, when F6 is pressed repeatedly, then focus alternates main, region, main, region, and Shift+F6 walks back the other way. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "can F6 to a nested landmark region that is first")
- Given a region nested as the last child of main, when F6 is pressed repeatedly, then focus alternates main then region, and Shift+F6 reverses it. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "can F6 to a nested landmark region that is last")
- Given main containing two labelled regions, when F6 is pressed three times, then focus goes main, region 1, region 2, then wraps to main; Shift+F6 visits region 2, region 1, main. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "goes in dom order with two nested landmarks")
- Given focus on the first link inside the navigation landmark, when F6 is pressed, then focus moves to the next landmark (main). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "can F6 to the next landmark region")
- Given focus inside the navigation landmark, when F6 is pressed past the last landmark, then navigation wraps around to the first landmark's last focused element (the first link). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "landmark navigation forward wraps")
- Given a page with nav and main landmarks, when Shift+Tab is pressed from the start, then focus enters the last focusable element (the text field) then the last link, again never landing on the landmark itself. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "can shift+tab into a landmark region")
- Given nav and main landmarks with nothing focused, when Shift+F6 is pressed twice, then focus goes to main first then to navigation (backward order). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "can shift+F6 to a landmark region")
- Given focus on the text field inside main, when Shift+F6 is pressed, then focus moves back into the navigation landmark and lands on its last focused element (the third link). (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "can shift+F6 to the previous landmark region")
- Given focus on the first link in the first landmark, when Shift+F6 is pressed, then navigation wraps backward to the main landmark. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "landmark navigation backward wraps")
- Given a landmark whose inner element was focused earlier, when F6 returns to that landmark, then focus restores to the last focused element inside it rather than to the landmark element. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "F6 should focus the last focused element in a landmark region")
- Given a navigation landmark and a main landmark with a region, when Alt+F6 is pressed, then focus jumps straight to main and stays there on repeat presses, while plain F6 continues the normal cycle. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "can alt+F6 to main landmark")
- Given a page with no main landmark, when Alt+F6 is pressed, then focus does not move. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "alt+F6 does nothing if no main landmark")
- Given main as the only landmark, when Alt+F6 is pressed, then main is focused and repeat presses keep it focused. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "can alt+F6 to main landmark if main is the only landmark")
- Given a main landmark containing a region wrapped in `aria-hidden="true"`, when F6 cycles forward and backward, then the hidden region is skipped entirely and only main and the visible region are visited. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "skips over aria-hidden landmarks")

### Pointer (mouse, touch, pen, virtual click)

- Given a navigation landmark, when mouseDown and mouseUp fire on it, then focus stays on the body: landmarks are not mouse focusable. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "cannot focus landmark with mouse")

### Focus management

- Given a navigation landmark containing an ActionGroup and a main landmark containing a TableView, when F6 is pressed, then focus goes to the element each component's own focus manager last had (the second action button, then the table cell), so components that manage focus keep control. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "components that already handle focus management, should handle focus themselves")
- Given landmarks with no tabIndex, when F6 focuses one, then that landmark temporarily gains `tabIndex="-1"` and the other landmark has none; moving on transfers the attribute. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "landmark has tabIndex=\"-1\" when focused")
- Given a focused landmark, when Tab moves focus to a link, then the landmark's `tabIndex="-1"` is removed. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "loses the tabIndex=-1 if something else is focused")
- Given a focused landmark, when the active element is blurred so focus falls to the body, then the landmark loses tabIndex; pressing F6 again refocuses the same landmark and restores tabIndex. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "focus restores to previously focused landmark after blur and F6.")

### State and controlled/uncontrolled

- Given three landmarks with the focus cycle already walked, when the region is removed from the DOM by a rerender, then Shift+F6 navigates to the navigation landmark and never to the removed region. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "Should not navigate to a landmark that has been removed from the DOM")
- Given nav and main landmarks, when a region is added by a rerender, then F6 includes the new region in the cycle. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "Should navigate to a landmark that has been added to the DOM")
- Given a rerender that adds a region inside an existing main landmark, when F6 cycles, then the order is navigation, main, region. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "Should navigate to a landmark that has been added as a child to an existing landmark.")
- Given an existing region landmark, when a rerender wraps it in a new main landmark, then F6 focuses the newly added parent landmark. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "Should navigate to a landmark that has been added as a parent to an existing landmark.")
- Given two navigation landmarks with distinct labels, when a rerender makes their labels identical, then the duplicate-label console warning fires at that point, so label changes re-run the check. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "updates the landmark if the label changes")

### Dismissal and layering

- Given a button with its own onKeyDown next to a navigation landmark, when F6 is pressed while the button is focused, then focus moves to the landmark and the button's handler never sees the key (the manager stops propagation); after all landmarks unmount, F6 reaches the button's handler again, proving the listeners are cleaned up. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "cleans up event listeners if all landmarks are unmounted")

### SSR and hydration

- Given a component calling useLandmark with `role: 'main'`, when server rendered and hydrated, then no errors occur. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.ssr.test.js: "should render without errors")

### Accessibility tooling

- Given two navigation landmarks that each have an aria-label, when rendered, then no console warning is emitted. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "Should allow 2+ landmarks with same role if they are labelled.")
- Given two unlabelled navigation landmarks, when rendered, then a console warning names the duplicated role and passes the offending elements: "Page contains more than one landmark with the 'navigation' role. If two or more landmarks on a page share the same role, all must be labeled with an aria-label or aria-labelledby attribute: ". (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "Should warn if 2+ landmarks with same role are used but not labelled.")
- Given two navigation landmarks sharing the label "First nav", when rendered, then a console warning says landmarks with the same role must have unique labels and passes the elements. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "Should warn if 2+ landmarks with same role and same label")

### Notes and edge cases

- Given a focused landmark, when the browser tab is switched away and back (blur, visibilitychange hidden then visible, window focus, element focus, the Chrome event order), then the landmark is focused again and keeps `tabIndex="-1"`. This pins a Chrome tab-switching quirk. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "focuses the landmark again after toggling browser tabs")
- Given a focused landmark, when the browser window blurs and refocuses, then the landmark stays focused with its tabIndex intact. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "focuses the landmark again after toggling browser windows")
- Given focus inside the first landmark, when F6 wraps forward past the last landmark and a `react-aria-landmark-navigation` window event listener calls preventDefault, then focus does not move and the event fires once with `detail: {direction: 'forward'}`, which is how an outer shell (for example a browser extension or host app) can take over landmark navigation. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "landmark navigation fires custom event when wrapping forward")
- Given the same setup, when Shift+F6 wraps backward and the custom event is prevented, then focus stays put and the event fires once with `detail: {direction: 'backward'}`. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "landmark navigation fires custom event when wrapping backward")
- Given no landmarks and no controller, when F6 is pressed, then no landmark navigation event fires; after `UNSTABLE_createLandmarkController()` the key fires the event once, and after `controller.dispose()` it stops firing again. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "should ensure keyboard listeners are active")
- Given a controller and focus on the first link, when `controller.focusNext()` then `controller.navigate('forward')` run, then focus moves to main and then wraps to the first link. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "should navigate forward")
- Given a controller and focus in the text field, when `controller.focusPrevious()` then `controller.navigate('backward')` run, then focus moves to navigation and then back to the text field. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "should navigate backward")
- Given a controller and focus in the text field, when `controller.focusMain()` runs, then main is focused. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "should focus main")
- Given any landmark controller, when created, then the manager is stored on `document[Symbol.for('react-aria-landmark-manager')]` exposing a numeric `version`, `createLandmarkController`, and `registerLandmark`, which is how multiple copies of the library share one manager. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "should store the landmark manager on the document")
- Given an existing manager and controller, when a higher-version manager object is put on the document and a `react-aria-landmark-manager-change` event is dispatched, then the new manager gets registerLandmark and createLandmarkController called once each, the existing controller proxies navigate (with the direction and undefined options), focusNext, focusPrevious, focusMain and dispose through to the new controller, and unmounting the component calls the new manager's unregister. (react-spectrum: packages/react-aria/test/landmark/useLandmark.test.tsx: "should replace the singleton with a new version")

## Test infrastructure notes

### Runner and environment

- Jest with `@swc/jest` as the transform, `testEnvironment: 'jsdom'`, `testTimeout: 20000`, roots at `packages/`, and `testMatch: **/packages/**/*.test.[tj]s?(x)` (jest.config.js).
- The main config ignores `*.ssr.test.*` and `*.browser.test.*`, so there are three suites: jsdom unit tests, an SSR suite, and a real-browser suite.
- The SSR suite runs from `jest.ssr.config.js` with `testMatch: **/packages/**/*.ssr.test.[tj]s?(x)`, a 30s timeout, and `globalSetup`/`globalTeardown` from `@react-spectrum/test-utils-internal/src/ssrSetup`. `testSSR(__filename, source, assertFn)` renders the JSX source string on the server, runs the callback against the server HTML, then hydrates and lets the test assert again, failing on any hydration mismatch warning.
- `*.browser.test.tsx` files run in a real browser under vitest with `vitest-browser-react`, for behavior jsdom cannot model: `scrollIntoView`, real layout and `getBoundingClientRect`, virtualizer scrolling, CSS grid arrow navigation, shadow DOM focus, and real pointer events. `ComboBox.browser.test.tsx` notes that `enableShadowDOM()` is a one-way flag, so shadow DOM tests must come last.
- `clearMocks: true` globally, so every `jest.fn()` is cleared between tests.

### Global setup (scripts/setupTests.js)

- `@testing-library/jest-dom` matchers are available everywhere (`toHaveAttribute`, `toHaveFocus`, `toHaveTextContent`, `toBeInTheDocument`, `toBeDisabled`, `toHaveValue`, ...).
- `mock-match-media/jest-setup` replaces `window.matchMedia` and `cleanupMatchMedia()` runs after each test. `simulateMobile()` and `simulateDesktop()` from `@react-spectrum/test-utils-internal` drive this mock, which is how the iOS and Android tray code paths are exercised in jsdom.
- Any `console.error` or `console.warn` throws and fails the test, except a short allowlist (`ReactDOM.render is no longer supported in React 18`, `ReactDOMTestUtils.act is deprecated`, Browserslist staleness). React act warnings and prop-type warnings hard-fail, which is why nearly every interaction is wrapped in `act`. Tests that expect a warning use `using spyWarn = jest.spyOn(console, 'warn').mockImplementation(() => {})` with explicit resource management.
- `unhandledRejection` is rethrown so async failures do not silently pass.
- Custom matcher `expect.extend({toContainObject})`: asserts an array contains an object matching the given subset.
- `window.IntersectionObserver` is stubbed with a no-op observe/unobserve/disconnect in a global `beforeEach` and deleted afterwards. Suites that need to drive it use `setupIntersectionObserverMock({observe})` and call `observer.instance.triggerCallback([{isIntersecting: true}])` to fire load-more sentinels.
- `document.documentElement.clientWidth`/`clientHeight` are forced to 1024x768 in a global `beforeEach` because jsdom reports 0. Overlay positioning depends on this.

### Interaction style

- Newer tests use `@testing-library/user-event` via `userEvent.setup({delay: null, pointerMap})`, where `pointerMap` comes from `@react-aria/test-utils`. `delay: null` means no real waiting between key events, so timer-dependent behavior is advanced explicitly. `user.keyboard('{ArrowUp>3/}')` produces held-key repeats; `user.pointer({target, keys: '[MouseLeft>]'})` and `'[TouchA]'` separate mouse from touch.
- Older tests use `fireEvent` directly, usually in matched pairs (`pointerDown`/`pointerUp` plus `mouseDown`/`mouseUp` plus `click`, or `touchStart`/`touchEnd`) because `usePress` listens to whichever event family exists. Many suites run the same body under `describe.each(['mouse', 'keyboard', 'touch'])`.
- Virtual clicks (screen reader activation, `detail: 0`, `pointerType: 'virtual'`) are simulated with `fireEvent.click(el, {detail: 0})` or `el.click()`; several components have dedicated tests for that path.
- `installPointerEvent()` from `@react-aria/test-utils` defines a fake `global.PointerEvent` subclassing `MouseEvent` that exposes `pointerType`, `pointerId`, `pageX/pageY`, `width`, `height` in `beforeAll` and deletes it in `afterAll`. Suites call it to switch the press code onto the Pointer Events branch and to make touch detection work; without it the code falls back to mouse and touch events.
- `installMouseEvent()` patches `MouseEvent` so `pageX`/`pageY` passed to `fireEvent.mouse*` are readable. Slider, color area, and drag tests rely on it.
- `triggerLongPress({element, advanceTimer, pointerOpts})` fires the pointer sequence and advances past the 500ms long press threshold (`DEFAULT_LONG_PRESS_TIME` in packages/@react-aria/test-utils/src/utils.ts). `triggerTouch(el)` is used where `user.pointer` would register as a virtual press in jsdom.
- `mockClickDefault()` installs a window click listener so link navigation can be asserted without jsdom navigating; some call sites pass `{capture: true}` or `{once: true}` and remove the listener by hand.
- `jest.useFakeTimers()` is the norm for anything with a transition, delay, or animation: overlay open and close, menu and submenu hover delays, tooltip warmup, long press, typeahead timeout, the 500ms loading spinner delay, the 400ms then 60ms stepper auto-repeat, toast timeouts, virtualizer scroll debounce, and combobox announcements. `act(() => jest.runAllTimers())` or `jest.advanceTimersByTime(n)` steps them; `new User({advanceTimer: jest.advanceTimersByTime})` bridges the testers to fake timers, and several suites deliberately run the same flows under both real and fake timers.
- jsdom gaps are patched per suite with `jest.spyOn(HTMLElement.prototype, 'getBoundingClientRect')`, `offsetWidth`/`offsetHeight`/`clientWidth`/`clientHeight`/`scrollHeight` via `Object.defineProperty` or getter spies, `scrollIntoView`, `window.getComputedStyle = el => el.style` (the real one is slow in this jsdom), `document.elementFromPoint`, `window.ontouchstart`, and `jest.spyOn(navigator, 'platform'|'userAgent', 'get')` for Mac, Windows, iPhone, iPad, and Android behavior. The live announcer is usually replaced with `jest.mock('react-aria/src/live-announcer/LiveAnnouncer')` so `announce` calls can be asserted.

### @react-aria/test-utils testers

`new User({interactionType, advanceTimer})` builds a `userEvent` instance (`delay: null`, `pointerMap`) and `user.createTester('<Pattern>', {root, ...})` returns a pattern tester. `interactionType` is mouse, touch, or keyboard and every method can override it per call. `advanceTimer` defaults to a real `setTimeout` promise and is needed for patterns with timers.
Testers exported: CheckboxGroup, ComboBox, Dialog, GridList, ListBox, Menu, RadioGroup, Select, Table, Tabs, Tree. There is no Autocomplete, Slider, NumberField, DateField, or TagGroup tester; RAC instead ships shared parameterized suites (`AriaMenu.test-util.tsx`, `AriaAutocomplete.test-util.tsx`, `AriaTree.test-util.tsx`) run once per renderer, and Spectrum's TableView reuses `test/table/TableTests.js` the same way.

- MenuTester: `setInteractionType`, `open({interactionType, needsLongPress, direction})` (press, long press, or ArrowUp/ArrowDown in keyboard modality, then waits for `aria-controls` to resolve), `close()` (Escape, then asserts focus returned to the trigger and the menu left the DOM), `getTrigger()`, `getMenu()` (resolved through `aria-controls`, so null while closed), `getSections()`, `getOptions({element})`, `getSubmenuTriggers()` (options with `aria-haspopup`), `findOption({indexOrText})`, `toggleOptionSelection({option, interactionType, menuSelectionMode, keyboardActivation, closesOnSelect, needsLongPress})` which opens the menu if needed, throws on a disabled option in keyboard mode, and waits for focus to leave the menu when it should close, and `openSubmenu({submenuTrigger, interactionType})` which returns a nested MenuTester rooted at that trigger.
- ListBoxTester: `setInteractionType`, `getListbox()`, `getOptions({element})`, `getSelectedOptions()`, `getSections()`, `findOption({indexOrText})`, `toggleOptionSelection({option, interactionType, keyboardActivation, needsLongPress, selectionBehavior})` which adds Ctrl or Cmd automatically when `selectionBehavior: 'replace'`, and `triggerOptionAction({option, interactionType, needsDoubleClick})`.
- ComboBoxTester: `setInteractionType`, `open({interactionType, triggerBehavior})` where triggerBehavior is manual or focus, `close()`, `getCombobox()`, `getTrigger()`, `getListbox()`, `getSections()`, `getOptions({element})`, `getFocusedOption()` (resolves `aria-activedescendant`), `findOption({indexOrText})`, `toggleOptionSelection({..., closesOnSelect})`.
- SelectTester: `setInteractionType`, `open({interactionType})` (click, focus plus Enter, or a touch press, then waits for the listbox), `close()` (focuses the listbox, Escape, asserts focus returned to the trigger), `getTrigger()`, `getListbox()`, `getSections()`, `getOptions({element})`, `findOption({indexOrText})`, `toggleOptionSelection({..., closesOnSelect})` which infers closesOnSelect from `aria-multiselectable` and throws on disabled options.
- GridListTester: `setInteractionType`, `getGridlist()`, `getRows()`, `getSelectedRows()`, `getCells({element})`, `findRow({indexOrText})`, `toggleRowSelection({row, interactionType, checkboxSelection, selectionBehavior, needsLongPress})` which targets only the given row, `triggerRowAction({row, interactionType, needsDoubleClick})`. Both reject on a disabled row.
- TableTester: `setInteractionType`, `getTable()`, `getRowGroups()`, `getColumns()`, `getRows({element})`, `getSelectedRows()`, `getFooterRows()`, `getRowHeaders()`, `getCells({element})`, `findRow({indexOrText})`, `findCell({text})`, `toggleRowSelection(...)`, `toggleSelectAll({interactionType})`, `toggleRowExpansion(...)` for tree grids, `toggleSort({column, interactionType})`, `triggerColumnHeaderAction({column, action, interactionType})`, `triggerRowAction(...)`.
- TreeTester: `setInteractionType`, `getTree()`, `getRows()`, `getSelectedRows()`, `getCells({element})`, `findRow({indexOrText})`, `toggleRowSelection(...)`, `toggleRowExpansion(...)`, `triggerRowAction(...)`.
- DialogTester, TabsTester, CheckboxGroupTester, and RadioGroupTester exist too; the dialog one is used by menu, select, and combobox tests to reach an open overlay.
- Worth knowing for a conformance suite: `toggleOptionSelection` is also what the tests use to fire a plain action on a non-selectable menu, and several tester methods contain their own `waitFor` assertions about focus restoration, so a test that merely calls them is implicitly pinning focus behavior.
